jobs.occupation: Research Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Pferformance Portability (Softwareentwickler/in)
jobs.description: The German Climate Computing Centre (DKRZ) is the central simulation and data processing facility for the German climate and Earth system modelling community and one of the leading institutions in this field worldwide. DKRZ not only operates supercomputers of the highest performance class and one of the largest data and archive systems, but also participates in many national and international projects aimed at improving the software and infrastructure for climate modelling. Here we are offering a position asResearch Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Performance PortabilityYour tasksA key focus for DKRZ is the development of the climate and weather model ICON, and its further preparation for current and future HPC systems. Within the European PHOENIX project, we aim to develop a maintainable, performance-portable version of ICON that runs efficiently on heterogeneous CPU and GPU architectures. In this context, you will contribute to the development, integration, and optimisation of ICON on the largest European supercomputers.Your work will focus on several aspects of performance-portable scientific software, depending on your background and interests. This includes integrating ICON components based on different programming approaches, such as C++/Kokkos, DaCe, and gt4py, improving their interoperability, and enabling efficient execution on different HPC architectures, particularly NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, but also possible future compute architectures.Further areas of work include improving ICON's efficiency and scalability at very high spatial resolutions. You may also explore the use of mixed precision and AI-oriented hardware features for climate models, or improve the efficient concurrent execution and coupling of ICON with other components. The specific focus of your work will be determined together with the project team, allowing complementary contributions to the different development tasks.Qualifications / Experiences● Academic degree in computer science, applied mathematics, computational physics/engineering, or a related field with a clear focus on scientific computing● Experience in high-performance computing, performance portability, and optimising scientific applications for modern hardware● Experience with scientific software development, ideally involving large, collaboratively developed applications● Programming experience with Fortran or C/C++, ideally in the context of scientific or parallel applications● Experience with parallel programming, for example MPI or GPU programming● Familiarity with performance-portable programming approaches such as DaCe, gt4py, or similar technologies is an advantage● Programming experience under Unix/Linux, including scripting languages such as Python or Bash; experience with HPC environments, performance analysis, or code optimisation is an advantage● Motivation to support open, collaborative, and community-oriented software development● Very good communication skills and knowledge of EnglishEmployment conditionsWe offer work in interdisciplinary teams and excellent connections to national and international research networks. In addition to specific development goals and requirements from our project partners, your work will be characterised by the freedom to explore and implement solutions at the interface between high-performance computing, scientific software engineering, and Earth system modelling. Participation in international conferences, project meetings, and hackathons provides opportunities for further training, exchange with the international HPC community, and presentation of your own results wherever meaningful.We are based in Hamburg, but want to create a suitable working environment by offering flexible working hours and location (up to 100% work from home within Germany). Remuneration will be based on the candidate's qualifications according to TVöD-Bund. You can ideally start already in February 2027, but the exact starting date can be agreed individually. The position is financed by third-party funded projects and is limited until the end of 2029.Interested applicants are requested to compile a single pdf document containing a cover letter, a detailed CV and any additional documents (e.g. professional references). Applications must be submitted via the portal https://dkrz.softgarden.io/de/vacancies.Application deadline : Priority will be given to applications received by 30 November 2026.Questions? Dr. Jan Frederik Engels (engels@dkrz.de) and Dr. Hendryk Bockelmann (bockelmann@dkrz.de) will be happy to answer them in advance.

Constructor University is a private, state-accredited, English-language research university located on a green, 34-hectare residential campus in Bremen, Germany. Founded in 2001, the university offers Bachelor's, Master's, and PhD programs across three schools: the School of Science, the School of Computer Science and Engineering, and the School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences. Constructor University is home to approximately 2,500 students and researchers from more than 120 countries. All teaching, research, and academic administration are conducted in English, within an international community that is among the most diverse of any university in Germany. According to the 2027 Times Higher Education World University Rankings, Constructor University ranks among the top 17 percent of universities worldwide in both Social Sciences and Engineering; moreover, it scores 92 out of 100 for International Outlook and 84 out of 100 for Industry. The indicators that reflect both the quality of its academic environment and the breadth of its engagement with the wider world.The School of Business, Social and Decision Sciences brings together management, behavioral science, data analytics, and decision theory under one roof. Its programs, ranging from undergraduate studies in International Business Administration to the MBA, MSc in Data Science for Society and Business, and doctoral education, attract professionally ambitious and internationally minded students. The School is also home to approximately 50 doctoral researchers, contributing to an active and growing research environment. Marketing represents a strategic new direction for the School, and this position offers an opportunity to help shape the field from the outset, develop an independent research agenda in a genuinely interdisciplinary environment, and contribute to a School that is actively expanding.Constructor University invites applications for the following position, to be filled ideally by Fall 2027:Assistant Professor of Marketing (f/m/d)(Full-time; 38,5h/week, tenure-track)School of Business, Social and Decision SciencesYour Responsibilities:In this position, you will support our research and teaching activities in the field of Marketing. The successful candidate will be teaching courses (for example Digital Marketing), supporting and advising students on their studies and supervising Bachelor, Master’s and PhD theses and research projects.Possible areas of interest are: - Design and teach innovative, contemporary modules in Marketing at undergraduate and master’s levels, including within MBA, MA, and MSc programs.- Engage, advise, and mentor students; supervise Bachelor’s, Master’s theses, and doctoral research- Build and sustain an active research agenda with publications in leading peer-reviewed journals- Establish a research group and pursue external funding from national and international sources- Contribute to curriculum development, new program initiatives, and departmental serviceThe university is highly supportive of junior faculty, providing both formal and informal mentoring, administrative support, as well as a flexible budget for establishing an internationally visible research group. Several opportunities exist to develop transdisciplinary research projects in collaboration with other research groups or our industrial partners.Your Qualifications and Experience:- PhD in Marketing or a closely related field- Evidence of high-quality research and a strong publication pipeline- Ability to design and teach core Marketing courses at undergraduate and graduate levels- Expertise in areas such as Digital Marketing, Marketing Analytics, Consumer Behavior, AI in Marketing, or related fields is particularly welcome- Readiness to pursue external research funding and contribute to collaborative research projects- Ability and willingness to supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s theses and contribute to doctoral supervision- Willingness to work and teach in a multicultural, English-speaking academic environment- Excellent written and spoken English and strong intercultural competenceWhat you can expect at Constructor University: Constructor University guarantees the academic freedom of every faculty member. Junior faculty receive formal and informal mentoring, administrative support, and dedicated start-up and research group budgets to help establish their work. The university has an active portfolio of Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ funded projects and a culture of interdisciplinary collaboration across its three schools, creating genuine opportunities for joint initiatives and externally funded research. Beyond the academic environment, you will find a campus that is genuinely close-knit: small classes, direct faculty-student engagement, and a community where diversity is lived rather than declared. Language courses and sports facilities are part of everyday life on campus. Constructor University consistently achieves top results in national and international university rankings, in the CHE Ranking, the most comprehensive and detailed ranking of the German-speaking higher education landscape, Constructor University has achieved top placements every year since its first participation in 2005. The campus is located in Bremen. Bremen is a vibrant, livable Hanseatic city with an international character, affordable by European standards, well connected by rail and air, and home to a growing academic and innovation community. Relocating here is, for most, a pleasant discovery.The position is tenure-track, with review after an initial three-year contract, followed by a second three-year contract. Successful evaluation leads to permanence and typically promotion to Associate Professor level. Constructor University is an equal opportunity employer and particularly welcomes applications that would improve the university’s faculty profile with reference to gender and national origin.Your Application:If you have any questions about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Çağrı Bulut via Mail (cbulut@constructor.university (https://mailto:cbulut@constructor.university) ).Constructor University offers full equal opportunity to all qualified applications. We value diversity and inclusion and encourage all qualified people to apply. We especially encourage applications from traditionally underrepresented groups.Please upload your documents in a single PDF document, including a letter of motivation stating your field of expertise, curriculum vitae, teaching portfolio, publication record, copies of certificates and diplomas, certification of English proficiency (optional), and the names and addresses of two referees in our application management system.The deadline for submission of applications 15.01.2027.The review of applications will begin immediately.Please note that only applications submitted through the official application portal will be considered for recognition.Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Department of Marine Zoologyat the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as 06 January 2027:** Researcher (m/f/d) in Deep-Sea Biodiversity and Taxonomy****(Part-Time: 50%)**Employment scope: 50%Part-TimeType of contract: Limited to 1 year (06 January 2027to 10 February 2028)Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.Funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG), the HADALquake project investigates how earthquake-induced submarine landslides affect life and elemental cycles in the deepest parts of the ocean. The project focuses on comparing conditions before and after recent earthquakes in the Kermadec and Tonga trench systems in the South Pacific.Your tasks- The scientist is primarily responsible for processing of the benthic animal groups:- Assistance in sorting the benthic material- Quantitative extraction and determination of the macrofauna with special consideration of an abundant, selected taxon, such as the Isopoda or another peracarid taxon.- Biodiversity analysis and analysis of biogeography of the Isopoda- Biogeographical comparison of selected taxon with previous data from the South Pacific- Preparation of individuals for genetic analysis (barcoding gene fragments and other gene fragments to support taxonomic questions and phylogenetic analysesYour profile- A completed university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in biology, marine biology or a related discipline.- Research experience in the taxonomy, biodiversity and biogeography of deep-sea benthic invertebrates, particularly isopod crustaceans.- Practical experience in scientific research cruises, biological sample processing and species identification.- Experience in biodiversity data management and statistical analyses using R.- Good written and spoken English.- Willingness and availability to participate in the research expedition: 06 January 2027, departure in Suva, Fidschi to 10 February 2028, arriving in Wellington, New Zealand.Desirable skills- Knowledge of deep-sea sampling. Identification of deep-sea Isopoda, Amphipoda and/or another peracarid taxon (Crustacea, Malacostraca).We offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply, as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 08.11.2026.Please submit your application via our online application system. You don't just oversee compliance – you actively get your hands dirty solving the technical problems that stand between an idea and a certified aircraft.You lead our Engineering, Development, and Certification functions, coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers, and act as the technical interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness, ensuring robust oversight, clear accountability, and the highest standards of regulatory compliance. and Design Assurance Responsibilities- Establish, maintain, and continuously improve the documented Design Assurance System — hands-on, not just on paper.- Ensure that all design work is undertaken in accordance with the Design Assurance System, BCAR A8-21, and other applicable airworthiness regulations.- Ensure that all design activities remain within the scope of the company's approved design privileges.- Ensure that for all design work, compliance with the applicable type certification basis or equivalent is properly demonstrated and verified.- Ensure that flight testing is carried out in accordance with regulatory requirements.- Sign Declarations of Compliance after satisfactory verification of compliance with applicable airworthiness requirements.- Confirm that all design procedures specified in the Design Organisation Exposition have been followed by signing a Declaration of Compliance for each type approval, type certification, design change, or repair design.Organisational and Management Responsibilities- Lead and manage the Engineering, Development, and Certification functions of the Design Organisation, staying close to the technical detail rather than managing from a distance.- Manage and coordinate external Compliance Verification Engineers.- Provide technical oversight and interface to the independent Head of Airworthiness function.- Ensure qualification, competency, and training of engineering and certification personnel.- Coordinate and manage design, development, certification, and flight test programmes with internal and external stakeholders.- Provide strong project management across design, development, certification, and flight test programmes — planning, scheduling, and managing resources with internal and external stakeholders to keep programmes on time and on budget.- Provide technical authority for design decisions, certification strategies, and design changes, personally stepping in when problems get stuck between departments.- Ensure complete, controlled, and traceable design documentation for certification, production, continued airworthiness, and future investigations.- Provide technical support to production, quality, customer support, and incident investigations where required.- Actively identify inefficiencies and gaps in existing processes and drive their resolution with an entrepreneurial, get-it-done mindset.Required Qualifications- Degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or a comparable technical qualification.- Extensive professional experience in a regulated industrial environment; experience gained within a German company as well as senior-level experience from the automotive industry are highly desirable.- Proven track record in leading engineering teams, driving technical decisions, and taking full accountability for results, timelines, and compliance.- Strong and practical expertise in complex systems engineering, including electrical and avionics integration.- Solid experience with regulatory frameworks and compliance environments (e.g. DULV BUT, BCAR Section T, UK CAA, FAA, CAAC).- A true problem solver: someone energized rather than deterred and decision-making authority — someone who rolls up their sleeves rather than delegating every difficult problem.- Ability to challenge existing structures, enforce standards, and drive implementation across interfaces (Engineering, Certification, Production, Quality).- High level of ownership, resilience, and confidence when operating in complex, regulated, and time-critical environments.- An intrapreneurial mindset: you treat the Design Organisation as if it were your own venture, take initiative beyond the formal job description, and are comfortable building and improving processes rather than just following them.- English, German & Chinese: mandatory (written and spoken).Benefits- Dynamic working environment with the global leader in gyroplane manufacturing.- Comprehensive onboarding and continuous training opportunities.- Supportive and international team culture.- Flexible working hours (flexitime) to support work–life balance.- Corporate fitness programme (Hansefit).- Employer contributions to the pension scheme.- Employee discounts via our corporate benefits platform.- Regular company events that strengthen team spirit.- Free daily lunch at our headquarter.- Overtime compensation and additional paid leave for special occasions.- Unique aviation experience – including a gyrocopter sightseeing flight.Are you ready for an exciting career in aviation? PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. jobs.description: Create your own happiness!Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?What you can look forward to…The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term, but an extension is possible.Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the children (age 1-6) entrusted to us in line with our educational approach, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. In your daily work, you would speak mainly English.We would appreciate at least some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.The Team: One for all, all for one!Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.Has this piqued your curiosity? Then you should definitely keep reading…Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.Feel free to get to know us!The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 42-48 children are currently cared for by nine early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

jobs.description: ...you're in the middle of itThe Institute of Clinical Pharmacology at Goethe University Frankfurt is seeking a PhD Candidate / Doctoral Researcher to join the research group of Dr. Hahnefeld. The successful candidate will contribute to an interdisciplinary research project in cooperation with the Fraunhofer ITMP Frankfurt at the interface of analytical chemistry, lipid biology and inflammation research.The project investigates how lipid metabolism and lipid-mediated signaling are regulated in inflammatory settings. The work combines cell-based experiments with mass spectrometry-based lipidomics, fatty acid analysis and targeted lipid mediator measurements. A particular focus will be placed on the development, optimization and application of robust analytical and computational workflows for the analysis of complex biological datasets. The research group uses high-resolution mass spectrometry and reproducible bioinformatic approaches to investigate lipid-mediated mechanisms in inflammatory and metabolic diseases. The position offers the opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment with interdisciplinary partners in lipid biology, immunology, imaging and proteomics.The position is limited up to three years.Your Role:- Plan, conduct and document experiments in cellular models of inflammation and metabolic perturbation.- Prepare biological samples and perform LC-HRMS-based lipidomics and methods.- Perform comprehensive quality control, raw-data validation, data annotation and statistical analysis of complex mass spectrometry datasets.- Develop and apply reproducible workflows for data processing, visualization and interpretation using R and/or Python.- Contribute to the integration and interpretation of lipidomics data with complementary datasets generated by collaborating groups, including imaging- and proteomics-based data.- Validate selected findings in close collaboration with project partners.- Present research results in scientific publications, project meetings and at Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.About UsThe Hannover Medical School (MHH), with about 10,000 employees the biggest company of Lower Saxony, is a university institution for research and teaching in the human and dental medicine and a university hospital of supra-maximum medical care. Research, teaching, medical care and administration work hand in hand in the integration model at the MHH-campus.The Peter L. Reichertz Institute for Medical Informatics (PLRI) is one of the largest university centres for medical informatics in Germany. It belongs to two leading universities, is situated in one of Europe's most research-intensive regions, and offers excellent opportunities for research. In interdisciplinary projects, the PLRI collaborates with health centres, research institutes, corporations, and public institutions in order to shape the future of the health system and medicine. The activities range from diverse topics on the local level, to regional, national, and global collaborations.The research group "Clinical Data Science" focuses on the detection of novel routine clinical and -omics biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis to personalize and thus improve patient treatment. To achieve this, we integrate phenotypical information and routine clinical as well as (multi)-omics data by high-dimensional statistics and state-of-the-art artificial intelligence to gain novel insights into underlying disease pathomechanisms. Moreover, we are interested in developing and implementing research data platforms for complex (multi-)omics data. The project "MALDIDive: Enabling AI Research with Public MALDI-TOF Fingerprints across Microbial Diversity", to be carried out within an interdisciplinary research team and funded by the German Research Foundation, will establish a well curated data platform of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry datasets from the Leibniz Institute German Collection of Mircoorganisms and Cell Cultures GmbH (DSMZ). We are looking for an enthusiastic PostDoc who is interested in omics data platform development and deployment for future AI use.Your Responsibilities- data platform architecture, backend, and frontend development as well as deployment for MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry database/platform and associated metadata- development of interactive data visualization concepts and their implementation into data platform- development and realization of short explanatory videos for platform users- co-organization and co-leading of stakeholder workshops to define user requirements and conduct user test cycles- presentation to the scientific community, i.e., by publishing in high-level journals and via presentations at international conferences- close collaboration with interdisciplinary project partners from AI / data science, analytical, and micro­biological research communities, particularly the DSMZ- bachelor / master student co-supervisionYour Profile- PhD / Dr. rer. nat. / Dr.-Ing. degree in data science / bioinformatics / computational biology / informatics / physics or similar research fields- expertise in the work on databases, interactive platform development, -omics and biomedical data, and / or artificial intelligence / machine learning- proficiency in backend / frontend development and / or database programming, including one or more of the following programming languages: VueJS, TypeScript, SQL, PYTHON, R Shiny, nginx, Docker, etc.- proficiency in English (written and oral)- desired: experience with code documentary systems and RestAPI- desired: knowledge of the German languageWe offer- a full-time position initially limited to two years with 38.5 hours per week at one of the largest employers in the state of Lower Saxony- depending on your individual jobs.occupation: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project (Fachinformatiker/in - Anwendungsentwicklung)
jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation, CV, relevantcertificates and references, if available) electronically as a single PDF by 15. November2026.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt am MainFor specific questions about this role, please contact Dr. Hanieh Saeediat hanieh.saeedi@senckenberg.de

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its institute Senckenberg am Meer, German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research in Hamburg , starting as soon as possibleResearch Scientist and Project Coordinator (m/f/d) in the field of Zooplankton Biodiversity(full time / part-time )Location: HamburgEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options availableType of contract: temporary contract limited until 30.09.2029Remuneration: collective agreement of the state Hesse, TV-H E13﻿The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.As part of the institute “Senckenberg am Meer” located in Wilhelmshaven, with its two departments Marine Research and German Centre for Marine Biodiversity Research (DZMB), the Hamburg research site, which belongs to the DZMB, focuses on researching taxonomy and systematics of marine life forms.The position is based within the Zooplankton Working Group and is part of the joint project ZooM-In (Innovative Methods for National Zooplankton Monitoring), contributing to the further development and standardization of modern methods for marine biodiversity monitoring. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety (BMUKN) through the National Biodiversity Monitoring Centre’s initiative Sustainable Biodiversity Monitoring.The project will be carried out in close cooperation with the Helmholtz Institute for Functional Marine Biodiversity (HIFMB) as well as federal and state authorities.Your tasks- Project management of the project ZooM-In- Organisation of and participation in monthly expeditions (March-October, 3-4 days per months) to the North Sea- Organisation of project workshops- Assessment of zooplankton biodiversity by imaging technologies- Cross validation of zooplankton biodiversity assessment by traditional microscopy, molecular genetics and imaging methods- Communication of project results to stakeholders- Publication of project results in peer-reviewed journals- Writing of a project reportYour profile- Master degree in marine biology or natural sciences- Expertise in the application of plankton imaging technologies (ZooScan and/or PlanktoScope)- Relevant knowledge on molecular genetic analyses of organisms, ideally metabarcoding of zooplankton- Experience in data analyses, preferably using R- Experience with sea-going expeditions on research vessels and sampling of plankton, resilience to motion sickness- Willingness to participate in interdisciplinary work- Very good communication skills, ability to work in a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary and international environment- Very good command of English (written and spoken)- Sound command of the German language is essential for this positionWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension plan- Senckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) (as a single PDF, max. 10 MB) on our career pagehttps://www.senckenberg.de/de/karriere/ by 8 November 2026 .For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/.For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de.ContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.If you have any specific questions about this role, please contact Prof. Dr. Jasmin Renz at jasmin.renz@senckenberg.de.

The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. We welcome applications from all background.The Max-Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals.To apply please complete the online application form and attach you English CV and motivation letter as well as all relevant certificates latest 15th November, 2026.If you have any questions, please feel free to contact contact Dr. Friedjof Tellkamp by email at friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:friedjof.tellkamp@mpsd.mpg.de) or Dr. Lars Tiemann at lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de (lars.tiemann@mpsd.mpg.de) .Detailed information about the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter and the online application portal can be found on our website at: https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/karriere/jobs)We look forward to your application.

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years; the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile - Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills - Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer - Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card  with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement  – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply? Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/)For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de (http://www.senckenberg.de)Contact Senckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 40%

jobs.occupation: 23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – HamburgResearchThe program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. jobs.description: In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number ofPostdoctoral Researcher positions.- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department currently hosts Ramin Golestanian (director), Philip Bittihn (group leader), Suropriya Saha (group leader), and a number of postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.The researchThe postdoctoral researchers will engage in theoretical and computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter. For more information, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).Your profileWe are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated researchers with relevant background and good communication skills to join our research team. The ideal candidate should have:- A PhD/DPhil degree (or comparable) with a background in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;- Prior experience with nonequilibrium statistical physics and a strong interest in active matter physics;- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary is in accordance with the German state public service salary scale (E13 TVöD-Bund) and the corresponding social benefits. Working hours are full time. We offer opportunities regarding work life balance as well as health promotion services. The postdoctoral appointment is for two years. The starting date is flexible.The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. We encourage applications from women, especially in areas where they are underrepresented, which includes theoretical physics. Moreover, we are committed to providing suitable working environment for everyone including individuals with disabilities.Your applicationTo apply, please follow this link (https://s.b-ite.com/vd1cg)  and submit your CV, publication list, a statement of research interest, and contacts of two referees. jobs.occupation: PhD Position on Femtosecond Spectroscopy of Chiral Molecular Ions (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Job available in 2 locations: Kassel, BremenWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionA PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.About the TRILOGY Doctoral NetworkTRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.About the PhD ProjectThe selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.Key Research Activities- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.Candidate ProfileApplicants should have:- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection- Excellent written and spoken English.- Good written and oral communication skills.- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.MSCA Mobility and Eligibility RequirementsAs the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.Application DocumentsApplications should include:- Cover letter- Detailed curriculum vitae- Academic transcripts- Copy of the Master's thesis- Scientific publication, if available- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.Selection ProcessCandidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.Key InformationPosition: PhD Researcher / Doctoral CandidateNumber of positions: 1Research areas: Physics, Engineering, ChemistryResearcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)Contract: Temporary, full-timeWorking hours: 35 hours per weekCountry: GermanyWork locations: Bremen and KasselFunding: Horizon Europe – Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral NetworkProject: TRILOGYMarie Curie Grant Agreement: 101226887If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter.At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Your applicationPlease submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable.We look forward to receiving your application!Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.Your tasks•  Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil.•  Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses.•  Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility.•  Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico.•  Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings.Your qualifications•  Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field.•  Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided.•  Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning.•  Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research.•  Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English.•  Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite.We offer•  A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration.•  Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise.•  An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences.•  Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies.•  Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified.This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration.The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT.
