• Some knowledge of SimCorp Dimension is clearly a plus, especially if you have worked with front-office, portfolio management, or investment workflows.

Ways of working

• Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

• Ability to structure ambiguous problems and turn them into practical next steps.

• Curiosity about users, workflows, and the “why” behind product decisions.

• Pragmatic, outcome-oriented mindset.

• Ability to zoom out to understand portfolio manager goals — and zoom in to refine workflows, interactions, and details.

• Confidence working with engineers, designers, product peers, and client-facing colleagues.

• Willingness to learn product-management practices if your background is advisory, consulting, or pre-sales.

As a person, you:

• Collaborate naturally with colleagues across disciplines.

• Are comfortable questioning assumptions and navigating complexity.

• Communicate clearly and speak up when needed.

• Balance structure with creativity.

• Care deeply about usability — not just functional completeness.

• Are motivated by creating software that solves real client problems.

**Benefits

**Competitive salary, bonus scheme, and pension are essential for any work agreement. At SimCorp, we believe we can offer more.

In addition to traditional benefits, we provide excellent work-life balance, flexible working hours, and a hybrid workplace model. We also have innovation and personal-development sprints, giving you dedicated time each quarter to master your skills and contribute to company development. There is never only one route — we practice an individual approach to professional development to support the direction you want to take.

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible. We process incoming applications continuously. Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.

Our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to help assess whether this is the right opportunity for you.

uisition process and aim to make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. During the process, we may ask you to provide feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become a leading provider of integrated investment-management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

About the job

At Saxo, we are building the Markets Data Office as part of our Data Governance Programme. The team is organised across four domain areas: Products, Operations, Counterparty Risk and Market Risk. Together, these areas reflect how critical data is used across Markets.

We are a newly established team and still very much in the build phase. Our first permanent colleagues joined in September 2026. Today, we are eight people, and we are growing to twelve.

jobs.description:
_Would you like to help develop financial models, applications, and quantitative solutions that support our trading of financial instruments in Nykredit Markets? Are you motivated by combining financial insight, technology, and quantitative analysis in a high-performing environment with strong expertise, significant responsibility, and visible impact? Then this could be the opportunity for you.

_A key part of Nykredit Markets’ new strategy is a comprehensive upgrade of our quant platform and models. In Quantitative Solutions, we are responsible for this initiative and are currently developing Dragonfly – a modern, scalable, and highly optimized quant platform used for market making, pricing, and risk management of financial instruments across asset classes.

We are therefore looking for a Desk Quant who wants to work close to the business and contribute to developing and maintaining solutions used daily by traders, sales professionals, and other specialists in Nykredit Markets.

**Your primary responsibilities:

**

• Trading support: Work closely with our trading desks and contribute to daily market activities where Dragonfly and other quant solutions are used.

• Financial modeling and quantitative analysis: Configure, analyze, and apply our models for pricing and risk management of financial products.

• Development of analytics applications: Design, develop, and maintain Dragonfly applications and tools for the business.

• Model setup and risk calculations: Contribute to the setup, maintenance, and further development of models and risk calculations in both Dragonfly and other trading systems.

• Monitoring and optimizing production flows: Ensure robust processes, high data quality, and stable operation of our models and quant platform.

• Markets-focused use of AI: Help identify and implement AI-driven solutions where they create business value.

**Are you the one we are looking for?

**We welcome applications from recent graduates, final-year Master’s students, and candidates with up to three years of relevant work experience. Depending on your qualifications and experience, the role will be at Analyst or Associate level.

We expect that you:

• hold a relevant university degree in finance, economics, natural sciences, or engineering, with strong academic results,

• have strong analytical skills and are motivated by solving complex financial challenges,

• have a solid understanding of quantitative modeling and financial theory,

• have programming experience in Python and strong Excel skills,

• have an interest in, and preferably experience with, AI or machine learning,

• thrive in a fast-paced environment with a strong performance focus and multiple parallel tasks,

• have an interest in financial markets and products.

**Your new team

**You will join the QS Pricing & Structuring team, one of three teams in Quantitative Solutions. We are a department with a high level of professional expertise, where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and continuous development are central to our day-to-day work. The department consists of desk quants, quant developers, and financial engineers. Together, we ensure that Nykredit Markets has the right models, applications, and analytical decision support to remain at the forefront of the market.

**About Nykredit Markets

**Nykredit Markets is part of the Nykredit Group, one of Denmark’s largest financial institutions. Nykredit Markets offers a broad range of financial services and products within capital markets, including trading in bonds, credit, FX, and equities. We serve both institutional and private investors with advisory services and tailored investment solutions.

**Want to know more?

**You are welcome to contact me, David Sloth Pedersen, Head of Quantitative Solutions, at quant@nykredit.dk if you have any questions about the position.

If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our recruitment team at nytjob@nykredit.dk.

_We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and review applications as we receive them.

_We look forward to receiving your application and CV.

• Own the data and infrastructure work behind your own agents on the cloud.

• Implement responsible-AI practices for operational energy data: access control, data isolation between clients, logging, and guardrails

• Ship early and iterate put prototypes in users’ hands fast and feed what you learn back into the roadmap

• Collaborate with Product Owners and stakeholders to understand what they need, and push back when AI is not the right tool

• Document what you build so others can maintain, extend, and trust it

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Alliance Management and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:

Your new position

This Senior Director position reports to the SVP for Alliance Management, within a growing area of Commercial. The ambition is to evolve the mandate from ensuring partnerships are well governed and deliver against contractual obligations to maximizing the strategic, scientific and commercial value of our external partnerships across the asset lifecycle: from early science through development, regulatory approval, launch and lifecycle management. As we grow, the position offers the opportunity to build a "partner-to-market" value proposition for the entire organization and to shape the area that delivers it.

• Shape and drive the partner-to-market agenda, keeping the route to market in focus and contributing to the strategy, operating model and growth of the area

• Maximize the value of partnered assets through strong alliance governance, timely milestone delivery and proactive risk management across the partnership portfolio

• Drive cross-functional alignment between Zealand teams and partners, and resolve escalations and conflicts constructively and swiftly

• Prepare partnerships for commercial success through launch readiness, market access collaborations and co-commercialization models

• Unlock lifecycle expansion opportunities with partners, including new indications that extend the value of Zealand assets

Your profile

You are motivated by the path from molecules to market, and by combining Zealand's strengths with those of our partners to reach patients faster and further. Alliance management experience is a strength, and you have a genuine motivation to drive partnership progress with the patient always in view. You are a strategic and commercially minded partner who builds trust easily, influences without relying on formal authority, and is energized by building something new in a growing organization. Curiosity, resilience and a bold, collaborative approach come naturally to you.

• Solid understanding of US market dynamics, including pricing, payer and market access considerations that shape partnered commercial strategies

• Solid understanding and experience working with Chinese market is an advantage

• Ability to challenge early science and clinical development programs with the end product in mind, ideally with experience within obesity and metabolic health

Your new team

Alliance Management reports to the Executive Vice President for Commercial and works at the interface between our partners and our internal functions across research, development, regulatory, commercial and business development

Let's bond and be bold

We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Ready to lead change with us?

**About Sofigate

We are more than 800 top notch professionals with diverse backgrounds, working with customers from all sectors and various industries. We are a people business, and we believe it’s our people’s competence that counts.

We want you to add your skills into the mix. At Sofigate, you will find plenty of collective know-how to draw on, along with opportunities to learn and grow

Our values Dare, Care and Grow are visible in our every day life - find out more about Sofigate and join us!

**The Impact You'll Make

As our Lead Engineer, Data Science, you’ll play a key role in transforming product, sensor and operational data into meaningful insights that support innovation, energy efficiency and data-driven decision-making across Danfoss Climate Solutions.

Working closely with business teams, engineers and data platform specialists, you’ll combine strong analytical capabilities with engineering and domain knowledge to identify high-value opportunities, shape AI and analytics use cases and help build a robust, AI-ready data foundation for future intelligent solutions.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Collaborate with data engineers and platform teams to improve data quality, accessibility and usability across analytics and data products

• Contribute to semantic models and knowledge graph capabilities that capture relationships between sensors, devices, assets and their operational context

**What We're Looking For

• Good understanding of modern data and ML environments, including cloud platforms and the machine learning lifecycle

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, data and business teams

About the role

Cimalys helps Danish companies put AI to work through process audits, AI literacy workshops, AI policy setup and custom automations. Delivery is in place. What we need is someone to open doors and close deals.

You'll own the front of the funnel: finding the right companies, starting conversations with directors and heads of operations, booking meetings and closing. You don't need to be technical. Our team handles scoping and delivery, and you focus on the relationship.

What you'll do

- Find and reach out to Danish small and mid-sized companies via LinkedIn, email and your own network

- Run first calls, qualify leads and book audits and workshops

- Close deals using our clearly defined offers

- Keep the pipeline up to date in our CRM

- Join a short weekly check-in on pipeline and results

Who you are

- Driven. You'd rather hear a lot of nos than send no messages at all. Experience is a plus but not required.

- Comfortable talking to business owners and directors, in Danish and English

- Curious about AI. You don't need to build it, but you should be able to explain why it matters.

- Self-organised: you set your own hours and hit your own targets

- Bonus: an existing network among Danish business owners, or B2B sales experience

What you get

- Commission on everything the clients you bring in pay during their first year, covering workshops, policy packages and custom projects

- A bonus for every paid audit you book

- Fully flexible and remote: work when and where you want

- A path to a bigger role and partnership for the right person

How it works

- Apply with a few lines about yourself, and tell us about something you sold or a goal you hit through pure persistence.

- A short intro call.

- A test sale: you pitch one of our offers to us as if we were a client. We'll send you the material in advance.

- A trial period with clear, agreed targets.

This is a part-time student job or part-time position with a fixed hourly wage plus commission.

For more information or questions please contact us at nlej@cimalys.com

Working at

Cimalys ApS

Cimalys helps Danish and Nordic companies put AI to work: safely, practically, and without hiring an AI team. Most companies with 20–300 employees know AI matters. Their staff already use ChatGPT, but with no policy, no approved tools and no idea where it actually saves time. Since February 2025, the EU AI Act has also required them to ensure their staff's AI literacy. Big consultancies are too expensive and slow for this size of company, and freelancers can't cover both strategy and the actual build. We start where the value is: a process audit that maps how a company actually works and pinpoints where AI and automation save real time and money. From there, we deliver exactly what each company needs: - AI literacy workshops: hands-on sessions where teams learn to use AI on their own work, safely, so they leave with working automations rather than notes about someday. - AI Foundation: a company-specific AI policy and a list of approved tools, so leadership knows what's allowed and employees know what to use. Operational guidance, not legal advice. - Custom automations and AI agents: built by our in-house developer and scoped from the audit, taking over the repetitive workflows that eat up people's days. Why us: the team that diagnoses the problem also builds the solution. No handover between a consultant who writes a report and a vendor who has to reinterpret it. No pyramid of juniors learning at the client's expense. Clear, fixed-scope offers, delivered fast. Why now: AI adoption in small and mid-sized companies is happening anyway, mostly unmanaged. Employees paste client data into free tools, every department picks its own apps, and leadership has no overview. The companies that put structure in place now will compound the gains, and the rest will spend the next years cleaning up. We want to be the partner that gets them there first. Where we are: Cimalys is an early-stage, founder-led company with delivery capacity in place and a productized offer ready to sell. What we need now is someone who loves opening doors and closing deals, so we can bring this to many more companies.

Some jobs teach you a skill. This one teaches you how to grow. We are looking for a curious, driven Business Development Representative to own outbound in Sweden, part time, from our Copenhagen office.

Who we are

Cludo is a Danish tech company that builds AI powered, intelligent search for content rich websites. The way we all search has changed: we no longer want a list of links, we expect a direct answer. Cludo gives website visitors exactly that, a modern search experience that understands what they are looking for and answers them directly.For communication, marketing and web teams, Cludo is also a platform for insight. They see what their users search for, spot the gaps and use those insights to keep improving both their content and the search experience. Organizations across Europe and beyond trust us to do this, guided by our four values: Growth, Passion, Reason and Sincerity.

Why business development matters here

Business development is the engine of Cludo. Most of our new growth starts with a conversation a BDR opened, which makes this team central to the success of the whole company. It is also one of the few places where you see your impact straight away. In sales you never have to wonder whether you are doing well: the numbers tell you, every single week.

The role: own outbound in Sweden

We opened the Swedish market three years ago, and the foundations are in place: real customers, real references and a proven playbook. Now we are looking for someone to pick up that momentum and own outbound in Sweden. You will work in tandem with our Swedish Account Executive. You open the doors and build the pipeline; they take the opportunities forward to close. Together, you are responsible for growing the Swedish market. Our focus segments are the public sector, higher education, regions, banks and insurance companies.

This is a part time role of around 15 to 20 hours per week, built to fit around your studies. Your hours are flexible, but we want you in our Copenhagen office for most of them, because that is where the learning, the energy and the team are. You report to Matteo Pasquato, who leads our Global BDR team.

What you'll be doing

• 
Own the outbound motion in Sweden, from building target lists to booking the first meeting

• 
Research organizations across the public sector, higher education, regions, banking and insurance, and find the right people to talk to

• 
Start real conversations by phone, email and LinkedIn, and turn curiosity into meetings

• 
Use AI to work smarter and faster: research accounts, find the right organizations and people, and personalize your outreach so every message lands

• 
Qualify opportunities and hand them to your Account Executive with the context they need to win

• 
Plan campaigns together with your AE and adjust them based on what the numbers tell you

• 
Support marketing initiatives in Sweden, both digital and in person

Who you are

Your background matters less than your mindset. We care more about who you are becoming than about what is already on your CV.

• 
Curious. You ask questions, dig deeper and want to understand how things work. The more curious you are, the faster you learn.

• 
Eager to learn. You want to become a better version of yourself every day, and you see feedback as fuel.

• 
Driven. You set goals, chase them and take ownership of your results.

• 
Resilient and consistent. A no does not slow you down for long. You show up with the same energy on the hard days as on the good ones.

• 
Fluent in Swedish and strong in English, both written and spoken.

• 
Organized and analytical, with a love for figuring things out.

A big plus

An additional language beyond Swedish and English. We are continuously experimenting in new markets, so every extra language opens doors, for you and for us. Bonus points too if you have done outreach or customer facing work before, or already know your way around the Swedish public sector.

The team you join

You join Cludo's BDR team: multicultural, made up of people from different countries and backgrounds, and set to grow in number over the coming years. We are the most active, and probably the loudest, team at Cludo. High energy, high tempo.

Three words sum up what we stand for: fresh, energetic and inspirational. Expect shared wins, honest feedback and teammates who pick you up when you need it.

The honest part

This role is not easy. Outbound sales is a game of consistency, and there will be ups and downs: weeks where everything clicks and weeks where nothing seems to land.

What matters is what you do with the downs. Every no teaches you something, and you will never have to figure it out alone. Your manager and your team are there to coach you, back you and help you turn setbacks into progress.

What you take with you

The BDR role is a talent factory and a starting point, not a destination. It is a great first step for any career, whatever your background. The skills you build here, from communication and resilience to structure and discipline, will serve you in your professional life and your private life alike. Whether your next step is in sales or somewhere else entirely, you will carry what you learn here with you.

What we offer

• 
Real impact from day one in a fun, informal and creative environment

• 
Flexible hours that fit around your studies and schedule

• 
A commitment to work life balance, proudly Danish style

• 
A front row seat to see how a tech company scales

• 
A bright, buzzing office in Copenhagen, with daily lunch from our amazing kitchen crew

• 
Onsite perks like a motion room, sauna, winter bathing access and kayaks (yes, really)

• 
Cold dips and breakfast with the team every Friday morning

How we hire

• 
Apply.

• 
First interview. Meet Matteo, Ville (our VP of Sales) and a few of your future teammates (about 1.5 hours).

• 
Culture and context. Wrap up with a conversation with Tina, our Scandinavian AE.

Curious? Apply, and let's see where you get.

Cludo is transforming the way organizations build relationships with their customers by easily connecting them to relevant content. We make it easier for visitors to find relevant information via a more natural and intuitive guided website search experience. Headquartered in Copenhagen, we are an ambitious and customer-focused international team. Join us today and help us scale to the next level of success! Every employee at Cludo has the ability to bring meaningful work to their job. We are in a unique company stage where everyone contributes to the business in a positive way, driven by our values of Growth, Passion, Reason, and Sincerity. We want individuals to join our team for the right reasons and feel it’s important to find people who want to contribute and help us scale up! We are a company that encourages direct feedback and celebrate wins together to get our company to the next level of success. If you are looking for a career that will challenge you to be a better professional while enjoying some great perks – you’re in the right place!

A few years into RevOps, most people end up choosing between staying close to admin and reporting, or moving towards building automations and the AI tools that now sit on top of the CRM. The second path is hard to get onto if you haven't done it somewhere first.

In this job you'd do both, in a commercial team that already works with AI day to day through assistants connected to Salesforce, support tickets and product data, while marketing is being rebuilt the same way. You'd build on that, starting next to the person who set most of it up and taking over the technical side from them. You'd also keep the CRM and the data underneath it in good order. That's a lot of upkeep, like permissions, data cleanup and renewal notices to thousands of customers, and there's no ops team to share it with.

Airtame makes wireless screen-sharing devices and the cloud software that manages them, used in schools and workplaces around the world. Most of our volume goes through distributors on several continents, sometimes to customers our own reps sent them. Our sales team also works deals directly, and smaller orders come through our Shopify store. Running all three through one Salesforce makes for a harder data model than most RevOps roles come with.

We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and we'd prefer you to work from the office there. Remote from elsewhere in the EU works too. You'd report to our Director of Customer Experience & Revenue Operations, who sets the roadmap with you and owns the metric definitions, and you'd work with sales, customer experience, marketing and product every week.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

Own the Commercial Stack: By the end of the year the technical side has moved over to you, including the AI tools the team uses. You bring the roadmap to your manager and build it, and when sales or support want a system changed, you decide how it's done.

Send the Right Renewal Message: Thousands of customers receive renewal notices. We're starting to ask customers in our cloud software how they intend to renew, and you'd build the email flows that act on it, with a separate path for each way of renewing. If a notice doesn't go out, you know within hours.

Make the Numbers Agree: Pipeline, bookings, ARR, renewals and churn come out the same in every dashboard and every AI assistant, whether the sale came through Shopify, a rep or a distributor. Your manager sets the definitions, and you make sure every system uses them.

Automate the Manual Work: Find the processes worth automating and keep shipping them, tested in a sandbox first with a way back if something goes wrong. The first one is turning the pricing claims our distributors send, in all sorts of formats, into line-item pricing in Salesforce with an audit trail. As AI assistants get better at connecting to things on their own, part of this is also deciding what's still worth building ourselves.

Bring Support onto Intercom: We're moving customer support from Zendesk to Intercom. Depending on when you join, you'd help finish the move or pick it up just after go-live, then own Intercom, including its Salesforce sync and the AI setup that gets customer feedback to the product team.

Who You Are

• You know Salesforce from the inside. A few years of hands-on admin, including Flow Builder, permissions and the data model. You write SQL and SOQL and can model data for a report yourself.

• You ask why before you build. You can tell us about a request you pushed back on, or a process you changed or dropped instead of automating it as asked, and what it was for in the first place.

• You work with AI by default. You use AI tools every day to write flows and queries, and you keep up with what's new on your own. When a new connector makes something we built unnecessary, you're happy to retire it. If you've connected tools through their APIs or written some Python or JavaScript, that's a strong plus.

• You've run a commercial system on your own. At some point you've been the only or main admin of a Salesforce org or a similar system, and you left documentation behind that someone else could take over from. Here there's no ops team behind you, so a broken sync in the morning and a dashboard request in the afternoon are both yours.

Why Airtame?

• Building on Top of Admin: You'd keep the CRM running and build automations and AI tooling on top of it, starting next to the person who set most of it up.

• Most RevOps roles are purely SaaS or purely e-commerce. Here, you get to solve the unique intellectual challenge of bridging a hardware supply chain with a high-velocity digital subscription model.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Catered lunch in the office.

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

Do you enjoy turning complex business challenges into innovative, scalable and commercially viable cloud solutions?

You will be a trusted technical partner throughout the customer engagement, helping translate complex requirements into practical, future-proof solutions.

What you'll be doing

You should also be comfortable working in an international environment and travelling occasionally when required.

Why join T-Systems?

At T-Systems, you will have the opportunity to work on complex and meaningful cloud transformation projects, collaborate with experienced specialists across our international organisation and help shape solutions for leading customers.

You will be part of a business where technical expertise, collaboration and fresh thinking are valued, and where your ideas can contribute to how we develop our cloud services.

We believe that our culture is shaped by the everyday actions of our people. Each of us has the opportunity to make a positive impact on our colleagues, our customers and our business.

Because at T-Systems, our people make the difference. #peoplemakethedifference

If you are excited about combining cloud technology, customer engagement and solution innovation, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
**Job Description

****Join us in building a new strategic integration capability

**Are you motivated by shaping new solutions from the ground up? Do you enjoy turning complex business ambitions into secure, scalable technology?

We are establishing a new team in the Customer & Sector Integration tribe to accelerate ERP-to-Bank. The initiative will enable corporate customers to securely share ERP data with Danske Bank, creating opportunities for automated financial processes, improved customer experiences and data-driven products and advisory. You will help determine how Danske Bank connects directly with ERP platforms and through ERP data aggregators, and how ERP data can be securely acquired, governed and made available to internal consumers.

As Solution Architect and IT Solution Owner, you will set the technical direction and lead the architecture of this new solution area. You will work closely with the Product Owner, engineers, internal stakeholders and external ERP ecosystem partners.

**You will

**

• Define and drive the solution architecture for ERP-to-Bank.

• Act as IT Solution Owner for the solutions established within the domain.

• Translate business needs into secure, scalable and maintainable designs.

• Shape integrations with ERP platforms and ERP data aggregators.

• Establish architectural principles, solution boundaries and technical roadmaps.

• Guide decisions related to APIs, data, security, identity and cloud technologies.

• Ensure alignment with enterprise architecture, regulatory requirements and technology standards.

• Coordinate dependencies across business areas, tribes and external partners.

• Support engineers through technical guidance, sparring and architecture reviews.

The combined role brings responsibility for both technical direction and the lifecycle, governance and operational health of the solutions.

**About You

**

• At least five years of experience in software engineering, solution architecture or technical leadership.

• Current experience as a solution architect, technical lead or IT Solution Owner.

• Strong experience designing integration-heavy, business-critical solutions.

• Knowledge of API-based, event-driven and cloud-native architectures.

• Experience designing secure integrations with customers or external partners.

• The ability to communicate complex technical topics to both technical and business stakeholders.

• A collaborative and pragmatic approach to architecture and delivery.

Experience with banking, ERP platforms, accounting data, payments, cash management or third-party data providers would be an advantage.

**Why join?

**You will join a new team and help define the architecture, integration model and technology choices from the beginning. It is an opportunity to work at the intersection of banking, ERP ecosystems, data and modern integration technology, while turning a strategic ambition into a sustainable production capability.

The workplace can be in Lithuania or Denmark. If you are hired in Lithuania, the monthly salary range: from 5760 EUR to 8640 EUR gross (based on competencies relevant to the role).

Your title in job contract will be Software Architecture.

**Interested?

**Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Please include a short motivational letter with your CV. If you have questions about the position, contact Tribe Architect Kenneth Mejnert on mejn@danskebank.dk

jobs.description:
We're looking for a senior AI engineer with hands-on experience in generative AI, API integrations, and advanced agent-based applications. The ideal candidate brings a mix of full-stack, AI, and cloud engineering experience.

**What You'll Do

**This role cuts across multiple tech stacks and is a central part of how we deliver AI solutions for our clients.

**In This Role, You'll

**

• Translating early ideas into working prototypes and iterating them into production-ready solutions using modern full-stack frameworks

• Designing and deploying generative AI applications and autonomous agents using LLM APIs and established agent frameworks

• Integrating AI capabilities into client systems and managing deployment pipelines in cloud environments

• Collaborating with engineering, product, and business stakeholders to build solutions that address real needs

• Mentoring junior engineers and keeping pace with emerging AI and software engineering paradigms

**What You'll Bring

**We're looking for someone with at least five years of software development experience, including at least two in generative AI and agent-based applications, and a master's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field.

**Beyond That, You'll Bring

**

• Full-stack capability across TypeScript (React, Next.js, Vite) and Python, with experience shipping production systems

• Hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, Agno, or DSPy

• Proficiency with RESTful APIs, cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP), and containerisation tools such as Docker and Kubernetes

• Strong communication skills across technical and non-technical stakeholders

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

Take AirPlay and Miracast from beta to default. They're in beta today. A year from now they should be solid enough to ship on by default across the Airtame product line, so customers get them without opting in and never have to think about which protocol they're using. Judge it by connection success rates on the fleet, and by how many customers rely on them day to day.

Make firmware releases boring. The best release is the one nobody has to think about: a predictable cadence, an automated quality bar, and shipping to the whole fleet as routine. A year from now, cutting a release should be a low-drama process the team trusts, and that should let you ship improvements more often. Judge it by release frequency, and by the confidence behind each one.

Turn the next board into a shipping Airtame. New silicon has to boot, hold a network, manage its heat, and run conferencing well enough to sell. By year-end there's a repeatable path from a board landing on a desk to a build QA can test, and you own it. Judge it by how long that path takes, and whether the thermal and acoustic targets hold.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've set a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped writing code. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• At home where software meets hardware. Embedded Linux is your familiar ground: the kernel, the BSP, userspace, C and C++ running on the device itself. You've spent time close to the metal: wireless stacks, streaming protocols, drivers. You can reason about a bug whether it lives in the firmware, the network, or the silicon.

• You ship to hardware you can't reach. When it's firmware on a device mounted in someone's meeting room, a bad release doesn't just roll back with a hotfix. You've owned software that ships to the field, so staged rollouts, over-the-air updates, and testing on the devices themselves come naturally. "Works on my bench" isn't the finish line for you.

• You've turned new hardware into a product. Bare silicon arrives, and someone has to make it boot, talk to the network, manage its heat, and eventually stream. You've done that kind of bringup, or worked close enough to it to lead the people who do.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.

**Logistics

**Location: Remote in Europe, or hybrid from our Copenhagen office.

Employment type: Full-time preferred. We're also open to a project-based contract scoped to delivering the native protocol implementations.

****Why Airtame:

• A shift worth architecting. Airtame's software is moving onto a widening range of devices, including hardware from partners. Leading Platform now means designing for that spread, a bigger and more open problem than keeping one hardware line running.

• A span you can hold. From the bootloader to the release that reaches the field, the whole layer is one person's to shape here, at a size where you can still keep it in your head.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Significant responsibility and ownership over projects and your field of expertise.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

jobs.occupation: Tech Lead, Video Conferencing & Screen Sharing
jobs.description:
Most companies that do conferencing hand you one slice of it. The desktop app, or the media pipeline, or, maybe, the join flow. Everything else you pass over a wall to another team. Not in this case. One team owns the whole path across the Airtame platform: Airtame 3, Airtame Go, Virtual Airtame, and browser, desktop, and mobile apps that go with them. The bar remains at an effortless experience. Someone walks into a room, and starts sharing. No app to hunt for, no login to chase.

The team is four engineers, and we're hiring their technical and people lead: someone who spends about 60% of time hands-on with the hardest problems, and the rest growing the engineers around them.

jobs.occupation: Senior Program Director, Global Business Transformation
jobs.description:
Are you ready to shape the future of Ambu's global operations processes and business functions through major **ERP, QMS, and PLM transformation?

**We are seeking a visionary leader to drive a landmark multi-year digital transformation across our global footprint, optimising production, quality, procurement, and supply chain processes.

Currently in the initial scoping phase, this initiative will consolidate enterprise operations globally using the Infor M3 ERP platform and the Dassault Systèmes ecosystem.

This high-impact role will drive the guiding principles for our future ERP, QMS, and PLM operating model. The position requires a leader who can drive a complex program incl. effective change management, simplify complex workflows, deliver business transformation, eliminate fragmented Excel-dependent processes, and ensure global standardization within an ambitious 3–4-year timeline.

Reporting to the CFO, you will set the pace, resolve cross-functional roadblocks, and hold the program, external system integrators, and business stakeholders accountable.

Core Responsibilities Governance & Strategy

Drive the future-state global process, business transformation roadmap, and operating model, balancing multi-entity standardisation with critical local requirements. Define and drive the ERP implementation roadmap to maximise business improvements, value realisation, consistency, and cost efficiency.

Lead a large global program team consisting of e.g. Global Process Owners, Global business owners, Technical Workstream Lead etc. in a mix of direct and dotted reporting lines, while operating in a matrix organisation across six VP-led functional areas.

Manage the external vendor relationships with the vendors selected to support the program

Process Optimisation & Innovation

Drive and be responsible for implementing the program, harmonising processes across Finance, production, quality, procurement, and supply chain functions, and translating this into measurable business improvements. Lead digitalisation initiatives, including AI-driven methods and process intelligence solutions, in collaboration with business stakeholders and external system integrator consultants.

Business Transformation

Lead the development of a dedicated team of process managers, business managers, and subject matter experts. Execute a global change management strategy tailored to a fast-paced, compliance-driven culture, ensuring alignment across regions and driving business improvements and value realisation throughout.

Compliance & Data Harmonization

Partner with Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs to ensure that platforms meet international compliance requirements. Lead migration, cleansing, and structuring of legacy data into a unified and scalable architecture.

**Required Experience & Technical Skills Executive Track Record

**15+ years of leadership experience managing large global transformation projects, digital transformation programs, or enterprise application implementations. Ideally a background incl. commercial, financial or operational leadership roles.

Transformational Delivery

Proven experience leading end-to-end ERP, PLM, or QMS implementations and business process transformation within multinational organizations. Experience with Infor M3 and Dassault Systèmes is highly advantageous.

Industry Context

Strong background in manufacturing, quality, and supply chain operations within highly regulated industries (e.g., medical devices, life sciences, or pharmaceuticals).

Education

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related discipline.

Soft Skills & Leadership Qualities Executive Presence

Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to bridge operational requirements and technology solutions while influencing senior leadership.

Resilience & Adaptability

Thrives in complex and demanding environments, demonstrating strong cultural awareness and the ability to resolve alignment challenges with diplomacy and determination.

Global Mobility

Flexibility to travel internationally and spend extended periods at manufacturing sites during critical project phases. Expected travel commitment of approximately 50–80 days per year, including visits to Malaysia, China, Mexico, and the United States.

What We Offer

**Ambu – a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international head office with an informal working environment.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

jobs.occupation: Wear Group is looking for an Order Manager, Private Label/Mass Market
jobs.description:
Would you like to work with one of Europe’s largest retail customers and thrive in a fast-paced environment with significant responsibility and demanding deadlines?

Wear Group is looking for an experienced Order Manager to take a key role in managing our cooperation with a major mass-market retail customer.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

As Order Manager, you will have operational responsibility for your orders from order placement through production to final delivery.

You will be the key link between the customer, Wear Group, suppliers and factories, ensuring deadlines, quality requirements and procedures are followed.

Your main responsibilities include:

•Daily management and follow-up of customer orders

•Close communication with suppliers and factories

•Monitoring production progress, critical deadlines and deliveries

•Follow-up on samples, approvals, testing, inspections and documentation

•Coordination with buying, quality, logistics and sales

•Identifying risks early and driving corrective actions

•Ensuring clear and timely communication with the customer and internal teams

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

You come from a similar position within textiles, apparel, private label or a related industry, such as Order Manager, Production Coordinator or Buying/Production Coordinator.

Experience working with major German or international retail customers is a strong advantage.

We expect that you:

•Have solid experience in order and production management

•Understand the full process from order placement to final delivery

•Are highly structured and strong at follow-up

•Take ownership and drive issues through to resolution

•Can manage multiple priorities and critical deadlines

•Communicate professionally with customers, suppliers and colleagues

•Are fluent in English; German is an advantage

YOU THRIVE IN A FAST-PACED ENVIRONMENT

Our customer operates with high expectations, fixed deadlines and strict requirements. You must therefore be comfortable managing several critical tasks simultaneously while maintaining structure and control. You work proactively, identify potential problems early and take action before they impact the customer or delivery.

Structured | Persistent | Accountable | Solution-oriented | Resilient

WHAT WE OFFER

At Wear Group, you will join an international organization with close relationships across customers, suppliers and factories.

You will have a central role with significant responsibility, short decision-making processes and the opportunity to make a real impact on one of our most important customer partnerships.

ARE YOU OUR NEW ORDER MANAGER?

If you have the experience, overview and drive to manage a major international retail customer – and thrive with responsibility, high expectations and a fast-paced working environment – we would very much like to hear from you.

APPLICATION

Please send your CV and application in English. We review applications on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Mette Birkemose, Wear Group, at +45 51509271 or email mb@wear-group.com

With an IoT platform connecting more than 6 million units — and growing — Trackunit is building the platform that will enable the construction industry to work faster, smarter, and more securely. And we need you to help run and scale it.

As an SRE, you will join our Europe-based team and be part of a global SRE organization spanning Europe and Canada. This is a hands-on role focused on the daily operation and continuous improvement of our platform, with room to grow into larger design and architecture work as you build depth.

The platform owned by SRE consists of an AWS cloud, Kubernetes clusters (EKS), and our IaC setup running Terraform and Terramate, as well as a GitOps delivery platform built on Argo CD and Atlantis.

We support engineering teams with 150+ developers. You will help keep a platform used by 15,000+ active users every day secure, available, and easy to build on.

We're looking for someone curious and collaborative — happy to share knowledge and ask questions as well.

Experience level: roughly 2–5 years in an SRE, DevOps, platform, or infrastructure operations role. If you're further along and the day-to-day scope appeals to you, apply anyway — we'll have the conversation.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

**What's in it for you?

**

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

**What You'll Do

**Your week will be a mix of keeping things running well and making them better.

• Operate and improve the platform. Monitoring, alerting, capacity, cost, and the steady stream of small improvements that keep a large AWS and Kubernetes estate healthy.

• Work in code, not consoles. Infrastructure changes go through Terraform and Helm, reviewed as pull requests and delivered through Atlantis and Argo CD.

• Keep the platform secure. Patching, vulnerability remediation, base image updates, and closing findings — a recurring, meaningful part of the job rather than a side task.

• Take part in incident response. You'll join our on-call rotation (SRE team, business hours) and contribute to incidents and follow-up work.

• Handle triage and requests from developer teams. Understanding what they need, unblocking them, and spotting when a repeated request could be automated.

**Who You Are

**We think you'll need

• Hands-on experience running workloads on AWS.

• Basic knowledge with Kubernetes.

• Basic knowledge about infrastructure as code, ideally Terraform.

• Comfortable with Git, Linux and Windows.

• Clear written communication — a lot of our work happens in tickets, PRs, and docs.

**Nice to have, not expected

**

• EKS specifically, or tooling like Karpenter, Argo CD, Atlantis, or Terramate.

• Observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, Sumo Logic, or similar).

• Scripting in Python or Go.

• Security or compliance work — vulnerability management, CIS benchmarks, certification programmes.

• Multi-region or multi-account AWS architecture.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You’re curious and self-driven, while also knowing when to ask for help when needed.

• You finish things. Small, well-tested changes shipped consistently beat big ideas that stall.

• You care about the developers and customers using the platform, not just the platform itself.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement. An interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work — including MCP servers and agents against our own platform — and we expect that to grow. We don’t expect you to have experience with this—but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries — this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

**How You'll Grow Here

**We hire at this level expecting you to move beyond it, and we've structured the team so that happens on purpose rather than by accident.

• A rotation model that protects your focus. The team splits between operational duty and project work, so you're not permanently interrupt-driven. You get real blocks of time to go deep on something.

• Mentorship that's built in. Senior colleagues review your PRs and pair with you on incidents. Asking questions is the expected behaviour, not a sign you're struggling.

• Exposure to the big architecture work. You'll start with scoped pieces and take on more as you build context.

• A clear conversation about your development. Regular 1:1s that cover where you want to be, not just what you shipped last sprint.

**What We're Building Next

**Trackunit is moving from a SaaS company to a platform built on telemetry data from the construction industry worldwide. For SRE, that means going beyond delivering infrastructure to building the capabilities that let our developers and customers spin up environments tailored to their needs in the regions they need them.

Things on our roadmap include:

• Expanding the platform into a true multi-region architecture.

• Building self-service platform capabilities so developer teams move at their own pace.

• Making better use of AI in our own operations, through MCP servers and agents.

You won't be expected to lead these on day one. You will be in the room, and there will be pieces with your name on them.

**What Happens From Here — Recruitment Process Overview

**

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with a member of our Talent Partner team

• Personality-based interview. You will be asked to complete an online personality assessment prior to the interview. There are no correct answers and we are not trying to categorise you — the aim is a dialogue about the results and Trackunit's culture, so you get to know us better as well.

• Assignment-specific interview. You will be given a case to prepare after the initial screening interview. You will present the case to relevant colleagues across Trackunit, who you will also work closely with in the role.

• Virtual meet and greet. Meet with Engineering Manager, Kåre Brandborg and an SRE team member.

• References and background checks (if needed). If required, we will obtain references from former employers and perform level-specific background checks, if you have not provided these yourself.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We're lucky to have you!

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction — one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

The question is: Are you in?

jobs.occupation: Experienced Senior Lean Consultant for Project Excellence at Novo Nordisk Engineering
jobs.description:
If you’re energised by driving lean transformation at a company level and you thrive on turning complex challenges into tangible business impact, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Lean Consultant to join our team of highly skilled colleagues in the Project Excellence department. In Project Excellence, we act as internal consultants grounded in Lean, supporting projects and leadership across NNE by strengthening performance management, structured problem solving and continuous improvement practices.

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you will work closely with project organisations and leaders to set direction for improvement initiatives, build Lean capabilities and drive performance. At the same time, you will take an active, hands-on role in facilitating problem solving and implementing improvements on our most critical projects, ensuring that ideas translate into real impact.

This role offers a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of leadership, Lean transformation and project execution, contributing to building a strong and sustainable performance and improvement culture across NNE.

You’ll be based in our Virum Office, but the role requires you to visit our project sites in Kalundborg and around the Copenhagen area on a regular basis.

How you might spend your days

As a Senior Lean Consultant, you’ll be:

• Helping the Project Excellence department set direction for continuous improvement and Lean in NNE, aligned with NNE’s strategy

• Building Lean capabilities by developing and embedding structured problem solving, lean project management and continuous improvement practices

• Designing and delivering training in Lean tools, Lean principles and Lean ways of working across NNE

• Coaching leaders and teams to strengthen performance management and Lean leadership behaviours

• Facilitating and driving structured problem-solving on major projects, using A3 thinking as our core approach

• Advising on consistent implementation of improvements, ensuring solutions are anchored and deliver real impact

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Passionate about Lean thinking and driven to create real lasting business impact

• Confident in engaging, challenging and developing leaders and teams at all levels

• Comfortable operating in complex environments, bringing clarity, structure and direction

• Pragmatic and execution-focused with a great drive to turn ideas into results

• A credible role model who takes ownership and leads by example

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• Extensive experience driving continuous improvement and lean transformations in complex organisations

• Proven ability to lead and implement change with measurable impact

• Solid experience working closely with senior leaders on performance and improvement agendas

• A relevant academic degree at Master level

• Excellent facilitation, coaching and stakeholder management skills across organisational levels

Life at NNE

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer here.

Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

Deadline of application is 13th November 2026

Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Please Contact Director Daniel Iwarsson at +45 3075 7823 or Principal Consultant, Mikkel Bonne at +45 3191 8723 between 12.00-15.00 (12 AM-3 PM) on weekdays.

Please note:

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

Fair hiring:

At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.

jobs.occupation: Senior/Lead Software Engineer | OTC Product Area, Fintech Solutions
jobs.description:
Who We Are

For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world's leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,500+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds in general.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated in our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

While striving to deliver client value, we believe it is vital to consider our people and our planet in every business decision we make. Acting responsibly is not optional. It is essential.

Why This Role is Important to Us

We are looking for Software Engineers at middle level to join our engineering team that builds fintech solutions for managing OTC (Over-The-Counter) financial instruments within our asset management platform, SimCorp Dimension and SimCorp One. Our work delivers value in two major areas. First, we implement new features that drive the business forward and shape the future of our platform. Second, we focus on extending and maintaining our established solutions to ensure our clients’ operations remain uninterrupted and always available.

What You Will Be Responsible For

• 
Designing, building, and extending existing solutions and APIs for our OTC asset management product, delivering value to customers incrementally.

• 
Working primarily in C#. Our codebase also includes OCaml and APL therefore prior experience with these languages is a strong plus.

• 
Understanding, refactoring and modernizing our legacy codebase without disrupting the business it supports.

• 
Focusing on the systems as a whole and being able address fundamental changes that improves the quality, performance and user experience.

• 
Collaborating closely with your product owner to refine requirements, clarify business needs, and shape how features get built.

• 
Working as part of a team of skilled engineers — pairing, reviewing code, and sharing ownership of the solution with fellow engineers.

• 
Following good engineering practice: clean code, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
Building, extending and consuming REST APIs.

• 
Communicating clearly with both technical and business stakeholders.

• 
Continuously learning — and helping the team and product grow with you.

Required Skills & Experience

• Interest in creating innovative features for a complex platform, working on areas such as API scalability, automation, performance, and operational resilience - having space to explore, design and influence the final solution.

• Solid C# skills. This is the core language for the role; your level of seniority will determine how much ownership and architectural input you're expected to bring.

• Experience with, or genuine interest in, functional programming. Familiarity with OCaml, APL, F#, Standard ML, Scala or Haskell is a real advantage but not required — a willingness to learn is what matters most.

• Experience (or strong interest) in refactoring existing code and working with legacy systems.

jobs.description:
Are you approaching the end of your studies and looking for a graduation project early 2027. Does deep dive into the protection of the primary equipment enabling transport of wind energy to shore excite you? Then we have the project for you.

The projects

Protection study

Today we apply state of the art, cutting edge protections of the primary equipment, 220/66kV transformers, shunt reactors, subsea cables etc. Functions like line differential protection, restricted earth fault protection, distance protection with fiber optic accelerations schemes and different mechanical protections.

But how well do the different protections cover the primary equipment?

Are all protections feasible, considering how often we statistically experience faults?

Grounding

Today the MV grid, connecting the wind turbines to the Offshore Sub Station is impedance grounded. This creates different problems and side effects that needs to be considered during engineering. Some primary equipment becomes expensive and hard to procure. Protection against earth faults becomes challenging because of the reduced fault current.

Investigate the benefits and disadvantages of isolated, impedance and effectively grounded MV grid.

How will the protections need to be set up?

What will the implications be on primary equipment, transformers, cables, wind turbines etc.

Does it excite you to work with shaping the equity story of a peptide-based biotech company and strengthening relationships with investors and analysts across Europe, and do you have experience with investor relations and corporate communications in biotech or pharma? You will translate complex science, clinical progress, and strategy into a clear and credible narrative for shareholders, prospective investors, analysts, and the broader financial community. We offer exciting responsibilities:

Strengthen and expand relationships with European institutional investors, sell-side analysts, and other capital market stakeholders, serving as a primary point of contact for investor inquiries

• 
Prepare financial results communications, earnings releases, investor presentations, scripts, Q&A materials, and annual and interim report content

• 
Monitor and analyze market trends, competitive intelligence, investor sentiment, and shareholder composition, particularly in Europe, and provide insights and recommendations to leadership

• 
Contribute to corporate communications, including press releases, media relations, and social media content, and safeguard consistent corporate messaging across channels, while ensuring compliance with applicable disclosure and market regulations in collaboration with Legal, Finance, and Corporate Communications

Your profile

You are a credible and confident communicator who builds trust easily with both scientific and financial audiences. You are strategic and analytical, with strong financial acumen and sound judgment when handling sensitive and market-moving information. You are highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple projects at pace. You are a natural collaborator who works effectively across functions.

• 
Significant experience in investor relations, corporate communications, equity research, investment banking, or a related capital markets role, within biotech, pharma, or healthcare

Strong understanding of drug development, clinical data, and biotech valuation drivers, as well as in-depth knowledge of financial markets and listed-company disclosure and reporting requirements

• 
Proven track record of building and maintaining relationships with institutional investors, sell-side analysts, and the media, ideally with an established network in the European investment community

• 
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial data and industry trends

University degree in finance, economics, communications, business, life sciences, or a related field; an MBA is a plus

Your new team

The position reports to the Vice President, Head of Investor Relations, and is part of the Investor Relations team that reports to the CFO. The team includes an Investor Relation coordinator and we work very closely with Corporate Communications.

Let’s bond and be bold

We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new drugs for metabolic health for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let’s bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than 12 November 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.

In addition, you will represent Semco Maritime in customer interactions and industry forums, contribute valuable market insights, and help strengthen our commercial processes and best practices across the organisation.

Your tasks will include but are not limited to: 

• Driving strategic sales opportunities from qualification through contract award and handover.
• Developing and executing winning strategies for key tenders and commercial opportunities.
• Building and maintaining strong relationships with strategic customers and supporting key account development.
• Leading customer negotiations in collaboration with technical, operational, legal, procurement, and finance stakeholders.
• Identifying and pursuing business growth opportunities, including cross-selling, upselling, and framework agreements.
• Ensuring high-quality commercial proposals, risk assessments, and governance approvals.
• Promoting a strong culture of safety, quality, compliance, and integrity in all commercial activities.

Your profile & qualifications 

We are looking for a commercially driven professional who thrives in a customer-focused environment and has a proven track record of managing complex sales opportunities - preferably from the wind industry. 

To succeed in this role, we imagine that you: 

• Have significant experience with complex B2B sales, opportunity and tender management, contract negotiations, and the development of winning strategies for strategic sales opportunities.
• Bring experience from offshore wind, renewable energy, maritime, technical service, or related industries.
• Have a strong understanding of customer decision processes, competitive positioning, value creation, and commercial risk management.
• Have experience with key account management, account planning, and building long-term customer relationships.
• Are comfortable coordinating cross-functional sales and bid activities involving multiple stakeholders.
• Possess strong communication, presentation, and negotiation skills and work in a structured, proactive, and results-oriented manner.
• Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing, and are willing to travel as part of the role. 

Welcome to Semco Maritime

At Semco Maritime, we create change. For people. For projects. And for the global energy sector. With us, you will join a community of over 2,300 of the most dedicated thinkers and doers in the energy industry who are driving real change and making their own personal mark on the global energy landscape.

While everyone knows why the energy transition is vital, we are concerned with the journey. How to get there. By providing the answers needed to make change real. Because we believe that global energy ambitions can only be realized through hard work and clever pragmatic solutions. This is what we do. This is what we invite you to participate in.

Safety is at the core of everything we do, and we are committed to protecting our people, partners, and the planet as we work towards a sustainable energy future.

So yes, working for us will change the energy sector – and may well change you too. 

We know that our people are our greatest strength. We strive to build an inclusive workplace where everyone can be themselves, contribute their perspectives, and feel part of the team. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and believe that diverse teams help us find better solutions and move the energy transition forward.  

Care to join the movement?

Change. With us.
Semco Maritime is an international engineering and contracting company with 2,300 employees and 40 years of dedication rooted in both the conventional energy sector and the offshore wind industry. This puts us in a unique position to bridge today's and tomorrow’s solutions, constantly seeking clever and pragmatic ways to realise global energy ambitions. We do this through comprehensive project management across all phases of energy projects together with world-leading partners across the globe.
