About CUE

Healthcare has been reactive for too long, focused on treatment after problems appear, not prevention.

CUE is the alternative.

We’re building a health optimization platform that helps you understand your biology, track what matters, and take action.

Personalized. Data-driven. Proactive.

We are a small team. Moving fast. If you want to help shape a new model for modern healthcare from the ground up - this is your chance.

The Role

We’re looking for a gynecologist with a genuine interest in longevity and preventive medicine.

CUE is built for both men and women. This role has a dedicated focus on women’s health - an area where hormones, fertility, perimenopause and menopause shape long-term health for decades, yet are rarely followed proactively.

You will lead how CUE approaches women’s health, from the fi rst consultation to long-term follow-up as part of a clinical team serving all our clients.

This is not traditional clinic work.

It is a hybrid role between: gynecological practice, longevity, prevention, and product thinking.

CUE Model

CUE is a health optimization platform built around continuous insight, not episodic care.

We combine:

• Clinical expertise

• Biomarker data

• Continuous tracking

• Personalized interventions

To help users understand their health before symptoms appear.

We don’t replace healthcare.

We extend it into everyday life.

What you’ll do

• Take clinical ownership of women’s health at CUE - hormonal health, fertility, perimenopause and menopause

• Work directly with and take responsibility for clients coming into CUE, including consultations and ongoing clinical follow-up

• Develop clinical frameworks and protocols for preventive gynecology and hormonal health across life stages

• Help define how female-specific biomarkers are interpreted in the product

• Contribute to longevity protocols where women’s health meets metabolic, cardiovascular and bone health

• Collaborate with product and data teams to translate clinical knowledge into scalable digital experiences

• Help shape how CUE approaches prevention, optimization, and long-term health outcomes

• Work closely with the wider clinical team to ensure a coherent approach for all CUE clients, men and women alike

• Participate in ongoing refinement of health models and recommendations

You

• You are a licensed medical doctor and specialist in gynecology and obstetrics

• You have experience in one or more of:

• Hormonal health and hormone therapy

• Perimenopause and menopause

• Fertility and reproductive health

• Endocrine gynecology

• You have a genuine interest in longevity and preventive medicine

• You are curious about how data and technology can support clinical decisions

• You are comfortable working outside traditional healthcare structures

• You want to be part of the journey - building something from the ground up in a small, fast-moving team

• You care about long-term health outcomes, not just treatment

How we work with healthcare

At CUE, healthcare is not reactive - it is continuous.

We don’t only treat symptoms.

We work with patterns, prevention, and optimization.

We focus on:

• Early detection through data

• Hormonal and metabolic balance across life stages

• Personalized interventions

• Continuous tracking and feedback loops

• Translating clinical insight into daily action

Practical information

The position is based at our clinic in Grønnegade, Copenhagen K.

You can be affiliated a few days per week, scaling up to full-time over time.

Start date: as soon as possible.

Application

Send your application and CV to per@cuelife.com.

We hold interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire as soon as we have found the right candidate.

Jupiter Bach is taking the next step in its development as a partner to the global wind industry. Building on our strong position within composite manufacturing, we are expanding our capabilities across engineering, assembly and full-system delivery, supporting leading wind OEMs globally.

This means getting involved earlier in the customer dialogue and taking greater ownership of how customer requirements translate into technically sound and commercially viable solutions.

As our new Customer Solutions Engineer, Composites, you will be an important part of that development.

The opportunity

You will work at the intersection of customers, Sales and Engineering, shaping composite solutions from early customer engagement through to handover to Product Execution.

Your role is to understand the customer need, challenge and clarify requirements, and apply your composite engineering expertise to develop the right solution. Working closely with customer technical teams and specialists within Jupiter Bach, you will drive the technical dialogue and pre-project activities while considering both engineering feasibility and commercial implications.

This is a role for an engineer who wants to use technical depth beyond the traditional engineering function. You will be close to the customer, influence solutions at an early stage and help create a strong foundation for successful engineering and execution.

What you will work with

You will take responsibility for the technical side of customer opportunities during pre-sales and early project phases.

A key part of the role will be to:

• Act as the technical interface towards customers during pre-sales and early project phases

• Translate customer requirements into feasible composite engineering solutions

• Apply your understanding of composite structures, loads, geometry and strength to solution development

• Support Sales in customer meetings, proposals and negotiations

• Drive pre-project activities and technical alignment between customers and internal specialists

• Prepare and validate technical cost calculations and provide input to pricing decisions

• Assess engineering changes and their technical and commercial impact

• Support customer claims through root cause analysis and corrective actions

• Work within PPAP and APQP4Wind processes to ensure quality and robustness

You will be part of a growing team that combines different technical competencies with ownership of specific customers and opportunities.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for an engineer with strong composite expertise who is motivated by applying that knowledge in a customer- and solution-oriented role.

You understand how composite products move from requirements and design through manufacturing and into serial production. Just as importantly, you can communicate your technical knowledge and work effectively with customers, engineers, manufacturing specialists and commercial colleagues.

We expect you to bring:

• An engineering background in Composites, Materials, Structural or Manufacturing Engineering, or another relevant discipline.

• Experience with the design and manufacturing of composite structures or GFRP products

• Understanding of load conditions, geometry and strength evaluation in composite design

• Relevant experience from the wind industry or another technically complex manufacturing environment

• Good understanding of manufacturing processes and engineering interfaces

• The ability to balance technical, operational and commercial considerations

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

• Professional fluency in English

Experience with PPAP and APQP4Wind is an advantage. Danish language skills are an advantage but not a requirement.

Why Jupiter Bach?

Jupiter Bach is expanding from a strong composite manufacturing base towards broader engineering and full-system capabilities.

For an experienced composites engineer, this creates an opportunity to move closer to the customer and influence solutions much earlier in the process.

You will join an international organisation working with leading wind OEMs and have the opportunity to contribute directly to how Jupiter Bach develops its future engineering and customer solution capabilities.

Contact

For more information about the role, please contact recruitment partner, Lotte Christensen, at loc@slaterconsult.com.

Slater Consult is Jupiter Bachs’s recruiting partner for this position.

jobs.occupation: Senior Consultant to Sustainability & ESG – Climate specialization
jobs.description:
With more than 2,700 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit & Assurance, Tax & Legal, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology, and Transformations.

About the team

Our Sustainability Team is made up of experts from different backgrounds, each bringing skills that complement one another. We work together to find practical solutions that help our clients make meaningful progress in sustainability. By understanding their challenges, we develop strategies that create lasting benefits for both businesses and the environment. Our team thrives on collaboration and innovation, ensuring that each project we take on leads to real, measurable improvements in sustainability practices.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced and practically minded Senior Consultant with a specialisation in climate to join our team and support large public- and private‑sector clients in planning and delivering credible decarbonisation and net‑zero strategies. The role combines technical GHG accounting and target-setting expertise with commercial consulting skills to design actionable pathways that reduce emissions, manage climate risk and meet emerging regulatory and investor expectations.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Lead and deliver end‑to‑end GHG accounting engagements across Scope 1, 2 and complex Scope 3 categories, ensuring methodologies align with the GHG Protocol and recognised standards (e.g. CDP, SBTi and ISO).

• Lead SBTi target development and submission projects end-to-end, including scoping, target calculation, documentation, internal alignment and submission support; coordinate validation queries and evidence provision.

• Design, model and present decarbonisation and net‑zero pathways (short, medium and long term), quantifying emissions reductions from levers such as energy efficiency, fuel switching, electrification, renewables procurement (PPA/RECs), process improvements, product design and supply‑chain interventions.

• Build robust emissions models and scenario/modelling frameworks (e.g. marginal abatement cost curves, scenario sensitivity, pathway comparisons) to support strategic decision making.

• Provide guidance on carbon removal, offsetting principles and credible use of removals in net‑zero strategies (aligned to SBTi Net‑Zero Standard and best practice).

• Advise on climate‑related disclosure and compliance (CSRD, TCFD/ISSB-aligned disclosures, CDP), and shape clients’ governance, risk management and climate strategy integration.

• Lead supply‑chain engagement programmes to improve data quality, develop Scope 3 models, and evaluate levers/initiatives (incl. supplier questionnaires, segmentation, data collection tools, supplier capacity building).

Qualifications

We seek a candidate with a solid foundation in climate sustainability and a keen interest in consulting. Experience with climate frameworks, the GHG Protocol, SBTi standards and methodologies and decarbonization approaches is a must. Strong communication and problem-solving skills are essential to succeed in this dynamic environment.

What you bring to the team:

• 3-5+ years’ relevant experience in climate sustainability, GHG accounting and decarbonisation advisory — previous experience at large consultancies and/or engineering background

• Hands‑on experience applying the GHG Protocol (including Scope 3 guidance) and SBTi criteria and methodologies.

• Proven track record delivering SBTi submissions and/or net‑zero strategies that have progressed through validation or board approval.

• Strong quantitative and modelling capability — able to build, interrogate and explain emissions models (Excel; experience with Python/R, SQL or specific decarbonisation tools such as SimaPro, GaBi, or bespoke models is desirable).

• Practical knowledge of energy markets and renewable procurement options (corporate PPAs, I‑REC, GO/REC frameworks), and of carbon removal/offset markets and quality principles.

• Strong project management skills with the ability to engage diverse stakeholders

• A genuine passion for consulting and helping clients achieve their sustainability goals and a proactive approach to driving climate impact

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application and CV by 09th November 2026.

We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Please do not hesitate to contact Anna Boss at anboss@deloitte.dk if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Environmental Science programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Dynamic flood exposure in Denmark: where will people live when the water comes?

Research area and project description
The overarching aim of this PhD project is to understand how flood exposure in Denmark evolves over time as a result of household location decisions, and to make that dynamic available for cost–benefit analysis of climate adaptation. This is a quantitative PhD: the work combines applied econometrics on Danish register and property-transaction data, a discrete choice experiment, and agent-based simulation modelling. The project is co-financed by the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI) and Aarhus University, and the PhD student will be part of the research environments at both institutions.

The project in a nutshell: Cost–benefit analyses of flood adaptation in Denmark evaluate investments over horizons of 80–100 years, yet they treat the spatial distribution of people, buildings and assets as fixed at today's values. Over the coming decades, urban development, demographic change and the gradual repricing of flood risk by insurers, banks and public authorities will reshape who lives in flood-prone areas and what is at risk. At the same time, Danish evidence suggests that flood risk is only weakly reflected in property prices and settlement patterns – households appear to locate under incomplete information about the risk they face. This PhD project treats flood exposure as an emergent outcome of household behavior rather than a fixed physical quantity, and develops an agent-based model of household location decisions under bounded rationality that can project exposure to 2075 under alternative scenarios for institutional risk signals: business as usual, insurance repricing, tighter mortgage lending, and full information.

Qualifications and specific competences
Required qualifications:
• An M.Sc. in economics or spatial data analyses or a closely related quantitative field
• Training in econometrics and experience with R, Python or Stata
• Good written and oral EnglishIt is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have:
• Experience with panel data, difference-in-differences, hedonic analysis or discrete choice modelling
• Experience with large administrative datasets, e.g. Danmarks Statistik registers
• Experience with or curiosity about agent-based modelling
• Reading proficiency in DanishWe do not expect any candidate to have all of these requirements. The PhD programme includes training in register data, choice experiment design and agent-based modelling, and you will be supervised closely throughout the scholarship. If you have a solid quantitative foundation and are interested in the questions, we encourage you to apply. The role of the PhD student in this project will be particularly focused on the following objectives: 1) a register-based analysis of who lives in flood-prone areas in Denmark and how residential mobility responds to flood events, using Danmarks Statistik microdata linked to building and flood hazard data; 2) a hedonic price analysis of the extent to which flood risk is capitalized in Danish property prices, including event studies around major flood events; 3) a discrete choice experiment estimating how households respond to explicit risk information and to changed signals from insurers, banks and public authorities; and 4) the integration of these results into an agent-based model that simulates exposure trajectories under alternative institutional scenarios and delivers inputs for flood cost–benefit analysis.

The PhD student will enter a research environment with a strong focus on climate adaptation. At the Department of Environmental Science, the student will join the Environmental Social Science and Geography section, which works on environmental valuation, flood damage modelling and the economics of climate adaptation. At DMI, the student will be part of the National Center for Climate Research that produce Danish flood hazard data and climate projections for decision-making at national and municipal levels in Denmark. The student will have office space at both institutions and is expected to take part in the daily research life at both.
You must upload a project description about how you intend to approach the objectives of the project.

Qualifications and specific competences: The ideal candidate is highly motivated candidate with an M.Sc. degree with specialization in economics and spatial data analyses, or closely related quantitative fields. Demonstrated oral and written communication skills in English are required. The applicant is expected to present results at international conferences and publish them in international peer-reviewed journals. The applicant should be interested in working in an international and interdisciplinary academic environment. jobs.occupation: Postdoc in RNA Biomarkers and Extracellular Vesicle Biology
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment, Roskilde University, invites applications as post-doctoral fellow in RNA cell biology from April 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Description of the post-doc project
A fully funded postdoc position (18 months) at Roskilde University in the research group of Professor Dalgaard, funded by Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond (Independent Research Fund Denmark) through the project "Enabling RNA Biomarker Origin Detection by Multiplexing Extracellular Tracing". The project will develop a multiplexed extracellular RNA (exRNA)-tracing platform capable of identifying the cell-of-origin of secreted RNAs in plasma and cell media samples and will demonstrate its use by tracing RNA released by pancreatic islet cells and adipose tissue, both highly relevant to type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. The platform will be valuable for validating novel RNA biomarkers and for discovering RNA-based therapeutic targets in metabolic disease.

Responsibilities and tasks
The postdoc’s work will include research within ExRNA biology, RNA biomarker discovery, and multi-omics profiling, with focus on tracing the cellular origin of secreted RNAs relevant to type 2 diabetes and metabolic disease. In addition, some amount of teaching is also required. 

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead the development and validation of a multiplexed exRNA-tracing platform, based on integration of bio-orthogonal proximity labeling and metabolic RNA labeling systems.
• Perform in vitro and in vivo tracing experiments in pancreatic islet cells, adipose cells, and other relevant cell models to determine the cellular origin of secreted extracellular RNAs and extracellular vesicles (EVs).
• Apply proteomics and small RNA sequencing/omics approaches to characterize the RNA and protein cargo of pancreatic islet- and adipose-derived extracellular vesicles and biofluid samples.
• Analyze and validate candidate RNA biomarkers relevant to T2D and metabolic disease, using plasma and other biofluid samples from relevant cohorts or models.
• Mentor younger or graduate students within the focus of the research project.
Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent within cell biology, molecular biology, biochemistry, or a related field. Qualifications within the following scientific areas are required:

The ideal candidate has an outstanding track record of accomplishments and a critical mindset. Moreover, an open mentality with focus on research communication, inter-disciplinary curiosity and teamwork will be required to succeed. Moreover, the following qualifications are relevant:

• Certified training in laboratory animal research is required.
• Advanced experimental experience in RNA biology and/or extracellular vesicle (EV) biology is required
• Hands-on experience with proteomics and/or small RNA sequencing or other omics-based biomarker profiling techniques is required.
• Experience with research in metabolic disease, in particular type 2 diabetes or obesity, and/or experience working with pancreatic islets or other metabolically relevant primary cells/tissues, will be highly valuable.
• Experience with publication of original relevant scientific data in peer-reviewed journals will be an advantage.
The ideal candidate should be enterprising and possess good communication skills, be visible and involved in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department and with project collaborators.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to;

• Experience and qualifications as stated above.
• Academic excellence and scientific production relevant to the description above.
• The ability to promote and utilize research results.
• Experience in mentorship and teaching.
• Ability to communicate in written and spoken English.
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperations.
The Department of Science and Environment
Department of Science and Environment is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, chemistry, physics, environmental sciences, and mathematics. Bachelor programs are offered within these areas, as are interdisciplinary Master programs. The Department’s laboratories are equipped with modern infrastructure and shared state-of-the art instrumentation. This includes recently acquired NMR, mass spectrometry (LC- and GC-MS, including high-resolution measurements and proteomics), and microscopy (AFM, confocal and fluorescence) instruments, GMO class 1 and 2 labs, flow cytometry, NTA, coulter counter, NGS, Q-PCR facilities, pipetting robots, calorimetry (ITC and DSC), chromatography (HPLC), and scattering (DLS, SAXS) instruments.
The post-doctoral position is within the Section of Molecular and Medical Biology: Molecular and Medical Biology | Roskilde University (ruc.dk)
Read more about the Department of Science and Environment at: https://ruc.dk/en/department-science-and-environment

Questions
For further information about the postdoc, please contact Professor Louise Dalgaard (tel. (+45) 4674 2713) or email: ltd@ruc.dk).

Terms of employment
The position is available from 1/5 2027. The employment is full time, and you will refer to Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management
jobs.description:
Department of Science and Environment (DSE), Roskilde University, invites applications for a position as assistant professor in Sustainability and Environmental Management, from January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is limited for a period of 4 years.

In announcing the position, DSE looks to strengthen its research in environmental sciences within the following fields: Sustainability transitions and circular economy in institutional and healthcare settings, sociotechnical systems analysis, behavioural and consumption analyses, the economic valuation of environmental and health externalities; and the wellbeing economy as a framework connecting these to the circular transition. The Department is interested in applicants who see large-scale, cross-sectoral shifts of this kind - spanning production and consumption systems - as necessary to address today's pressing environmental challenges across the natural- and social-scientific fields represented in the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The position is closely linked to and partly funded by an Innovation Fund Denmark grant for a newly initiated interdisciplinary research project ROUNDS: Rethinking the cost of care – including the cost of externalities in circular transitions. The project links human health risk assessment, ecological economics, and behavioural research to reduce reliance on single-use plastics and textiles in the healthcare sector.

The Department is interested in applicants whose research and teaching profile includes all the above subject areas in combination with an interest in building interdisciplinary research and collaboration on education. The Assistant Professor’s duties will comprise research at a high international level and a strong commitment and contribution to teaching broadly in the environmental science programs at bachelor’s and master’s level. The Assistant Professor will teach in an interdisciplinary environment and engage in problem-oriented project work with extensive student involvement and responsibility.

DSE is one of four departments at Roskilde University. The Department conducts basic and applied research within medical biology, molecular biology, environmental sciences, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Bachelor and Master programmes are offered within these areas. Research and education within the fields take place in a collaborative and interdisciplinary university environment, also spanning collaboration with the other departments, covering social sciences and humanities, where relevant. The department is organised into four Sections comprising the research and education activities.

The Assistant Professor will be part of the Section for Environmental Dynamics. The Section’s current members primarily have a background within one or more of the fields of aquatic ecology, ecotoxicology, biological production (including aquatic biotechnology), and geochemistry. DSE has a well-established shared infrastructure with state-of-the-art equipment facilities, including field spectroradiometer, Mass-spectrometry (LCMS, GCMS, ICP-MS), CHNS, various microscopy facilities and access to workshops.

Read more about the section at https://ruc.dk/en/research-group/environmental-dynamics

Responsibilities and tasks
The assistant professor’s work will include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication, and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within one or more of the fields of the Assistant Professorship and in general activities at the environmental science programme activities.

In addition to research and research-based teaching, the position also requires sharing knowledge with the rest of society - including participation in public debate. To a limited extent, this may also include performance of other activities.

As assistant professor, you are also expected to complete the educational training program for assistant professors at RUC (up to 220 hours). The training programme will give you pedagogical and didactic tools as well as familiarize you with the Roskilde University educational model called Problem oriented project learning (PPL). Applicants are referred to the university’s Faculty expectations (https://ruc.dk/en/working-roskilde-university ) for specifications on the required level of qualifications within research, teaching, networking, fundraising, impact and outreach etc.

The ideal candidate is expected to:

• Lead and further develop research within the circular economy, sustainability transitions, and environmental management in institutional and healthcare settings, including engagement in the research project ROUNDS
• Develop the field of interdisciplinary research by actively collaborating with other scientific fields within the department or at other departments, connecting environmental science with social science and economics
• Contribute to the development of the research profile of the department
• Maintain a significant record of publications
• Collaborate with colleagues in establishing a vibrant research community
• Participate actively in research networks and external research funding activities
• Teach, supervise, and assess students at BSc and MSc levels. This also implies developing the field in relation to teaching
Qualifications
You must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Science or in the interface between the natural and social sciences applied to environmental and sustainability questions. In addition, a documented qualitative and/or interdisciplinary approach to sustainability transitions is required.

Documented research production at international level within one or more of the following scientific areas are required:

• Circular economy and sustainability transitions in institutional or healthcare settings
• Sociotechnical systems theory and analysis of organisational/infrastructural change
• Valuation of environmental and health externalities, including in relation to public procurement
The ideal candidate has:

• Teaching experience within one or more of the fields of the Associate Professor
• A keen interest and experience in project-based, problem-oriented teaching as well as teaching in an interdisciplinary environment
• Documented experience with interdisciplinary research and interdisciplinary collaborations will also be seen as an advantage.
In addition, it will be seen as an advantage if you can contribute to research and teaching within one or more of these areas:

• Environmental management and monitoring
• Political economy of sustainability transitions
• Health systems and behavioural aspects of circular practice
The ideal candidate must be enterprising, possess good communication skills, and be a visible and involved participant in the department’s daily activities, in addition to being willing to engage in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration across the department.

At the time of appointment, successful candidates must master English for academic purposes.

Assessment
In the assessment of the candidates, consideration will be given to:

• Relevance of research topic
• Scientific production at an international level
• Research prospective and the ability to promote and utilise research results
• Experience in teaching and education
• Other academic experience, e.g. from organising research conferences or seminars
• Ability to contribute to development of the department’s internal and external cooperation
Questions
Potential applicants from outside Denmark will find information about life in Denmark (taxation, healthcare etc.) at www.lifeindenmark.borger.dk

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Section Kristian Syberg on tel. (+45) 4674 3776 or e-mail: ksyberg@ruc.dk or Head of Department Susanne Sørensen by email: susa@ruc.dk.

Terms of employment
The employment is on full time, 37 hours per week and in the daily work you will refer to Professor Kristian Syberg. Your head of staff will be Head of Department Susanne Sørensen.

The position will be filled according to the Agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. 

According to the Pay Transparency Directive, the salary ranges for the various job categories at Roskilde University are listed here. 

Application procedure 
After the deadline for applications the Head of Department will shortlist applicants for assessment with assistance from the recruitment committee including the chairperson of the assessment committee.

Shortly after the application deadline all applicants will be notified whether or not their application has been selected for assessment.

The shortlisted applicants will be informed about the composition of the assessment committee, and each applicant will be given the opportunity to comment on the composition of the committee and - later on - their assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed, all applicants will be informed of the outcome of their application.

Application 
To apply for the position go to www.ruc.dk/en/job/ 

Only applications in English are accepted. 

Applications must include: 

• Cover letter
• CV
• Documentation of education
• Teaching portfolio (read more about teaching portfolio at Roskilde University here)
• A complete list of publications
• A maximum of 5 relevant scientific works that you want included in the assessment
If any of the publications that you want included in the assessment are the result of a joint effort, the extent and the nature of your contribution to each individual work must then be clarified in a co-author statement (find template here).
• Research plan (maximum 2 pages)
Please submit your application no later than 13th of November 2026. 

Material received after this date will not be taken into consideration. 

Roskilde University wishes to reflect the diversity of society and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background. 

The hiring process at Roskilde University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Health & Safety Specialist, Nyborg, Denmark

Do you want to be the Safety Shoulder and make a real difference to safety in one of Europe’s most complex industrial environments?

Be the trusted Health & Safety voice in daily operations at NG Nordic’s hazardous waste treatment facility in Nyborg.

As Health & Safety Specialist, you will work close to the operational teams, helping managers and employees turn safety requirements into practical actions. You will be part of a five-person team in Nyborg and work as an integrated partner to Operations.

Nyborg is a Seveso III facility and is described as the EU’s largest hazardous waste treatment plant. Here, health and safety is not simply a compliance exercise: the risks are real, and your work can have a direct impact on people, processes and operational reliability.

Your role combines visible presence in the plant with reporting, statistics, procedures, training and improvement projects. You will advise and challenge Operations constructively, build trust across functions and help ensure a safe, professional operation.

The position is based in Nyborg and requires regular engagement with employees, supervisors and managers throughout the facility.

You will turn safety requirements into practical improvements in daily operations

You will participate in daily and weekly operational meetings, identify and prioritise EHSQ risks, and help the organisation address the issues that matter most. You will balance proactive safety work with administrative responsibilities and timely follow-up.

Your key tasks will include:

• Acting as the Health & Safety partner to Operations, advising managers and employees and participating in daily and weekly operational meetings

• Conducting safety walks, workplace inspections, toolbox talks and awareness activities, and following up on identified risks

• Preparing safety reports, statistics and KPI follow-up, identifying trends and recommending actions

• Developing and implementing practical safety procedures, training programmes, onboarding and contractor inductions

• Supporting risk assessments, audits, investigations and structured root-cause analyses of incidents and near misses

• Driving and prioritising safety improvement projects, monitoring corrective actions and supporting compliance with Danish legislation, internal standards and Seveso-related requirements

Experience from health and safety in industrial operations

We imagine that you have a relevant technical or health and safety qualification and approximately five years or more of experience in a comparable operational environment. Experience from process industry, chemicals, hazardous waste, energy or other high-risk facilities is especially relevant.

You understand occupational health and safety legislation, operational risk assessments, incident investigation, safety management systems and the importance of effective training and documentation. You are comfortable working with reports, statistics and digital tools.

You can translate complex safety requirements into clear, workable solutions. You communicate confidently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing, and you know how to engage colleagues across functions and organisational levels.

You build credibility through presence, sound judgement and constructive dialogue. You have the natural authority to challenge unsafe practices while maintaining trust and respect, and you are robust enough to handle disagreement and pressure.

You are structured, proactive and able to prioritise competing tasks. You enjoy combining hands-on operational work with analysis, administration and continuous improvement, always keeping the most significant risks in focus.

Make an impact with us

In this role, you will be a trusted partner to managers and teams, helping them turn business priorities into value adding people actions. You will create impact through thoughtful coaching, strong relationships and the confidence to help managers build strong teams.

About the role

You will report to the Head of People & Culture HQ and become part of our global People & Culture team, collaborating with colleagues across regions and specialist areas.

What makes this role interesting is the breadth. One day you may coach a manager through a sensitive performance conversation; the next, you may facilitate a leadership-team workshop, support a recruitment process or turn engagement insights into focused action. You will have room to influence, while staying close to the managers and teams you support.

What you will do

• Coach and challenge managers on leadership dilemmas, team effectiveness, engagement, development and retention, building their confidence to lead well.

What you bring

How you will make a difference

• You will thrive in this role if you are curious about the business, easy to work with and motivated by helping managers succeed rather than taking ownership away from them.

• You build trust quickly, keep momentum when topics are complex and can move comfortably between strategic perspective and hands-on support.

• You are decisive and comfortable working independently, while knowing that support and sparring from colleagues are always close at hand.

• You bring empathy to sensitive situations, but you are also clear, pragmatic and willing to challenge when it matters.

Meet the team

You’ll join People & Culture HQ, a collaborative team of 6, working closely with managers, employees and specialist colleagues across Milestone. We care about making People & Culture support useful, consistent and close to the business.

We share perspectives, help each other and keep things practical. You will have space to shape your partnerships and contribute to how our People Partner model continues to develop.

How we support you

At Milestone, we want you to have the opportunity to do meaningful work, develop your skills and grow your career.

We offer you:

• Individual development plans aligned with your career goals

• Access to training, learning resources, and certifications

• Flexible working arrangements

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about working closely with managers and teams, shaping meaningful people solutions and helping leaders navigate both opportunities and difficult moments, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Clinical position as staff specialist combined with a clinical associate professorship (research) in Paediatrics- Børn og Unge, Sjællands Universitetshospital
jobs.description:
A clinical position as staff specialist of Paediatrics at the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position as staff specialist is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical associate professor (research) in Paediatrics at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

With this new position the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Zealand University Hospital wishes to strengthen the leadership in clinical research and teaching in collaboration with the collaboration with the University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the clinical associate professorship (research) and the clinical position.

About the Department

The Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine at Zealand University Hospital is a well-established clinical and research-active department with sites in Roskilde (planned move to Køge 2028) and Nykøbing Falster. The department provides comprehensive care across the full spectrum of paediatrics, including specialised services within paediatric endocrinology and the management of childhood diabetes.

The treatment of childhood diabetes in Region Zealand is organised across multiple sites, enabling strong cross-site collaboration and the development of shared clinical pathways. The department works closely with Steno Diabetes Center Zealand and collaborates with paediatric departments both within and beyond the region.

The department offers a dynamic research environment with a focus on strengthening clinical research, including dedicated research within childhood diabetes. This field involves distinct clinical and developmental considerations compared to adult diabetes, and research activities address treatment outcomes, patient development, quality of life and health equality.

Teaching and supervision of medical students and junior doctors are integral parts of the department’s activities, and there is a strong emphasis on developing future clinicians and clinical researchers.

Qualifications:

Applicants for a position as staff specialist must be board-certified specialist in Paediatrics.

Conditions:

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the clinical associate professorship (research)) and to the hospital (the clinical position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the clinical associate professorship (research). Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as staff specialists at Zealand University Hospital.

Salary and conditions of employment as staff specialist are as agreed between the Danish Regions and the Danish Association of Medical Specialists and between the Capital Region/Region Zealand and University of Copenhagen.

As clinical associate professor (research) at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g. research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine.

Application procedure:

The application must include the following:

• Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• A description of how the applicant is qualified as

- Clinical expert

- Communicator

- Collaborator

- Manager/administrator/organizer

- Health advocate

- Scholar/researcher/teacher, professional

For more information please refer to https://sundhedsstyrelsen.dk/en/news/2013/the-seven-roles-of-physicians.

For applicants with a foreign license also a copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Paediatrics recognition.

The closing date for applications is 30.11.2026.

Further information:

For further information please contact Head of Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, Malene Boas, mboa@regionsjaelland.dk

The advertisement for the clinical associate professorship (research) is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

171819 Clinical Associate Professor (Research) of Paediatrics (Fixed-term, 5 years)

Ansættelsesområde

Region Sjælland og Region Hovedstaden bliver den 1. januar 2027 til Region Østdanmark som følge af sundhedsreformen. Dit ansættelsesområde vil være Region Østdanmark med alle tilhørende organisatoriske enheder.

Læs mere om betydningen af ansættelsesområdet på Region Østdanmarks hjemmeside.

Regionen er forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startlønnen for stillingen. Du får oplyst grundløn, centralt fastsatte tillæg og pension i den relevante overenskomst. Udover startlønnen, kan lønnen indeholde eventuelt forhandlede tillæg afhængigt af stillingen, dine erfaringer og kvalifikationer.

Se startlønnen på regionens hjemmeside

Om Sjællands Universitetshospital

Sjællands Universitetshospital er Danmarks nyeste universitetshospital med aktiviteter i Køge, Roskilde og Nykøbing F. Vi er et modigt og udadvendt universitetshospital, hvor vi hver dag arbejder for at skabe et sammenhængende sundhedsvæsen og større lighed i sundhed for borgerne i regionen.

Vores optageområde er præget af flere borgere med kronisk sygdom og sociale udfordringer end landsgennemsnittet. Derfor arbejder vi målrettet med innovation, nye samarbejdsformer og løsninger, der bringer behandling tættere på borgerne.

Hos os bliver du en del af en ambitiøs arbejdsplads, hvor samarbejde på tværs, høj faglighed og løbende forbedringer er en naturlig del af hverdagen. Vores ledelsesværdier er nytænkning, følgeskab, ordentlighed og fællesskab, og de sætter retning for, hvordan vi arbejder, udvikler os og skaber gode resultater – for både borgere og medarbejdere.

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The AP Manager leads the Accounts Payable team and is responsible for ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely processing of supplier invoices and payments globally, safeguarding financial integrity and operational efficiency. The role ensures high-quality Accounts Payable execution across the team, oversees month-end and audit processes, and acts as the escalation point for suppliers and internal stakeholders. As part of Shared Services, reporting to the Head of P2P, this position leads a team of 7 FTEs across multiple entities and is accountable for financial governance, KPI performance, and driving the function's transition from manual to automated, scalable processes. **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Approve journals and oversee approval of new vendors and vendor changes.

• Own the monthly close process for Accounts Payable, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery.

• Manage and delegate audit deliverables across quarterly, interim, and yearly cycles.

• Own KPI reporting and performance tracking, providing visibility to the Head of P2P and key stakeholders.

• Drive continuous improvement, leading automation and process projects to move the function towards scalable, less manual ways of working.

• Ensure adherence to company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements, maintaining strong governance within the AP function.

**KEY EXPECTATIONS

**In this role, you take full ownership of your team's output and workload distribution, manage complex operational and people challenges, and drive process improvement across the function. You lead rather than execute - setting direction, removing blockers, and holding the team accountable to a high standard. You build the case for change, adapt quickly when priorities shift, and are a dependable leader who drives both team performance and function-wide results.

• Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

jobs.occupation: Kickstart your Career with Deloitte’s Finance Consultancy Programme
jobs.description:
Are you interested in working in an exciting and challenging consulting role, where you can deploy and develop your skills and competencies within the CFO domain of companies? Do you hold a business-related Master’s degree by the summer of 2027, and are you ready to embark on a life-long learning journey in a leading global consulting firm? If yes, then we might have the perfect opportunity for you!

Who we are

Joining our Finance Consultancy Programme, you will get to collaborate with experienced consultants on a wide variety of assignments and development opportunities. At Deloitte, we work with different project sizes across finance disciplines and industries, but the foundation is always the same: Our genuine passion for the CFO area and creating value together with our clients.

Finance Transformation is part of Deloitte Technology & Transformation (former Consulting) consisting of more than 350 consultants in Denmark who work across all areas of the CFO function. We engage with clients to operate, advise, optimize, and transform their finance functions. Our clients range from domestic to international, from private to public, across various industries, sizes, and time horizons.

You will join a team that emphasizes collaboration, collegiality, coaching, and talent development. At Deloitte, we value diverse skills, experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, encouraging an inclusive and collaborative environment.

Exciting tasks await you

As an Analyst in Deloitte Finance Transformation, you will experience that no workdays are the same. You will face a wide range of tasks, both in the form of interim-based roles and project-based assignments. Projects and tasks will vary across finance disciplines (e.g., operational finance or business finance) and industries (e.g., private or public), and within the first years of your career, you will be assigned to as many different projects and tasks as possible to expand your toolbox and build on your financial craftmanship.

Based on the specific client's needs and your interests, experiences, and competencies, typical assignments and projects could be within the scope of:

• Finance operations optimization and transformation, e.g., controlling, month-end closing, and reporting

• Transformation and digitalization of finance functions, e.g., process optimization, closing excellence, internal controls advisory, and leveraging technology solutions

• Enterprise performance management, e.g., analytics, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting

• ERP-enabled finance transformations and finance systems implementation, e.g., outlining the ERP-strategy, defining business requirements and ensuring consistent data migration

• Finance strategy and operating model, e.g., designing service delivery models, outlining roles and responsibilities and conducting assessments

• M&A readiness and finance post-merger integration

• Global business services transformations, e.g., assessing, developing and implementing shared service functions and aligning service delivery with corporate strategy

• Internal business development and leadership support, e.g., assisting on client proposals, facilitating events and developing material to strengthen our market offerings.

Onboarding and learning

When joining us, you will participate in our onboarding programme designed with the purpose of giving you the best foundation for kickstarting your career in Deloitte. During your first two weeks, you and your peers will attend our Finance Transformation Nordic Bootcamp and our Consultant Academy, where the content is tailored to match your competencies as recent graduates. The Finance Transformation Bootcamp helps you in building your finance craftmanship and toolbox, while the Consultant Academy prepares you for your consulting role in Deloitte Technology & Transformation. Also heavily focused on social activities and team-building, the onboarding programme provides a smooth transition from university as it offers a unique opportunity to connect and build strong relations with your fellow new joiners from day one.

At Deloitte, we believe in life-long learning, and we are committed to investing in your individual development, both professionally and personally, throughout your career. You will experience this with our Finance Consultancy Programme, which is a highly structured learning programme, aimed at equipping you with the appropriate skillset and the right level of competencies needed to succeed in your role.

Leadership and culture

To support your learning, you will also be assigned a People Leader as your closest leader and go-to sparring partner. Your People Leader will help you set the overall direction of your journey in Deloitte and provide guidance across projects to make sure that your individual aspirations and professional development goals are met. Every career path is unique, and together with your People Leader you get the chance to shape your own.

We believe in leadership at all levels, and we have committed ourselves to creating and maintaining an inclusive and psychologically safe culture, where you are encouraged and empowered to take responsibility while leading both yourself and others. We combine this with a substantial focus on continuously staying relevant and being a meaningful social community to our people. We are a people’s business, and therefore we strongly believe that this is an essential prerequisite for making an impact that truly matters – for ourselves and for our clients**.**

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for you, who are passionate about consulting and the CFO-area and who are willing to go the extra mile to deliver sustainable impact that truly matters to our clients. You show an eagerness to make a difference for both clients and colleagues and you are able to see the opportunities and potential in all types of assignments. As our business can be highly changeable, it is important that you are curious by nature, and that you face challenges with an open-minded and solution-oriented approach.

In addition to this, you:

• Have completed a master’s degree within the fields of finance, economics, business, accounting, social sciences, IT, or similar areas in the summer of 2027 or before

• Have achieved academic results from your bachelor’s and master’s degree that you are proud of

• Demonstrate a flair for both oral and written communication and are fluent in English

• Have a legal working permit in Denmark

Although relevant job experience might be an advantage, this is not a requirement.

Want to know more?

Click the "I'm interested"-button above and upload your CV and grade transcripts from your bachelor’s and master’s degree if you are interested and ready to join our team**. Instead of an application letter, we would like you to answer the questions you will be presented with on the next pages** (please only consider the required (*) fields). As we process applications and arrange interviews on an ongoing basis, we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Application deadline: Hiring on an ongoing basis.

Please do not hesitate to contact Giulio Marano (gimarano@deloitte.dk / +45 30 93 64 11) or Maria Banke (mbanke@deloitte.dk / +45 20 97 64 15) if you have any questions about the position.

The Role

The Finance Systems Engineer will own the systems, data infrastructure, and internal tooling that power Teton’s finance function.

As Teton continues to scale, we need reliable financial data, connected systems, and automated workflows that allow the business to operate efficiently and make informed decisions. You will help strengthen our operational finance capabilities by ensuring our data is accurate, our systems work as intended, and our internal processes are scalable.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of finance, systems engineering, and data. You will build integrations between our accounting platform, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems, develop tools that make business intelligence data easier to access, and establish controls that maintain data integrity.

What You’ll Own

Finance Data and Systems Infrastructure

• 
Own the systems and data flows supporting Teton’s finance function, ensuring financial information is accurate, accessible, and reliable.

• 
Maintain and improve integrations between accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems.

• 
Identify infrastructure gaps and implement scalable solutions that support Teton’s growth.

Systems Integrations and Automation

• 
Build and maintain integrations and automated workflows that reduce manual work across finance and business operations.

• 
Troubleshoot integration issues, resolve data discrepancies, and implement lasting technical solutions.

• 
Identify opportunities to streamline processes through automation and better system design.

Data Integrity and Financial Controls

• 
Develop internal tools and automated checks to identify missing data, inconsistencies, and potential errors across systems.

• 
Establish reliable reconciliation processes and improve the traceability of financial data.

• 
Strengthen data validation and controls to support accurate reporting and dependable financial operations.

Operational Finance Support

Partner with the finance team to improve day-to-day workflows, reporting capabilities, and access to business-critical information.

• 
Translate operational needs into practical technical solutions that reduce administrative overhead.

• 
Build a scalable systems foundation that supports increasingly sophisticated financial and business intelligence needs.

Built a reliable, scalable finance systems infrastructure with accurate data and strong integrations across accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal platforms.

Strong technical skills in integrations, automation, APIs, and data workflows.

About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

The position requires a physical presence at our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data.

In this role, you will focus on:

• 
Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

• 
Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

• 
Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them.

• 
Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

• 
Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

• 
Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

• 
Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

•

Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis

Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis

About ChemoMetec

ChemoMetec is a worldwide leading manufacturer of cell counting and analysis equipment. We specialize in developing and producing high-precision instrumentation, delivering consistent data for thousands of customers across biotech, pharma, and academic segments.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and analytically skilled Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis to support customers and colleagues using our cell-counting instruments. In this role, you will combine cell culture biology with data analysis to help users achieve reliable results, investigate unexpected data, and turn insights into product improvements. The ideal candidate holds a PhD in a relevant field, has hands-on cell culture experience, and enjoys working with data in Python.

We are hiring two Product Specialists for our technical support team: one focused on data analysis and one on documentation. You will be part of the Product Management Department and work closely with R&D, QA, Field Application Scientists, and commercial teams. You will provide application and technical support, analyze instrument and experimental data, and contribute to the successful testing and launch of new products.

This position is based at our headquarters. The role includes occasional travel, both domestically and internationally, depending on needs.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide application and technical support for our instruments, helping customers and colleagues with assay setup, sample preparation, and interpretation of results.

• Analyze customer and internal data sets to identify the root causes of unexpected results and recommend solutions.

• Write and maintain Python scripts to automate data analysis, visualization, and reporting.

• Design and analyze experiments and comparison studies for new features and product releases.

• Support product launches with a focus on application readiness, validation data, and training.

• Contribute to technical documentation, including application notes, troubleshooting guides, and data analysis protocols.

• Assist in troubleshooting instrument software, including reading logs to support root cause analysis.

Qualifications

• PhD in Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Biomedical Science, or a related field.

• Hands-on experience with cell culture and common cell-based assays.

• Solid statistical knowledge, including experimental design and method comparison (e.g., precision, linearity, and regression analysis).

• Strong data analysis and data visualization skills.

• Experience with Python scripting for data analysis (e.g., pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib).

• Familiarity with pharmaceutical workflows and regulated lab environments (e.g., GMP) is a strong advantage.

• Structured, curious, and detail-oriented, with a passion for problem-solving.

Preferred Skills

• Experience with software debugging and troubleshooting, such as reading code and log files.

• Experience with cell counting, image cytometry, flow cytometry, or microscopy.

**

Why join ChemoMetec?**

At ChemoMetec, we believe that great people make a great workplace. We value both personal and professional development and offer an environment where you can grow, take responsibility, and make an impact. You will become part of a team of talented and supportive colleagues who enjoy working together in an informal and welcoming atmosphere. We also believe that strong relationships go beyond the workplace, which is why we regularly bring colleagues together through company-wide events to build connections and strengthen relationships across the organization.

**

Practical information**

Both positions are on-site at our HQ in Allerød, Denmark. You will refer to Director, Ph.D. Product Management Bassam Tawfik.

Starting date is as soon as possible, and we conduct interviews on an ongoing basis. Deadline for applying is 20 November 2026.

Are you passionate about renewable energy and motivated by turning complex needs into practical solutions? PEAK Wind is seeking a consultant to support product and project delivery across Data & Intelligence. You will help drive the delivery of our data, analytics, reporting, and digital solutions. This is a hands-on role for someone who can connect clients, renewable energy specialists, and technical teams, and who enjoys taking responsibility from the first conversation to a solution that creates measurable value.

Introducing the Data & Intelligence Team

You will become part of our Data & Intelligence (D&I) team, where we work within PEAK Wind’s operations management service offering and manage full value chain data management for our clients. We support renewable energy assets worldwide through data management, reporting solutions, analytics, digital products, and AI capabilities, helping deliver data-driven solutions that support our clients and renewable energy projects. Our team consists of highly motivated professionals who bring diverse backgrounds and a strong commitment to excellence. We support one another, share knowledge, and celebrate both individual and collective achievements.

You will report to the Head of Data & Intelligence and work closely with colleagues across D&I, Asset Management, Engineering, HSEQ, Finance, and Business Development. You will coordinate day-to-day delivery with data engineers, data scientists, developers, and renewable energy specialists, while acting as a clear and trusted point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders.

How You Will Make an Impact

In this role, you will combine product ownership with project delivery, turning business and client needs into well-defined, commercially sound, and successfully delivered D&I solutions. You will take ownership of selected products and projects, create structure around delivery, and ensure that commitments move from proposal and plan to implementation, adoption, and follow-up.

Your work will span both recurring services and new opportunities. This includes day-to-day ownership of selected digital products, coordination of analytics and reporting solutions based on operational and SCADA data, and delivery of selected AI and automation initiatives. You will help ensure that our products and services solve real operational problems rather than becoming isolated technical exercises.

On smaller assignments, you may own the full process from client dialogue and scoping through delivery and handover. On larger assignments, you will work with a multidisciplinary team and keep scope, responsibilities, budget, timeline, quality, and stakeholder expectations aligned. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Own and coordinate selected D&I client projects and internal initiatives from initial need and scoping through delivery, adoption, and follow-up

• Translate operational and commercial challenges into clear requirements, work packages, priorities, acceptance criteria, and delivery plans for technical teams

• Take day-to-day ownership of selected digital products and reporting solutions, including backlog management, stakeholder coordination, implementation planning, user feedback, and continuous improvement

• Coordinate analytics and reporting use cases involving SCADA data, availability, production losses, alarms, asset performance, and operational reporting

• Support proposals and commercial scoping by defining deliverables, assumptions, team setup, effort, pricing input, risks, dependencies, and expected client value

• Act as the link between clients, renewable energy specialists, Product Owners, data engineers, data scientists, and software developers

• Manage delivery governance, including progress tracking, budgets, risks, decisions, actions, dependencies, and clear communication to stakeholders

• Drive selected AI, reporting, and automation initiatives together with technical specialists, ensuring that solutions are useful, governed, and adopted

• Challenge requests constructively, clarify the underlying problem, and recommend a simpler or non-technical solution when that creates better value

• Create clear documentation, client material, handovers, and ways of working so solutions can be operated, supported, and scaled

• Capture lessons learned and contribute to D&I frameworks, templates, playbooks, product roadmaps, and continuous improvement across PEAK Wind

What Will Make You Successful in This Role

At PEAK Wind, we know success comes in many forms. What matters most is your ability to create clarity, build trust, and get valuable work delivered. The following qualities and experiences will help you succeed in this role:

• A degree in engineering, renewable energy, data, business, project management, or a related field, or an equivalent track record from technical consulting or digital delivery

• Experience managing client-facing projects, digital products, analytics solutions, or operational improvement initiatives from scope to implementation

• A strong understanding of project and product delivery, including requirements, prioritisation, planning, budgets, risks, stakeholder management, and handover

• The ability to work across commercial, operational, and technical topics and translate effectively between specialists and decision-makers

• Experience preparing proposals, scopes of work, estimates, presentations, or business cases, with an understanding of how delivery choices affect client value and profitability

• Professional experience in renewable energy, asset management, operational analytics, or another complex technical environment; wind operations, SCADA, availability, or performance reporting experience is a strong advantage

• Familiarity with data and digital products such as Power BI, APIs, cloud platforms, reporting systems, workflow automation, or AI-enabled solutions; hands-on software development is not required

• Clear and effective communication skills in English, both spoken and written, and confidence working directly with clients and senior stakeholders

• A structured and pragmatic approach to problem-solving, with the initiative to create momentum when requirements are incomplete or responsibilities are unclear

• Sound commercial judgement, attention to detail, and the ability to balance quality, timeline, effort, and business value

• A collaborative mindset and the ability to stay calm, constructive, and accountable in an international, cross-functional environment

We care more about your ability to structure ambiguity, build strong relationships, and deliver useful outcomes than about a specific job title or number of years.

Why Join PEAK Wind

• A central role in shaping and delivering data, analytics, reporting, and digital solutions that directly support renewable energy assets and client decision-making

• An international, inclusive, and diverse workplace where differences are valued

• The opportunity to work on leading renewable energy projects alongside experienced industry professionals

• A broad role with direct exposure to clients, commercial decisions, operational challenges, and modern data and AI solutions

• A flat organisational structure where you can take ownership, challenge constructively, and see the result of your work

• A strong focus on your learning, development, and professional growth across product, project, commercial, and renewable energy disciplines

• A culture that values commitment, meaningful contributions, and having fun

Our Commitment to Inclusion and Fair Hiring

We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace drives innovation, creativity, and stronger results. At PEAK Wind, we are committed to fair and transparent hiring processes, welcoming candidates from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Our hiring decisions focus on what each person brings to the role and our team, and we are committed to ensuring transparent salary structures, with pay decisions based on clear, objective, and gender‑neutral criteria. Salary information, including the relevant salary band, will be shared with candidates when they are invited to a first interview.

How to Apply

We look forward to receiving your application. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found. Please apply directly through our website. If you have any questions or would like to know more about the position, please contact People & Development at recruitment@peak-wind.com.

About PEAK Wind

PEAK Wind is an independent renewable energy specialist in commercial, financial, and technical operations, delivering advisory, intelligence, and asset management services to investors and developers around the world. From onshore and offshore wind generation to Power-to-X, we work across the entire energy lifecycle to optimise operations and maintenance, enhance asset performance, and provide a holistic view of renewable infrastructure portfolios.

Our values - Expertise, Passion, Unity, and Integrity - are reflected in everything we do, from how we support our clients to how we collaborate as a team. At PEAK Wind, you will be able to apply your professional skills in a dynamic environment and experience a meaningful responsibility and involvement.
