jobs.employer_name: KU- SCIENCE - CHEM og MATH og NBI-HCØ
jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

   

  Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applicants for PhD stipends in mathematics.

  The start date is ordinarily September 1, 2027, but can be subject to negotiation.

  There will be PhD stipends available in:

   	
• Algebraic and Arithmetic Geometry, Applied algebra, Combinatorics, Geometric group theory, Geometry and Geometric Analysis, Number Theory, Representation Theory, and Topology as covered by the section Algebra & Geometry and  Copenhagen Center for Geometry & Topology (GeoTop).    	
• Classical Analysis, Descriptive Set Theory, Functional Analysis, Geometric group theory, Harmonic Analysis, History of Mathematics, Mathematical Physics, Operator Algebras, Partial Differential Equations, Quantum Information, Quantum Computation and Quantum Simulation as covered by the section Analysis and Quantum, the Centre for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory  and the Quantum for Life Center.   You are welcome to contact any member of the department to discuss research projects.

   

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the field of Mathematics or nearby fields, whose background and research interests are a strong fit with the areas of mathematics above.

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members; around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics, and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website http://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research  conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/.  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  You can find more information about the PhD program on the homepage http://www.math.ku.dk/english/programmes/ph.d/. 

   

  The PhD programme 

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. mathematics or closely related. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled in one of the faculty’s master’s programmes in Mathematics or Quantum Information Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme  (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional experience, including publications (if any) 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics 	
• Good English skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, publications (if any), language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or Master’s and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Reference letters (if available; letters can be uploaded as part of the application or sent to hr-math@adm.ku.dk by the reference person).   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 GMT+1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

   

  Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applications for PhD stipends in Statistics and the mathematics of Insurance and Economics.

  The start date is ordinarily September 1, 2027, but can be subject to negotiation.

  We invite applications for PhD stipends in the following areas, all within the sections of Insurance and Economics and Statistics and Probability Theory:

   	
• Optimal transport and adapted Wasserstein metrics (contact Johannes Wiesel, wiesel@math.ku.dk) 	
• Causality and reliable ML at the Copenhagen Causality Lab. Applicants should propose their own angle and argue how it fits the group and wider network, including the Pioneer Centre for AI and SMARTbiomed (see https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us). 	
• Other areas within statistics, mathematics-economics, and actuarial science besides those mentioned above (contact PhD coordinator Helle Sørensen, helle@math.ku.dk)   We encourage you to specify preferred project(s) and supervisor(s) in your application. 

  You are welcome to contact any member of the sections of Insurance and Economics and Statistics and Probability Theory to discuss research projects.

   

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates with an education in Statistics, Insurance, Economics or nearby fields and with strong mathematical qualifications.

   

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members, around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors' programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website http://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/.  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  You can find more information about the PhD program on the homepage http://www.math.ku.dk/english/programmes/ph.d/. 

   

  The PhD programme 

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant with the help of the supervisor.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes. Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  ***************************************************************************

  Responsibilities and tasks:

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teach and carry out knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at internationally recognized journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    

  We are looking for candidates with the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional experience, including publications (if any) 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics and its applications 	
• Good English skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, publications (if any), language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Reference letters (if available; letters can be uploaded as part of the application or sent to hr-math@adm.ku.dk by the reference person).   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Application deadline

  The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowships, please contact the people mentioned in the beginning of the call.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**We are looking for several Lead Business Consultants to join our EMEA Consulting Services team, working with our clients across the UK and the Nordics. Our client base in the region is growing, and so is the breadth of expertise our implementation projects require. Rather than hiring for one narrow profile, we are opening multiple positions for implementation specialists across the full front-to-back platform, and we will match you to the projects where your depth is strongest.

The team allows for consulting excellency, efficiency in configuration and standardization as well as knowledge sharing and collaboration across divisions and market units. As a Lead Business Consultant you are, or will become, a trusted business and technology advisor for our clients in one or more of the following areas:

• Investment accounting and financial reporting (ABOR)

• Investment book of record (IBOR), position keeping and valuation

• Investment operations, settlement and post-trade processing

• Data management, interfaces and communications (Data & Com)

• Front office: portfolio management, trading and order management

• Compliance, regulatory and internal restrictions

• Performance measurement and attribution

• Risk management (market and liquidity)

• Alternative investments and private markets

• Instrument valuation and analytics (theoretical pricing)

You will be exposed to the complete spectrum of financial instruments and their valuation, from plain vanilla equity and fixed income instruments to complex OTC derivatives and private market assets. Furthermore, you will work with all processes related to your area of specialization.

As part of your induction you will be ‘hands-on’ in our software system and attend the three-weeks’ SimCorp Dimension® Academy.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**As a Lead Business Consultant you will take over a range of tasks in a project team, such as:

• Be responsible for major parts of SimCorp implementation projects in your area of specialisation: you anticipate client needs based on your understanding of the relevant business processes at asset managers, asset owners, insurers or banks and act as a trusted advisor to the client

• Design and configure solutions across multiple modules and project streams that enable our clients to reach their desired outcomes

• Connect your specialism to the wider front-to-back solution, working closely with colleagues who cover the adjacent areas of the platform

• Advise on and improve standard implementation processes as well as product and service offerings

• Identify opportunities for growth and explore new ideas, feeding this back to the organisation and supporting its development

• Participate in sales processes when required to position SimCorp concepts and offerings

• Instruct and mentor less experienced colleagues on the job and share knowledge with colleagues on an international level

**What We Value

**You like to deep dive into business processes in investment management and enjoy modelling them in our software. You have in-depth knowledge about the business at asset managers, fund managers, insurers or banks. In addition you bring with you:

• Degree in economics, finance, mathematics, computer science or similar qualification

• Previous experience as an Analyst or (Implementation) Consultant for asset managers, asset owners, banks or consulting firms

• FRM, CFA, CIPM or other relevant certifications/designations are desirable

• Team spirit and a desire to share your knowledge

• High communication and consulting skills

• High degree of commercial awareness, customer orientation and quality consciousness

• Fluency in English

• Readiness to travel

**Benefits

**SimCorp provides a range of benefits that may influence decisions regarding job offers. With operations in more than 30 offices globally, the benefits package can differ depending on the country. SimCorp implements a global hybrid work policy, requiring employees to be in the office two days per week and permitting remote work on other days. Additional information about location-specific benefits is available from the recruiter.

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually.

**Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.

**At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

For any questions you are welcome to contact our Lead Talent Acquisition Partner, Azeta GUITI. If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp and you can see yourself contributing and thriving in the position described above, but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway.

SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become a prominent provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 4,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, without regard to race, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide high-quality solutions to our clients

**WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the bar by creating great guest experiences, and use every shift as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of Juicers who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You will learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path, our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The AP Manager leads the Accounts Payable team and is responsible for ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely processing of supplier invoices and payments globally, safeguarding financial integrity and operational efficiency. The role ensures high-quality Accounts Payable execution across the team, oversees month-end and audit processes, and acts as the escalation point for suppliers and internal stakeholders. As part of Shared Services, reporting to the Head of P2P, this position leads a team of 7 FTEs across multiple entities and is accountable for financial governance, KPI performance, and driving the function's transition from manual to automated, scalable processes. The role is a full-time position and reports to the Head of Procure to Pay.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Lead, coach and develop a team of 7 FTEs across the Accounts Payable function.

• Approve journals and oversee approval of new vendors and vendor changes.

• Own the monthly close process for Accounts Payable, ensuring accuracy and timely delivery.

• Manage and delegate audit deliverables across quarterly, interim, and yearly cycles.

• Maintain control and oversight of the supplier invoice workflow, including monitoring and clearing backlog to keep processing on track.

• Own KPI reporting and performance tracking, providing visibility to the Head of P2P and key stakeholders.

• Drive continuous improvement, leading automation and process projects to move the function towards scalable, less manual ways of working.

• Ensure adherence to company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements, maintaining strong governance within the AP function.

**KEY EXPECTATIONS

**In this role, you take full ownership of your team's output and workload distribution, manage complex operational and people challenges, and drive process improvement across the function. You lead rather than execute - setting direction, removing blockers, and holding the team accountable to a high standard. You build the case for change, adapt quickly when priorities shift, and are a dependable leader who drives both team performance and function-wide results.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

• Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role & Department

**As part of Genmab’s strategy to become an integrated end-to-end biotech innovation powerhouse, the company has expanded its focus to include commercialization and direct marketing of its own products. To ensure continued strong quality oversight during a period of parental leave, we are seeking a fixed-term GMP QA Manager (maternity cover) to join the QA Commercial & Lifecycle team until July 2027.

The role is based in Denmark and reports to the Director of QA GMP Commercial & Lifecycle. You will be part of a well-functioning and experienced team responsible for quality oversight of Drug Products (DP) and Finished Goods (FG) for commercial products, working closely with CMOs, partners, and internal SMEs.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Contribute to review and release (delegated QP) of commercial Drug Products and Finished Goods

• Handle deviations, CAPAs, and change controls in compliance with Genmab SOPs and applicable regulatory requirements

• Provide QA oversight of contractors and vendors related to outsourced GMP activities

• Maintain strong collaboration with internal stakeholders, partners, and CMOs

• Support Quality Management Reviews (QMR) and Annual Product Reviews (APR)

• Review and author QMS SOPs, work instructions, and templates as required

• Represent QA GMP in project teams and advise on GMP compliance

**Requirements

**

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant life science discipline

• Minimum 5 years’ experience in the pharmaceutical industry, preferably within QA GMP

• Experience with DP and FG GMP production and delegated QP responsibilities

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills; fluent in English

• Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and changing environment

• Results-oriented and committed to contributing to Genmab’s overall success

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK563.040,00---844.560,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

**About Us

**You know that rental bike you unlocked with your phone this morning? Or the tracker on your dog's collar that tells you he's two streets away, again? Neither of those works without a network connection. Onomondo is the layer that makes sure the data actually gets through.

We're the infrastructure behind the Internet of Things (IoT). Companies building connected products come to us for the connectivity that keeps their devices online, anywhere in the world, and for the platform where they manage, monitor, and troubleshoot it themselves.

****Where we sit

****We're somewhere between SaaS and telecom. We sell software, so we move fast, ship often, and care about the user experience. But we also operate inside telecommunications: which is more complex and technical than most software. Our customers are engineers, they ask hard questions and the relationship starts rather than ends at purchase.

That mix also makes us sticky. Most SaaS tools are nice to have. If our connectivity stops, our customers' products stop. That means our business grows as our customers and the industry grows. We've been growing fast and we don't plan to slow down, which is exactly why we need this role.

****What the role is

****We're looking for a Data & Automation Specialist who loves digging into data, and wants to use that foundation to make every team at Onomondo work smarter.

Your starting point is data. You'll work with complex, messy, multi-source data, from billing and revenue to product usage and commercial pipelines and turn it into analysis, dashboards and answers the business can act on. You'll partner with teams across the company (Sales, Customer Success, Finance, Operations) to understand what they need to know, and build the reporting that gets them there.

From that foundation, you'll look for where the data shows us time being lost, and fix it. That might be a script, an integration, a scheduled job, or an AI skill where that is the right approach. Getting there often means untangling messy data or a half-broken process first and you don't shy away from that groundwork when it's what the job actually needs.

AI is a real and growing part of the toolkit here. As you settle in, there's plenty of room to grow into that area. This includes our AI infrastructure and production agent stack, ready to be taken to the next level. Our vision is a backbone data warehouse with all data sources available so that our colleagues can self-service with trust through AI.

You'll report to our Data Analytics Manager, Jonathan, and be part of the Insights team.

****What you'll do

• Working with complex data across billing, revenue, product usage and commercial systems. Cleaning, modelling and making sense of it

• Building dashboards and visualizations that teams actually use to make decisions. We currently use Tableau for most of our complex visualizations, but we foresee leaning into an in-house setup. Groundwork is already in place to allow for broader adoptions and flexibility

• Running deeper analyses on the questions that matter, from revenue and billing trends to customer behavior and operational efficiency

• Finding the manual, repetitive workflows that cost the company the most time, and automating them in whatever form actually fits

• Building and maintaining integrations between the tools teams already use (Slack, Notion, HubSpot, Google Workspace, and others)

• Authoring and iterating AI skills where they're the right tool, using Onomondo's existing skill framework

• Growing into deeper AI/agent infrastructure work over time. Connectors, permissioning, production agents and moreNot all at once, of course. We'll start with what matters most, build it to scale, then keep going.

****What we're looking for

• Strong with data: comfortable with SQL, working in a data warehouse (we use BigQuery), and handling complex, imperfect datasets

• Experienced in data visualization and analysis. You can turn a messy question into a clear chart and a clear answer

• Comfortable writing code (Python or similar) to analyse, transform and automate

• A fixer by instinct. You notice friction and want to remove it, without needing to be asked

• Curious about AI, LLMs and agents, and keen to explore how they can make data and processes work better - even if that's not your primary experience yet

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity: nobody will hand you a fully-scoped ticket, you'll often have to find the problem first

• Communicates clearly and works well directly with non-technical stakeholders across teams

Nice to have, though not required: experience with Tableau or similar BI tools, billing or financial data, data modelling, workflow orchestration tools, exposure to LLMs/agents or MCP, or a general understanding of how SaaS businesses run (subscriptions, revenue metrics, GTM tooling, and the cross-team workflows common at software companies).

****Applying

****Your application doesn't need to be polished and you don't need to check all the boxes, to apply.

Tell us what you built, what you were trying to move, and what happened.

****Life at Onomondo

****The things we build have global reach. The way we build them is personal. We're a team of engineers, operators, and commercial minds in Copenhagen who debate passionately about technical or GTM approaches and then go for a run together. Or padel. Or a beer. Or a boardgame night. People here stay curious, speak up when something feels off, and bring energy whether it's a product launch sprint or a Friday bar.

Practically speaking, that looks like: paid health insurance, catered cooked-on-site lunch every day, an in-office gym with workouts (HIIT of yoga) three times a week during work hours (we're serious about this), quarterly Friday bars, an espresso machine, a full snack and drink-bar and a pretty impressive breakfast setup.

****Our hiring process

****We care deeply about creating a fair and inclusive process.

**That means:

**

• We don’t need your picture

• We select candidates based on skills and relevant work experience for the role.

**What you can expect:

**

• Screening call with Madalina, our Head of People (Online, 30 minutes)

• Skill interview with Jonathan & Mateusz, our Data Analytics Manager & Head of Revenue Operations (In-Person, 1 hour)

• Meet with our Co-Founder, Michael (In-Person, 30 minutes)

Note - We review and interview candidates continually, and therefore encourage you to apply at your earliest convenience.

_Are you an experienced reward professional who enjoys turning complex problems into practical solutions delivering value to Pandora? Do you want to shape how performance and reward are applied across Pandora’s Global Office while enabling leaders and HR teams to make confident, consistent decisions? If so, this could be the opportunity for you!

_We are looking for an exceptional Manager, Performance & Reward Global Office to join our Performance & Reward CoE at Pandora’s Global Headquarters in Copenhagen.

As the Performance & Reward partner for the Global Office, you will act as the primary connection between the business and our global team. You will play a key role in shaping and governing reward solutions, bringing business needs into global design and equipping HR Business Partners with the guidance and tools they need to make high-quality decisions.

This role offers the opportunity to combine strategic reward expertise with close business partnering in a truly global environment. You will provide expert guidance and oversight across key Performance & Reward matters, while helping to strengthen capabilities throughout Pandora’s People Function.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Strategic Performance & Reward Advisory: Advise HR Directors and HR Business Partners on complex, high-impact Performance & Reward matters, ensuring that global reward principles are applied effectively within the Global Office context.

• Capability Building: Translate Performance & Reward frameworks and principles into practical guidance, tools and learning that enable the People Function to manage standard matters with greater confidence and independence.

• Reward Design & Governance: Lead local reward design and governance across areas such as benefits, market benchmarking, budgeting and salary ranges, ensuring alignment with global principles and evolving business needs.

• Senior-Level Moves: Advise on Band 3+ moves, engaging early to identify implications, ensure alignment with global principles and connect stakeholders with the relevant global Performance & Reward experts.

• Pay Equity: Monitor pay equity, identify material risks and recommend evidence-based actions in collaboration with HR Business Partners and Performance & Reward experts.

• Global Insights: Share insights across the Performance & Reward Centre of Excellence to identify emerging business needs and continuously improve global frameworks and guidance.

**We’re Looking For Someone Who Brings

**A strong foundation within Performance & Reward and the ability to turn complex frameworks into practical, business-focused solutions. You are comfortable advising senior stakeholders and can balance global principles with local business needs.

You build trust through sound judgement, attention to detail and a collaborative approach. You enjoy working across different functions and are motivated by enabling others to make consistent, high-quality decisions. You take ownership, communicate clearly and contribute positively to a culture of shared success and continuous improvement.

**In addition to that, we also see that you have:

**

• Solid general experience within performance, reward, compensation or benefits.

• Experience advising HR leaders and HR Business Partners on complex reward matters.

• The ability to manage stakeholders across a variety of business areas.

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to navigate complex information.

• Knowledge of Danish employment legislation is an advantage.

• The ability to translate global principles and frameworks into clear, practical guidance.

• A collaborative mindset and confidence working across a global and multicultural organization.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in English.

**Additional Information

**

Do you want to structure compliance obligations and do you know how to communicate such obligations to an internal organization. Then you might be our new Compliance Manager.

Continia develops add-on solutions for Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central. Our solutions for accounts payable automation, e-documents, expense management and bank integration help more than 20,000 customers worldwide automate everyday finance processes, delivered through a global network of more than 1,800 reselling partners.

At Continia, we are looking for a Compliance Manager who can structure and manage our compliance obligations from both internal policies and legislation. The role is part of our Legal & Compliance team, where you will contribute to ensuring that Continia complies with its obligations and has an appropriate governance structure for it.

Why now?

Continia has been scaling a lot over the last years both in terms of customers, revenue and employees and is now ready to take a more formalized approach to compliance. You will be in the front of that change.

About the role

As Compliance Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring compliance with all relevant legal, regulatory, and international standards. You will be responsible for developing and structuring a compliance program that aligns with industry best practices and supports our business objectives.

Continia is ISO27001 certified and we have an ISAE3402 assurance report. You will be responsible for maintaining the certification and assurance report, but not for carrying out all the controls etc. under the frameworks.

This is not an IT Security or data protection expert role. You will have colleagues who are that.

You will work closely with our IT Security employees and your colleagues in Legal & Compliance. You report to Brian Jürs, Head of Legal & Compliance.

You will know you are succeeding when the day-to-day compliance runs smoothly and when your colleagues know what is expected of them and when.

What you will be doing

• Develop, implement, and maintain Continia’s information security and compliance program.

• Operate our ISO27001 and ISAE3402 frameworks, so we can maintain our certification and assurance report, including following up on completion of allocated tasks.

• Develop and maintain an annual wheel for compliance with obligations from both internal policies and legislation.

• Create awareness about and train the organization in relevant compliance obligations.

• Follow up with relevant stakeholders to ensure that compliance processes are adjusted in accordance with changes in policies, legislation etc.

• Collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders across departments to ensure company-wide compliance.

Who are you?

We are looking for a proactive and results-oriented professional with a strong work ethic and passion for compliance. You thrive with building up compliance structures, following up on obligations and have excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

We imagine you, have:

• Experience in developing and implementing compliance programs.

• Strong knowledge about operation of the ISO 27001 framework and maybe also the ISAE34002 framework.

• 3+ years of experience in a similar role, preferably in an international IT company.

• Strong communication skills

• Fluency in English, written and spoken. Danish is a plus.

Experience is important, but so is the drive to grow. If you do not tick every box, do not let that stop you from applying.

What do we offer?

At Continia, you will become part of an international SaaS company with strong ambitions and a unique partner driven go to market model.

You will get:

• A great possibility to implement a strong compliance program and really influence how compliance is done in practice

• A small team of close colleagues who will help you succeed with your tasks.

• Flexible working hours at the office and in your home office. You will be based in Copenhagen and work from the office at least 3 days a week

• A competitive compensation package, including pension and health insurance

• Local benefits such as subsidized lunch and an active employee association

• Company events where you meet colleagues from all around the world

How to apply

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, please upload your CV along with a short motivation for your application. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

For questions about the position, please contact Brian Jürs, Head of Legal & Compliance at brdj@continia.com.

Continia is committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all applicants with a Danish residence and work permit. For GDPR and processing reasons, all applications and CVs must be uploaded via the provided link and not sent by email or otherwise.

About Continia

At Continia, we value diversity and encourage authenticity. We are team players who respect each other's thoughts and ideas, and we expect everyone to take ownership of their work. We focus on personal and professional development to grow internally within our organization.

In our day-to-day work, we are pragmatic and result-oriented, and we aim to stay entrepreneurial by keeping things simple and focusing on our employees. We celebrate our wins and releases and aim to have one major event each year where all employees meet up in one place.

We recognize that time is what matters most. Continia solutions give customers more time every day to work and live. That's why "It's About Time" is our motto. Our success is built on partnering with more than 1,800 reselling partners, serving more than 20,000 customers worldwide.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**We are seeking a Senior Manager, Digital Solutions (Web & Martech Platforms) to join our centralized Web & Martech Hub within the Data, Digital & AI organization. The role will play a key part in enabling Genmab's EU and International digital expansion while driving adoption and effective use of our enterprise Web and Martech platforms.

As a member of the Hub team, this role will partner with regional Spoke teams and cross-functional stakeholders to translate market needs into scalable platform capabilities, enable adoption of common standards and reusable solutions, and support the continued evolution of our Web and Martech ecosystem, including the implementation of Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) and Edge Delivery Services.

**Responsibilities

**

• Serve as a key Hub partner for EU and International Web & Martech initiatives, working with regional stakeholders to understand market needs and enable successful adoption of enterprise digital platforms and capabilities.

• Support the continued expansion of Genmab's Hub-and-Spoke model by enabling regional teams to effectively consume Hub-provided platforms, reusable components, standards, and delivery practices.

• Play a key role in the implementation and evolution of AEM and Edge Delivery Services, including planning, prioritization, and enablement of reusable components and capabilities required across global and regional websites.

• Partner closely with the Platform Architect, Design Agency of Record, business stakeholders, and implementation partners to translate business and market requirements into scalable and reusable Web capabilities.

• Support platform management and enablement across the broader Web & Martech ecosystem, including AEM, Salesforce Experience Cloud, GA4/GTM, OneTrust, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, and other supporting technologies.

• Partner with Data Privacy, Information Security, Enterprise Architecture, Design, and other cross-functional teams to ensure platform capabilities and implementations align with enterprise, security, privacy, and design standards.

• Work with technology and delivery partners, including HCL, to coordinate platform enhancements, component development, market enablement, and implementation activities.

• Identify common requirements across markets and promote reuse of components, templates, integrations, and established platform patterns rather than market-specific solutions.

• Support platform roadmaps, demand prioritization, adoption tracking, and continuous improvement based on business needs and market feedback.

• Develop and maintain platform guidance, playbooks, and enablement materials to help Spoke teams adopt Web & Martech capabilities consistently and efficiently.

• Act as a bridge between EU/International stakeholders and the broader Web & Martech Hub, ensuring requirements, dependencies, risks, and decisions are effectively coordinated.

**Requirements

**

• 12+ years of experience in digital platforms, enterprise Web, Martech, product/platform management, technology delivery, or related roles.

• Strong understanding of enterprise Web platforms, component-based development, and modern digital delivery practices.

• Experience working with global and regional stakeholders across complex, matrixed organizations.

• Ability to translate business requirements into scalable platform capabilities and coordinate across architecture, engineering, design, business, and delivery teams.

• Experience working with Agile delivery models and external technology or implementation partners.

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to combine sufficient technical depth with strong business, platform management, and delivery capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications

**

• Experience with Adobe Experience Manager / Edge Delivery Services, Salesforce Experience Cloud, or comparable enterprise CMS/DXP platforms.

• Exposure to Martech technologies such as GA4, GTM, OneTrust, and Salesforce Marketing Cloud.

• Experience with reusable component libraries, design systems, or component-driven Web development.

• Experience with Hub-and-Spoke or other federated platform operating models.

• Experience supporting European and/or international digital initiatives and working across multiple markets.

EUR0,00---0,00

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in breast cancer epidemiology / clinical epidemiology
jobs.description:
The Department of Clinical Epidemiology at Faculty of Health at Aarhus University invites applications for a position as postdoctoral research fellow in the field of Breast Cancer Epidemiology as per 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. This is a two-year position is fully funded by the Health Insurance Denmark.

The Department of Clinical Epidemiology is a research department at Aarhus University Hospital, within the Institute of Clinical Medicine at Aarhus University. Researchers in the department use advanced epidemiological methods to study the prognosis of patient populations. The department is engaged in a variety of activities regarding clinical epidemiological research, including cancer prognosis research. The department is involved in counselling health care professionals to improve the quality of health care and treatment. A large number of projects in the department are carried out in cooperation with Danish and international collaborators.

About the research project
The position entails research within clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship. The successful candidate will join a project focusing on studies related to adherence to breast cancer treatment; side effects and complications of breast cancer and its treatment; and how these may influence quality of life, long-term survivorship, and early and late breast cancer recurrence. The project investigates the association of pharmacological, genetic and socioeconomic factors and adherence to cancer treatment; employing advanced epidemiological methods including emulated target trials, group-based trajectory modelling, mediation analyses, and Bayesian modelling approaches to investigate adherence to cancer treatment and recurrence. The research fellow will join a vibrant and dynamic multinational and multidisciplinary project team (the Predictors of Breast Cancer Recurrence – ProBeCaRe – project team) with established successful long-term research collaboration. 

The successful applicant will contribute to the development of the department through research of high international quality. They will work closely with colleagues, receiving supervision and guidance. Emphasis will be placed on the applicant’s interest in building bridges between clinical, epidemiological and biostatistical research.

The main tasks will consist of:

• Research in clinical epidemiology, specifically within breast cancer and breast cancer survivorship.
• Make applications as needed for access to Danish population-based and medical registries.
• Independently perform statistical analysis using programmes such as R, SAS, or equivalent.
• Collaborate within an active research group with national and international collaborators.
• Contribute to teaching at the Aarhus University and its collaborators, as necessary.
• Take part in grant writing and participate actively in research fundraising.
• Gain experience supervising students.
• Conduct independent research of high international quality, including publication.
• Write scientific articles and participate in international congresses.
• Perform other tasks within the Department of Clinical Epidemiology fields of interest. Please see our webpage at www.kea.au.dk.
Your competences
You have academic qualifications at PhD/DSc level preferably within one or more of the following areas: epidemiology, clinical epidemiology, cancer epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, and/or can document familiarity with epidemiological research at an international level. Research experience in cancer and pharmacologic research would be advantageous, but not essential. Research experience in epidemiologic methods, analysing and incorporating data from Danish registries, including data from the National Clinical Quality Cancer Databases (specifically data from the Danish Breast Cancer Group), the Health Services Register, and the National Patient Registry, would be useful, particularly data incorporating socioeconomic factors. Research experience in cancer survivorship, patient reported outcomes and national surveys would be a benefit as well. Evidence of the ability to secure competitive research grants would be advantageous. As a person, you are motivated, ambitious, take ownership and possess good communication and interpersonal skills. We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English, with good knowledge of Danish.

In order to be assessed as qualified for this position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be used.

Principal supervisor
Deirdre Cronin Fenton, PhD, Professor

Phone: +45-87168209 / E-mail: dc@clin.au.dk

Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Clinical Institute, Aarhus University, Olof Palmes Alle 43-45, 8200 Aarhus N.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Deirdre Cronin Fenton tel.: (+45) 8716 8209 or dc@clin.au.dk.

Your place of work will be the Department of Clinical Epidemiology, Olof Palmes Alle 43-45, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Terms of employment

The base salary includes a position related supplement and pension (18.07 %). Additional supplement(s) for special qualifications can be negotiated. Authorisation supplemement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.

Application
Your application must include the following:

We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Department of Ecoscience seeks candidates for a 2-year position as academic employee to safeguard our eddy covariance stations within the ICOS and Geobasis projects at Zackenberg in Northeast Greenland.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This 2-year full-time position is expected to be filled by 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description
We are hiring an Academic Employee for Integrated Carbon Observation System (ICOS) and GEM/Geobasis activities at the Zackenberg Research Station. You will oversee all aspects of operations, including:

• Maintenance and supervision of eddy covariance stations and other monitoring stations in the field.
• Processing and analysis of eddy covariance, meteorological, and vegetation sampling data.
• Communicating and collaborating with the ICOS Ecosystem Thematic Center.
You will also go on extended field trips to harsh, remote locations in Northeast Greenland.

Your profile
You have a master's degree in Physical Geography, Environmental Science, Geophysics, or a similar field.

Experience in fieldwork, maintaining advanced measurement systems, and handling large datasets is required. Practical experience with eddy covariance systems and data loggers, and prior knowledge of ICOS standards and protocols, are an advantage. Experience with GIS software and programming languages such as Python or R is also a strong asset.

We encourage everyone interested to apply, regardless of background. We want to hire the best qualified candidate and will consider a broad range of competencies relevant to every part of the position, with a focus on collaborative skills.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience is project-based and does research, talent development, and consultancy across all major biological sub-disciplines. Our research areas include ecosystem ecology (including Arctic environments and ecosystems), aquatic biology and ecology, and biodiversity and conservation biology. The Department currently employs approximately 280 academic and technical staff.

The Department has a strong position in international biodiversity, nature, and environmental research and is a national leader in research-based consultancy in both Denmark and Greenland. Our research examines how ecological framework conditions, historical conditions, natural processes, and human-caused changes in nature and the environment affect surrounding nature. We study the underlying ecological and geographical mechanisms and human impact on biodiversity and ecosystems, with particular attention to how current climate change and other global human-caused environmental changes affect nature and biodiversity.

The Department is a leading adviser to the Danish and Greenlandic authorities on environmental issues. It also leads the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring (GEM) programme, which focuses on the effects of climate change on Arctic ecosystems. The Zackenberg Research Station is one of GEM's central research sites.

What we offer
We offer a 2-year position to safeguard our greenhouse gas flux monitoring at Zackenberg in Northeast Greenland National Park. You will join the ICOS and Geobasis teams and the research community at Zackenberg.

The Department of Ecoscience offers an informal research environment and has a long tradition of collaborating with leading international university partners. The working environment is built on teamwork and close working relationships, with established professional and social networks for young scientists. The working languages are English and Danish, and we welcome applicants from abroad. Read about Danish work-life balance and the services available when relocating to Aarhus University at www.au.dk/work.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Frederiksborgvej 399, DK-4000 Roskilde, Denmark.

For questions, please contact Professor Torben Røjle Christensen (torben.christensen@ecos.au.dk ; +45 93 50 90 49) or Head of Section professor Niels Martin Schmidt (nms@ecos.au.dk; +45 41 91 56 64).

jobs.description:
The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics, Faculty of Humanities, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), Denmark, invites applications for a two-year postdoctoral fellowship in Computational Lexicography and Linguistics to be filled by the 1st of March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The Department of Nordic Studies and Linguistics is home to 1600 students and 160 members of staff. It provides the setting for international research and education from BA to PhD studies within language, language technology, Natural Language Processing, literature, media, culture, and gender studies.

  The successful candidate will be attached to both the Centre for Language Technology (CST), which is one of the research centres of the department, and to the Society of Danish language and Literature (DSL) which compiles and publishes dictionaries and language technology resources for Danish at a scholarly basis, often in research projects in collaboration with CST. The latter affiliation will amount to around six months of the total hiring period of 24 months.

  CST conducts research in different areas of interest for language technology, such as Natural Language Processing, construction of NLP resources, Computational Cognitive Modeling and Multimodality, NLP infrastructure and policy, Representation Learning for NLP and Digital Humanities, among others.  It has a strong international profile, at the same time as pursuing the development of language technology methods and resources for the Danish language. The Centre has considerable experience managing international research projects, frequently attracts visiting researchers, and has organised major conferences in the field. In collaboration with the Department of Computer Science at the University of Copenhagen, it offers an international MSc programme in IT and Cognition. The programme, which currently admits about 30 students a year, comprises a range of courses in Natural Language Processing and Cognitive Science. In addition, we teach at several BA programs and electives, such as the BA ‘Kognitions- and Datavidenskab’ hosted at the Department of Psychology and an elective package on Language-Centric AI for students in the Humanities.

  Job content
 The successful candidate will contribute to the project ELEXAI, which focuses on a European Lexicographic Infrastructure for Artificial Intelligence (https://www.eurac.edu/en/projects/elexai), granted by the European Commission under the Horizon Europe Program.

  The candidate will in particular contribute to the project’s work packages on LLM Benchmarking, the so-called LexBench, which is led by CST and also involves DSL. This part of the project investigates how benchmarks for Natural Language Understanding can be compiled mono- and multilingually from lexical resources and datasets. The position involves designing and compiling such benchmarks in close collaboration with DSL and the other European partners of the project and to apply them in diverse evaluation scenarios. A particular focus will be put on benchmarking word understanding capabilities and on the understanding of figurative language, including the cultural bias that this part of the language may evoke in LLMs.

  Ideal candidates for this work have a background in computational lexicography and/or computational linguistics, with experience in lexicographical work and with good programming skills. It is an advantage although not a requirement, if the candidate has good knowledge of the Danish language.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement, since the candidate will not be involved in teaching.

  Qualification requirements
 Applicants will primarily be assessed on their research qualifications, including publications, the ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and experience in research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the project described above. 

  Application
 Applications must be submitted online in PDF or Word format. Click on the “Apply now” button at the bottom of this advertisement to apply.

  Applications should be written English and must include the following attachments:  

   	
• Letter of motivation 	
• CV  	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma)  	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories:    	
• Peer-reviewed publications:  	 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 	 	 	
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 	 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc. 	 	   Applicants can attach a maximum of 4 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered [1-4]. 

   	
• Research plan. 	
• Work on the dissemination of research.   Only documentation in English will be assessed.  

  Applicants are invited to familiarize themselves with the faculty’s strategic landmarks here: Strategic landmarks – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Salary and terms of employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range starts at DKK 39.993,75 (EUR 5.350,62) + a 18,07% contribution to the pension scheme. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.

  The recruitment process
 Once the deadline for applications has expired, the Head of Section will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Section will then set up an expert assessment committee to consider the applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. They will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment of their application before the appointment is announced.

  Further information on the recruitment process at University of Copenhagen can be found here:  Recruitment process – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. For more on the diverse working place environment at the University and the University’s participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, see HR Excellence in Research – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  International applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a wide variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about these services as well as information on entering and working in Denmark, here: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Contact information
 Information about the recruitment process is available from HR SOENDRE, email:HR-SOENDRE@adm.ku.dk, please refer to ID number: 211-2697/26-2L

  Additional information about the position can be obtained from Professor Bolette S. Pedersen, email: bspedersen@hum.ku.dk, The deadline for applications is 30 November 2026, 23:59 [CET] 

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered.
