It is built into the way we design, source, produce and deliver world-class foundry machines. We are looking for a Quality Engineer who wants to be close to the product, close to production and close to the decisions that improve how we work.

This role is for someone who enjoys solving real quality challenges in a manufacturing environment. Someone who is structured, curious and persistent enough to follow an issue from first observation to sustainable improvement.

What You’ll Do

• Take ownership of quality improvements across supplier quality, production quality and internal quality processes.

• Handle non-conformities, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and ensure follow-up until issues are properly closed.

• Work closely with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers to identify risks, solve quality challenges and prevent repeat issues.

• Support and develop supplier quality performance through audits, structured follow-up, documentation and improvement plans.

• Use data, facts and structured problem-solving tools to analyze trends, set priorities and recommend practical quality improvements.

• Contribute to audits, customer requirements and management systems, with ISO 14001 as an area where you have basic knowledge or interest.

Why You’ll Love Working with Us

• A role where quality is at the center — not a side responsibility.

• The chance to work hands-on with complex, high-precision equipment and see the impact of your improvements in real production.

• A workplace where your structure, curiosity and follow-through help prevent issues before they reach the customer.

• Close collaboration with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers, so you can turn observations into practical improvements.

• The opportunity to help strengthen quality culture in a global industrial company with strong products, proud craftsmanship and long product lifetimes.

You will not be sitting far away from the product or the people making it. You will be part of the daily dialogue around quality, helping colleagues and suppliers understand what went wrong, why it happened and how we make sure it does not happen again.

Who You Are

• You have a background in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Production Technology or a similar field.

• You have experience with quality work in a manufacturing, production or industrial environment.

• You are motivated by root cause analysis, corrective actions and the satisfaction of closing issues properly.

• You understand supplier quality or are eager to work closely with suppliers on deviations, audits, documentation and improvement plans.

• You like being close to the shop floor and working with people across functions to solve practical quality challenges.

• You are analytical and structured, but also pragmatic enough to find solutions that work in real life.

• You follow through — because you know that quality improvements only matter when they are actually implemented and sustained.

• You have knowledge of ISO 14001 or an interest in building a basic understanding of environmental management systems.

If you are driven by quality, manufacturing and continuous improvement, and if you enjoy turning problems into clear actions and better ways of working, we would like to hear from you. You do not need to tick every box; what matters most is your quality mindset, your curiosity and your ability to follow through.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

We will review candidates continuously, so please send your application as soon as possible. If you have any questions about the role, please contact Johnny Rasmussen at johnny.rasmussen@norican.com.

About Norican

NORICAN. Metal. Made. Possible.

We are Norican, a global industrial group designing, building and supporting bestinclass machines and technologies for metal formation and surface treatment.

Bringing together five leading brands - DISA, Simpson, StrikoWestofen, Wheelabrator and Monitizer – we deliver one connected solution across the production process, supported by fullservice expertise and digital solutions.

Across green sand molding, die casting, sand preparation, melting, transport and dosing, and surface treatment, we help manufacturers improve performance and transform production across a wide range of industries. We build lifetime quality and longterm partnerships by combining the strengths of our legacy brands to lead the industry through innovation, sustainability and profitable growth.

DISA:

DISA design, build and support premium green sand moulding and cashing machines for the ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industries. For 125 years they have delivered machines that last for decades, and they are highly respected by customers and peers for excellent levels of quality and service. DISA machines keep customers producing relentlessly to the very highest standards. And they empower foundry productivity with a lifetime of efficient and a lower cost per casting.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

Application and Contact:

If you wish to know more about the position, please reach out to Dr. Kasra Nowrouzi, CTO at QuNorth, at kasra@qunorth.com

Please be aware that we will be reviewing applications on an ongoing basis.

All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

We look very much forward to receiving your application.

Job Description:

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with wind turbine drivetrains or comparable large rotating machinery is preferred. Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. We also welcome specialists who want to broaden their understanding of the complete drivetrain.

What can you look forward to?

You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

About Goldwind

Goldwind Energy ApS (also called Goldwind Denmark) is a R&D focused subsidiary of GOLDWIND SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. (Goldwind), a world leading wind turbine technology and energy solutions provider headquartered in Beijing, China.

Through the implementation and investment in industry-leading turbine technology, water treatment solutions and other green energy technological ventures, Goldwind has been hailed as one of China’s most innovative companies.

Interested?

Nordic Talent Collab is managing the recruitment for Goldwind Denmark. Please submit your CV and a short application as soon as possible. Interviews are held on an ongoing basis.

If you have any questions about the role, please contact:

Kristian Kantsø

Nordic Talent Collab

T: +45 2834 1509

M: kristian@nordictalentcollab.dk

Do you want to help build one coherent way for a global technology organization to deliver, bringing scaled product-centric ways of working project and program execution _together into a single system, rather than running them as separate worlds? Are you as comfortable helping shape that system and turning it into ways of working people actually use in the room with the people who'll actually use it?_We are hiring a Manager, Delivery Enablement to help shape and evolve how Pandora's D&T organization delivers. D&T spans the full range of technology that keeps Pandora running: from customer-facing platforms to manufacturing systems, ERP, logistics and operations, security, covering build, run, and operate across all of it. This role does not carry people-management responsibility. Your impact comes through the quality of what you build and how well it lands across the organization.

You'll join Delivery Enablement, a team combining operating-model design and implementation, coaching, and delivery tooling capability. It's built to make Digital & Technology (D&T) faster, clearer, and more coherent at scale. Delivery Enablement sits within Delivery Excellence, alongside the Scrum Masters, Delivery Leads, and Project and Program Managers. You will work with the wider team to shape ideas and turn them into practical ways of working across D&T.

**Your Role

**You will help harmonize and evolve how scaled agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery work together, building on what already exists across D&T rather than replacing it, closing gaps only where they cause real friction. This is as much about leading change as it is about designing structure. You will also advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape, and help teams and entities build the capability to adopt the model as it evolves.

You will work closely with the wider delivery community, as well as product, engineering, and leadership more broadly, to facilitate structural workshops, build the case for change, and make sure what gets designed is something people actually want to use, not just a document on a shelf. A key part of the role is building the relationships, networks and momentum needed to bring ideas to life across D&T.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Co-design and evolve how scaled agile and structured, plan-driven delivery work together, harmonizing and building on existing practice rather than replacing it

• Advise on structuring new or reshaping delivery entities (product lines, programs, organizational changes, or other setups) as they take shape

• Lead workstreams that take new or improved delivery processes (for example dependency management or capacity planning) from idea through pilot, rollout, adoption and continuous improvement

• Support onboarding and capability-building for teams and entities adopting the model, working alongside the team's wider coaching capability

• Facilitate structural workshops and working sessions with the wider delivery community to shape and pressure-test the model

• Build relationships, networks and communities that help change spread and stick across D&T

• Pilot approaches, learn from feedback, and scale what works

• Help translate high-level decisions about how delivery is prioritized, funded, resourced, and executed into practical structures and standards teams can use

• Help projects and programs connect into the wider D&T Operating Model, including common governance, planning, dependency management and delivery tooling

• Contribute to keeping the model coherent as it evolves, spotting where new structures overlap or conflict with what already exists

• Provide point-in-time advisory support where operating-model gaps are most costly

• Document how the operating model works and how it evolves over time

• Build strong relationships across the wider delivery community and leadership to ensure what gets built is genuinely adopted

**What Is Needed To Succeed

**

• ignificant experience in delivery transformation, operating-model implementation, PMO, program/project delivery or organizational change within a large, complex technology organization

• Demonstrated experience working across both scaled/product-centric agile delivery and more structured, plan-driven delivery, with enough understanding to contribute credibly to how they work together

• Track record of taking new ways of working from idea through implementation, adoption and continuous improvement

• Ideally a mix of hands-on delivery experience and consulting or advisory experience, but real, first-hand delivery experience matters more than advisory polish alone

• Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, and narrative-building skills across senior and operational levels

• Comfortable leading through organizational change: helping people, not just structures, adapt as delivery models shift

• Able to build trust, networks and momentum without relying on formal authority

• Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate your own analysis, design, and documentation work

• Working understanding of how delivery tooling (e.g. Jira/Confluence, or equivalent) underpins an operating model, enough to design frameworks that translate into practice, not to configure the tooling yourself

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: building on foundations already in motion, while still shaping significant parts of the model from scratch

• Systems thinking: able to see cross-domain and cross-entity dependencies, not just local fixes

• Pragmatic bias toward incremental, adoptable change over comprehensive upfront design

• Relevant certifications (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2, SAFe) are an advantage

**Did we get your attention?

**We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

**Icing on the cake

**You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Test Method Specialist, Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory
jobs.description:
**_Imagine if robust test methods and reliable test equipment helped ensure the quality of both new and existing Coloplast products. That is where you come in.

**_As our new Test Method Specialist, you will become the technical focal point for selected test methods and related equipment in Coloplast Mørdrup, primarily supporting the QA Lifecycle Laboratory and Pilot SVS. This is a practical, hands-on specialist role in which you will work directly with laboratory equipment, including troubleshooting, service and calibration follow-up, qualification, and software and computer upgrades. You will support the full test method and equipment lifecycle, from implementation and qualification to maintenance, transfer and continuous improvement.

If you are motivated by hands-on technical problem-solving, equipment responsibility, quality assurance and data evaluation, this role offers meaningful responsibility and broad organisational impact. You will also work closely with many internal and external stakeholders, making clear communication, coordination and strong stakeholder management an important part of your success.

_“In this role, your technical judgement and ability to create robust solutions will help ensure reliable test results and compliant laboratory processes throughout the product lifecycle,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

_**Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

**At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of laboratory technicians and test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations and test method activities.

You will be part of an engaged team with a strong mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, Operations, Global Test Method teams and international manufacturing sites. We value curiosity, knowledge sharing, flexibility and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Own and develop test methods and equipment

**As Test Method Specialist, you will act as a one-point contact and technical superuser for selected test methods and test equipment. A significant part of the role is practical equipment responsibility. You will work hands-on with equipment and coordinate activities to ensure it is qualified, calibrated, serviced, maintained and performing as intended. You will also support software and computer upgrades connected to the equipment, as well as reliable data handling and traceability.

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Acting as technical owner and one-point contact for selected test methods and related test equipment

• Planning, coordinating and performing qualification of test equipment, including relocation, capacity expansion and replacement of critical parts

• Preparing and maintaining qualification protocols, reports, procedures, test method documentation and one-point lessons when needed

• Performing hands-on troubleshooting of test equipment and methods, evaluating test results and leading root cause investigations when failures occur

• Taking practical responsibility for test equipment, including service activities, calibration follow-up, preventive maintenance and ensuring that equipment performs as intended

• Handling changes, nonconformities and CAPAs related to test methods, calibration and test equipment

• Supporting compliant storage and traceability of raw data before product release

• Planning and participating in transfers of test methods and equipment to international manufacturing sites

• Providing technical support and sparring to colleagues in the Pilot Plant, Global Operations and international manufacturing sites

• Collaborating with Global Test Method teams and contributing technical input to the development and improvement of test methods

• Training specialists, laboratory technicians, operators and other users in test methods, test principles and use of equipment

• Coordinating software and computer upgrades for test equipment, assessing their impact on qualification and documentation, and managing suppliers, service visits and relevant service agreements

• Participating in internal and external audits related to test methods, equipment and documentation

• Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, systems and ways of working

**Bring strong technical judgement and a quality mindset

**To succeed in this position, you combine technical depth with a structured, practical and hands-on approach. You enjoy working directly with equipment, take ownership and work systematically when resolving technical issues. You are comfortable making decisions based on data, risk and regulatory requirements.

The role involves close collaboration with many internal and external stakeholders, therefor you communicate clearly, coordinate effectively and are able to build strong working relationships across functions, sites and suppliers.

We imagine that you bring:

• A master’s degree within science, engineering, mechanics, physics, chemistry, pharmacy or a comparable technical field, or have at least five years of relevant experience with test methods

• Solid hands-on experience with test methods, measurement principles and qualification of laboratory or production test equipment

• Strong problem-solving skills and experience with structured root cause analysis

• Confident evaluating, analysing and presenting technical data skills, including the use of statistical methods

• Ability to write, review and understand technical documentation, protocols and reports

• Knowledge of quality systems and regulated environments; knowledge of ISO 9001, ISO 13485 and GMP is an advantage

• An understanding of validation, calibration, design control, specifications and process risk management

• Abitlity to plan and prioritise your work effectively and follow activities through to completion

• Strong stakeholder management skills and collaborate effectively across disciplines, functions, geographical locations and external suppliers

• Communicating skills professionally in English, both written and spoken; Danish is an advantage

• A comfortable competence using digital tools for documentation, data analysis and traceability; experience with Microsoft Office, Veeva, JMP or similar systems is an advantage

**A specialist role with broad impact

**This is a permanent specialist position in the QA Lifecycle Laboratory. The role has no direct reports and includes collaboration with international colleagues and manufacturing sites. Some travel may be expected in connection with transfers, supplier activities and site support.

You will join a working environment where quality, safety, technical excellence, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement are central to our daily work. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network and influence how test methods and equipment are managed across the product lifecycle.

**Interested?

**If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory, at dklst@coloplast.com.

We invite candidates for interviews continuously, so we encourage you to submit your CV with a description of your motivation for applying, as soon as possible.

_Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

__Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$158,720.00---$238,080.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

jobs.description:

jobs.occupation: Expert, Business Area Manager Ecotoxicology and Environment
jobs.description:
Could your expertise in ecotoxicology help shape better environmental decisions—and unlock new opportunities for science-led advisory services?

At DHI, you’ll connect ecotoxicology, environmental science and water modelling to help clients tackle complex challenges in aquatic environments. Join our international Environment & Toxicology team to broaden your impact while helping grow our environmental advisory business.

Responsibilities and Challenges

We are looking for a senior colleague with expertise in ecotoxicology and environmental science with insights and interests in developing our advisory solutions and business.

As a member of DHI’s international Environment & Toxicology team, you will help clients address complex challenges related to chemicals, ecotoxicology and the aquatic environment. You will work closely with clients and colleagues across disciplines to develop practical, science-based solutions that protect human health and the environment.

The main responsibilities are to:

• Deliver expert advisory within the area of regulatory and scientific aspects of eco-toxicology, environmental exposure- and risk assessment, management of chemicals and/or environmental hazardous substances in water environments, and other client projects.

• Lead business development within advisory area of environment and eco-toxicology, enabling and bringing to life the strategy to build on the markets for advisory on environmental exposure- and risk assessment, management of chemicals and/or environmental hazardous substances (incl. micropollutants) in water environments.

• Plan and execute of internal and external activities of knowledge distribution (i.e. network meetings, conferences or courses) as well as business development activities.

• Serve as project manager in own projects, as well as deliver as project participant in projects within the portfolio.

• Perform quality assurance and mentor young colleagues, ensuring high scientific level of solutions.

• Establish and maintain good practices for international collaboration in E&T.

What We're Looking For

Required education, experience and capabilities

• A relevant university degree in ecotoxicology, environmental chemistry, environmental science, biology, chemistry, chemical engineering, water or environmental engineering, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or other advanced qualification is an advantage.

• At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in ecotoxicology, environmental chemistry, environmental risk assessment, chemicals in the environment or a closely related advisory field.

• A strong professional track record gained in consultancy, industry, public authority, research organization, or a comparable environment.

• Demonstrated experience assessing chemicals or environmentally hazardous substances in aquatic or water-related environments.

• Experience leading technically complex projects, including responsibility for scope, quality, budget, schedule and stakeholder management.

• A proven ability to originate or develop business, build client relationships and contribute to successful proposals or tenders.

• A good understanding of relevant environmental regulation, market developments and the needs of industry and public-sector clients.

• Experience working in an international or multidisciplinary setting.

• Proficient in English (professional level)

Additional experience and strengths, which will contribute to success in this role:

• Experience with establishing environmental quality standards and predicted no-effect concentrations, and/or assessing chemicals in wastewater or other water environments

• Knowledge of the EU Water Framework Directive, Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive, Drinking Water Directive or related national requirements.

• Experience with environmental fate, transport or exposure modelling

• Collaboration with authorities, utilities, industrial clients, industry associations, research programmes or international consortia.

• Experience developing services or markets across Denmark and the wider European region.

• Serving as the technical lead and/or mentor for colleagues in a team.

Skills and competences

The successful candidate combines scientific credibility with commercial awareness and a genuine interest in understanding client needs. We are looking for a person who can translate complex scientific and regulatory matters into clear advice and practical solutions.

You are:

• Scientifically strong, with the ability to provide authoritative advice within your field.

• Client-oriented and commercially aware, with the confidence to initiate conversations, develop opportunities and build lasting professional relationships.

• An effective project leader, able to maintain direction and quality across technically complex assignments.

• A clear communicator, capable of engaging scientific experts, decision-makers, authorities and other stakeholders.

• Collaborative and internationally oriented, with an interest in working across disciplines, markets and organisational boundaries.

• Proactive and accountable, taking ownership and exercising sound professional judgement.

• Generous with your expertise, contributing to knowledge sharing, mentoring and the professional development of colleagues.

Why join DHI?

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that is the global leader in solving the world’s toughest challenges in water, environment and sustainability.

In this position we offer to you the opportunity to join a strong company with dedicated colleagues to:

• Shape and grow DHI’s ecotoxicology and environmental advisory business.

• Work at the intersection of chemicals, water environments, environmental regulation and data-driven decision-making.

• Collaborate with ecotoxicologists, environmental scientists, toxicologists, water specialists and modellers across an international organisation.

• Lead meaningful assignments for industry, authorities, utilities and partners.

• Take on a visible expert role with opportunities to influence strategy, develop clients, lead projects and mentor colleagues.

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminate our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

Location & Mobility

• The role location is at DHI office, Hørsholm, Denmark

Travelling must be expected in the role to enable collaboration with clients and/or inside DHI. Travelling rules as included in employment contract

How to apply

• Please submit your application including CV via the relevant job posting on DHI’s website: http://www.dhigroup.com/careers

• Deadline for application is 26th November 2026.

• For further information please contact Yong Quan Lim, Talent Acquisition Specialist by by email liyq@dhigroup.com / Lise Lyck, Senior manager, Environment & Toxicology by email lly@dhigroup.com.

_Are you motivated by becoming the technical expert behind products and solutions that support clean water and energy? Do you thrive in a role where you connect technical development, business needs, and customer requirements? Are you excited by the opportunity to influence products throughout their entire lifecycle while collaborating with stakeholders across the organization?

**Here Is What The Job Entails

**In the role as our next Technical Product Specialist within our software applications, your job will be to provide technical expertise across the product lifecycle while ensuring that products, solutions, and technical documentation remain accurate, compliant, and competitive.

More specifically you will be:

• Acting as the technical liaison between Research and Development, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders

• Providing technical support including tender support, sales support, product training, and advanced troubleshooting

• Serving as the technical expert on products, configurations, software solutions, and applications

• Maintaining technical product information and documentation

• Supporting product lifecycle activities including new product development, maintenance, and phase in and phase out activities

You will experience the freedom to act and leave your mark on how we manage and support our products throughout their lifecycle. Therefore, you will work closely with technical and commercial stakeholders across the organization, gain deep insight into our products and technologies, and play a key role in ensuring knowledge sharing, product adoption, and continuous improvement.

**Meet your future team

**With direct reference to Senior Manager, Technical Product Management, you will become part of the technical product management team. As a team, we are committed to ensuring our products remain technically accurate, competitive, and capable of meeting both market and business requirements, and you will have a key role in achieving this. In the team you will experience close collaboration with colleagues across product management, development, customer service, sales, and supply chain. Together we support products throughout their lifecycle while ensuring strong stakeholder engagement and knowledge sharing across the organization.

Did you know? As a Technical Product Specialist, you will work with stakeholders from many different functions, making every day an opportunity to learn something new about our products, technologies, and customers.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for a Technical Product Specialist who is ready to take ownership of technical product activities and who is motivated by solving complex challenges. You achieve this through strong collaboration skills, technical curiosity, and a structured approach to your work.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Hold a degree in Engineering within Electronics, Software, Mechatronics, or a similar field.

• Have an understanding of product development, product lifecycle management, and technical product support

• Have experience with, or an understanding of, software-related systems such as Swagger documentation, Jira, Confluence or comparable platforms. A general end-to-end understanding of hardware and connectivity along with insights to APIsis an advantage.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills combined with the ability to communicate technical information clearly

• Have experience with product related systems such as Configure Price Quote, Product Lifecycle Management, Enterprise Resource Planning, or similar platforms.

We also value experience developing and delivering technical training and knowledge sharing activities

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

**We are more than the ordinary workplace

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization you are bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, cycle team, during our yearly summer festival or on the padel court. For example, is our Head of System Engineering and Information Technology Denmark also our volunteer padel instructor while our Software Test Engineer runs weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

• Beneficial health care and insurance package

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

**Please submit your application by using the link below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.

The job will be located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Senior Manager, Technical Product Management, Kirsten Sahl, by phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

**Get to know us

**At Kamstrup, you'll become part of a close-knit community that genuinely cares about one another, fostering connections both in and out of the workplace. Our team comprises innovators, dreamers, and doers, united by an unyielding passion to challenge the status quo, find better solutions, and constantly push the boundaries of what's possible all with the purpose of securing clean water and energy to the maximum number of people. With an unwavering commitment to growth, we offer opportunities for you to leverage your skills and drive our business to new heights, empowering you to leave your mark on our future and grow with us. Explore more on our website, see our annual report, and stay updated through LinkedIn for the latest news and job openings.

Architect, build, and scale AI systems that hold up in production

Take ownership of how AI is architected, built, and scaled across our products. You will design the agentic systems at the core of our pension and advisory platforms, with a focus on reliable and responsible AI.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help lead our newly established AI team, working on our Life product for pension companies. The team is focused on the practical and responsible use of AI and is still in its early stages, so as a senior member you will play a defining role in setting the technical foundation, design patterns, and ways of working that the rest of the team builds on.

You will work closely with the AI Team Lead and Chief Architect, who own the overall architecture, helping shape the design within that direction. You will also be part of an agile team with a flat structure, where collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning are central to the culture.

This role is primarily about designing and building agentic and LLM systems end to end, with a meaningful share of your time spent owning how we evaluate them and prove they hold up. It suits someone with 5+ years of relevant experience who wants to move beyond implementation into designing AI systems, and who enjoys raising the bar for the engineers around them.

Why this matters

This is core infrastructure, not edge tooling. Our Life product runs policy and capital administration for some of Europe’s largest pension providers, including PensionDanmark and APG, and is on track to support more than 8 million members and over €800bn in retirement assets.

The AI you design must meet that bar: fast and innovative, but also accurate, secure, and reliable enough for systems that people depend on for their financial security in retirement. Building it well and being able to prove it works, are two sides of the same job.

What you’ll do

As a senior member of the AI team, you will help shape how we build with Large Language Models and agentic systems across our products, contributing to high‑level design decisions, turning ambiguous business problems into robust system designs, and ensuring high‑quality coding standards and design. You will be hands‑on, with a real say in the architecture, standards, and technical judgement that guide the team.

In practice, you will:

Help shape the technical direction

• Contribute to the AI tech stack across our products: help define the high‑level system design, reference architectures, and design patterns the team builds on.

• Help shape AI strategy: identify where AI can create genuine value, frame the trade‑offs, and feed into a coherent, prioritised technical roadmap that fits our wider platform.

• Inform major architectural decisions: model and framework selection, build‑versus‑buy, and how AI components fit into our existing Java platform, integrate with surrounding systems, scale, and stay maintainable over time.

• Reason about trade‑offs in the open: weigh latency, cost, accuracy, security, and reliability, and explain and defend those choices to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Architect and build (hands‑on)

• Design LLM systems end to end: from retrieval, agent orchestration, and data pipelines through to deployment and monitoring.

• Design and build agentic systems: single‑ and multi‑agent, covering orchestration, tool use, action groups, knowledge‑base integrations, and patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation, and result aggregation for complex, reliable production workflows.

• Engineer RAG pipelines that connect agents to internal structured and unstructured data.

• Drive quality through design: prompt strategy, system prompts, and memory systems that produce hallucination‑resistant outputs with strong relevance and faithfulness.

• Make cost‑aware architectural choices: balancing latency, cost, and quality across model selection and orchestration patterns so what we ship is sustainable at scale.

• Set the standards for prompt strategy, RAG, orchestration, and cost management that the wider team adopts.

Evaluate and prove

• Build evaluation frameworks: eval sets, golden datasets, and LLM‑as‑judge pipelines, with offline regression suites wired into CI and online evaluation on production traces.

• Evaluate the whole agent, not just the answer: task success, trajectory and tool‑use correctness, and RAG faithfulness and grounding, so you know whether failures come from retrieval, reasoning, or generation.

• Measure what gates shipping: relevance, faithfulness, latency, cost, and reliability across repeated runs, turned into quality gates the team ships against.

Collaborate and grow the team

• Collaborate and mentor: work with the AI Team Lead, Chief Architect, senior developers, and product teams to translate business needs into working, well‑tested solutions, and support more junior engineers as the team grows.

What we’re looking for

You bring a strong technical foundation, hands‑on depth with modern AI tooling, and the judgement to design systems that hold up in the real world. You don’t need deep expertise in every area below, but we do expect real depth in agentic systems and AI architecture, backed by a solid grasp of how to evaluate what you build.

Required

• A master’s degree in computer science or a similar field, preferably with an AI focus.

• 5+ years building software, with significant hands‑on work applying Large Language Models.

• Strong proficiency in a statically typed, object‑oriented language, Java or C# (we build in Java). Python is welcome for demos, evaluation tooling, and experiments, but it is not our production language.

• Deep experience designing, building, and operating agent‑based systems, with hands‑on use of one or more orchestration frameworks (e.g. LangChain/LangGraph, Microsoft Agents, Claude Agent SDK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel).

• A track record of designing and building AI systems, including how the components fit together, scale, and are maintained over time.

• Solid, practical experience with prompt strategy, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and the cost considerations of LLM usage and model selection.

• Working knowledge of LLM and agent evaluation: eval sets, LLM‑as‑judge, and the metrics that distinguish a good system from a confident‑but‑wrong one (faithfulness, relevance, task success, latency, and cost).

• Experience designing AI or backend systems that fit into a larger production platform, collaborating with senior engineers and architects to align on a shared technical direction.

• Strong communication skills to explain and defend architectural trade‑offs to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Experience building automated evaluation pipelines or CI gates for AI systems.

• Familiarity with observability and tracing tooling for LLM applications (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Braintrust).

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation, automation, and red teaming.

• Broader machine learning experience.

• Hands‑on experience building and integrating MCP servers.

• Experience working in regulated or high‑reliability domains such as finance, insurance, or healthcare.

Who you are

You are a confident, hands‑on engineer who takes ownership of complex and sometimes undefined problems, and who is just as comfortable designing a system as proving it holds up. You think in systems, balance pragmatism with quality, and care about building things that work in production rather than just in a demo. You lift the people around you, stay open to feedback, and bring strong technical judgement of your own. You are curious, persistent, and result‑oriented.

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join us as a DevOps & Platform Engineer, where you will play a pivotal role in building, operating, and continuously enhancing the platforms and services that drive product development, testing, validation, deployment, and operations within Siemens Gamesa’s digital ecosystem. Whether you are modernizing platform services or contributing to cloud-enabled solutions, your efforts will significantly accelerate how engineering teams deliver innovative solutions. Become part of an international team that values ownership, innovation, and knowledge sharing in a culture driven by a strong engineering mindset.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Develop automation solutions that enhance reliability, scalability, security, and operational efficiency.

• Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code, automated deployments, CI/CD pipelines, and platform tooling.

What You Bring

Must Have

• Experience in Platform Engineering, DevOps, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Software Engineering, or Infrastructure Automation.

• Strong experience with automation technologies such as Ansible, PowerShell, PowerCLI, Python, Git, Infrastructure as Code, and CI/CD tooling.

• Proven ability to create and maintain automation frameworks, deployment pipelines, APIs, integrations, or platform services.

• Familiarity with virtualization and platform technologies like VMware vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, ESXi, Proxmox VE, or similar enterprise platforms.

• Knowledge of Linux and/or Windows administration, scripting, troubleshooting, and system integration.

• Experience with monitoring, observability, logging, incident management, performance analysis, and service reliability practices.

Nice to Have

• Experience in Agile environments using Scrum or SAFe methodologies, along with tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Git-based workflows.

• Familiarity with platform modernization, self-service platforms, developer experience initiatives, or Infrastructure as Code practices.

• Experience supporting engineering applications, industrial systems, SCADA environments, or operational technology solutions.

About the Team

You will join the Infrastructure Performance & Operations (IPO) team within Digital Products & Solutions. This team is dedicated to developing, operating, and evolving the digital platforms that support product engineering, validation, testing, and business operations across Siemens Gamesa. jobs.occupation: PhD stipend in thermal modeling and advanced solutions for high-power modules and magnetic components
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a PhD stipend is available within the general study programme in Electrical and Electronic Engineering. The stipend is open for appointment from 1 December 2026 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years and the position is full-time.

Your work tasks
The position is offered in relation to the GreenMag project, and you will be positioned in the Section of Power Electronics Systems and Materials within the research programme Sustainable Power Electronics and Electrification (SPELL) at AAU Energy, Aalborg University. You will be based at the Aalborg campus in a highly international research environment with close collaboration with academic and industrial partners in the field of power electronics and energy systems.

The increasing electrification of transport, industry and renewable energy systems is driving the development of high-power-density power converters operating at megawatt levels. Advanced planar magnetic components are emerging as a key technology for achieving higher power density, manufacturability and integration in such converters. However, thermal management remains one of the major challenges that limit the performance, reliability and scalability of planar magnetic solutions, especially at high power and high frequency.

In this PhD project, you will work on the development of innovative thermal management technologies for megawatt planar magnetics used in future electrification systems. Your research will combine advanced modelling, experimental validation and prototype development to improve heat dissipation and thermal reliability while maintaining the required electrical and magnetic performance. You will analyse thermal behaviour and heat transfer mechanisms in high-power planar magnetic components, design and evaluate cooling concepts and contribute to the integration of these solutions in realistic converter systems.

You will conduct cutting-edge research on thermal behaviour and heat transfer mechanisms in megawatt-class planar magnetic components and use this knowledge to propose and evaluate new design strategies. You will develop multiphysics simulation models using finite element modelling tools to investigate the thermal performance of planar magnetics and to study alternative cooling concepts and material choices. You will design, manufacture and experimentally validate novel thermal management solutions for planar magnetic structures, and you will explore advanced materials and cooling technologies that can be applied in megawatt-class magnetic components. As part of the GreenMag project, you will collaborate with academic and industrial partners, disseminate your research results through publications in international journals and conferences, and contribute to teaching and supervision activities within the department as part of the PhD education programme.

Your competencies 
You have a relevant educational background within Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, Energy Engineering or a closely related field, and you hold a Master’s degree that qualifies you for enrolment in the PhD programme. You are motivated to work at the interface between thermal science, electromagnetics and power electronics, and you are interested in both theoretical and experimental research.

You bring strong analytical skills and a structured approach to modelling and problem solving, and you are comfortable working with numerical tools for thermal and multiphysics analysis. Experience with thermal analysis, power electronics or magnetic component design will be considered an advantage, as will experience with finite element analysis tools such as COMSOL Multiphysics or ANSYS. It is beneficial if you have worked with experimental testing, prototype development or laboratory work in previous projects and if you are prepared to work with both simulation and hands-on experiments in this PhD.

As a person, you are curious and creative, and you are motivated by addressing challenging research questions in collaboration with others. You are able to work independently, take responsibility for your project and contribute actively to collaborative research activities across groups and institutions. Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, are required, as you will present your results in scientific publications, at international conferences and in meetings with project partners.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are    
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges. Aalborg University is recognised internationally for excellence in power electronics and energy systems research, and AAU has been ranked among the leading universities in Europe within energy research. At AAU Energy, you will be part of a highly international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges associated with electrification and the green transition.

The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs approximately 300 staff members from a broad range of nationalities and disciplinary backgrounds, creating a vibrant international research environment with extensive opportunities for collaboration and professional growth. The department offers world-class laboratory and workshop facilities, and maintains close collaboration with industrial partners. As a PhD student, you will have access to advanced facilities for the design, manufacturing and testing of high-power magnetic components and power electronic systems, and you will be part of an active research community in Sustainable Power Electronics and Electrification.

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Responsibilities and technologies

The team takes a pragmatic and technically grounded approach to governance, risk and compliance, and works closely with the Application Security team, the Operations organisation, Internal IT and other business functions across the group.

The GRC team is a small team of colleagues with complementary profiles. We do not expect any one candidate to cover every area described below. Instead, we are looking for broad profiles with solid experience across several of these areas and the motivation to develop within the rest.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

• Developing, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuityDeveloping, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuity

Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen is seeking top early-career researchers for a number of attractive one- to three-year postdoctoral positions.

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences has strong research groups in many areas of applied mathematics, and has an active postdoc and visitors' program. Applicants in all areas of mathematics covered by the research groups of the department will be considered.

  There will be postdoc stipends in the following specific areas:

   	
• Insurance mathematics, optimization and operations research, mathematical finance, econometrics and financial economics, and applied probability theory, covered by the Section for Insurance and Economics. 	
• Probability theory, mathematical statistics and applied statistics, covered by the Section for Statistics and Probability Theory.   In particular, the following specific positions are open:

   	
• Variational analysis in the Wasserstein space of stochastic processes (contact Johannes Wiesel wiesel@math.ku.dk) 	
• Causal modelling and related questions in reliable machine learning (contact Sebastian Weichwald, https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us). Applicants are encouraged to describe a concrete research direction, what they bring to it, and why it fits the group’s work. 	
• Causal Inference and Interpretability in Complex Models (contact Nikolaj Thams, thams@math.ku.dk ) 	
• Optimization under decision-dependent uncertainty (contact Giovanni Pantuso, gp@math.ku.dk)    

  The postdoc’s duties will include research within mathematics as well as teaching. The teaching load is typically two half-semester courses per year, of which one usually is as a teaching assistant. The post may also include performance of other project-specific duties.

  The positions are open with starting date in 2027, ordinarily September 1st or as soon as possible thereafter. The salary is very competitive and researchers from outside Denmark may qualify for a reduced tax rate (see terms below).

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://www.math.ku.dk/ . Inquiries about the position can be made to the Head of Department Mogens Steffensen, mogens@math.ku.dk.

   

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae: 1-3 pages, including list of publications. 	
• Cover letter: Substantiate your qualification for the postdoc position and your motivations. 	
• Diplomas: Master and PhD degree or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date. 	
• Research plan: Description of current and future research plans (1-3 pages). 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers (not mandatory)    

  The deadline for applications is 15th of November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. We expect to send invitations for interviews in December 2026 or January 2027. The interviews will typically take place in January and February of 2026, and our search is expected to be concluded around April 2027.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.
