This is a hands-on internship where you will work closely with our management and project team to identify funding opportunities, develop fundraising strategies, create new project ideas, and prepare grant applications.

You will help turn ideas into real projects by researching funding programmes, developing project concepts, planning activities, preparing budgets, and writing applications for funding.

Our main focus is on Erasmus+ projects, Danish foundations, municipal funding opportunities, and international programmes supporting youth work, education, inclusion, community development, sustainability, and international cooperation.

Responsibilities:

• 
Fundraising Strategy: Research and develop fundraising strategies for PYN, identify potential funding sources, analyse funding requirements, and help create a long-term fundraising plan for the organisation.

• 
Funding Research: Identify relevant grants and funding opportunities from Erasmus+, Danish foundations, municipalities, EU programmes, and international funding organisations. Monitor application deadlines, eligibility requirements, funding priorities, and available budgets.

• 
Project Development: Help develop new local and international project ideas based on PYN’s mission, community needs, and funding opportunities. Contribute to defining project objectives, target groups, activities, expected results, and long-term impact.

• 
Grant Writing: Prepare and write funding applications, including project descriptions, needs analysis, objectives, activities, methodology, expected outcomes, sustainability plans, and dissemination strategies.

• 
Project Budgets: Support the preparation of project budgets, financial plans, funding requests, and cost estimates in cooperation with the management and accounting team.

• 
Partnership Development: Research potential local and international project partners, foundations, sponsors, and organisations. Support communication with stakeholders and help develop partnerships for future funding applications.

• 
Project Planning: Help create project timelines, work plans, activity schedules, responsibilities, and implementation strategies for proposed projects.

• 
Funding Database: Maintain an organised overview of funding opportunities, application deadlines, eligibility criteria, application progress, submitted proposals, and funding results.

• 
Organisational Development: Contribute ideas for improving PYN’s financial sustainability, expanding its activities, and developing new services or initiatives that could attract additional funding.

Skills & Qualifications:

We are looking for someone who is interested in fundraising, project management, international cooperation, and NGO development. And has:

• 
Good written English (preferably B2 or higher)

• 
Strong research and analytical skills

• 
Good organisational skills

• 
Attention to details

• 
Creativity

• 
The ability to work independently

You should feel comfortable using Google Docs, Google Sheets, or similar digital tools and be interested in developing and writing structured project proposals.

Nice to have:

Previous experience with Erasmus+, grant writing, fundraising, project management, budgeting, research, or NGO work. Familiarity with EU funding programmes, Danish foundations, or project application processes is an advantage but not required.

Personal qualities:

We appreciate people who are proactive, curious, responsible, detail-oriented, and motivated to learn. You should enjoy developing ideas, researching opportunities, solving problems, and turning concepts into practical project proposals.

Relevant study backgrounds:

Project Management, International Relations, Business Administration, Economics, Public Administration, Political Science, Social Sciences, European Studies, Nonprofit Management, or related fields. Students from other backgrounds are also welcome to apply.

Working Style & Environment:

Our office and youth space are located in Student Village Kamtjatka, in the city centre of Horsens, Denmark.

A hybrid working setup is possible, but we prefer interns who can be present on-site for teamwork, project development meetings, and organisational activities.

Typical office hours are around 9:00:00–16:30, Monday–Friday, with the remaining working hours arranged according to the internship agreement and team needs.

You will join a small, international team working across project management, fundraising, marketing, community events, accounting, web development, and youth work.

You will work closely with PYN’s management and receive guidance on project development, funding research, and grant writing. At the same time, you will have opportunities to take responsibility for your own research, project concepts, and application drafts.

What You Gain:

• 
Practical Fundraising Experience: Learn how NGOs identify funding opportunities, approach funders, develop fundraising strategies, and prepare grant applications.

• 
Real Project Development Experience: Participate in developing actual local and international projects, from the initial idea to a complete funding application.

• 
Erasmus+ Knowledge: Gain practical insight into European funding programmes, international partnerships, project planning, grant writing, and the management of EU-funded initiatives.

• 
Professional Development: Improve your research, analytical thinking, project design, budgeting, strategic planning, professional writing, and stakeholder communication skills.

• 
International Working Environment: Become part of a supportive international community and collaborate with young people, interns, volunteers, and partners from different countries.

• 
Networking Opportunities: Build connections with NGOs, foundations, international organisations, local stakeholders, and potential project partners.

• 
Erasmus+ Mobility Opportunities: Depending on your availability, eligibility, and participant profile, you may have opportunities to join Erasmus+ youth exchanges and training courses (typically 5–10 days), where travel, food, and accommodation are covered by EU funds.

• 
Meaningful Impact: Contribute to securing resources that help PYN organise free community activities, international learning opportunities, youth projects, and initiatives that benefit young people.

Note:

This is an unpaid internship. Pangaea Youth Network does not provide monetary compensation or financial support.

We offer practical professional experience, supervision, an international working environment, networking opportunities, access to relevant Erasmus+ activities, and opportunities to contribute to real projects with a positive social impact.

jobs.employer_name: KU- SCIENCE - CHEM og MATH og NBI-HCØ
jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

   

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen is seeking top early-career researchers for a number of attractive one- to three-year postdoctoral positions.

  The salary is very competitive and researchers from outside Denmark may qualify for a reduced tax rate (see terms below).

  The Department of Mathematical Sciences has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics, and has an active postdoc and visitors' program. Applicants in all areas of mathematics covered by the research groups of the department will be considered. In particular, there will be postdoc stipends in the following specific areas/centers of the department:

   	
• Algebraic and arithmetic geometry, applied algebra, geometric group theory, combinatorics, geometry and geometric analysis, Lie theory, representation theory, number theory, and topology, as covered by the Section for Algebra & Geometry and the Copenhagen Centre for Geometry & Topology (GeoTop). 	
• Functional analysis, operator algebras, geometric group theory, descriptive set theory, harmonic and classical analysis, history of mathematics, mathematical physics, partial differential equations, quantum information and quantum computing, as covered by the section Analysis and Quantum, the Center for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory (QMATH), and the Quantum for Life Center.   Further information about the Department of Mathematical Sciences is linked here.
 Inquiries about the position should be made to postdocapply@math.ku.dk. You are also welcome to directly contact any faculty member closest to your research area.

  The postdoc’s duties will include research within mathematics as well as teaching.
 The teaching load is typically two quarter (half-semester) courses per year, of which one usually is as a teaching assistant. The post may also include performance of other duties.
 
 The position is open with starting date in 2027, ordinarily September 1st or October 1st.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
  

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Negotiation for salary supplement is possible. Potential applicants from outside of Denmark can find information about life in Denmark - including taxation, healthcare, etc. – at https://ism.ku.dk/salary-tax-pension

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Curriculum vitae, including list of publications. 	
• Cover Letter: Substantiate your qualification for the postdoc position and your motivations. 	
• Diplomas: Master and/or PhD degree, or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date. 	
• Research plan: Description of current and future research plans. 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers (not mandatory)   The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1 (midnight local time).

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. We expect to send invitations for interviews in December 2026 or January 2027. The interviews will typically take place in January and February of 2027, and our search is expected to be concluded around April 2027.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integration of High-Temperature Heat Pumps in Industrial Processes - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want your research to help industry decide how to electrify its heat supply? At DTU Construct you will combine thermodynamics, optimisation and machine learning to build tools that make the business case for industrial high-temperature heat pumps clear, fast and reliable.

We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade low-grade waste heat to up to about 250 °C.

Your project will address decision making support for heat pump end-users from a first viability check to integration with the process, to flexible operation. You will demonstrate the findings in industrial use cases together with our partners.

Supervision: Prof. Ahmad Arabkoohsar and Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be, through adequate methodological advancements, to cuts the time and effort needed to assess where and how high-temperature heat pumps should be integrated into industrial sites, and what is their economic value. Your main task will be:

• Develop models to rapidly estimate performance and break-even point for specific sites
• Extent methods for heat pump integration that co-optimize heat recovery, electrification and flexibility provided by heat pumps
• Refine and validate methods during industrial secondments 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
 
You have:

• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
 
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Ahmad Arabkoohsar ahmar@dtu.dk and Professor Adriano Sciacovelli adrsc@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on integration of high-temperature heat in industrial processes: select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Are you our new Business Controller?
jobs.description:
Do you understand the story behind the numbers - and can you help the business act on it?

We are looking for an experienced Business Controller who can connect financial performance with the operational and commercial developments behind it. You will take ownership of key reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes, work closely with leaders across the organisation and turn financial results into clear insights, priorities and actions.

The department “Analytics & Modelling” works across Momentum Energy Group and provides reporting, performance analyses and financial decision support to business units, senior management and the Board. You will join a small team of 3 with broad exposure across the organisation and play an important role in strengthening how Momentum understands, forecasts and manages its financial performance.

Momentum Energy Group develops, invests in, owns and operates renewable energy assets across Denmark, Germany and Sweden. We are one of Denmark's largest owners of onshore wind turbines, with activities spanning the full lifecycle of renewable energy projects and a development pipeline comprising wind, solar PV and hybrid projects through a clear growth agenda.

What are your tasks?

As a Business Controller, you will contribute to, deliver, and coordinate central parts of Momentum's performance management cycle. You will work closely with business unit leaders and Group Finance to understand developments in revenue, costs, and profitability while ensuring these drivers are reflected accurately in our reporting and outlook. You will be a trusted financial partner who combines a deep financial understanding with a strong and curious commercial perspective.

Your responsibilities will include:

• As part of a team delivering the monthly management reporting, including timeline management, inputs, quality assurance and financial commentary based on consolidated accounts received from Group Finance.

• Analysing monthly performance against budget, forecast and prior periods and explaining the underlying revenue, cost, and profitability drivers.

• Working closely with business unit leaders to understand operational and commercial developments and translate them into financial implications.

• Participating in budgeting and forecasting processes for relevant business areas, including assumptions, risks, opportunities and scenario analysis.

• Following up on budgets and forecasts with the business and ensuring that deviations, risks and required actions are identified and addressed.

• Developing and maintaining relevant financial and operational KPIs that provide transparency into business performance.

• Preparing business cases, profitability analyses and ad hoc decision support for commercial and operational initiatives.

Who are you?

You are an experienced and commercially minded finance professional who wants to understand and communicate how the business operates. You build strong working relationships across functions, but you are also comfortable challenging assumptions and conclusions constructively. You can move seamlessly between detailed financial analysis and discussions with senior stakeholders, translating complex findings into clear, actionable insights.

You are motivated by working in a developing organisation where the role will evolve over time, creating opportunities to take ownership of new tasks and areas of responsibility as the business matures.

Qualifications

• At least 5-7 years of relevant experience within business controlling, FP&A, performance management or a similar finance role.

• A relevant degree within finance, economics, accounting, business administration or a related field.

• Strong experience with management reporting, budgeting, forecasting and variance analysis.

• A solid understanding of financial statements and the interaction between operational performance, profitability, cash flow and the balance sheet.

• Strong analytical and financial skills, including proficiency in Excel.

• Experience preparing concise management presentations and communicating financial insights clearly to financial and non-financial stakeholders.

• A proactive and independent approach, combined with strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

What we offer

You will join a small and ambitious team with broad exposure across Momentum and direct interaction with business unit leaders and senior management. We prioritise professional development, personal balance and an inclusive workplace.

You will work at new our office in Roskilde together with 70 colleagues. Benefits include health insurance and a healthy lunch and fruit scheme.

Do you want to be a part of the journey?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, please apply as soon as possible, and no later than November 17, 2026, as we will be reviewing candidates on a rolling basis.

For questions about the role, please contact Head of Analytics & Modelling, Karoline Nylander at kny@momentumgreenenergy.com.

At Momentum, we believe that diversity strengthens our team. We therefore encourage everyone—regardless of gender, age, background, or culture—to apply for this position.

jobs.occupation: Market Director Health and Public Institutions
jobs.description:
_**Market Director Health and Public Institutions – Buildings & Industry

**__**Lyngby or Aarhus, Odense or Vejle

**_

_**Do you want to help shape some of Denmark's and the Nordic region's most important healthcare, education and public building projects? Can you build trusted relationships with key clients, grow business opportunities, and lead complex pursuits in a market with significant societal impact? And do you combine solid commercial acumen with deep insight into the health and public institutions sector? Then join COWI as our new Market Director for Health & Public Institutions within Buildings & Industry and apply your knowledge and curiosity to enable a better tomorrow.

**_

_**Shape the future of healthcare and public buildings

**_To strengthen COWI’s customer-centric approach, we are looking for a Market Director to drive business development and coordinate sales efforts within Health & Public Institutions in our Buildings & Industry sector.

This is a key role in one of COWI’s strategic growth markets, covering healthcare, education, research, cultural facilities and public development projects across Denmark and the Nordics. You will help position COWI on major hospital developments, universities, public institutions, refurbishment programmes and other complex projects that contribute to the development of society.

What makes this role unique is its pure focus on market leadership, where success is defined by customer value, business growth, and a strong market presence. Working closely with specialists, project managers and technical experts, you will build relationships, identify opportunities and grow COWI’s presence in the market. You will also become part of an experienced business development community that shares best practices and drives commercial excellence across COWI.

As part of a team of 25 experienced market professionals across COWI and Arkitema, you will work at the forefront of our business development efforts. Reporting to the Senior Market Director, you will collaborate closely with colleagues across the organization to deepen client relationships, unlock strategic opportunities, and lead pursuits from early engagement through to project win, contributing directly to the continued growth of our business.

With increasing investments in healthcare, public buildings and sustainable transformation, the market offers significant growth potential. Your sector insight, commercial mindset and customer understanding will help position COWI as a preferred partner for public clients and healthcare organisations across the Nordic region.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Grow business development and growth across the Health & Public Institutions market segment by identifying, prioritizing, and converting strategic opportunities.

• Build and maintain close relationships with key customers, partners, and decisionmakers, acting as a trusted advisor and Key Account Manager for selected clients.

• Develop and manage a healthy sales pipeline, manage Go/No-Go decisions, and drive capture planning for major pursuits and tenders.

Lead and support complex proposal processes, ensuring compelling value propositions and effective collaboration across disciplines and business units.

• Provide direction and coordination for the Business Development team supporting the market segment, ensuring effective collaboration and delivery of market priorities.

• Monitor market trends, upcoming investments, and customer needs to help shape market strategies and long-term growth initiatives.

• Represent COWI externally through customer meetings, industry networks, conferences, and strategic partnerships.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**Like us, you believe that successful business development is built on trust, collaboration and long-term relationships. You are motivated by creating opportunities, understanding customer needs and bringing together the best teams to deliver value for clients and society. You thrive in a collaborative environment and enjoy working closely with fellow Market Directors and multidisciplinary teams to achieve shared goals.

To perform well in this role, it is essential that you bring solid market insight and a well-established network within healthcare, public institutions or the built environment sector. Equally important is your ability to build internal alliances and leverage the collective expertise of the organisation rather than acting alone.

On top of that, you will have:

• A relevant educational background such as engineering, architecture, business or a related discipline.

• Extensive experience in business development, client management, or market leadership within healthcare, public institutions, architecture, construction, or engineering consultancy.

• Deep knowledge of public-sector customers, procurement processes, and market dynamics, combined with a well-established professional network.

• Demonstrated skill in building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and converting opportunities into long-term partnerships.

• Experience contributing to large and complex tenders, proposals, and commercial negotiations.

• Demonstrated ability to provide leadership, direction, and coordination across Business Development teams, account managers, and framework agreement holders, ensuring a shared focus on market growth and client development without formal personnel responsibility.

• Solid communication and stakeholder management skills, with professional proficiency in both Danish and English.

jobs.description:
Research assistant in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
Are you interested in turning IoT data into intelligent digital twins of real-world systems? The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Aarhus University invites applications for a 6-month research assistant position in the Robots4Green project, working at the intersection of IoT data, artificial intelligence and digital twin technology. The position is based in Aarhus, Denmark, and starts on 1 January or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 6-month position from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
We are seeking a motivated research assistant with a strong background in data science and machine learning to contribute to research on AI for IoT data and digital twin technology. You will work with sensor data and develop the models that allow digital twins to monitor, understand and predict the behaviour of physical systems.

Your tasks will include:

• Applying signal processing and feature extraction methods to sensor time series, for example wind and environmental data
• Designing, training and evaluating machine learning models for forecasting and anomaly detection, with an emphasis on interpretable and reliable models
• Contributing to data pipelines and to the integration of models into a digital twin platform together with the project team
• Supporting experiments and demonstrations together with project partners
• Documenting results and contributing to scientific publications and project deliverables

The position may also include assisting in supervision activities at the department.

Prior experience with IoT or digital twins is an advantage. You will gain hands on experience with IoT data and digital twin technology while working closely with researchers in the Networks and Analytics research group and with academic and industrial partners in the project. The position is an excellent stepping stone towards a PhD or a career in industry.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science or a similar field.

We are looking for candidates with:

• Solid programming skills in Python for data analysis and modelling
• Experience with machine learning frameworks such as scikit-learn and PyTorch or similar AI frameworks
• A strong foundation in statistics, probability and signal processing
• A good understanding of time series analysis
The following qualifications are considered advantages:

• Experience with graph-based machine learning, such as graph neural networks, or graph signal processing
• Knowledge of IoT systems, sensor data or data platforms
• Familiarity with digital twin concepts and simulation
• Experience from research projects, including interdisciplinary collaborations
• Teaching or supervision experience

Personal skills
We value good communication skills in English, the ability to work independently as well as in an international team, curiosity and a proactive, structured approach to problem solving.

Who we are
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Aarhus University is a leading research institution with strong expertise in computer science, electrical engineering and wireless communication systems. We maintain active collaborations with industry partners and are involved in multiple national and international research projects on IoT, AI and digital twins.

You will be joining the Networks and Analytics (NAN) research group, which focuses on research and innovation in developing and applying internet technology across a wide selection of fields in electrical and computer engineering for real-world, large-scale applications. The NAN group has strong expertise in wireless networks, IoT, network security, data analytics, AI and cooperative multi agent systems, with extensive experience in smart energy grids, smart and integrated transport and satellite communication systems.

Our research group provides a dynamic and supportive environment where interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged, and where you will work with both academic researchers and industry professionals on projects with real world impact.

Department website: https://ece.au.dk

What we offer
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering offers:

• An exciting opportunity to work on applied research in IoT data, AI and digital twin technology
• A well developed research infrastructure with access to laboratories, IoT equipment and computing facilities
• Close collaboration with industrial partners and direct pathways to real world validation
• An interdisciplinary and international research environment
• Opportunities to co-author scientific publications and build a foundation for a PhD
• A supportive work environment that values work-life balance, professional development and openness

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Helsingforsgade 10, 8200 Aarhus N (Denmark), and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Professor Rune Hylsberg Jacobsen, +45 41893252, rhj@ece.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 17 November 2026.

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

**Your impact begins here

**As Senior Manager, Search & Evaluation, you will help Novo find and assess the external drug and technology opportunities that could shape our future portfolio. You will evaluate early ideas, take promising opportunities through due diligence and build the value story that helps senior leaders decide. Working globally with scientists, biotech companies and investors, you will help bring new science towards people living with diabetes, obesity and other serious chronic diseases.

**What You’ll Bring

• A master’s degree in business or life sciences.

• 5+ years of experience in R&D, business development or professional services within the pharma or biotech industry, or in an equivalent role.

• Project management skills and experience.

• The ability to analyse complex ideas and data and turn them into clear, well-founded recommendations for senior stakeholders.

• Experience working in cross-functional teams, with clear communication and strong teamwork.

• Strong written and presentation skills.

• Strong networking, collaboration and stakeholder management skills.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

**Who You’ll Work With

SE&I is the primary entry point for external drug and technology opportunities at Novo, running proactive scouting campaigns across start-ups, biotechnology companies and venture capital firms.

You will work closely with Business Development teams in Denmark and Cambridge, USA, and with colleagues across the value chain who help assess each opportunity. Externally, you will use and grow your network across biotech companies, venture capital firms and large pharma communities.

This role works globally, so you will bring different perspectives together, create clarity and keep opportunities moving.

**What You Can Expect Here

You will build new skills through exposure to different therapy areas, functions and external partners, and grow alongside colleagues in a global, fast-moving environment.

**What We Offer

• Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 y 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience. Further details to be shared during the recruitment process.

• Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to find and shape the partnerships behind Novo’s next breakthroughs, apply for the Senior Manager, Search & Evaluation role by 4 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

**About GoWish, Ønskeskyen ☁️

**At GoWish, we’re building the world’s leading wish-list and social shopping platform - a place where you can make a real impact and have fun doing it.

We’re on a mission to reinvent gifting for millions. We win together, driven by curiosity, ownership, and bold ideas that turn into real products. We experiment cross-functionally, push for excellence, and keep things playful as we grow - together.

**Team & Role Overview

**We are looking for a systems-minded Senior ML Data Engineer to own the offline-to-online feature infrastructure that powers our real-time recommendation and search engines at scale. You will be building the low-latency data syncs and feature-serving layers that bridge our analytical warehouses with operational databases, caches, and Feature Stores. This is a role for a performance-driven engineer who excels at pipeline orchestration (Airflow, dbt), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Docker), and database tuning, ensuring our recommendation systems receive reliable data under strict low-latency SLAs. If you thrive on solving complex data synchronization challenges, scaling operational storage for millions of users, and acting as the operational bridge between Data Science and Backend Engineering - you will play a critical role in powering our product's core ML capabilities.

**What You'll Do

**

• Offline-to-Online Feature Pipelines: Build and operate resilient feature pipelines syncing transformed data from analytical warehouses (e.g., BigQuery) into operational storage layers (e.g., AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models at scale.

• Pipeline Orchestration and Transformations: Design, test, and maintain robust Apache Airflow DAGs and modular dbt transformations to automate end-to-end data ingestion and feature generation under strict low-latency SLAs.

• Infrastructure as Code and Reliability: Provision, scale, and automate cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines, implementing automated data quality testing and monitoring across all feature syncs.

• Cross-Functional System Design: Partner directly with Data Scientists and Backend Engineers to define online/offline feature contracts, optimize database schemas for sub-second queries, and eliminate training-serving skew for millions of active users.

**What we’re looking for 🌟

****We Imagine That You Have

**

• 4+ years of experience

• Operational Data Pipelines: Proven experience moving batch features from analytical warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) into low-latency online stores (AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Deep hands-on experience provisioning, scaling, and managing cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD automation pipelines.

• Pipeline Orchestration & Transformations: Strong track record building, scheduling, and maintaining workflow orchestrations (e.g., Airflow, Dagster) and modular data transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt).

• Database Performance Tuning: Advanced SQL skills across both OLAP and OLTP systems. Ability to optimize schemas, indexing, partitioning, and queries.

It is further seen as an advantage to have experience with:

• Production Feature Management: Experience managing Feature Stores (e.g., Feast, Tecton) or low-latency key-value stores (e.g., Redis) to serve online ML features with zero training-serving skew.

• Real-Time OLA): Experience with ClickHouse, Pinot, Druid or others for ultra-fast aggregations over live event streams.

• Event Streaming: Hands-on experience with streaming tools like GCP Pub/Sub, Kafka, or Flink for real-time feature updates.

Are you an experienced Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) professional with a passion for advancing evidence-based MHPSS practice in humanitarian settings? Danish Red Cross (DRC) is looking for a MHPSS Advisor to provide technical expertise, capacity development, and quality assurance to the Red Cross Red Crescent National Societies (RCRC) National Societies delivering community-based MHPSS interventions in humanitarian settings.

About the position and the assignments  

You will be based at the Danish Red Cross HQ in Copenhagen and will be part of the Health Team in the Technical Quality and Impact Unit of the International Department. The Health Team comprises technical advisors within health and mental health and psychosocial support. It ensures the availability of the necessary technical capacities to provide timely and relevant assistance and advice to DRC-supported operations, with a primary focus on the Africa, while also supporting MHPSS interventions in MENA, Europe and Asia regions as needed.

As a member of the Health Team, you will be working under the line management of the Health Team Lead and will also work closely with other colleagues at the DRC HQ and Regional and Country Offices (COs), as well as with NSs staff and volunteers. You will also collaborate with the colleagues from the International Federation of the Red Cross Red Crescent (IFRC) and the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The position does not have programme management responsibilities but supports programmes through technical accompaniment, mentoring, and quality assurance.

Your main responsibilities will be to:

• Strategic planning and direction: Contribute to defining and rollout of DRC’s strategic directions within MHPSS in humanitarian settings. Support development and rollout of strategies, policies, and technical frameworks for MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
• Technical support and guidance: Provide evidence-based guidance and advice to DRC COs and National Societies on MHPSS priorities, approaches and activities, remotely or through country visits and missions to ensure that MHPSS interventions follow industry standards and good practice. Support development or adaptation and rollout of relevant technical tools and guidelines to meet operational needs.
• Strengthening of capacities: Support National Societies in assessing technical capacity needs, and in designing and implementing capacity-strengthening plans, including trainings, coaching, mentoring, and technical supervision. 
• Program monitoring and evaluation:  Support planning and undertaking of assessments, baselines, endlines, reviews and evaluations, and monitoring of MHPSS interventions.
• Advocacy: In close collaboration with relevant humanitarian diplomacy (HD) colleagues, contribute to DRC’s policy influencing, advocacy and HD efforts on MHPSS in humanitarian settings.
• Resource mobilisation: Support proposal development by contributing to the design and quality assurance of MHPSS components in the project proposals that align with donor requirements and organisational goals and priorities.
• Partnerships and collaboration: Foster thematic partnerships and joint MHPSS initiatives within the RCRC Movement and with external stakeholders. 
• Surge deployments: Undertake MHPSS surge/deployments in support of DRC bi-lateral operations and wider RCRC Movement responses, including multilateral deployments with the ICRC and the IFRC.  
 

Your profile

We are looking for an experienced MHPSS professional with at least five years of experience working on community-based MNHPSS with humanitarian and development organisations, including at least three years in international postings in Africa and MENA regions. You hold a master's degree, or equivalent experience, in MHPSS, social sciences, or another relevant field. You have sound technical, strategy and advisory skills within community-based MHPSS in humanitarian settings and migration. You have proven experience developing and adapting technical guidance, tools and training materials, as well as designing and facilitating capacity-development initiatives for staff and volunteers of partner organisations. 

You have experience supporting assessments, technical reviews, evaluations, and the development of quality assurance processes for community-based MHPSS interventions. You are an excellent facilitator and communicator with strong interpersonal and cross-cultural skills. You work collaboratively, are well organised, and are able to manage multiple priorities while meeting deadlines. You are willing and able to undertake field missions, including emergency deployments, with travel of up to four months per year. Professional working proficiency in both English and French is required. Experience of working for the International RCRC Movement is considered an asset. 

We offer

A job with an opportunity to improve the lives of the most vulnerable people around the world. We further offer a unique opportunity to influence the strategic development and mainstreaming of MHPSS in humanitarian settings.

The position is a full-time position - 37 working hours per week. The position is 12 months with possibility for extension.

Salary and employment conditions are in accordance with Danish Red Cross’s collective bargaining agreement with HK and AC, depending on experience and qualifications. The position is based at the Danish Red Cross headquarters in Copenhagen and requires on-site presence. As this is a national position based in Denmark, the salary package does not include relocation assistance to Denmark and housing or family-related allowances.

Your future workplace

The International Red Cross and Red Crescent network is the largest humanitarian network in the world, with a presence and activities in almost every country. All Red Cross and Red Crescent activities have one central purpose: to help those who suffer, without discrimination, whether during conflict, in response to natural or man-made disasters, or due to conditions of chronic poverty. Our work is guided by seven fundamental principles: humanity, impartiality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality. 

DRC’s international department’s approx. 300 staff supporting RCRC NSs with planning and implementing humanitarian and development interventions in some of the most challenging contexts in 20 countries across Africa, MENA, Asia, and Europe.

We offer a meaningful work at a purpose-driven workplace with truly engaged colleagues. We focus on professional challenges, well-being and a flexible organising of your work life. All of us contribute to a great work environment and colleagueship. 

 

Application and further information

For any specific questions about the position, please contact us at zesd@rodekors.dk subject “MHPSS Advisor 2026”.

Interviews will take place in the second part of November with an expected start date as soon as possible and no later than 01 January 2027. 

We look forward to receiving your application and CV no later than 18 November 2026. Application and CV in English are accepted only through our online recruitment system. Applications made by email will not be reviewed.

Do you want to develop new methods for quantitative modelling of the shallow subsurface and geological processes? The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland (GEUS) is looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and an interest in combining geoscientific observations, numerical modelling and scientific software development. 

  The position is a three-year, time-limited researcher position in the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology (SURFACE) in Aarhus, expected to start on 1st of January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  About the position 

  The position lies at the intersection of geology, geophysics, glaciology, numerical modelling and scientific software development. You will develop computational approaches that combine geological and geophysical observations with process-based and probabilistic models to create quantitative representations of the subsurface and glacial environments. 

  You will initially contribute to two ongoing research projects, ICESYNC and DREAM, while also taking part in research and development related to the national groundwater mapping programme and other activities at GEUS. 

  In ICESYNC, you will work with process-based modelling of erosion, sediment transport and deposition and investigate how modelled ice dynamics and sedimentary processes can be linked to geological and geomorphological observations. The work includes development of reproducible modelling workflows and pilot studies in Greenland and Denmark. 

  In DREAM, you will contribute to the development of a high-resolution probabilistic geological modelling framework based on drone-based TEM data. You will work with the integration of high-resolution resistivity models and their uncertainties with geological prior knowledge and other geoscientific data. The aim is to develop a semi-automatic, open-source workflow for constructing detailed geological voxel models and to test the approach using synthetic and field data. 

  Across these activities, you will work with numerical, probabilistic and process-based approaches to geological modelling and with integration of geophysical observations, geological data and process-based models. An important part of the position will be the development of reproducible computational workflows and scientific software for geoscientific analysis and modelling. You will also contribute to geological interpretation and modelling in research projects and applied activities, including the national groundwater mapping programme. 

  The position includes publication and communication of research through peer-reviewed papers, project deliverables, presentations and open-source software. You will also be expected to contribute to the development of new research ideas, project proposals and collaborations with Danish and international partners. 

  Who are you? 

  You hold a PhD, or have submitted your PhD before the application deadline, in geoscience, geophysics, computational geoscience or a closely related field. 

  We are looking for a researcher with a strong geological background and a good understanding of geological processes, combined with experience in quantitative geoscience. This may include numerical modelling, geological modelling, probabilistic or statistical methods, inverse problems, geostatistics or related approaches. 

  You should have a good understanding of geophysical data and their geological interpretation and strong programming skills, with experience in scientific software development, for example in Python, Matlab or a similar language. You should be able to work independently and systematically while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment, and you should communicate well in written and spoken English. 

  Experience with TEM data, process-based modelling, 3D geological or voxel-based modelling, open-source scientific software or reproducible computational workflows would be valuable. Knowledge of Quaternary geology, glacial geology, sedimentology or groundwater geology would also be relevant, as would experience from externally funded research projects and preparation of research proposals. We do not expect applicants to cover all of these areas. 

  As Danish is the primary organisational language at GEUS, you should be prepared to learn Danish if you are not already a Danish speaker. 

  Meet your new colleagues 

  At GEUS, you will join the Department of Near Surface Land and Marine Geology, where we conduct research on a wide range of topics related to the processes, resources and geology of the upper 300 metres of the subsurface, both onshore and offshore. 

  Based at the university campus in Aarhus, the department consists of around 35 enthusiastic colleagues working in an interdisciplinary environment. We combine field observations, laboratory analyses, and advanced modelling to address scientific questions and societal challenges. 

  As part of the team, you will work alongside colleagues committed to scientific excellence, collaboration, and knowledge sharing. We work closely with public authorities, universities, and international research networks, providing a strong platform for developing your research, building collaborations, and making a meaningful contribution to both science and society. 

  A working environment with a focus on professional development and well-being 

  There are many good reasons why you should choose a working life at GEUS. 

  We are a diverse staff of about 300 committed employees. Trust and flexibility are keywords. The working environment is lively, informal and international. Our tasks are versatile and there are plenty of opportunities for you to influence the development of your task portfolio.

  We prioritise professional development, among other things by offering access to courses and other relevant activities. Socialising is also very important at GEUS, and we have a rich social life with a staff club, an art association and more. 

  At GEUS, we prioritise the well-being of every single employee. We prioritise that the Heads of Departments are close to the employees, and we have flexible working hours that allow you to organise your life so that there is time for what matters to you. If you need to work from home occasionally, that is also possible. 

  Furthermore, we have associated physiotherapists. 

  Salary and terms of employment 

  Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the relevant trade union agreement. 

  The appointment area is the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities and its institutions. 

  The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities considers diversity to be an asset and encourages anyone regardless of gender, age, religion or ethnicity to seek the position. 

  Further information 

  If you would like additional information, please contact the contact Acting Head of Department Verner Brandbyge Ernstsen Verner vbe@geus.dk or Senior Researcher Anders Damsgaard on andam@geus.dk. 

  If you are an international applicant, you can read more about living and working in Denmark on GEUS’ website.  

  Are you interested? 

  If you are interested in the position, we would like to hear from you. The application must include a CV incl. your ORCID, a list of publications with a separate indication of articles registered in ISI Web of Science and any copies of individual publications of particular relevance to the position. Please enclose master's and PhD diplomas in either Danish or English as well as other material documenting qualifications at senior level. 

  Please apply for the position by clicking “Apply for position”. We must have your application at the latest on Sunday 15th of November 2026 (Danish time). 

  Applications or other material received after the deadline will not be considered. 

  The employment procedure 

  A professional assessment committee consisting of one internal and two external assessors at minimum senior researcher level will carry out an individual assessment of all applicants’ professional qualifications, and the applicants will be assessed as qualified or unqualified for the position. Afterwards, an internal employment committee will decide which of the professionally qualified candidates will be invited for a job interview. This procedure is in accordance with the “Order on employment and assessment of scientific staff at the Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland § 4 and 7”.

jobs.occupation: Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping (re-posting)
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology is looking for a highly motivated and independent Staff Scientist in RNA biology and metabolite RNA capping. The position is expected to commence on 1 January 2027 and is linked to the Lundbeck Foundation Experiment grant MINDtheCAP: A new role of RNA caps in intellectual disability.

  Our research
 The Section for Computational and RNA Biology combines experimental and computational approaches to investigate RNA biology, gene regulation and genome-wide molecular processes. The position will be anchored in the Vinther research group and will contribute to the section's research activities, collaborations and supervision environment.

  Your job
 The Staff Scientist will have scientific responsibility for the day-to-day implementation of MINDtheCAP and will independently plan and coordinate the work within the project's objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements.

   	
• Plan, prioritise and carry out the project in accordance with its scientific objectives, milestones, budget and reporting requirements. 	
• Analyse and interpret high-throughput sequencing and molecular data and refine the associated bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Coordinate project activities with laboratory technical staff and internal and external collaborators, and supervise students or junior researchers where relevant. 	
• Maintain research documentation and data-management practices and ensure compliance with laboratory safety, research-integrity and relevant institutional requirements. 	
• Prepare scientific publications, conference presentations, seminars, workshops, grant reports and relevant outreach activities. 	
• Develop follow-up research directions, collaborations and applications for further competitive research funding.   Because the work is research-driven, its detailed timing and sequence cannot be fully predetermined. Within the agreed scientific and institutional framework, the Staff Scientist will independently determine day-to-day priorities, experimental design and methods, the sequencing of experiments and analyses, and the coordination of collaborations.

  Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic Staff Scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Qualifications and Expectations 

   	
• A master’s degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, RNA biology or a closely related field. 	
• Interest in and/or experience with RNA biology, RNA capping or RNA biochemistry. 	
• Experience with molecular biology techniques and laboratory work. Experience developing and optimising RNA-related methods, sequencing-library preparation and quantitative experimental controls is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience with or interest in analysing and interpreting transcriptomic data and in using or developing bioinformatic workflows. 	
• Interest in data analysis and bioinformatics. Experience with bioinformatic tools or workflows is considered an advantage. 	
• Experience preparing scientific reports, manuscripts and presentations is an advantage. Previous scientific publications are considered an advantage.  	
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment within agreed milestones and budgets. 	
• Good written and oral communication skills in English.   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience managing externally funded research projects and contributing to competitive funding applications. 	
• Experience coordinating interdisciplinary collaborations and working with molecular or neuronal cell-model systems. 	
• Experience supervising students, junior researchers or technical staff. 	
• Ability to work independently, solve scientific and technical challenges, and collaborate effectively across disciplines.   Place of employment
 The place of employment is the Section for Computational and RNA Biology, Department of Biology, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment, with access to facilities and expertise in RNA biochemistry, molecular biology, high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics.

  Terms of employment

  The average weekly working time is 37 hours.

  The position is fixed-term for two years, from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2028.

  The position is classified as Staff Scientist (AC-TAP). Employment will be under The Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority) and there will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). The applicable pension contribution will be in accordance with the relevant collective agreement.

  Application
 If you are interested in the position, please submit your electronic application, including attachments, via the UCPH Job Portal (click the “Apply for position” link at the bottom of the job posting).

  Your application should be submitted in English and include:

   	
• A letter of application addressing the requirements, maximum one page. 	
• Curriculum vitae. 	
• A certified or signed copy of certificate(s) of education.   The application deadline is 9 November 2026

  Interviews are expected to be held shortly after the application deadline.

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Jeppe Vinther at jvinther@bio.ku.dk.
  

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

  The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration.

Your impact begins here

As Sr AI Process Designer in Rapid Enablement, you will help business areas across Novo rethink how work gets done with AI, rather than simply applying AI to what already exists. You will join cross-functional engagements that take an opportunity from an initial request to an evidence-based decision about what happens next. By designing future-state services around what AI and people each do well, and testing them with real users, you help the right ideas move forward fast.

What you’ll bring

You are proactive and structured, able to frame ambiguous problems independently, challenge an initial solution request constructively, and test a better future state under time pressure. You bring most of the following:

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in service design, interaction design, human-computer interaction or a related field.

• 4+ years of experience applying service design, human-centred design or closely related methods to complex services or business processes, including researching and mapping end-to-end processes across multiple actors, systems, channels and organisational boundaries.

• Strong facilitation experience, including online and in-person creative workshops and co-design sessions with senior, multidisciplinary stakeholders.

• The ability to turn research and operational evidence into clear design opportunities and future-state services, and to prototype and test concepts iteratively rather than relying only on analysis and documentation.

• Excellent visual and verbal communication skills: you make complex processes understandable to non-design and technical audiences, and challenge existing ways of working with confidence.

• A pragmatic mindset: good today is better than perfect tomorrow. You balance great user experiences with project constraints.

• Strong planning and project management skills, with the ability to own larger deliverables independently and translate strategy into ambitious, testable goals.

• Comfort working at pace with incomplete information, and strong collaboration skills with business subject-matter experts, software engineers and AI specialists.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience redesigning knowledge-work or enterprise business processes.

• AI-enabled service or workflow design, including human-in-the-loop patterns.

• Experience in enterprise transformation, internal consulting, or regulated and highly complex organisations.

• Designing services that span digital and non-digital interactions.

• Experience with experimentation, rapid prototyping and discovery methods, and connecting design decisions to measurable business value.

Deep AI expertise is not required. You do need to understand the possibilities and limitations of AI well enough to design effectively alongside technical colleagues.

What you’ll do

You will work in short iterations and test the riskiest unknowns first, making quick progress while reducing risk. You will facilitate the process from start to finish, bring others along without formal authority, and share findings so decision makers can act.

• Plan and facilitate workshops and co-design sessions with business and technical stakeholders to understand real users’ pain points, surface risky assumptions behind AI-driven ideas, and build shared understanding of the problem, target outcome and success criteria.

Your impact begins here

As Laboratory Technician in Research Bioanalysis, you will help early-stage research projects get the answers they need. You will develop and run immunoassays that measure proteins and peptides in biological samples, giving project teams data to predict how long new compounds stay in circulation and how they work in the body. Your work supports early research in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular diseases.

What you’ll bring

• A relevant education in laboratory technology or equivalent.

• Proficiency in general biological research laboratory techniques and workflows.

• Practical experience analysing biological samples.

• A keen interest in data analysis and a drive to keep data quality high.

• A flair for IT and laboratory instruments, with the willingness to learn and adapt.

• A proactive attitude towards building your analytical technical skills, with an open mindset.

• An energetic, self-driven and organised way of working, and a team-player mindset.

• Hands-on experience with immunoassays such as ELISA, MSD or AlphaLISA.

What you’ll do

New projects often call for new ways of measuring different proteins and peptides. You will spend a significant part of your time developing tailored methods, alongside analysing samples with established ones.

• Develop and implement new immunoassays for the proteins and peptides your collaborators need to measure.

• Analyse samples from in vivo and in vitro studies using immunoassays

• Plan and carry out sample analyses, using robotics and IT systems to handle samples efficiently and track data.

• Analyse data and safeguard data integrity, so project teams can rely on the results.

• Proactively improve laboratory workflows and integrate new digital tools and AI

• Help strengthen the culture of the department.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Research Bioanalysis, part of Therapeutic Discovery within Research & Development, in Måløv, Denmark. In Research & Development, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing. Curiosity, data, technology and collaboration come together to help meet future health needs.

Your team is high-achieving, multidisciplinary and international: seven laboratory technicians, one tech trainee, four associate scientists and eight scientists. You will also work with collaborators who provide the samples and rely on your data, and with colleagues in other departments as workflows are refined across the research process.

What you can expect here

You will work in a department that is putting automation, digital tools and AI to use in everyday analytical work. You will have room to build new technical skills, take ownership of method development and make your voice heard on how the work is done. You will be supported to perform at your best by colleagues who share their expertise.

jobs.description:
Enterprise AI

Ballerup, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Senior AI Engineer in Enterprise AI, you will turn strategic AI use cases into reliable products that create value across Novo. Working in cross-functional product teams in areas such as Commercial and Manufacturing & Product Supply, you will decide what each problem really needs, from conventional software to retrieval-grounded GenAI, and take it from prototype to production. Your work helps bring AI into everyday use for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You enjoy turning technology into business impact. You don’t need deep expertise in every part of AI engineering, but you do have a solid foundation in software delivery, production AI and cross-functional product work.

• 4+ years of experience building AI or software products. Demonstrated scope and capability matter more than tenure alone.

• Experience taking AI-centric applications from idea to production, and/or contributing to a product or platform team.

• Hands-on experience operating AI in production, including evaluation, monitoring, reliability and cost-performance trade-offs.

• A sound foundation in statistical and machine-learning concepts, with practical experience of modern AI application patterns.

• Strong programming and software engineering skills, including testing, documentation, APIs and CI/CD, preferably with GitHub.

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools and coding agents effectively in software delivery.

• Functional knowledge of modern AI interfaces and standards, such as model and tool integrations, MCP and observability approaches.

• An MSc, PhD or similar graduate degree in engineering, computer science, data science, statistics, machine learning or a related field. Candidates with a BSc and industry experience will also be considered.

You combine technical expertise with strong product sense and are comfortable clarifying needs with stakeholders and communicating technical choices to different audiences. You can take ownership of end-to-end AI delivery, make technical and product trade-offs, and ensure alignment throughout the process.

Beyond your technical expertise, we are looking for someone who is collaborative, curious and self-driven, with strong listening skills and a genuine interest in staying current as the AI landscape evolves.

Useful, but not essential

• Familiarity with pharma-specific AI domains, such as clinical NLP, drug discovery AI, regulatory automation or medical knowledge graphs.

• Experience with Databricks, Snowflake, Azure ML and Unity Catalog in an enterprise data and AI platform context.

• Knowledge of MCP (Model Context Protocol) server design and enterprise AI platform architecture patterns.

What you’ll do

You will be hired into AI Reinvent & Engineering, while much of your work happens in cross-functional product teams. A central part of the role is deciding whether a problem calls for conventional software or rules, optimisation, a predictive model, retrieval-grounded GenAI or a carefully bounded agentic workflow.

• Take AI- and ML-centric use cases from discovery and rapid prototyping through production and continuous improvement.

• Engineer the product-specific intelligence layer: data and feature transformations, decision logic, model and tool integrations, knowledge grounding, user-facing services, human-oversight controls and fallback behaviour.

• Partner with stakeholders and product managers to frame problems, agree priorities and define meaningful product outcomes.

• Build reliable, scalable, secure and observable products with appropriate testing, evaluation, documentation and CI/CD, using AI-assisted development tools and coding agents responsibly.

• Apply Responsible AI, data integrity, validation, traceability and auditability requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.

• Work with the AI Foundation team to reuse shared capabilities and turn lessons from individual deliveries into reusable components and engineering patterns.

• Own substantial delivery workstreams, shape technical and product choices, and support less experienced engineers.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the AI Engineering Solutions team within AI Reinvent & Engineering, part of Enterprise AI in Enterprise IT, based in Ballerup, Denmark. The team brings together engineers with different strengths across statistics, machine learning, AI and software engineering.

Day to day, you will often work in product teams in Commercial, Manufacturing & Product Supply and other business areas, alongside product managers, domain experts, data scientists and engineers. Staying close to the problems keeps the work relevant, while links to the AI Foundation team keep engineering practices shared. We are cloud-native, working across Azure and AWS, Databricks, Snowflake, foundation-model APIs and modern AI application frameworks, and we value technical rigour, direct feedback and continuous learning.

What you can expect here

You will work in a multinational environment where your expertise is valued and trusted. You will keep growing through continuous learning and hands-on experience across business areas, with room to shape technical and product choices and to support colleagues as they develop.
