At Factbird, we help manufacturers see what’s really happening on their lines, so they can make better, faster decisions. Our plug-and-play hardware and cloud platform turn live production data into clear insights, and we’re scaling fast across sites, teams, and countries.

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

About the role

Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

**

The team mission we are on:** Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

What You'll Do

• Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how

• Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.

• Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.

• Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes

• Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.

• Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.

• Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.

• Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.

• Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.

• Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.

• Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

About you

You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”

You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.

You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:

• A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.

• At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).

• Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.

• Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.

• Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.

• Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.

• Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.

• Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.

• A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.

• A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn’t one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We’ll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we’ll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what’s next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We’re proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We’d love to hear from you

**If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Khristel, our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead at khma@factbird.com

_At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

_

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws._

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird._

About Factbird

Great people make great things happen

Factbird is on a mission to make manufacturing more efficient. We build intuitive tools that give frontline teams the insights they need to reduce waste, improve processes, and stay ahead. Since 2016, we’ve helped manufacturers worldwide drive real change. Now, we’re searching for great people to help us do even more.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead takes ownership of ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, turning enthusiasm into real, safe, everyday value from the AI tools available to ALK employees. This role continues the adoption efforts from 2025 (over 1,000 employees trained in GenAI usage) and 2026 (more tailored training on ALK's AI solutions) and is key to achieving ALK's AI ambition within the Allergy+ strategy.

This role requires genuine enthusiasm for enabling people, facilitating great learning experiences, and driving change. The Senior AI Adoption Lead must work closely with people across all business areas, be proactive, reach out to employees, and drive AI adoption across the entire organization so that the change is permanent and sticks with employees.

This role owns ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, covering general enablement on GenAI, tailored upskilling for all employees, and engagement activities that drive adoption. This includes preparing and hosting AI training (both general-purpose and tool-specific), the training calendar, micro-learning, maintaining AI at ALK intranet site. The role also owns measuring GenAI usage across the organization, providing the data needed to support informed decisions in AI strategy implementation.

This is not an engineering role – the person does not need to build or configure AI solutions. It does, however, require basic understanding of both business and IT, so the Senior AI Adoption Lead can act as an effective bridge between the two. Genuine enthusiasm for new technologies, especially generative AI, is required. Experience with usage of those technologies in daily life and enterprise scenario is vital.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead acts as a proxy between business and IT: translating technical concepts into everyday business language, aligning business demand with IT delivery, triaging common issues, and accelerating adoption before escalation to IT.

This role is based in Denmark, where ALK has its headquarters and the majority of AI users. It also requires occasional business travel to conduct in-person workshops and training.

Major fields of responsibility:

• 
Communicate the need for AI adoption through meetings, newsletters, MS Teams, and Intranet; share success stories, best practices, and enthusiasm for upcoming initiatives.

• 
Foster engagement through targeted workshops for departments and business units, regular manager briefings, tailored communications, and a visible emphasis on the benefits of AI in daily work.

• 
Map use cases and design training courses (e.g. Foundations, Advanced Prompting, Leading with GenAI) and micro-learning, and activate and coordinate a network of AI Champions to extend reach.

• 
Provide accessible, tiered learning resources through the AI community and Learning Hub (Teams channel, SharePoint) — videos, live webinars, in-person workshops, quick-start guides, FAQs, and playbooks.

• 
Support enterprise-AI pilots with onboarding, enablement and value evaluation; collect feedback and resolve common non-technical issues; and maintain a tight feedback loop with IT on platform updates, governance, and support to keep adoption aligned and safe.

• 
Work side by side with the technical teams (programmers, architects, data and platform specialists): take part in solution and roadmap discussions, learn how the solutions work, ask questions from the end-user perspective, challenge and advise on usability, and translate the outcome into layman terms for the business.

• 
Define and measure adoption rates and satisfaction (usage, surveys, focus groups) and report impact to leadership; run iterative cycles to refine training content based on user feedback and business priorities; and recognize high adopters through awards and acknowledgment.

Qualifications:

• 
Minimum 10 years' experience in change management, IT systems adoption, and training management and delivery

• 
Proven facilitation, training and change-management experience

• 
Outstanding communication and stakeholder skills across all levels

• 
Fluent in English.

• 
Hands-on curiosity about generative AI

• 
Practical experience with creation of AI assistants (e.g. custom skills in Anthropic Claude or custom agents in M365 Copilot).

• 
Analytical mindset able to translate adoption data into actionable insights.

• 
Self-driven, organized and creative, comfortable working across business and IT**.**

Create high-quality Group reporting, strong internal controls and transparent financial processes across out international organization.

Would you like to help create and further develop the foundation that enables our European finance community to deliver high-quality consolidated reporting for decision makers and our owners on ongoing basis? On behalf of Scanmetals A/S, Leadr Recruitment is looking for a Group Finance Controller who combines strong group reporting and consolidation capabilities with curiosity for ERP, structure, IT tools and hands-on with data in an international environment.

You will work closely with the Group CFO, the executive management team and local finance functions across four countries. You will be the main driver of strengthening reporting, controls and performance reporting including compliance with Danish and International accounting standards.

Your role

You will take on a broad role in Group Finance, working close to the business. You will take the lead in monthly reporting and closing, while also developing the structures, tools and decision support behind the figures. Your work will cover areas such consolidation including eliminations of P&L, balance sheet, cashflow, investments and KPI´s, securing data quality, development of our consolidation platform along with the master data to secure the foundation for high-quality reporting - giving management a more precise basis for taking decisions.

Your key responsibilities:

• Gather and quality-assure monthly group reporting for all subsidiaries across Denmark, Germany, Spain and the UK, including the income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and operational KPIs.

• Handle consolidation entries, intercompany reconciliations and group adjustments.

• Drive and support month-end and year-end closing, coordinate documentation and participate in review meetings with the subsidiaries.

• Ensure consistent, high-quality data and work with IT to further develop reporting in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, Power BI, consolidation system and related tools.

• Contribute to financial budgets, forecasts, cash flow analyses and decision material for the CFO and executive management team.

• Maintain and develop internal controls, accounting processes and compliance across countries and entities.

• Coordinate audit activities and contribute to transfer pricing, tax, VAT, banking matters and the financial aspects of sustainability reporting.

• Drive practical improvements, standardisation and automation across Group Finance.

What you bring:

• A relevant master’s degree in finance, accounting, auditing or a comparable field.

• Experience from audit - preferably from a larger audit firm - combined with solid experience in group accounting or consolidation.

• A sound understanding of Danish and international financial reporting.

• Strong Excel skills and confidence working with ERP and reporting platforms. Experience with Business Central and Power BI is an advantage.

• Fluent English. Danish and/or German is an advantage, but not a requirement.

How you work

You are structured, detail-oriented and dependable, while keeping deadlines and commercial relevance firmly in view. You ask the right questions, are naturally curious, build strong relationships across functions and countries, and take ownership. You thrive in an entrepreneurial business where structures continue to evolve, and the impact of your work quickly becomes visible.

Why this role is worth considering:

• You will take on a central role in an international recycling and materials processing group with an active growth agenda.

• You will report directly to the Group CFO, have direct exposure to Group Management and work closely with the Group CFO and local finance teams.

• You will have a genuine opportunity to shape reporting, controls and data-driven decision support.

• You will join a hands-on culture with short decision paths and a clear ambition to professionalise and standardise.

Practical information

The position reports to Group CFO Dan Jensen.

The workplace is located in Slagelse, Denmark, with approximately 10-20 travel days per year.

The position is full-time.

Interested?

Leadr Recruitment is managing the search and recruitment process on behalf of Scanmetals A/S. Apply for the position via www.leadr-recruitment.dk.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and therefore recommend that you do not wait unnecessarily before applying.

All enquiries will be treated confidentially. If you would like an informal conversation about the role, please contact Claus Porse, Partner at Leadr Recruitment, on +45 2087 8617 or claus@leadr-recruitment.dk.

About Scanmetals A/S

Scanmetals A/S is an international group specialising in metals recycling and materials processing, with operations in Denmark, Germany, Spain and the UK. Headquartered in Slagelse, Denmark, the group recovers valuable non-ferrous metals from metal-bearing waste streams through its activities. Its technology and operational expertise return metals to the value chain and contribute to a more circular and resource-efficient economy.

Scanmetals A/S is growing and is therefore strengthening its organisation, systems and group-wide governance. The ambition is to professionalise without losing the entrepreneurial culture, short decision paths and focus on solutions that create visible results.

Head of Compliance – help us build a bank Europe can trust

We are looking for a Head of Compliance who sees regulation as part of how a bank is built, and part of its culture.

As a senior professional you are to become our Head of Compliance and Data Protection Responsible. Someone who knows the craft inside out, and would - if faced with a choice - choose to shape a smarter, leaner and specific compliance function over a more broad based big-bank machine.

As part of our second line of defence, you lead the Compliance function with overall responsibility for identifying, assessing, monitoring, advising on and reporting on compliance and data risks.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the governance and compliance culture of a fast-growing bank at an early stage. You work closely with Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and your judgement directly influences how we grow across Denmark, and the rest of the EU. If you pair deep regulatory expertise with integrity and a commercial mindset, this is a place where you can make a real difference.

What you will be doing

Compliance framework & monitoring

• You run and ensure timely development of our effective compliance framework (incl. Compliance AI) based on the bank’s business model and risk appetite, including the annual compliance risk assessment, the multi-year compliance review plan and the Compliance Procedure.

• You review and monitor the effectiveness of the bank’s methods and procedures across all areas relevant to financial regulation – including financial crime prevention (AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC), credit, DORA, GDPR, solvency and capital (CRR/CRD), PSD2/PSD3 and MiCA.

• You report regularly to Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and escalate significant findings, warnings or concerns when compliance risks or incidents arise.

Regulation & business development

• You monitor new and updated regulation, assess its impact on the bank and advise on implementation together with Legal.

• You take part in our business development process: reviewing new products, assessing new outsourcing and overseeing product governance.

• You take part in meetings with the Danish FSA and other supervisory authorities, and follow up on any remediation.

Data protection

• You take on the role as kompasbank’s Data Protection Responsible: the contact point for data protection authorities and data subjects, handling breach reporting and access requests, and advising on data processing agreements, transfer impact assessments and DPIAs.

Governance & culture

• You own our whistleblower scheme and case handling.

• You advise on the Remuneration Policy and supporting Executive Management on investor relations and equity and debt financing.

• You build a strong risk and compliance culture through training and awareness, and making sure the Compliance function has the resources it needs.

• Working closely with Risk Management to coordinate second-line reviews and risk assessments.

What we expect from you

• Legal background: A law degree (cand.jur., cand.merc.jur. or equivalent) and 10+ years of experience in financial services, with solid experience from a bank, a law firm, a fintech or a supervisory authority.

• Compliance expertise: Proven experience leading or holding a senior role in a compliance function in a regulated financial institution.

• Regulatory knowledge: Strong analytical capability within Danish and EU financial regulation, procedures and products; knowledge of the Danish Financial Business Act and Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks, etc., AML/CTF, DORA and MiCA is a strong plus.

• Data protection: Knowledge of GDPR and data protection practice in a regulated environment; experience from a data protection role is a strong plus.

• Collaboration and communication: You build strong relationships across the bank and explain complex regulation clearly to colleagues, management and regulators.

As Head of Compliance is a key function, the position is subject to a fit & proper assessment by kompasbank and the Danish FSA. You must therefore be able to document sufficient knowledge, experience and a good reputation, and have no criminal record or ongoing insolvency proceedings that could affect your suitability.

What we offer

• A key leadership role with real influence and a direct line to Executive Management and the Board.

• A high-energy, collaborative work culture built on trust, humor, ambition, and innovation.

• Competitive salary, attractive pension scheme, six weeks of paid holiday, and comprehensive health insurance.

• 60+ skilled, ambitious, and friendly colleagues.

• A modern office in beautiful green surroundings in Vedbæk, north of Copenhagen.

• Ongoing learning and development opportunities.

About kompasbank

Europe runs on small and medium-sized businesses. SMEs make up 99% of all EU companies, employ around 100 million people and generate more than half of Europe’s GDP. Yet they are the part of the economy that the financial system serves worst: too complex for automated retail credit, too small to be worth a traditional corporate bank’s attention. The Draghi report on European competitiveness was blunt. Europe is falling behind the US and China in growth, productivity and technology, and fragmented, slow-moving capital is a central reason why. Europe will not become relevant again through a handful of champions alone. It needs thousands of ambitious mid-sized companies that can get financing, move money domestically and internationally, and scale across borders as easily as their American competitors. That is where kompasbank stands. Built on a full EU banking licence, we bank European SMEs properly, with serious service, data excellence and the regulatory rigour that lets us say yes where others say no.

We’re a cloud-native neobank with no legacy systems and no silos. Since opening our doors in August 2021, we’ve grown fast, expanding across Denmark, Germany and Spain, with a growth rate of more than 1,150% and top rankings on the Sifted lists – and we were named Best Bank for SMEs – Denmark 2024 by FDI Insider.

Job Description

At Netcompany, we are looking for both newly graduated candidates with a relevant master’s degree – or equivalent experience – who want to work as IT Consultants at the intersection of technology, business, and people. Do you want to help develop some of Denmark’s most complex and business-critical IT solutions, where software development, project management, and close client collaboration are central parts of everyday work?

Responsibilities and technologies

As an IT Consultant, you help translate client needs into the right technical solution. We choose the technologies that best fit each project and client. As a result, you should enjoy working across a variety of technologies and domains, while continuously expanding your knowledge and expertise.

A large part of our projects is based on web technologies such as Angular or React, and Java or C# on either a Java or .NET platform. In addition, we work with a wide range of standard platforms including Microsoft, Salesforce, IBM, Oracle, Adobe, Snowflake, Guidewire, and others.

As an IT Consultant, you contribute to all parts of system development with a focus on technical tasks. Your responsibilities will vary from project to project and evolve over time, but your responsibilites will typically include:

• Setting up and developing frameworks and integrations.

• Implementing features in user interfaces.

• Configuring and developing extensions for standard platforms.

• Automating business processes, for example through batch jobs.

• Developing tools and scripts for migrating large volumes of data.

You will join a team with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and areas of expertise. What we all have in common is a technical mindset and shared ambition to build the best possible IT solutions together.

Our projects include some of Denmark’s most innovative and mission-critical IT initiatives across the public and private sectors, meaning you will help shape and improve everyday life for a large part of society.

About you

We expect you to hold a masters's degree in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are a recent graduate or have a couple of years of experience – most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Possess strong technical skills in object-oriented programming.

• Have a solid understanding of software development and motivated to further develop your skills.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

• Full professional proficiency in Swedish and English (written and spoken) is a must. As you will be working closely with Danish clients and colleagues, you should be able to communicate and collaborate effectively in a Danish work environment.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

Company Description

Are you motivated by helping people and business functions unlock the value of AI in their daily work? Do you thrive in a role where you influence, enable, and drive change across a large international organisation?

As our new AI Business Enablement Lead, you will play a key role in accelerating AI adoption across JYSK. Based at our Head Office in Aarhus, you will work closely with business leaders and colleagues across functions to turn AI opportunities into practical solutions that create value.

This is a unique opportunity to join a newly established AI function and shape how AI becomes part of the way we work. As the first person in this role, you will help build the foundation for future growth while working closely with the Central AI team and stakeholders across the business.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

At JYSK, we believe that dedication creates opportunities. We offer you a role with a high degree of responsibility, visibility, and influence across the organisation. You will join a company where decisions are made quickly, ideas are welcomed, and colleagues work together with trust, respect, and a shared ambition to improve how we do business.

You will become part of a growing AI function that supports colleagues across JYSK, helping business areas build confidence and capability in using AI. At the same time, you will have excellent opportunities for both professional and personal development in an international environment.

As our first recruit in this new AI function, you will set the benchmark. For the right candidate with a strong, proactive mindset, this role offers a clear path to grow into leading our future team of AI Business Enablement Specialists.

Furthermore, we offer you:

• A unique opportunity to shape and drive AI adoption across JYSK

• Significant exposure to senior stakeholders and business leaders across functions

• Close collaboration with AI specialists, engineers, and data professionals

• A workplace built on trust, empowerment, and freedom with responsibility

• A modern Head Office environment in Aarhus with a strong team culture

• Attractive employee benefits, social activities, and staff discounts

• Opportunities for continuous learning, development, and future career growth

WHAT YOUR NEXT JOB WILL BE ABOUT

jobs.occupation: PhD position in adult clinical psychology/psychotherapy research: Treatments for Complex PTSD
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  
 
 The position and the project
 The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.
 
 Duties and responsibilities
 The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

  The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.
 
 Supervision and research group
 The PhD-student will be part of a research group at the Department of Psychology conducting psychological and psychiatric research on psychotherapy and trauma.
 
 Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to master’s level related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Psychology. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we may obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency.
 
 Place of employment
 The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (https://psychology.ku.dk/) is a vibrant, inclusive workplace hosting a large group of faculty, post docs and PhD-students. The research of the department covers a wide range of topics and methodologies and has an international work environment.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competence to change society for the better. 	
• Energizing global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact   For more on the faculty strategy, see: https://socialsciences.ku.dk/.
 
 The recruitment process
 Further information on the recruitment process at University of Copenhagen can be found here:  https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. For more on the diverse working place environment at the University and the University’s participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, see https://employment.ku.dk/working-at-ucph/eu-charter-for-researchers/
 
 International applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about these services as well as information on entering and working in Denmark here: https://ism.ku.dk/
 
 Contact information
 We encourage you to first consult our website, where most questions concerning the recruitment process as well as the academic content and structure of the PhD programme are answered:

  Structure of the PhD programme

  How to obtain a PhD scholarship.

  For information about the project and the position, please contact PI Assistant Professor Sara Kerstine Kaya Nielsen, sara.nielsen@psy.ku.dk. Information about the recruitment process is available from HR, e-mail: HR-SOENDRE@adm.ku.dk Please refer to ID number: 211-2569/26-2H
 
 How to apply
 Submit a complete application at our online portal. Click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of the page to apply. The documents must be in Adobe PDF or Word.  

  Your application must be written in English and include the following documents:

   	
• Motivated application 	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diploma (master and bachelor) 	
• Other relevant material   
 The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026.
 Applications or enclosures received thereafter will not be considered.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in environmental microbial ecology
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year, fixed-term postdoctoral position in environmental microbial ecology, starting 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is part of a project funded by the Villum Foundation's Villum Experiment programme.

The project
Electrically conductive iron minerals are widespread in anoxic aquatic sediments, yet we know little about the microorganisms that live on them. The project aims to characterize the phylogenetic identity and ecophysiology of microorganisms associated with these minerals. We hypothesize that, by facilitating extracellular electron transfer, the minerals provide a distinct niche that selectively enriches electroactive microorganisms relative to the surrounding sediment.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two–year position from 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 31 January, 2029.

Job description
You will identify, visualize and characterize bacterial and archaeal cells associated with iron minerals by combining fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and correlative imaging, DNA- and/or RNA-based omics, and stable isotope incubation experiments. You will have considerable freedom to shape the methodological approach and to develop your own ideas within the project framework. Project collaborators in Germany will contribute chemical characterization of the minerals, giving you the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary team. Participation in supervision of BSc., MSc. and PhD students and possibly some classroom teaching is also expected.

Your profile
You hold a PhD in biology, earth and environmental science, biotechnology or a related field (or expect to complete it before the start date), and you have a research background in microbiology or microbial ecology.

Essentials:

• Experience with advanced microscopy and/or molecular microbial ecology methods.
• Interest in microbial physiology and electromicrobiology.
• A systematic approach to method development and testing.
• A publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, relative to your career stage.
• Very good written and oral communication skills in English.
Desirable:

• Experience with FISH, correlative microscopy, stable isotope probing, or omics data analysis.
• Experience working with sediment or other environmental samples.
• Experience with microbial physiology and/or electromicrobiology.
• If you are excited about the project but your experience does not match every point, we still encourage you to apply.
At the Department of Biology, we value a collegial and inclusive working environment and place strong emphasis on good relationships among colleagues and students. We welcome colleagues who bring an open, constructive and collaborative approach.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (Aarhus University) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the department. The Section for Microbiology (https://bio.au.dk/en/about-biology/sections/microbiology) employs 12 associate and full professors and offers a vibrant, international research environment for studying microbial physiology, evolution, ecology, and biogeochemistry. The section integrates basic and applied research, addressing the functions, eco-physiology, and evolution of microorganisms in natural and biotechnological systems. The section has well-equipped laboratories, a permanent support staff of highly skilled laboratory technicians, and access to advanced imaging facilities on the AU campus.

What we offer
• A two-year position in a stimulating, international research environment
• Access to state-of-the-art laboratories and imaging facilities.
• A work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion.
• A work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities.
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Aarhus University, and the place of employment is Section for Microbiology within the Department of Biology (https://bio.au.dk/en/), Aarhus University, Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
Applicants seeking further information are invited to contact Assoc. Prof. Kasper Urup Kjeldsen at AU (kasperuk@bio.au.dk).

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 29 November, 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Om Aarhus Universitet

Aarhus Universitet er et fagligt bredt og forskningsintensivt universitet med høj kvalitet i uddannelse og forskning, og et stærkt engagement i samfundsudviklingen nationalt og globalt. Universitetet tilbyder et inspirerende uddannelses- og forskningsmiljø for 37.500 studerende og 9.000 medarbejdere med en årlig omsætning på 8,9 mia. kr. Læs mere på www.au.dk

Join us in this role where you’ll be working as a Senior Operational Technology (OT) Security Officer to strengthen the security, resilience, and compliance of Ørsted Bioenergy. In this role, you will act as a trusted security lead across OT, IT, engineering, and operations, helping protect critical systems while enabling safe, reliable, and efficient operations. Further more we are partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability – and we “translate” technical cyber risk into clear business, safety, and operational impact requirements. We operate in complex, multi-site, international, or safety-critical operational environments.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of OT Security where you, together with your colleagues, will be working on Ørsted Danish powerplant. Our task is to protect the powerplants ability to produce electricity and heat against hacker attacks. So you need to understand Danish, when you’re out on the powerplants. We are a small team of 4 persons located in Jutland (Jylland) who works together and strive in helping each other in our daily tasks. As a team, we have an open and direct commutation where we discuss ideas strategy and ideas to develop and mature our solutions, so they are robust and they deal with the reality we face.

You’ll play an important role in:

• leading the development and continuous improvement of OT security governance, policies, standards, and procedures

• assessing, managing, and reducing cyber risk across OT environments, including industrial control systems, SCADA, PLCs, IIoT, and related networks

• defining and supporting secure OT architecture, including network segmentation, secure remote access, asset visibility, access control, logging, monitoring, and vulnerability management

• conducting OT security risk assessments, gap analyses, and maturity reviews aligned with recognised frameworks e.g. Danish legislation “Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren”, IEC 62443, ISO 27001 and relevant regulatory requirements

• partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability requirements

• driving OT security awareness and training for technical and operational teams.

To succeed in the role, you:

• hold a relevant degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Technology, Automation, or equivalent practical experience

• understand and know how to operate in ICS systems and possess understanding of 24/7 production environment

• are familiar with IT networks like, Purdue model, firewall, data diodes etc.

• hold knowledge about EIC 62433, ISO 27001 and "Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren" as we operate according to this legislation

• are a good team player and at the same are strong on being responsible of incl. conducting your own tasks – you need to be fluent in both Danish and English language as well due to nature our stake holder landscape

• are flexible - both in terms of taking on tasks outside your comfortzone, being curious in learning new areas and assist your team in whatever tasks are needed.

Some travel within Denmark to the different sites must be expected in the this role.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application and CV to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr55,040.00- kr82,560.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11 % contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3 % holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and well-being programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, and internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**Pre-employment background check:

**This position requires a background check as part of the hiring process and the offer is dependent on the outcome of this check. You will receive more information during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

jobs.description:
The Department of Chemistry invites applicants for a 2-year postdoc position within Theoretical Catalysis under the ERC-SyG DEMI, starting from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  DEMI (Directed Evolution of Metastable Electrocatalyst Interfaces for Energy Conversion) is an ERC Synergy Grant funded by the European Research Council Executive Agency.

  In the Theoretical Catalysis group, we aim to provide a deeper understanding of catalytic processes and catalytic materials by atomic scale simulations. We have a special interest in electrocatalytic reactions and high entropy materials, and the methods include DFT-simulations, machine learning potentials, Monte Carlo simulations and statistical analysis. We enjoy a close collaboration with experimental groups, both at the department and other universities in Denmark and abroad. The DEMI project is a collaboration with research groups from University of Bern, Ruhr University Bochum and Helmholtz-Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg.

  The Theoretical Catalysis group is part of Center for High Entropy Alloy Catalysis.

  The successful candidate holds a Ph.D. in computational chemistry, DFT-simulations, physical modelling or a similar background. Experience with theoretical catalysis or electrocatalysis is a benefit.

  The postdoc’s duty is primarily research within Theoretical Catalysis but may include performance of other duties.

  Further information on the Department is linked at www.chem.ku.dk. Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Jan Rossmeisl, phone +4550719584 or email: jan.rossmeisl@chem.ku.dk.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Consultancy in Otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery combined with a clinical professorship in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology
jobs.description:
A clinical position as consultant of Otorhinolaryngology at the Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical professor in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the professorship and the consultancy.

The advertisement for the professorship is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About the department

The Department of Otorhinolaryngology and Audiology is responsible for the full spectrum of diagnostics and treatment within the ENT and audiological fields, encompassing both general patient care and highly specialized services. A total of more than 100 clinically active physicians is employed within the department. In addition, there is a high level of research activity, including among the clinical staff. The department currently has five formally affiliated professors, three of whom are clinical professors in otorhinolaryngology. As a university hospital department, it also has teaching obligations at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including for healthcare professionals beyond the medical field of both the primary and secondary health sector.

Clinical functions and focus areas of the department

The consultant position in head and neck surgery requires a strong interest and proven surgical expertise within malignant head and neck surgery. The ideal candidate will demonstrate solid experience in teaching and research, including involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate education, as well as supervision of PhD students. Emphasis is placed on candidates with a robust, long-standing, and continuous research background. The candidate is expected to have extensive knowledge and research experience with head and neck cancer epidemiology and documented experience with national registries and particularly with HPV-driven head and neck cancer. A broad knowledge of benign ENT conditions is also expected. Further the candidate should be active and involved in thyroid cancer research.

The position offers significant opportunities for further specialization and skill development within advanced surgical techniques, including the potential for training in robotic surgery. The consultant will also be expected to take on administrative responsibilities such as patient triage and task coordination.

As the department provides highly specialized ENT services at a university level, applicants must have documented surgical experience and a demonstrated research interest.

Applicants must submit documentation of board certification in Otorhinolaryngology. According to the regulations of the Capital Region of Denmark, applicants must have held a specialist certification for at least five years to be appointed as a consultant at Rigshospitalet, unless an exemption is granted. Furthermore, applicants must provide evidence of clinical experience within head and neck surgery, as well as documentation of scientific and educational activities.

Strong collaboration skills are essential, including the ability to work professionally and constructively in interdisciplinary teams.

Organizationally, the consultant will report to the Head of Department. For professional matters related specifically to head and neck surgery, reference will be made to the lead consultant in that subspecialty.

We offer a dynamic and rewarding position in a busy and active department housed in brand-new, state-of-the-art facilities. The position includes excellent opportunities for involvement in research and clinical development.

Work Schedule: The position includes on-call duty (approximately every 14 days), shared equally among the department’s consultants.

Salary and terms of employment will follow the applicable collective agreement.

Please note: The position is subject to regulations requiring a child protection certificate ("børneattest"). Employment is contingent upon the ability to present a clean certificate.

Research and teaching

With the establishment of the new position as Consultant in Otorhinolaryngology and Clinical Professor in Oto-rhino-laryngology with special focus on Head & Neck Surgery, the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology seek to significantly strengthen leadership and strategic development within clinical research and teaching. The professorship is conceived as a pivotal academic and clinical role that will unify and advance research activities across the specialty, with a particular emphasis on translational and interdisciplinary head and neck research.

The position will serve as an academic anchor not only for Rigshospitalet but also for Nordsjællands Hospital and, more broadly, for Region Østdanmark (RØST), with the explicit ambition of fostering coordinated research efforts across Eastern Denmark. The clinical professor is expected to provide academic leadership, facilitate collaboration between hospital departments and regional research environments, and contribute to the development of shared research strategies and priorities across institutions.

In research, the position entails responsibility for initiating, leading, and consolidating high-quality clinical and translational research programmes within head and neck surgery and related disciplines. This includes strengthening existing research groups, promoting multicentre and cross-regional studies, supporting early-career researchers, and ensuring integration of research activities across hospitals within RØST. The professor will play a key role in attracting external funding, enhancing national and international visibility, and embedding research as a core component of clinical practice throughout Eastern Denmark.

In teaching, the position carries responsibility for academic leadership in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education within otorhinolaryngology and head and neck surgery. The professor will contribute to curriculum development, pedagogical innovation, and supervision at all levels, ensuring alignment between clinical training, academic standards, and regional workforce needs. Teaching activities will be coordinated across clinical sites, thereby supporting a unified and high-quality educational environment for medical students, residents, and fellows within RØST.

Overall, the position is designed to function as a unifying professorship that integrates research, teaching, and clinical excellence across Nordsjællands Hospital, the wider hospital network in RØST, and academic partners, thereby strengthening the academic foundation and future development of the specialty across Eastern Denmark.

Qualifications

Applicants must be board-certified specialist in Oto-rhino-laryngology.

Conditions

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the professorship) and to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the professorship. Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as consultants at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

Salary and Employment Conditions

The position is subject to the Collective Agreement for Specialist Doctors and Consultant Physicians (Overlæger) and the applicable Working Time Agreement between the Danish Regions and the relevant medical professional organization.

Detailed information on employment conditions, collective agreements, and salary levels can be found here:

• Collective Agreement: https://laeger.dk/foreninger/overlaegeforeningen/ok26-overlaegeforeningen

• Collective Agreement (PDF): https://laeger.dk/media/15odzzl1/overenskomst-for-speciallaeger-og-overlaeger-2026.pdf

• Salary information: https://www.regionh.dk/om-region-hovedstaden/fakta/arbejdsplads/sider/startloen.aspx

As clinical professor at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology, Rigshospitalet. Additional support and details on the working conditions must be negotiated with the head of the Department of ORL, Head and neck sugery and audiology,Rigshospitalet.

Application procedure

The application must include the following:

• 
Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• 
Copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Otorhinolaryngology.

• 
A description of how the applicant is qualified as

• 
Clinical expert

• 
Communicator

• 
Collaborator

• 
Manager/administrator/organizer

• 
Health advocate

• 
Scholar/researcher/teacher

• 
Professional

For more information, please refer to Sundhedsstyrelsen: The Seven Roles of Physicians.

The closing date for applications is 8. November 2026.

Further information

For further information please contact Head of Department Mads Klokker tel. + 45 3545 6033, or email: mads.klokker@regionh.dk

**Job Description

**Do you want to define the evaluation methodology and technical requirements that underpin effective AI evaluation and monitoring within the business at one of the leading financial institutions in the Nordics?

Join Danske Bank's newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management. As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will hold a 1st Line of Defence role with clear ownership of the technical methodologies used to evaluate AI models and AI-enabled solutions, and of the technical requirements for the platforms that support their evaluation and ongoing monitoring. You will translate business-owned risk and control needs into clear methods, metrics, data, evidence, traceability and platform capabilities that can be implemented consistently across the Bank's technology landscape.

This is a unique opportunity to shape a consistent, scalable and evidence-based capability through which the business identifies, evaluates, monitors and manages AI model risk.

This role can be based in Copenhagen, Denmark, Vilnius, Lithuania, Warsaw, Poland, Stockholm, Sweden or Helsinki, Finland.

**What You Will Be Doing

**The AI Model Assessment team is a business-owned control capability that performs evidence-based assessments of AI models and AI-enabled solutions across the Bank. We work with business owners, developers, engineers and platform teams to understand how solutions operate, define the evidence required for assessment, and establish the evaluation and monitoring capabilities needed to identify, assess and manage model risk where it arises.

Our mission is to enable responsible innovation by providing the business with a consistent and scalable framework for evaluating AI systems, monitoring their performance and risk, and demonstrating that appropriate controls are operating effectively.

As AI Evaluation Methodology & Platform Requirements Lead, you will own the evaluation methodology and define the technical requirements for the platforms, tooling and data capabilities used by the 1st Line of Defence to evaluate and monitor AI models and AI-enabled solutions. Your mandate is to ensure that the business has robust, implementable and auditable means to assess its AI risks and controls. Your focus will be on specifying what the evaluation and monitoring capability must deliver rather than owning software development or platform operations.

You will work closely with the independent 2nd Line AI model risk function, which sets the overarching risk framework and provides oversight and constructive challenge. You will translate that framework into practical evaluation methodologies, technical requirements and business-owned controls, provide transparent evidence of how requirements are implemented, and support the resolution of identified gaps.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• Owning, developing and maintaining the methodology for evaluating AI models and AI-enabled solutions, including evaluation objectives, test approaches, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Defining the functional and technical requirements for evaluation and monitoring platforms that enable risk management, including data ingestion, test execution, metric calculation, observability, evidence capture, reporting, access controls and auditability.

• Translating model risk, business and assessment requirements into reusable evaluation methods, representative datasets, metrics, thresholds, monitoring indicators and structured evidence requirements.

• Determining how AI system architectures, components, dependencies and data flows affect evaluation scope, test design, monitoring coverage and the technical capabilities required from supporting platforms.

• Defining platform-agnostic requirements that support evaluation and monitoring across environments such as AWS Bedrock and AgentCore, Databricks, Azure OpenAI and embedded third-party AI platforms.

• Setting requirements for reproducibility and end-to-end traceability across models, prompts, datasets, configurations, system components, evaluation results, monitoring signals and changes over time.

• Prioritising opportunities to standardise and automate evaluation and monitoring activities, and working with evaluators, platform owners and engineers to convert approved control requirements into practical platform capabilities.

• Engaging with the Second Line model risk function to interpret applicable requirements, demonstrate how they are operationalised, respond to constructive challenge, and ensure that evaluation and monitoring evidence supports effective independent oversight.

**About You

**An experienced AI evaluation, model risk, data, architecture or platform professional who can establish rigorous evaluation methodologies and turn business risk and control needs into clear, implementable technical requirements for enterprise platforms and tooling.

You have:

• Proven experience designing or governing AI/ML evaluation methodologies, including test objectives, datasets, metrics, thresholds, acceptance criteria and evidence standards.

• Experience translating evaluation, monitoring, risk and control needs into functional and technical requirements for platforms, tooling, data pipelines and reporting capabilities.

• Experience with AI/ML evaluation, business-owned model risk management and controls, technical assurance, MLOps, LLMOps, AI platforms or AI observability.

• Familiarity with cloud AI services or enterprise AI platforms; experience with AWS Bedrock or AgentCore, Databricks or Mosaic AI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable platforms is an advantage.

• Strong understanding of evaluation and monitoring principles, including representative datasets, experiment configuration, metric design, regression testing, monitoring indicators, traceability and evidence capture.

• Ability to distinguish methodology and requirements ownership from platform implementation, while collaborating effectively with engineers and platform owners. Python or similar tools for analysis, prototyping or investigation are an advantage, but software development is not the primary focus of the role.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to articulate evaluation, monitoring, risk and control requirements across business, assessment, platform, engineering, architecture, data and risk functions.

Experience with AI evaluation or observability technologies, for example Phoenix or comparable tools, is an advantage but is not a prerequisite.

**What We Offer You

**You will join the newly established AI Model Assessment team in Business Controls & Product Management, helping build the Bank's consistent and scalable business-owned capability for AI evaluation, monitoring and model risk management.

The team combines technical AI evaluation expertise with model risk management and works across the Bank's AI initiatives. In this role, you will connect evaluators with platform, engineering, architecture and data teams by defining the methods and technical requirements their solutions must support, ensuring that risk ownership and control evidence remain anchored in the business.

If hired in Lithuania, your monthly salary would range from 4320 EUR to 6480 EUR gross (based on your competencies relevant for the job).

Additionally, each Danske Bank employee receives employee benefits package which includes:

• Growth opportunities: professional & supportive team, e-learnings, numerous development programs; (incl. professional certificates); 100+ professions for internal mobility opportunities.

• Health & Well-being: a diverse, inclusive, work & life balance work environment; additional health insurance; mental well-being practices; partial psychologist counselling compensation; silence and sleep zones at the office; game rooms.

• Hybrid working conditions: Work from home up to two days a week; home office budget (after the probation period); modern Danske Campus workplace developed with anthropologist for the best employee experience.

• Additional days of leave: for rest, health, volunteering, exams in higher education institutions, and other important activities. Moreover, for seniority with Danske Bank.

• Monetary compensation package: accidents & critical diseases insurance; financial support in case of unfortunate events, travel insurance; IIIrd Pillar Pension Fund contribution.

See all the benefits HERE**.

**Your job function (position) in the job contract will be AI Science

**Are you ready for the next step?

**If you are passionate about defining robust AI evaluation methodologies and the technical requirements for scalable evaluation and monitoring platforms that support effective business ownership of AI risk, we would love to hear from you.

For questions about the role, please contact Khaled Alizai, Head of AI Model Assessment at khali@danskebank.dk. We are screening the applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply.

Join us and help build the business-owned foundation for effective AI model evaluation, monitoring and risk management at Danske Bank.

Uni-Tankers

AI Lead

Shape the technical future of AI at Uni-Tankers

At Uni-Tankers, we see AI as an opportunity to work smarter, make better decisions, and create greater value across the business. We are looking for an AI Solutions Architect/Engineer who can turn business needs and enterprise data into secure, reliable, and practical AI solutions.

As our first AI specialist, you will have a unique opportunity to help shape how AI is designed, developed, and applied across Uni-Tankers. You will be hands-on in building agents, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions. This role is for someone who enjoys building the solutions that empower the organization in a meaningful way.

Reporting to Thomas Thomsen, CFO, you will play a key role in connecting business needs, data, and technology. You will work closely with colleagues across the organization, including our Business Intelligence Controller, to make effective use of enterprise data and take AI solutions from early ideas into secure and maintainable production use.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Understanding business needs and translating them into AI solutions

• Designing, building, testing, and deploying AI agents and applications

• Collaborating with stakeholders, partners, and consultants while retaining technical ownership

• Embedding security, governance, compliance, and responsible AI into solutions from day one

• Contributing to the AI roadmap by prioritizing opportunities based on impact and feasibility

Are you the one to build our AI foundation?

We are looking for someone who combines technical capabilities with curiosity, ownership, and business understanding.

You may have a background in software engineering, data engineering, cloud architecture, machine learning engineering, applied AI, solution architecture, or a related field. Your exact background is less important than your ability to design, build, and deliver AI solutions that work reliably in practice.

You are comfortable moving between architecture and implementation. You can discuss a business challenge with a non-technical colleague, translate it into a technical solution, and then contribute directly to building and operating that solution.

You likely:

• Experience delivering AI, data, or software solutions from concept to production

• Experience with Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Foundry, including security, governance, and compliance

• Solid understanding of data engineering, ETL processes, data lakes, APIs, and systems integration

• Ability to make sound technical decisions balancing security, reliability, performance, maintainability, user experience, and cost

• Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical topics into clear business recommendations

• Experience in business process optimization and identifying opportunities for improvement

• A proactive and curious mindset, combining technical skills with the ability to understand business needs across functions

Experience with Microsoft Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Azure, Power Platform, Microsoft Fabric, OneLake, or similar technologies would be an advantage.  More importantly, you have a demonstrated ability to deliver real-world AI, data, or software solutions, regardless of platform or academic background.

Not checking every box?

You do not need to meet every requirement to do well in this role. AI technologies continue to develop rapidly, and we value people who can learn, adapt, and apply solid technical principles across different platforms.

If the opportunity excites you and you believe you can make a meaningful contribution, we welcome your application.

What you can look forward to

At Uni-Tankers, people make the difference. You will join a collaborative culture built on trust, ownership, and teamwork.

In this role, you will have a unique opportunity to help establish our technical AI foundation and shape how AI is applied across the organization. You will work closely with colleagues across functions and locations, turning business needs, technology, and data into practical solutions that create value for both the business and the people behind it.

You will have room to shape technical decisions, development practices, architecture, and future priorities while remaining close to hands-on delivery.

In return, we offer:

• An international environment with knowledgeable and dedicated colleagues

• A high degree of influence and ownership in a strategically important area

• The opportunity to build and implement solutions rather than only advise on them

• Close collaboration with colleagues working with data, technology, operations, and business development

• Attractive employee benefits, including pension, health insurance, and lunch arrangement

• Social activities and events throughout the year

• Modern office facilities at our headquarters in Middelfart.

Application

We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At IST, we're building the cloud platform that powers educational solutions used by more than five million users across Europe. Unlike most cloud teams, we run our own cloud — on our own hardware, in our own data center. That means the abstraction stops with us: when a node misbehaves, there's no support ticket to a hyperscaler.

There's a rack, and someone who knows it.

We're looking for a Cloud Engineer who finds that appealing rather than daunting.

About the role

As a Cloud Engineer, you'll help design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform — from the automation and orchestration layers our developers build on, all the way down to the switches, servers and cabling that carry it. You'll do this together with our Cloud Engineering team, architects, developers and stakeholders, whether the work happens at a keyboard or in a rack.

In practice, around a quarter of your time will be spent physically on site in the data center. Not as a separate duty, but as a natural part of the work: expanding capacity for a new cluster the team has just automated, replacing a switch that's been throwing errors in your own monitoring, tracing a network issue that turns out to be a cable rather than a config. Owning the platform end to end is what makes this role different from a pure cloud position.

The role is based at our office in Roskilde, Denmark, with the primary data center within reach. Some travel is required, primarily to our office in Växjö, Sweden.

What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. We apply an office-first policy, and given the hands-on nature of this role, regular physical presence at the office and in the datacenter is part of the job. Within that framework, there's room for flexibility on the days where your work doesn't require you on site.

You'll join an international and collaborative environment where you'll have real ownership, influence over strategic technology decisions, and the chance to help shape the future of learning.
