Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions  Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  Information on the department can be found at: http://www.sund.ku.dk/. 

  Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

  The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

  The successful candidate will:

   	
• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes. 	
• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications. 	
• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets. 	
• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems. 	
• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks. 	
• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making. 	
• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.  	
• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO. 	
• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group. 	
• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health. 	
• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets. 	
• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health. 	
• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.   The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

  The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• research, including publication/academic dissemination 	
• research-based teaching  	
• sharing knowledge with society  	
• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors    The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal. 

  After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

  Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area  	
• research experience within the field of the position    The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact. 

  The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills. 

  Salary and employment conditions
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is permanent. 

  Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. 

  There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions 
 For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application 
 The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents: 

   	
• Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas) 	
• A complete list of publications  	
• Research plan (2-4 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment  	
• Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)   Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.

  Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation. 

  The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply. 

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.

Tech-first. Ego-free. User-obsessed.

Over one million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes. We automate tax tracking, surface deductions people didn't know they had, and give users the insights they need to make better financial decisions — all directly connected to the Danish tax authority.

We're an independent company of around 50 people based in Copenhagen, with a 4.7-star rating and a simple mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

About the role

Path to Plus is the engine that converts users into paying members and keeps them there. As a Backend Engineer on this team, you'll be building and shipping features as part of a cross-functional product team with a direct commercial mission — not executing on a spec handed down to you, but helping shape what gets built and why.

This is a product engineering role. The team owns the problem, not just the delivery. That means getting involved before requirements are written, connecting your technical work to user and business outcomes, and iterating based on real feedback. You'll work closely with engineering leadership — not as a follower, but as a collaborator who contributes to the plan. If you've worked that way before — or you're actively looking to grow into it — this is the right environment.

Who we're looking for

You're a backend engineer with solid production experience who takes reliability and code quality seriously. You understand that the systems you work on affect the business directly, and you can move fast without cutting corners.

You've worked in a product team where engineers own outcomes, not just output — or you're genuinely looking to make that move. Either way, you know the difference.

You can look at a codebase, understand its strengths and weak spots, and work to make it better over time — without needing a perfect plan before you start. You take ownership, care about leaving code better than you found it, and are realistic about how to make that happen in a production environment.

What you'll do

• 
Ship features end-to-end as part of the team's product cycle, from problem shaping to production.

• 
Multi-broker architecture. Stock tax support is live. The next challenge is redesigning the current model to support multiple brokers — a real architectural problem you'll be part of solving.

• 
Observability. You'll help us own the health of critical business flows and catch issues before users do.

• 
Azure migration. We're migrating our systems in the coming months. Cloud architecture thinking will be an active part of the role.

• 
Tech debt on the roadmap. We believe tech debt belongs on the roadmap, not hidden under it. You'll help identify, prioritise, and plan for it alongside the team.

Must-have

• 
Solid experience with Java, JUnit, and Spring Boot. This is your expertise.

• 
Working knowledge of RabbitMQ or a comparable message broker.

• 
Familiarity with MySQL and relational data modelling.

• 
Genuine enthusiasm for AI. You use AI tools daily and are always looking for new ways to apply them. This is an engineering-wide expectation at Skatteguiden, not a nice-to-have.

• 
Experience in a product team with genuine ownership — where the team drove its own goals and collaborated cross-functionally to get there.

Nice-to-have

• 
Experience with Kubernetes, Argo, GitHub Actions, Grafana and Loki.

• 
Experience operating services in Azure — understanding how your code runs in production, optimising resources, and thinking about cost without needing to own the infrastructure.

Why join us

Real responsibility from day one. You're joining a team with a full pipeline and a clear commercial mission — your work will have a visible impact quickly.

A company serious about engineering quality. We're actively investing in elevating engineering practices across the organisation. You'll be part of that, not just a passenger.

Solid company. Independent, profitable, growing. No VC pressure, no bloated roadmap. Just a clear mission and a team that cares.

Good people. We take the work seriously without taking ourselves too seriously. The culture is professional, informal, and genuinely collaborative.

Room to grow. The scope of the work and the team's ambitions mean there's real room to step up.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen. We're an office-first company, and it's a deliberate choice. We're moving fast, we have big ambitions, and we genuinely believe that being physically together is one of the things that makes that possible. Things move quicker when you can turn your chair and talk to someone.

We're a five-minute walk from Rådhuspladsen, stocked with everything from fruit to fizzy drinks to afternoon snacks, and lunch is at Claus Meyer's canteen just across the street — proper food, not an afterthought. If you're putting in a long day, dinner is covered too.

Start: As soon as possible.

Salary: Competitive and based on your experience.

Reporting to: Senior Engineering Manager.

Our hiring process

• 
Screening call with our recruiter (30 min) — online

• 
Technical interview (60 min) — build something together with a Backend Engineer and Senior Engineering Manager — onsite.

• 
Culture conversation with the Senior Engineering Manager and CTO (60 min) — onsite

• 
Meet the CEO (30 min) — onsite

Job Description

At Netcompany, we are looking for recent graduates with a bachelor’s degree who want a challenging, social and developing start to their career as an Associate Consultant. Are you excited by the opportunity to work on complex IT solutions that make a real impact, while combining hands-on development with project delivery and close client interaction?

The Associate Consultant role exists across both Consulting and Application Services. The main difference lies in how you work with clients and solutions, and which setup fits your interests best. Responsibilities & technologies

As an Associate Consultant at Netcompany, you will contribute to translating customer needs into the right technical solutions. Depending on the project and customer, you may become part of either our Application Services or Consulting business area. In both areas, you will work closely with exciting customers and colleagues to develop and deliver high-quality IT solutions. Your work will span different projects, technologies, and domains, giving you the opportunity to continuously expand your knowledge and expertise. We work with a wide range of technologies and platforms, such as .NET, C#, Java, React, Angular, Salesforce, Microsoft, Oracle, Adobe and more.

As an Associate Consultant, you will contribute to all aspects of system development with focus on technical tasks. Your tasks and responsibilities will vary from project to project and evolve over time, but your responsibilities will typically include:

• Customer dialogue and requirements clarification.

• Development of frontend and backend features for customer solutions.

• Setup and development of frameworks, integrations, and extensions for standard platforms.

• Automation of business processes through, for example, batch jobs.

• Development of tools and scripts for data migration and other technical solutions.

About you

We expect you to hold a bachelor's degree or diploma in engineering, computer science, software, IT, or a similar field. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are newly graduated or have a couple of years of experience. Most importantly, you are passionate about taking your IT career to the next level.

• Possess strong IT technical skills within object-oriented programming.

• Have fundamental knowledge of software development and are motivated to develop your competencies.

• Think analytically, show initiative, and work in a structured way.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Send us your application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

At MFT Energy, we innovate energy trading through our people and technology.

Are you curious about how risk is managed in one of the fastest-moving industries in the world? At MFT Energy, we are looking for a Student Risk Analyst who wants to gain hands-on experience working with data and risk management in a dynamic energy trading environment.

The role as a Student Risk Analyst:

You will join our Finance, Risk & Treasury department, where you will be part of our Risk team working alongside experienced colleagues with deep industry expertise. The team works closely with stakeholders across the trading organization to provide transparency on the company’s overall risk profile and support informed decision-making.

In a business characterized by rapidly changing market conditions and significant volatility, the Risk team helps ensure a responsible balance between risk and return across all our trading activities.

In this role, you will work with a wide range of datasets, including trade data and market price data that form the foundation of our risk calculations. Through this work, you will contribute to maintaining reliable risk data and develop a strong understanding of how risk management supports a modern energy trading company.

The position offers a steep learning curve in a fast-paced environment where no two days are the same.

Your key responsibilities:

• Working with large trade and market price datasets to ensure the quality of risk calculations

• Developing data quality checks within our in-house data models

• Improving existing tools and developing new solutions (primarily using SQL, Power BI, Power Automate, and Power Apps)

• Automating tasks related to reporting, data processing and analysis

• Supporting the risk business partners with daily ad hoc tasks and analysis

• Gaining exposure to different types of risks including liquidity, market, credit and operational risk

Your qualifications and personal skills:

• Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Economics, Finance, Mathematics or a similar field.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• Ability to work independently and take initiative

• Coding skills are a plus but not required. The most important thing is an interest in learning, as much of the data work will involve SQL

• Interest in energy markets and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment

• Curious and open-minded approach to learning and problem-solving

Working in MFT Energy

At MFT Energy, we combine a startup mindset with the strength of a global organization. We believe in empowering individuals to make data-driven decisions in a fast-paced environment. We are around 200 employees working out of our headquarters in Scandinavian Center, Aarhus C, and from our international offices in Turkey, Australia, New York, Singapore, Japan, and several remote colleagues working from all over the world.

We offer:

• A 15–20-hour student position with flexibility to plan your working hours around your studies

• A role where you will take ownership of your tasks while working closely with experienced colleagues who are always ready to support and spar with you

• An international and fast-moving environment where things develop quickly and you will continuously learn new things

• A strong student community and plenty of social activities, such as CrossFit, running club, Friday bars, team events, and more

• A culture where we enjoy celebrating both big and small successes - and luckily, we have many reasons to do so

Make the most of your talent! Join us!

If you think there is a fit between the role and your aspirations, we will be looking forward to receiving your application with a short cover letter and CV. For questions, please write to career@mft-energy.com.

Deadline: We will be screening and interviewing candidates on an ongoing basis.

Start date: As soon as possible.

You will experience a collaborative work environment where knowledge sharing, curiosity and openness is part of everyday life, giving you great opportunities to grow professionally as well as personally.

Did you know? It is safe to say that you will work with the team in Kamstrup, that has the largest number of gadgets in the office!

Besides the best program, we also offer:

• Multiple internship events and weekly internship lunches

• Employee benefits including a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

The applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, but you can expect a response within six weeks. Details about the internship will be agreed upon individually. However, the internship is expected to run from the beginning of February 2027 until the end of June 2027.

Kamstrup Head Quarter is in Stilling south of Aarhus, and bus number 200 takes you right to the door.

In case of questions regarding the position, please contact Functional Lead - Connectivity Technology, Lead Specialist, Jonas Drammestrup Poulsen, on phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

Let’s Talk

jobs.occupation: A Post doc position is available in the Grønbæk Group at Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC),
jobs.description:
We are searching for a skilled and experienced post doc with specific interest in investigating early myeloid disease, clonal haematopoiesis, metabolism and obesity.

  Our research/The group

  The focus of the Grønbæk group is Translational Haematology. The group is affiliated with Biotech Research and Innovation centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen and Rigshospitalet (Central Copenhagen University Hospital). 

  Our overall aim is to understand the molecular mechanisms of haematological cancers and based on this; to design, develop and implement novel, scientifically based, clinical trials, with a strong focus on epigenetic therapies. This is done by bridging between clinical research at Rigshospitalet and the basic cancer biology research at BRIC, and in international collaborations with, among others, the Van Andel Research Institute, Michigan, USA and the Nordic MDS study group.

  Our location at the Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC provides optimal conditions for interaction with the basic scientists at BRIC. The group currently consists of 14 scientists, MD/scientists and students, one clinical research coordinator, 1 research nurse and 2 biomedical laboratory scientists.

   

  The project: Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms.

  The current position is part of a joint project ‘Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms’ together with Professor George Vassiliou, Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom funded by a ‘Molecular Mechanisms Linking Obesity and Cancer (MMLOC)’ grant from the Novo Nordisk foundation, which supports collaborative research projects with the purpose ‘to reverse-translate clinical observations into mechanistic studies that will increase our understanding of how obesity impacts carcinogenesis’.

  Obesity is a global health issue linked to increased risk of cancer, including blood cancers such as myeloid neoplasms (MN). Many MN arise from clonal haematopoiesis (CH)—the abnormal expansion of blood stem cell clones carrying somatic mutations. Haematopoietic stem cells interact with bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), which increases with obesity, which may fuel CH growth and progression to MN. Epidemiological and genetic studies already suggest obesity accelerates CH, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

  This project integrates large-scale population data, clinical trials, and mechanistic mouse studies to investigate these links and explore preventive or therapeutic strategies.

   

  Your job

  The project focuses on translational analyses of live frozen human cells from patient bone marrow (BM)/(BMAT) and blood samples from completed and ongoing clinical trials. We are searching for a skilled post doc who is very interactive and enjoys collaborations with other scientists – including younger scientists and clinician scientists.

  Your tasks will include:

   	
• Process of live frozen patient material from clinical trials including isolation of defined cell populations, and quality control for downstream omics 	
• Perform in-house molecular techniques which may include Proteomics, PCR, ddPCR, and library/sample preparation for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and DNA methylation analyses 	
• Coordinate genomic, transcriptomic, lipidomic, metabolomic analyses with our internal and external collaborating laboratories and take the lead on designing relevant sub-studies, integrating and interpreting the data 	
• Help establish the practical and regulatory framework for these collaborations, including material transfer and data-sharing agreements 	
• Participate in grant and manuscript writing 	
• Present at local and international meetings 	
• Introduce lab techniques to new lab members and students 	
• Collaborate with both scientists and clinicians   Start: February 1st, 2027

  Duration: 2 years

  Profile

  We expect you to be a highly motivated and highly ambitious, independent scientist with the following qualifications: •

   	
• A PhD in Life Sciences with a preferred focus on haematology 	
• A strong background in mechanisms of normal and malignant haematopoiesis and molecular haematology techniques 	
• Comprehensive lab skills in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including work with primary human cells and cryopreserved patient material 	
• Experience with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, lipidomics, metabolomics and ability to analyse and interpret such data 	
• Experience with running projects across research groups 	
• Strong publication and presentation record in peer reviewed journals and international conferences 	
• Excellent written and spoken English skills 	
• Very collaborative 	
• Good social skills     

  Place of employment
 The workplace is at the Bartholin Institute which is part of Rigshospitalet, University of Copenhagen. The Bartholin Institute is located at Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC, close to the centre of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and a number of core facilities (animal unit, flow cytometry, in vivo imaging, NGS, etc.) shared between the research groups at BRIC (www.bric.ku.dk) and the neighbouring Finsen Laboratory. We have weekly journal clubs, data clubs, seminars with invited speakers and a young researchers club ASAP and our own PhD programme, MoMeD.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of two years. The starting date is 01.02.2027 or after agreement.
 Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025

   

  Questions 

  For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor Kirsten Grønbæk, kirsten groenbaek@regionh.dk; phone + 4535456086 / +4525211598.

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

   

  Application
 The application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page).

  2. CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

  3. A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

  4. List of publications.

   

  Recommendation 
 Furthermore, the applicant should provide two letters of recommendation or two references. To be taken into consideration, the letters must be signed by the supporting person on paper with institutional letter head and in PDF-format.

   

  Application deadline 15 November 2026, 23.59pm CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications 3 of 4 or letters of recommendation that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

   

  The further process

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

Are you an experienced Talent Acquisition (TA) professional with a strong track record in recruitment and proactive sourcing? Do you enjoy advising hiring managers, navigating challenging talent markets and finding specialist talent that is hard to reach? Would you like to help shape TA in a growing, international technology company?

Trackman is looking for an experienced TA Specialist to join our HR team at our headquarters in Hørsholm. TA is a newly established dedicated function within HR at Trackman. We are a small and collaborative team with responsibility for recruitment across the organisation.

Because we are a small team, everyone plays an important role. You will have a high degree of ownership and independence while working closely with your TA colleagues and the wider HR team. We are looking for someone who brings solid experience, can confidently run recruitment processes and sourcing activities independently, and is ready to contribute with ideas and best practices from day one.

You will join us at an exciting stage where we are continuing to develop our TA function, strengthen our sourcing capabilities and build more scalable ways of working. We value openness, collaboration and a good sense of humour. We help each other, share knowledge and ideas, and trust each other to take ownership.

What you will be doing

You will take ownership of recruitment processes and partner closely with hiring managers across the recruitment lifecycle, with a particular focus on identifying and engaging talent for specialist and hard-to-fill positions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Drive recruitment processes in close collaboration with hiring managers, advising on candidate profiles, recruitment strategy, processes and market conditions.

• 
Proactively source and engage talent through LinkedIn Recruiter and other relevant channels.

• 
Build and maintain talent pipelines for critical profiles.

• 
Ensure smooth and effective recruitment operations, from engaging job ads to well-managed candidate pipelines in our ATS, Recruitee.

• 
Ensure a strong and professional candidate experience throughout the recruitment journey.

• 
Contribute to employer branding and talent attraction initiatives.

• 
Continuously improve our TA processes and ways of working, including exploring how AI and automation can increase quality and efficiency.

Job requirements

What we are looking for

We are looking for an experienced TA professional with a strong recruitment foundation, demonstrated experience in proactive sourcing and a strong passion for the field. You are confident running recruitment processes independently, know how to navigate challenging searches and are comfortable acting as a trusted recruitment partner to hiring managers.

We imagine that you:

• 
Bring several years of solid hands-on experience within TA or recruitment, including end-to-end recruitment and proactive sourcing.

• 
Have a proven track record of managing recruitment processes from defining the profile and recruitment strategy to sourcing, assessment and closing.

• 
Know how to identify, approach and engage passive candidates, particularly for specialist and hard-to-fill profiles.

• 
Are confident advising and challenging hiring managers on candidate profiles, recruitment strategy, talent markets and hiring decisions.

• 
Can manage multiple recruitment processes and priorities while keeping things moving forward.

• 
Bring experience and perspectives that can contribute to developing and improving TA practices and ways of working.

• 
Have a strong focus on candidate experience and quality.

• 
Are curious about AI, automation and new TA technologies and how they can improve recruitment.

• 
Communicate confidently and professionally in English.

Experience recruiting within technology/engineering is an advantage, but not a requirement.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

jobs.occupation: Senior Backend Engineer wanted at Relewise
jobs.description:
Are you the kind of person who notices what others overlook? Do you need to understand the whole picture before you trust a solution? And do you get energy from learning new things while keeping an eye on the details?

Then read on!

For Relewise, we are looking for a sharp, hands-on engineer to help evolve Relewise's core platform. We are looking for someone with sound engineering judgment, system-wide understanding, and the ability to assess complex designs and implementations, including AI-generated work.

Hours: Full-time

Start date: As soon as we have found the right candidate

Location: Aarhus (or hybrid)

If you recognise yourself in this, you're the one we're looking for!

• 
You have a "no-bullshit" filter that errors rarely slip through. You notice what others overlook, and you dare to challenge when your critical sense catches something that doesn't make sense.

• 
You need to see the common thread before you act. You spot when things don't add up, and you want to understand the full context so you're not guessing.

• 
You value structure and deliver high-quality work. You are thorough, see your tasks through to the end, and make sure details are not forgotten on your watch.

• 
You're quick to learn new things and get to grips with new areas. At the same time, you dig to the bottom of things because you value thoroughness and precision.

• 
You always have a good overview, and you find it easy to work on even complex projects. You know where things stand, and you prioritise ruthlessly how your time is best spent.

• 
You get energy from solving problems, because challenges are fun and exciting to you. You're not afraid to take something apart to see what it is and what it can do, and you often think "what if".

Your responsibilities will be:

• 
Design and deliver features across the core search and recommendation engine, directing groups of coding agents as your own development team.

• 
Review code, both human-written and AI-generated, and, once sufficiently familiar with the platform, join the small group of "Last Defense" reviewers who determine whether changes are ready for production.

• 
Improve performance, scalability and resilience using profiling and production evidence.

• 
Own your changes through deployment and maintenance. When incidents occur, you investigate them systematically to find the root cause, ensuring we learn from the history and prevent similar issues in the future.

• 
Work closely with the Lead Engineer and CTO on design and the technical roadmap, and improve shared tooling, documentation and AI workflows.

What we expect from you:

• 
You have deep practical production experience with C# and .NET.

• 
You have experience with software architecture and domain modelling, and you apply SOLID, KISS and YAGNI pragmatically.

• 
You have owned and evolved a mature production backend with high throughput and low latency, and you remain close to the code.

• 
You have already or are more than ready to embrace AI throughout the development process, and you explain your decisions clearly to the team.

• 
You speak and write English fluently. Danish is a plus.

We'd be over the moon if you also have experience with:

• 
Search, recommendation systems and/or e-commerce.

• 
Azure, CI/CD and Windows Server/IIS.

• 
Domain-Driven Design. Clear modelling and sound reasoning matter more than terminology.

About Relewise and the team culture

Founded in 2020, Relewise is a headless personalisation and search platform serving more than 100 million requests daily, primarily for mid- to high-end e-commerce businesses in Denmark and Europe.

Our core platform was built from the ground up, including our own search technology, recommendation and personalisation algorithms, and proprietary event-sourced datastore. We control the complete pipeline, and scalability, exceptionally high performance and a low tolerance for errors shape our engineering decisions.

We are a small, close-knit team of senior engineers with substantial autonomy and clear alignment. We keep process overhead to a minimum by avoiding pointless meetings, but we value clear agreements, documentation, and a structured workflow so everyone knows where they stand.

You'll have daily technical partnership with our Lead Engineer and CTO, and every Friday we meet to discuss progress and lessons learned. The culture is informal and supportive; everyone's professional opinions are welcome, and we discuss lessons learned and improvements openly, turning mistakes into valuable insights for the whole team.

What we offer

• 
A role where you help set the standard for quality in a platform that reaches consumers across Europe.

• 
The opportunity to develop your skills in AI-first development alongside a highly skilled team.

• 
A work environment where we strive to understand you, so we can set you up for success in terms of tasks, leadership style and team culture.

• 
A competitive salary package with a warrant programme, pension, health insurance and paid vacation.

Talent profiling in the recruitment process

We use talent profiles in our recruitment process, so you will receive a link to the profile along the way.

It's not about giving right or wrong answers, but about whether your natural behaviour and strengths match the context you'll be working in here with us.

Do you recognise yourself in this job posting? Then we look forward to hearing from you!

Questions

If you have any questions, please contact:

Camilla B. Madsen

Recruitment Lead

TalentX

Tel: +45 5362 8226

Email: camilla@talentx.dk (for questions only. Please apply at this page)

jobs.occupation: Backend Engineer - Event Processing & Intelligence Services (C# / Python)
jobs.description:
Location: On-site with possibility to work remote

Team: Data & AI

Seniority: Mid-Level to Senior

**About The Platform

**Our team is building the platform that captures, stores, and exposes the complete history of mission-critical OT (Operational Technology) asset access. Through event ingestion, audit logging, activity tracking, and data services, we provide the foundation for compliance and security reporting as well as AI-driven insights. Reliability, traceability, and data integrity are at the core of what we do.

**About The Role

**We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a strong hybrid skill set across C#/.NET and Python to help us build the services that turn our audit and activity data into insight. Your main mission is to design and build the event-driven pipelines and backend services that sit on top of the audit platform: processing events as they arrive, enriching them with context, detecting meaningful patterns, and delivering the result to the people and systems that need to act on it.

You will work closely with colleagues in the Data & AI team to take analytical work from proof of concept into production. That means the plumbing that makes intelligence useful: pipelines triggered by platform events and completing inside a tight SLA, structured outputs stored in a schema that can evolve, APIs that expose those outputs cleanly, and delivery into customer tooling such as SIEM and collaboration platforms. Our data workflows run on Azure Databricks and our services run on Azure, and you will own significant parts of how these two worlds fit together.

This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of event-driven backend development, data engineering, and production operations. You will influence architecture across processing pipelines, detection logic, and integration interfaces.

We are looking for a self-driven and curious engineer who thrives in a collaborative environment. You value a healthy feedback culture, are open and approachable, and enjoy working closely with colleagues, ideally from the office, to solve problems together. You are focused, eager to learn, and motivated to continuously improve both our processes and your own work. You are comfortable navigating external constraints and can design robust solutions within those boundaries. You maintain a practical balance in documenting your work: thorough enough to ensure clarity and knowledge-sharing, yet efficient enough to avoid unnecessary overhead.

Beyond all that, this role is a fantastic chance to grow professionally, personally, and as part of a team that genuinely enjoys building great things together and having fun along the way.

**What You Will Do

****Event Processing & Pipelines

**

• Build event-driven pipelines in C# and Python that pick up audit events as they land, process them inside a time budget, and turn them into records the product and customer tooling can query

• Design processing that is correct under real-world conditions: retries, out-of-order delivery, poison messages, backpressure, and at-least-once semantics

• Decide how pipeline output is stored and versioned. Our audit data is append-only, so there is no going back and rewriting it. A schema decision here is closer to permanent than in most systems

• Take analytical work that has been proven in a notebook and make it a service that runs unattended: scheduling, retries, throughput, cost, and the monitoring that catches it when it stops being accurate

**Detection & Enrichment Services

**

• Build the backend that separates the handful of events worth investigating from the thousands that are routine: aggregation across sessions, users and devices, time windows, behavioral baselines, and risk scoring

• Keep the signal-to-noise ratio high enough that customers leave the feature switched on: deduplication, suppression, thresholding, and confidence scores that are honest about uncertainty

• Design a rules layer that customers can configure, without every new detection requiring a release

• Enrich raw events with the context that makes them actionable: severity, reasoning, and links back into the product

**APIs & Integration

**

• Design and build the C# APIs that carry this output to the three places it gets consumed: our own product UI, customer SIEM platforms, and downstream services

• Build integrations that deliver notifications and structured evidence into customer tooling (SIEM platforms, collaboration tools, downstream services)

• Design clean data contracts and event formats suitable for compliance, security, and analytics consumers

• Ensure APIs are robust, performant, and scale with growing event volumes

**Running What We Build

**

• Operate the services you build: monitoring, alerting, tracing, and incident response across Azure, Databricks, and our messaging layer

• Build the observability that tells us when output quality degrades, not just when a service is down

• Maintain CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and safe deployment practices for the services you own

**What You Bring

****Required Qualifications

**

• Solid experience with C#/.NET backend development

• Working proficiency in Python for data processing and pipeline work — you do not need to have been a Python-first engineer, but you should be productive in it

• Strong experience with event-driven and asynchronous systems — queues, event buses, or message brokers — and a clear understanding of their failure modes

• Experience designing and implementing ETL or data pipelines in a production environment

• Experience designing and building APIs (REST, and ideally streaming or event-driven interfaces)

• Experience with cloud-based data platforms (preferably Azure Databricks) and with working across a Python data stack and a C#/.NET production environment

• Solid understanding of relational and/or distributed data stores, including schema design and evolution

• Experience building multi-tenant systems where data isolation is a correctness requirement — authorization enforced in the data access path rather than bolted on at the edge

• Experience with CI/CD tools (GitHub Actions)

• Strong sense of code quality, testing, and maintainability

**Nice to Have

****Experience with any of the following is a plus:

**Platform and engineering breadth

• Queuing technology (e.g., RabbitMQ)

• Data streaming architectures (Kafka, Event Hubs, change data capture)

• Kubernetes and container-based deployments (Docker, AKS)

• Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Bicep, Terraform)

• Workflow orchestration tools (Databricks Workflows, Airflow, Azure Data Factory)

• Azure services (Functions, Container Apps, Data Lake, API Management, Monitor / Log Analytics)

• Observability tooling (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)

• Distributed systems failure modes and resilience patterns

• Append-only / immutable data stores and time-series databases

**Domain

**

• Familiarity with SOC tooling and concepts (SIEM integration, log forwarding, security event formats such as CEF/LEEF)

• Rules engines or customer-configurable detection logic

• Exposure to OT, ICS, or other mission-critical / regulated environments

• Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as NIS2, ISO 27001, or IEC 62443

**Machine learning and data science

**

• Working alongside data scientists or ML engineers to productionize models — packaging, serving, and versioning

• MLOps practices: experiment tracking, model registries, evaluation pipelines, confidence calibration, and drift detection (MLflow or similar)

• Databricks and PySpark, Delta Lake, or other lakehouse technologies

• Practical exposure to anomaly detection, behavioral baselining, or statistical/ML approaches to event data

• Applied use of LLMs in production systems — structured output, evaluation, and cost control

**Why Join Us

**You will be joining an ambitious and fast-growing team that is shaping how data and AI power our products. We move quickly, take ownership of what we build, and care about doing things well. This is a place where your work has visible impact, where your ideas are heard, and where you can grow alongside colleagues who genuinely enjoy solving hard problems together. If you want to be part of building something meaningful with a team that values curiosity, collaboration, and craftsmanship, you will feel at home here.

jobs.description:
Drive meaningful impact across the life sciences industry.

As our next Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups -locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most.

About the role

As a Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will work closely with clients and colleagues to address complex challenges across the life sciences value chain. You will take ownership of your work and contribute to delivering solutions that create real, lasting impact. This is a Senior role designed to provide project and program leadership to deliver strategic technical solutions that address complex client issues in the Life Sciences industry. You will be handling implementation/migration projects and programs to achieve desired outcomes and ensure successful business growth. You will also seek new business opportunities to help BASE life science grow its presence within existing and new customers.

Additionally, you will contribute to internal initiatives and training to further strengthen BASE life science’s project and program management methodologies, approach, and tools.

You will lead teams consisting of multiple workstreams, which could include BASE/Infosys, external third party, or client stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in, project/program management and the ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing responses to Requests for Proposals (RfPs), ensuring adequate planning for scope, timelines and budget

• Monitoring project/program status including milestones, risks, issues, budgets, etc.

• Acting as a delivery escalation point and proactively ensuring escalations are handled promptly with a clear action and communication plan.

• Creating and delivering tailored communication based on audience, i.e., executive level summaries for client stakeholders, or senior executives in BASE life science, status reports at a project or program-level at a suitable cadence for team members

• Intervening, when necessary, to ensure costs, timelines and quality are on track.

• Lead a cross-functional team to deliver projects/programs to the required scope, on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our life science industry stakeholders.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders in the life science industry to understand their needs and translate them into executable plans for the project team.

• Develop plans, timelines, and budgets for projects/programs for which you are responsible.

• Track and report on project/program progress, identifying and mitigating risks as needed.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration between the project team, life science industry stakeholders, and other teams within BASE life science.

You bring:

• 5+ years of experience as a technical project/program manager within Regulatory, Clinical, Quality or other GxP areas in the life science industry.

• Successful track record of managing technically complex projects/programs such as software development, implementation of IT systems, data migrations, etc.

• Experience leading technical teams and delivering data driven projects/programs.

• Experience with project management tools such as JIRA, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project etc.

• Experience with Agile project management methodologies such as SAFe.

• Strong communication skills, both in writing, meetings and in presentations.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.

Additionally, the ideal candidate has the following skills/certifications:

• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

• Experience selling either projects or products to clients.

• Experience working with Veeva Vault, SalesForce or similar technologies.

• Experience working with AI professionally

This position is offered in Denmark and Spain.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2015, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting company working exclusively in life sciences, built on a simple purpose: grow our people, and deliver real impact for our customers.

We don't think AI is a feature you bolt onto existing systems — we think it's the layer through which a life sciences company's strategy actually gets executed, end to end. Most of the industry is still proving AI can do one task at a time, function by function, pilot by pilot. We're building toward something bigger: AI that runs across clinical, regulatory, quality, and commercial work instead of stopping at the edges of a single application.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Spain, Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and the US, we work with top-10 pharma and ambitious biotechs alike, and with technology partners including Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, and Amass — turning that belief into deployed, compliant, sellable solutions, not slideware.

Why join BASE Life Science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact — grounded in five core values: team spirit, trust, openness, ambition, and execution.

• Ambition, encouraged through ownership and continuous learning.

• Execution — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice.

• Openness — your ideas are heard, challenged constructively, and supported as you grow.

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance.

• The opportunity to shape a practice, not just staff one.

Alongside this, we offer:

• Support for health and wellbeing, covering physical, mental, and social needs

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• Ongoing learning and professional development throughout your career

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

• Recognition of performance and impact, linked to contribution and results

• The opportunity to work on challenges that make a meaningful difference for patients and healthcare systems worldwide

Explore our work, values, and people at www.baselifescience.com

Interested?

If you find this position intriguing, don't delay—submit your application in English at your earliest convenience. We are continuously reviewing and assessing all incoming candidates and eagerly await your application.

At BASE Life Science, we value diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. Employment decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs

jobs.description:
Introduction

We are looking for a talented Field Service Engineer based in Ballerup, Denmark or in Southern Germany. The ideal candidate has a minimum of 7 years of experience in servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment**.

About the Role

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Field Service Engineer to join Sophion Bioscience’s small, dedicated service team.

You will work alongside curious, hands-on colleagues who solve problems, share knowledge, and support one another - even when working independently in the field.

The team values high-quality work, clear communication, and a straightforward, respectful customer experience. In this key role, you will ensure the reliable performance of our automated patch clamp and organ-on-a-chip instruments at customer sites. Your responsibilities will include troubleshooting, maintenance and repairs, system evaluations, customer training, and coordinating upgrades with cross-functional teams.

As an ambassador for Sophion, you will build strong customer relationships by communicating effectively and resolving technical issues promptly, helping drive the continued growth of Sophion Bioscience.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ On a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Installation and Commissioning: Conducting on-site installation and commissioning of Sophion Automated Patch Clamp and Ethica M instrumentation, ensuring it meets the client's specifications and quality standards.

• Maintenance and Repairs: Performing routine maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs of QPatch, Qube and Ethica M systems to ensure uninterrupted functionality. Responding promptly to service requests and providing timely resolutions.

• Documentation: Creating detailed service reports, documentation, and maintaining accurate records of all service activities. Providing feedback to the engineering and R&D teams for continuous product improvement.

• Training: Providing training to clients on the proper usage, maintenance, and troubleshooting of Sophion automated patch clamp & Ethica M instrumentation, ensuring they have a clear understanding of its features and capabilities.

• Customer Support: Serving as a point of contact for technical support, addressing client inquiries, and maintaining strong relationships with customers to enhance satisfaction.

• Collaboration: Collaborating with the Sales, Application Science and Engineering teams to communicate client feedback, potential product enhancements, and identify opportunities for upselling additional services or products.

Who You Are

You are an experienced service professional with a passion for customer success, technical excellence, and being a team player. You thrive in a hands-on environment where no two days are the same and enjoy executing your day-to-day responsibilities in close collaboration with the rest of the Sophion team.

We imagine that you:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Biomedical Engineering, a related field or equivalent certifications

• In-depth knowledge of liquid handling devices from various industry systems is a benefit.

• Experience with electrical and pneumatics preferred

• Must possess a good grasp of core engineering concepts which include the ability to read and interpret electrical/circuit Schematic drawings.

• Able to use test/measuring equipment like Digital Multimeter (DVM).

• Team player, critical thinker, and flexible for effective performance in the field.

• Experience with service management systems and processes

• Familiarity with the operation and maintenance of Festo pressure systems is a plus

• Manage MySQL and Oracle databases to ensure seamless system integration and performance.

• Network Configuration and Maintenance: configure and troubleshoot network setups, routers, and DHCP configurations to guarantee optimal system connectivity.

• Possess a basic understanding of Linux systems to address software and operating system-related challenges.

• Demonstrate excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities to address technical issues promptly.

• Communicate effectively with customers and colleagues, ensuring a positive and collaborative working place.

• Ability to travel 50-60% once initial training is complete.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the HR Director, Helene Fife, (+45 51 20 34 43).

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Do you want a broad accounting role with significant responsibility and excellent development opportunities?

If you are an experienced accounting professional who enjoys taking ownership, working independently, and being part of a collaborative team, this could be exactly the opportunity you have been looking for.

At Gubra, we are experiencing continued growth and development. As our business expands, so do the opportunities for our employees to develop professionally and take on increasing responsibility. A broad accounting role with responsibility across multiple areas

You will have ownership of your own areas while working closely with your colleagues in Finance. We take pride in supporting one another and working together to ensure successful month-end closings, reporting deadlines, audits, and daily operations.

An experienced accounting professional with a proactive mindset

We are looking for someone who takes ownership, follows through on commitments, and enjoys working in an environment that combines structured routines with changing priorities and deadlines.

In addition, you bring:

• Strong Excel skills and experience with financial systems

jobs.occupation: Two-year Postdoc position on Spintronic Quantum-inspired Computing
jobs.description:
Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher position within the newly funded QUANTRONIC – Spintronic Pseudo-Qubits for Room-Temperature Quantum Computing project, supported by the Villum Experiment programme of Villum Fonden.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate a new class of spintronic pseudo-qubits (p-qubits) based on spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). The project explores whether engineered stochastic spintronic devices can reproduce key computational mechanisms associated with quantum systems - including superposition-like states, probability-amplitude-based interference, and entanglement-like correlations—without relying on fragile quantum coherence or cryogenic operation.

QUANTRONIC is a high-risk, high-gain research project positioned at the intersection of spintronics, probabilistic computing, quantum-inspired computing, nanoelectronics, and integrated circuit design. The central concept is a novel SOT-MTJ architecture designed to represent and manipulate probability amplitudes and to enable synchronization between multiple pseudo-qubits. The project will combine physics-based modelling, device design and fabrication, experimental characterization, and system-level demonstrations.

The successful candidate will work within SDU Microelectronics and collaborate closely with international partners, particularly INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, on the design and fabrication of spintronic devices.

The position is expected to start in February 2027, with the specific starting date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

As a Postdoctoral Researcher in QUANTRONIC, your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Develop and refine physics-based compact models of SOT-MTJ-based pseudo-qubits, including stochastic switching and inter-device coupling.

• 
Develop Verilog-A models and integrate them into circuit-level simulation environments such as Cadence.

• 
Investigate the physical requirements for controlling probabilistic states and representing probability amplitudes in spintronic devices.

• 
Collaborate with project partners on the design and fabrication of SOT-MTJ devices and arrays.

• 
Experimentally characterize standalone devices and coupled arrays, including stochastic switching, synchronization, and entanglement-like correlations.

• 
Investigate quantum-inspired gate operations and system-level demonstrations using networks of pseudo-qubits.

• 
Contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations, including integer factorization and other quantum-inspired computational problems.

• 
Publish research results in high-quality international journals and conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

• 
Collaborate with researchers in spintronics, probabilistic computing, microelectronics, materials science, and quantum information.

 

What we offer

• 
A unique opportunity to work on a high-risk, high-gain research concept exploring a new computational regime between classical probabilistic and quantum computing.

• 
A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing research section with expertise in spintronics, probabilistic computing, neuromorphic computing, analog/digital IC design, and emerging computing architectures.

• 
Access to advanced facilities for electronic design, device characterization, measurement, and system prototyping.

• 
Close collaboration with INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory on spintronic device technology and fabrication.

• 
Opportunities to collaborate with national and international researchers in spintronics, quantum-inspired computing, quantum technologies, and nanoelectronics.

• 
An open, international, and collaborative research environment within SDU's Faculty of Engineering, supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, physics, materials science, and computing.

• 
Strong opportunities for developing an independent research profile in an emerging area of probabilistic and quantum-inspired hardware.

 

What we expect

Applicants should hold a PhD in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, nanotechnology, spintronics, or a closely related field.

The ideal candidate should have experience in one or more of the following areas:

• 
Spintronics and magnetic devices, particularly MTJs, STT-MTJs, SOT-MTJs, or related technologies.

• 
Physics-based modelling of nanoscale or magnetic devices.

• 
Verilog-A, SPICE, and Cadence or comparable circuit/device simulation environments.

• 
Experimental characterization of electronic, magnetic, or spintronic devices.

• 
Stochastic or probabilistic computing systems.

Experience in micromagnetic simulation, magnetotransport measurements, nanofabrication, probabilistic computing, or quantum/quantum-inspired computing will be considered a strong advantage.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and are comfortable combining device physics, modelling, experimentation, and computing concepts.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills are required.

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). The section conducts internationally recognized research in integrated circuits, spintronics, photonics, and neuromorphic computing, and plays a central role in SDU’s ambition to be a national and European hub for semiconductor and chip innovation. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact Professor Farshad Moradi (moradi@sdu.dk / email), Head of the SDU Microelectronics section and Associate Professor Hooman Farkhani (farkhani@sdu.dk / email), Deputy Head of SDU Microelectronics. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is February 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).
