jobs.occupation: Compliance Officer for Financial and Non-Financial Risk Areas
jobs.description:
About the role

Would you like to be part of an ambitious Compliance team where you play a key role in ensuring that Saxo meets its regulatory obligations within financial and non-financial risk areas?

If so, this may be the right opportunity for you at Saxo.

You will join the Prudential Oversight team within Group Compliance, Saxo's second line of defence function, based at our headquarters in Hellerup. Our team oversees compliance risks across a broad range of areas, including the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk, as well as non-financial risk areas such as ICT, operational risk, model risk, data governance and strategy, supporting the business in meeting regulatory requirements, market standards and internal policies.

Your primary responsibility will be to conduct compliance oversight and monitoring across the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk as well as non-financial areas such as operational risk, model risk and strategic risks in relation to policies, procedures, segregation of duties, limits, calculations, samples, controls, etc.

However, if you are curious about the other areas covered by the team, we will help you develop your skills and knowledge within these areas.

As a team, we balance professionalism with a sense of humour and maintain an informal atmosphere where people enjoy coming to work.

Responsibilities

• 
Perform compliance risk assessments

• 
Provide advice and compliance opinions to the business on managing compliance risks and regulatory requirements

• 
Conduct compliance monitoring activities

• 
Contribute to regular compliance reporting to senior management of the bank

• 
Participate in developing the bank’s compliance framework

• 
Interact with the business across organisational levels and seniority

Your profile

We are looking for a colleague with experience from working with one or more prudential risk areas, who is motivated to develop deeper expertise in these areas.

Further we expect you to have:

• 
At least 2 years of relevant experience from the financial sector, preferably within compliance, risk management, audit, finance, credit or another relevant first-line function

• 
A relevant educational background within economics, finance, accounting, audit or similar

• 
Interest in prudential risk areas such as capital, liquidity, market risk, credit risk, model risk, strategic risk, operational risk areas, governance, and internal controls

• 
Familiarity with regulatory requirements such as CRR/CRD, Basel guidelines, EBA/ESMA guidelines, the Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks and other relevant Danish financial regulation is an advantage

Moreover, we are looking for someone who is detail-oriented, can work independently while taking an active role in teamwork and enjoys collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across the entire organisation.

It is an advantage if you thrive in an environment with constant change, bring a positive and curious mindset to work, and do not buy into the word ‘cannot’.

You must possess strong stakeholder management skills and use your communication skills to ensure positive collaboration and progress in joint tasks. We are looking for a colleague who always brings a positive attitude when liaising with the business.

Please note! International applicants are encouraged to apply. To help us understand your circumstances, we kindly ask candidates currently based outside Denmark to include a brief summary of their relocation plans and expected timeframe for relocating to Denmark.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – IoT Platform, Load and Energy Management
jobs.description:
🚀 About the role

We're looking for a senior software engineer who writes solid, reliable code and wants that code to control real hardware. At FLEXECHARGE, our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe. Part of it runs at the edge, on an industrial PC next to chargers, batteries and solar inverters, and connected to the interfaces DSOs use to curtail load.

You'll build and maintain the TypeScript microservices that talk to those devices and turn their data into decisions. This is not a web-app role. It's software engineering for systems where the other side is physical, stateful and often unreliable.

⚡ What is special about this role

It sits where two worlds meet:

• 
Web and cloud toolchain: TypeScript, Docker, MQTT, Azure, Kubernetes.

• 
Operational technology and system integration: talking to real chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus and OCPP, running at the edge on an industrial PC.

Your code won't only talk to clean APIs in a data centre. It runs on site, next to real peripheral devices, and has to keep doing its job when those devices and the networks between them don't behave as expected.

We recognize that TypeScript is not typically used for edge computing or hardware interfacing. This is why we're looking for a strong software engineer who is interested in learning new techniques and applications, as well as applying their technical skills in novel ways.

🛠️ What you'll do

• 
Write and maintain a combination of TypeScript microservices and the business logic behind them: control algorithms, scheduling and decision-making, not just plumbing.

• 
Build and extend device drivers for chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus TCP, using our existing driver services as a starting point.

• 
Work with OCPP, which our platform already supports, as you ramp up.

• 
Run services in containers at the edge and connect them through MQTT and pub/sub messaging to our cloud backend.

• 
Profile and optimise software on edge hardware, where hardware resources are constrained.

• 
Help shape the long-term move of performance-critical services to compiled languages.

• 
Mentor and pair with colleagues on integrations and software craft.

🤔 Why compiled languages, if we write TypeScript?

It may sound odd, so here's the reasoning. Today the majority of our edge stack is TypeScript, and you'll develop in it from day one. Over time we want to move selected services, such as device interfaces and performance-critical paths, to a compiled language while keeping them part of the same stack.

To do that well, you need to understand both sides: the TypeScript services as they are now, and the concepts of memory, types and performance that compiled languages force you to think about. In our experience, it's much easier to go from a compiled language to a scripting environment than the other way around. So if you're a Go, C, C++, Rust or similar developer who is happy to work in TypeScript (or happy to learn), you're exactly who we're looking for.

✅ Must-have

• 
3–5+ years of professional software development, with strong software and engineering fundamentals.

• 
Professional experience in a compiled language (for example Go, C, C++, Rust, C# or Java).

• 
Proficiency in a scripting language, ideally TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript or Python, or a clear willingness to become productive in TypeScript quickly.

• 
Experience writing business logic with stateful calculations and operations, which can self-heal and recover gracefully.

• 
Comfort with asynchronous and event-driven systems that talk to unreliable external components or peripheral devices.

💡 Strongly preferred (but we'll teach it)

• 
Hands-on device or protocol integration: Modbus, serial interfaces, Ethernet/TCP-IP or comparable.

• 
Containerised applications. Docker, Docker Compose or Kubernetes are ideal, but any container technology counts.

• 
Pub/sub and distributed systems, ideally MQTT or another IoT messaging protocol, and an understanding of their reliability concerns.

• 
Working within constrained systems, including profiling software to find where CPU or memory limits bite.

🎁 Bonus, not a requirement

• 
OCPP experience.

• 
Energy, EV charging or power-systems domain knowledge.

• 
Edge deployment experience.

If you don't have these, apply anyway. Strong fundamentals and the right mindset matter more. 💪

🚫 This role is probably not for you if

• 
Your experience is mainly frontend or request/response web apps, with no compiled-language background.

• 
You prefer to stay in one language and aren't interested in working in TypeScript.

• 
You want a pure firmware or PLC role without writing higher-level services.

• 
You don't enjoy debugging the messy cases where hardware doesn't behave as documented.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXECHARGE?

• 
Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• 
You're covered with pension contributions.

• 
Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• 
We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities within each team.

• 
You'll have opportunities for individual development.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• 
A first conversation (about 30 minutes) with our recruiter. You'll get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further.

• 
Time with the team: a conversation with Kasper, our Head of Architecture & Systems, and Robert, our CTO.

• 
A technical stage: one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• 
A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

📍 Location & practical details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• 
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

• 
We do not offer relocation services.

🔐 Data privacy (GDPR)

Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

For more information or questions please contact us at iva@flexecharge.com

Working at

FLEXECHARGE

FLEXECHARGE is a cleantech scale-up which offers a powerful load & energy management platform, as a SaaS, to help Charge Point Operators (ex: Clever, eOn, etc.) to optimise their charging operations & business. Our mission is accelerate green mobility through our Smart Charging solutions that make charging faster, greener and cheaper. Our vision is to integrate charging infrastructures better with the grid supply and the ever more volatile & growing production of renewable energy. We want to connect electric vehicles with the grid in a whole new way. By seeing electric vehicles not as a risk for our supply grid, but as a crucial asset for the transition towards 100% renewable energy. We do this through constant innovation of new smart charging features which will make us the preferred partner for EV infrastructure owners, developers, and operators.

Department: DMPK and Modelling Sciences

Location: [Måløv]

Your impact begins here

As a Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics (PKPD) Senior Principal Scientist, you will shape how translational modelling supports decisions across drug discovery and development. You will set direction for PKPD strategies, connect preclinical evidence with human safety and efficacy, and help interdisciplinary teams progress a diverse research portfolio. Your scientific leadership will strengthen project decisions from early research through clinical development and regulatory submission.

What you’ll bring

You bring deep expertise in translational science and mathematical modelling, together with the judgement to turn complex evidence into clear recommendations. You communicate effectively across disciplines, work independently and help colleagues solve scientific challenges.

• A PhD in pharmaceutical, medical, physical, mathematical or engineering sciences, or another relevant discipline, combined with substantial pharmaceutical industry experience.

• Ideally, at least ten years of relevant experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Strong knowledge and hands-on experience in PKPD, quantitative systems pharmacology and/or physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling.

• Experience developing mechanistic models, or combinations of mechanistic and empirical models, to represent biological or other natural processes.

• Practical experience with pharmacokinetic and modelling software such as Phoenix WinNonlin/NLME, NONMEM or an equivalent platform, and with analytical tools such as R, Python or MATLAB.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence decisions and collaborate across scientific disciplines.

Useful, but not essential: Experience with machine-learning workflows, managing external service providers, or supporting due diligence within physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling.

What you’ll do

• Set the direction for translational PKPD screening and mechanistic modelling across different molecular formats, working with research, non-clinical and clinical stakeholders.

• Design preclinical PKPD/pharmacodynamic studies, interpret the results and communicate conclusions that support project decisions.

• Build mathematical models and run simulations of human PKPD using in-house in vitro and animal data, together with relevant literature.

• Guide project teams on preclinical study design, dose setting for toxicity studies, first-in-human dose selection and clinical trial design.

• Contribute scientific input to regulatory interactions and documents, including Investigational New Drug applications, Investigational Medicinal Product Dossiers and New Drug Applications.

• Advance scientific capabilities in mechanistic modelling and PKPD, solve complex problems and mentor fellow scientists.

Who you’ll work with

You will join one of two closely connected PKPD teams within DMPK and Modelling Sciences. Together, the teams advance the use of quantitative systems pharmacology, physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling and PKPD modelling across the research and development value chain.

Your closest collaborators will include in vivo pharmacologists, in vitro biologists, clinical modelling scientists, toxicologists, clinicians and regulatory affairs specialists. The area is part of Global Research within Research & Development and works with global discovery and development colleagues, project teams and external partners.

What you can expect here

You can expect a scientifically ambitious environment where knowledge-sharing and collaboration are part of the everyday work. You will have room to build your scientific and personal capabilities while contributing expertise that informs preclinical studies, first-in-human trials, clinical development and regulatory submissions. The role offers broad exposure across therapeutic areas and across the development pathway, from early research to submission.

Salary:

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000 to 1,245,100 (DK), corresponding to the level of the position. The confirmed JL9 pay table lists these as the annual minimum and maximum values, but the source does not state the currency explicitly.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy. The salary and benefits wording follows the approved pay-transparency section in Job Ad Guidelines.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to use translational modelling to strengthen decisions across research and development, apply for the PKPD Senior Principal Scientist role by 8**. November 2026.** Applications will be assessed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Line Hollesen Schefe, Manager, Non-clinical PKPD and PBPK, at +45 3077 6009.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Project manager for international research projects
jobs.description:
Are you enthusiastic about making a difference to large societal challenges such as green transition of energy, materials and food systems?

Do you have experience with research project management, funding administration and project development? 

Do you know your way around a Horizon Europe project and do you enjoy being the person who keeps a large international consortium on track?

Do you thrive in a dynamic working environment, with multiple external and internal stakeholders?

Then we might be looking for you!

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering at Aarhus University, we are busy conducting research on a broad range of topics related to green transition, sustainability and health. Our portfolio of EU-funded projects is growing, and we are therefore looking for an experienced EU project manager with international experience who can drive development and execution of international projects in close collaboration with researchers, external partners and the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team.

Expected starting date and duration
The position is a two-year fixed-term position starting on 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job descripton
At Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, we are experiencing an increase in externally funded, international research and innovation projects. As project manager you will play a key role in managing and coordinating the department’s participation in such projects, in particular large Horizon Europe projects with multiple partners, where our department has a leading role 

Working closely with the scientific coordinator, you will:

• Act as the day-to-day operational point of contact for the consortium. 
• Drive the coordination machinery: Track deliverables, milestones and risks, chase and quality-assure partner contributions.
• Prepare periodic/final reporting, and coordinate financial reporting with partners and with the administrative and financial experts in AU’s central research support office.
• Plan and run consortium, General Assembly and review meetings: Agendas, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Maintain the Consortium Agreement and support obligations on data management, ethics, dissemination, exploitation and communication.
In addition to this, you will:

• Support the department’s wider portfolio of international projects, being work package or task manager where relevant.
• Provide guidance and support to the development of new European grant proposals and the building of new consortia.
• Participate in and help organise externally oriented activities and events.
• Help shape the department’s way of working around externally funded projects, so that good practice is developed and shared.
The role is vested in the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team. The team supports our researchers within multiple aspects of externally funded research collaborations - from strategy development, visibility, partnership and project development to execution of complex projects. We are continuously developing our way of working to support increased activity level and creation of impact.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone who combines hands-on experience of EU project execution with the ability to work comfortably alongside researchers in a technical field.

Technical qualifications:

• Academic degree in a relevant field (e.g., technical sciences, international relations etc.).
• Experience with the day-to-day management of Horizon Europe or Horizon 2020 projects; including reporting, deliverable and milestone tracking.
• Experience of working with international research consortia and of coordinating contributions from partners in several countries.
• The ability to engage with technical content well enough to quality-assure deliverables and to discuss the work with researchers on their own terms.
Qualifications we regard as an advantage:

• Experience from the coordinator side of an EU project, rather than as a beneficiary partner only.
• Experience with proposal development, grant writing and consortium building.
• Familiarity with research areas related to the green transition; for example bioresources, biotechnology, chemical or environmental engineering.
• Familiarity with EU financial rules, cost eligibility and audit requirements.
Personal qualifications:

• Excellent communication skills, with fluency in English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and priorities effectively
• Service-minded attitude, flexibility, and a collaborative approach to working in a team
• Ability to travel internationally as needed (few times per year). 
Who we are
At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering we focus on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering etc. more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food.

At the department, we educate BEng, BSc and MSc graduates in engineering for Danish society.

Read more about the department and sections here:
https://bce.au.dk/en/research/key-areas-in-research-and-development

Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering offers:

• Opportunity to contribute to solutions of crucial importance to society and industry
• The possibility of being part of a dynamic research environment in rapid development
• An exciting, cross-disciplinary environment with strong external partnerships with industrial and academic partners in Denmark and abroad
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, trust and healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work Gustav Wieds Vej 10D, 8000 Aarhus, Denmark and the area of employment is Aarhus University, Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Deputy head of department, Thomas Lundgaard, +45 29 16 31 35 / thomas.lundgaard@bce.au.dk

Application deadline
9 November 2026.

Formalities and salary range
You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. For the right candidate, there will be an opportunity to be appointed as a Special Consultant, with remuneration in accordance with Appendix 4 of the collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Why Flatpay?

jobs.occupation: Warehouse operative for the switchboard workshop in Esbjerg
jobs.description:
We are stepping up in Esbjerg — we are looking for a warehouse operative for our new switchboard workshop.

About the position

The expansion of our Tech Centre Esbjerg continues: we are now opening a switchboard workshop, and it needs a warehouse operative to manage the flow of goods. Components, cables and materials come in through the gate, and at the other end products must go out to installation and service jobs. Everything passes through the warehouse — and it will be your job to keep the flow running.

Your responsibilities

• Receiving goods, checking them against the delivery note and registering them in the system

• Supplying the panel builders with components, cables and materials

• Picking materials for panel building, installation and service jobs

• Packing and preparing shipments for installation sites and service vans

• Keeping stock levels up to date and flagging in good time when something is running low

• Keeping shelving, labelling and walkways in order

We expect you to

• have warehouse experience — knowledge of electrical or industrial components is a plus

• have an overview and a sense of order, even when the workshop is busy

• be reliable and take responsibility

• be willing to take on general tasks as they arise

• A central role in the switchboard workshop — your work keeps production running

**

jobs.occupation: Laboratory technician at DTU Metabolomics Core - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
The DTU Metabolomics Core at DTU Bioengineering, Kgs. Lyngby, is looking for a skilled and motivated Laboratory Technician to join our team of excellent scientists and technicians collaborating on microbial molecules, trying to unravel their importance in nature, and discover how they can benefit humanity in various ways, such as in agriculture, and novel pharmaceuticals.

About the DTU Metabolomics Core
The DTU Metabolomics Core in the Department of Bioengineering is one of a several Core facilities within the Department that supports a wide range of research and teaching. The area in which the Metabolomics Core specializes is in the chemical analysis of small secondary metabolites from microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and microalgae. This analysis is undertaken in our extensive instrument suite (HPLC, LCMS, GCMS, MALDI etc.), a collection of instrumentation that you will work closely with as our new technician.

The primary job areas of responsibility
As Laboratory Technician in the Metabolomics Core, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of the facility in close collaboration with the Facility Manager. Your responsibilities will include:

• Operating and maintaining our analytical instrumentation, including high-resolution LC-MS systems (sample preparation, calibration, QC runs, routine troubleshooting and preventive maintenance in cooperation with service engineers)
• Running samples for internal researchers and external contract projects, from sample preparation to data acquisition
• Ordering and managing laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemicals, and keeping the lab stocked and organized
• Maintaining lab standards: cleanliness, safety, waste handling, documentation, and quality control routines
• Supporting users of the facility with practical guidance on sample submission and preparation
• Contributing to the ongoing development of workflows and procedures in the facility
• Supporting students
In addition to this is it expected that you will take part in some Department duties, particularly involving laboratory and chemical safety. This will be done in close collaboration with a team of 4 other technicians working within the same section that hosts the Metabolomics Core.

Qualifications
We expect that you:

• Hold a degree as a laboratory technician (laborant) and/or a BSc/MSc in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field
• Have hands-on experience with HPLC instrumentation. Experience with high-resolution MS (e.g., QTOF) is a strong advantage
• Are experienced in routine laboratory work, including sample preparation, solvent handling, and general upkeep of analytical labs
• Have knowledge of Good Laboratory Practice, safety regulations, and documentation standards
• Are structured, detail-oriented, and able to plan your own work independently
• Enjoy collaborating with researchers of different backgrounds and communicating in English (our working language)
• Ideally, have experience with natural products chemistry, and sample preparation
What we offer in return
With this job we offer you an exciting and versatile position in a multicultural, respectful and dynamic research and learning environment with many international employees and students. You will gain hands on experience with a wide variety of different analytical instrumentation and have the freedom to create your own daily agenda by prioritizing your tasks.

You will have:

• A central role in a well-equipped core facility with diverse and exciting projects spanning microbiology, natural products, and industrial collaborations
• Close collaboration with leading research groups at DTU Bioengineering
• A flexible, informal working environment at DTU's Lyngby campus
• Professional development opportunities, including training on new instrumentation and methods
Salary and appointment terms
Salary and appointment terms are in accordance with the OAO-S Joint Agreement and the organization agreement for Office Clerks, Laboratory Technicians and IT staff (HK/stat). In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for clerical employees OR laboratory technicians: https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The appointment is permanent full time. The position starts 1st December 2026 or as soon as possible after.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 4 November 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Facility Manager, Aaron Andersen by e-mail (ajca@dtu.dk) or by telephone (+45 45 25 61 38). DTU Bioengineering website: https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/english.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Department of Biotechnology and Biomedicine (DTU Bioengineering) is an international leader in the areas of biotechnology and biomedicine. Our engineering approach to all aspects of biotechnology and biomedicine positions us as a valuable player with unique competences in a growing bio-based economy and with health systems transforming towards personalized medicine. We have a clear focus on the needs in life science- and biotech industries and point towards innovation, new businesses, and scientific services for the benefit of society. The department has extensive collaborations with national and international research units and industry. DTU Bioengineering has approx. 400 employees, of which 2/3 are scientific staff. The department is located at DTU Lyngby Campus.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Faerch A/S

Faerch is a leading supplier of circular, rigid food packaging with integrated recycling capabilities. With more than 5,000 employees across Europe and the U.S., Faerch serves food manufacturers, food service providers, and retailers globally through a network of state-of-the-art production facilities.

The company is owned by A.P. Moller Holding and is driven by a clear purpose: to accelerate the transition toward a circular economy in food packaging.

With sustainability at the core of its strategy, Faerch develops innovative packaging solutions designed for recyclability and high levels of post-consumer recycled content. The company is currently undergoing a transformation to strengthen integration, customer focus and operational excellence, captured in its strategic ambition, “Ignite our potential”.

Read more at: www.faerch.com

Senior Director, IT & Digital

Faerch is looking for a Senior Director, IT & Digital to lead and further develop the global IT & Digital function and support the company’s continued digital transformation.

In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring a scalable, secure, and business-oriented foundation that supports operational efficiency, data security, and customer satisfaction through cutting-edge technology and digital solutions.

A key leadership role in Faerch’s digital transformation

In this role, you will be responsible for the continued professionalization of Faerch’s global IT function, with a strong focus on cybersecurity, infrastructure stability, uptime, data integrity and security, governance, and operational excellence.

You will lead an organization of ~55 employees located across several European markets, including a management team of three direct reports, while also being responsible for the IT budget ownership and spend management across the function. In addition, you will report directly to the Global CFO and be given the mandate to position Global IT & Digital as a strategic business partner to support the execution of the new strategy.

A key priority in this regard will be to accelerate the roll-out of M3 Cloud across Faerch’s factories and ensure that the ERP programme is managed, structured, and implemented as a global transformation. At the same time, you will be responsible for ensuring stable operations, high uptime, strong cyber security, and a simplified application landscape.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Leading the transition of the ERP system from a project-based implementation to a structured global programme in close collaboration with key functional leaders.

• Ensuring high operational reliability across business-critical systems and production environments.

• Strengthening maturity and governance within cyber security across the global IT landscape.

• Defining and maturing Faerch’s AI and digital agenda, including relevant use cases across the organization.

• Maintaining a responsive and efficient service desk that effectively addresses user needs and resolves technical issues promptly.

• Leading and motivating the IT organization, ensuring strong engagement, clear direction, and effective collaboration across disciplines and locations.

• Strengthening Global IT as a trusted business partner through alignment with stakeholders, and digital solutions that support operational and commercial priorities.

Who are you?

We are looking for an experienced IT leader who can strike a balance between strategic transformation and stable day-to-day operations. You bring a solid technical foundation and a proven track record of leading complex digital initiatives in international organizations – ideally from manufacturing companies or other operationally intensive environments with multiple sites and a high reliance on stable systems.

You have experience leading geographically dispersed digital teams across a range of disciplines and thrive in a role that involves setting the direction, creating structure, and ensuring progress. At the same time, you have a strong business acumen that enables you to translate business needs into effective solutions and value-creating initiatives. Furthermore, you are able to translate complex technological agendas into clear priorities that both specialists, managers, and senior stakeholders can understand and act upon.

Personally, you are a visionary and results-oriented individual with a genuine passion for technology, innovation and business impact. You are able to constructively challenge existing working methods with a view to driving improvements. As a leader, you are collaborative, build trust easily, and know how to foster engagement in daily operations.

If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Research Consultant Simone Svenningsen on tel. 2616 3704.

Please note that we only need your CV when you apply for the position. Your enquiry will be treated confidentially and will not be passed on without your consent.

**About GoWish, Ønskeskyen ☁️

**At GoWish, we’re building the world’s leading wish-list and social shopping platform - a place where you can make a real impact and have fun doing it.

We’re on a mission to reinvent gifting for millions. We win together, driven by curiosity, ownership, and bold ideas that turn into real products. We experiment cross-functionally, push for excellence, and keep things playful as we grow - together.

**Team & Role Overview

**We are looking for a systems-minded Senior ML Data Engineer to own the offline-to-online feature infrastructure that powers our real-time recommendation and search engines at scale. You will be building the low-latency data syncs and feature-serving layers that bridge our analytical warehouses with operational databases, caches, and Feature Stores. This is a role for a performance-driven engineer who excels at pipeline orchestration (Airflow, dbt), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Docker), and database tuning, ensuring our recommendation systems receive reliable data under strict low-latency SLAs. If you thrive on solving complex data synchronization challenges, scaling operational storage for millions of users, and acting as the operational bridge between Data Science and Backend Engineering - you will play a critical role in powering our product's core ML capabilities.

**What You'll Do

**

• Offline-to-Online Feature Pipelines: Build and operate resilient feature pipelines syncing transformed data from analytical warehouses (e.g., BigQuery) into operational storage layers (e.g., AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models at scale.

• Pipeline Orchestration and Transformations: Design, test, and maintain robust Apache Airflow DAGs and modular dbt transformations to automate end-to-end data ingestion and feature generation under strict low-latency SLAs.

• Infrastructure as Code and Reliability: Provision, scale, and automate cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines, implementing automated data quality testing and monitoring across all feature syncs.

• Cross-Functional System Design: Partner directly with Data Scientists and Backend Engineers to define online/offline feature contracts, optimize database schemas for sub-second queries, and eliminate training-serving skew for millions of active users.

**What we’re looking for 🌟

****We Imagine That You Have

**

• 4+ years of experience

• Operational Data Pipelines: Proven experience moving batch features from analytical warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) into low-latency online stores (AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Deep hands-on experience provisioning, scaling, and managing cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD automation pipelines.

• Pipeline Orchestration & Transformations: Strong track record building, scheduling, and maintaining workflow orchestrations (e.g., Airflow, Dagster) and modular data transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt).

• Database Performance Tuning: Advanced SQL skills across both OLAP and OLTP systems. Ability to optimize schemas, indexing, partitioning, and queries.

It is further seen as an advantage to have experience with:

• Production Feature Management: Experience managing Feature Stores (e.g., Feast, Tecton) or low-latency key-value stores (e.g., Redis) to serve online ML features with zero training-serving skew.

• Real-Time OLA): Experience with ClickHouse, Pinot, Druid or others for ultra-fast aggregations over live event streams.

• Event Streaming: Hands-on experience with streaming tools like GCP Pub/Sub, Kafka, or Flink for real-time feature updates.

Why GoWish should sit at top of your career wish list 💙

At GoWish, we believe great work comes from people who feel energized, supported, and excited to show up every day. That’s why we’ve built a workplace where celebration, growth, and genuine enjoyment are part of the journey - not perks on the side.

Take your birthday off with Happy Birthday Leave, enjoy 30 days of vacation to fully recharge, and join a team that fills the year with events and playful happenings. We invest in your future with pension and insurance, fuel your days with a weekly lunch scheme, and keep you going with unlimited snacks and sodas - because work should feel good.

At GoWish, you don’t just build great products. You build a great work life.

**Practical information

**We collaborate in a flexible hybrid setup, with most of our magic happening at our bright, modern office in Østerbro - perfectly placed between Nordhavn and Østerport Station. We’re ready for you to join us as soon as you are.

👉 Ready to help shape a platform that already empowers 18+ million users (and counting)? Join us at GoWish - and let’s build the future of data-driven innovation together.

Don’t wait to apply - we review applications continuously and may close the position once the right candidate is found.

jobs.occupation: Build your career in Transfer Pricing - Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 3000 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Consulting.

About the team

Join our Transfer Pricing team of more than 45 colleagues in Copenhagen and Aarhus. We help international and Danish businesses turn complex tax, finance and operating-model questions into practical solutions. You will build your expertise through real client work, structured learning and close collaboration and help clients navigate tax and transfer pricing challenges.

Job Description

You will work on a wide range of transfer pricing projects across various sectors. Together with your colleagues, you will help clients manage operational transfer pricing matters, audits and compliance, and provide both global and local advice. You can expect a steep learning curve, and  responsibilities that grow with your experience - supported by structured onboarding, regular feedback and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. Alongside your client work, you will have opportunities to attend training in Denmark and at Deloitte University in Paris, strengthening both your technical expertise and client-facing skills.

Ready to take the next step in your career? In this role, you will be involved in:

• Collect and analyse financial and business data for transfer pricing projects across sectors.

• Prepare transfer pricing documentation, benchmarking analyses and intercompany agreements.

• Support audits, international tax requirements and country-by-country reporting.

• Turn your analysis into clear client advice, join client meetings and follow up on agreed actions.

• Contribute ideas to proposals, AI-enabled tools and practical improvements to how we work.

We work in a dynamic, international environment with an informal tone, where quality, collaboration and different perspectives are central to how we create value for clients and for each other.

AI-enabled and digital tools are a natural part of how we work. You will learn to use them responsibly to explore data, support research and benchmarking, improve workflows and strengthen deliverables. No prior AI expertise is required - curiosity, sound judgement and a willingness to learn matter most.

We value the community that extends beyond client work. Our employee association brings people together throughout the year - from social events to shared experiences that cut across teams and business units. We celebrate the wins, big and small, and make a point of recognising individual and shared milestones

The role is full-time, and we are looking for professionals for our offices in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, Denmark.

Qualifications

We are looking for Consultants and Senior Consultants with 0–3 years of relevant experience.

We imagine that you are curious, ambitious and motivated by complex challenges. You take ownership of your responsibilities, collaborate openly with colleagues and clients, and contribute to bringing projects to a successful conclusion.

What you bring to the team:

• A relevant academic background, such as law, economics, finance, accounting or business.

• 0–3 years of relevant experience; internships and student roles are also valuable.

• Analytical, conceptual-thinking and problem-solving skills.

• Curiosity about technology and judgement when using AI-enabled tools.

• Clear communication and an interest in turning complexity into practical advice.

• Good energy and a strong client service instinct

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your CV, grade transcript and application in which you present yourself and elaborate on your motivation for pursuing a career in Transfer Pricing and/or highlight relevant projects or previous experience by 5 November 2026. We regularly call for interviews, so send your application already today.

Please do not hesitate to contact Partner Cecilie Emilie Rendtorff at +45 26 61 53 93 or Aske Haahr Lauridsen at +45 20 41 35 92 if you have any questions about the position.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: PhD position at the Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
jobs.description:
The Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA) at The Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark, is seeking a talented and highly motivated PhD student to work on the development of new theoretical frameworks for describing light–matter interactions in advanced van der Walls heterostructures probed by polaritons generated through inelastic tunneling. The position is funded by a Villum Young Investigator grant awarded to Assistant Professor P. André D. Gonçalves, who will supervise the PhD research.

The position is available starting 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will develop new theoretical frameworks and computational methods to investigate the fundamental limits of polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling in tunnel junctions based on van der Waals heterostructures composed of atomically thin materials. The project will employ a broad range of analytical, semi-analytical, and numerical techniques to explore electrically driven polaritonic phenomena. A major focus will be on harnessing polariton-mediated inelastic electron tunneling as a tool to probe and manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale, as well as to characterize the optoelectronic response of complex quantum materials.

We welcome candidates with a strong background in condensed-matter physics and/or quantum nanophotonics who are highly motivated and eager to pursue world-class research in theoretical quantum nano-optoelectronics. Experience with scientific programming is expected, while familiarity with numerical techniques is advantageous but not required. The ideal candidate will be enthusiastic about contributing to cutting-edge research in a dynamic and ambitious young research group, supported by the POLIMA Center and its extensive network of international collaborators.

POLIMA is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) for an initial period of 6 years (2023–2028), with the possibility of a 4-year extension. The center is led by Professor N. Asger Mortensen and currently consists of two Professors, three Assistant Professors, a Lab Manager, a Center Administrator, and approximately 10–15 PhD students, postdocs, and visiting scientists. Several POLIMA researchers have attracted prestigious personal grants, e.g., Villum Investigator, Villum Young Investigator, DFF Sapere Aude, Novo Nordisk’s Foundation RECRUIT and Data Science Investigator – Emerging, and Maria Skłodowska-Curie Fellowships. Read more on POLIMA’s website.

We offer a competitive and highly collaborative research environment with close interaction between experimental and theoretical activities. You will join a thriving community of researchers and benefit from a strong network of international collaborators. Our work environment is supportive, dynamic, and designed to foster creativity and the development of innovative projects.

 

We offer:

• A PhD student position in an ambitious and supportive, international research environment.

• A dedicated supervisor research team to support the academic development of the PhD student.

• Access to state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and infrastructure.

• A competitive salary and social benefits (e.g., health coverage, parental leave, social security, etc.) (https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/international-staff/getting-settled)

POLIMA is located at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense – 1h15min by train from Copenhagen Airport. The University of Southern Denmark offers dedicated assistance and support with various practical, social, and legal aspects (housing, visa, administration, tax, etc.), especially for international candidates through our international staff office (ISO) and the administrative staff at POLIMA.

 

For further information and details about the position, application, and the research center, please contact Assistant Professor Paulo André Dias Gonçalves (padgo@mci.sdu.dk).

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and an application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (copy of original and an official English translation).  

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

• 
An official document describing the grading scheme of the awarding universities (if not Danish). 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

Imagine a future where you'll protect the ability to supply electricity and heat to the end user and make sure that our critical OT systems are protected against hackers

We offer a workplace culture where you’ll be working from the office every work day.

Join us in this role where you’ll be working as a Senior Operational Technology (OT) Security Officer to strengthen the security, resilience, and compliance of Ørsted Bioenergy. In this role, you will act as a trusted security lead across OT, IT, engineering, and operations, helping protect critical systems while enabling safe, reliable, and efficient operations. Further more we are partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability – and we “translate” technical cyber risk into clear business, safety, and operational impact requirements. We operate in complex, multi-site, international, or safety-critical operational environments.

**Welcome to Bioenergy

**You’ll be part of OT Security where you, together with your colleagues, will be working on Ørsted Danish powerplant. Our task is to protect the powerplants ability to produce electricity and heat against hacker attacks. So you need to understand Danish, when you’re out on the powerplants. We are a small team of 4 persons located in Jutland (Jylland) who works together and strive in helping each other in our daily tasks. As a team, we have an open and direct commutation where we discuss ideas strategy and ideas to develop and mature our solutions, so they are robust and they deal with the reality we face.

You’ll play an important role in:

• leading the development and continuous improvement of OT security governance, policies, standards, and procedures

• assessing, managing, and reducing cyber risk across OT environments, including industrial control systems, SCADA, PLCs, IIoT, and related networks

• defining and supporting secure OT architecture, including network segmentation, secure remote access, asset visibility, access control, logging, monitoring, and vulnerability management

• conducting OT security risk assessments, gap analyses, and maturity reviews aligned with recognised frameworks e.g. Danish legislation “Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren”, IEC 62443, ISO 27001 and relevant regulatory requirements

• partnering with operations, engineering, maintenance, IT, and third-party vendors to ensure security controls are practical, risk-based, and compatible with operational safety and availability requirements

• driving OT security awareness and training for technical and operational teams.

To succeed in the role, you:

• hold a relevant degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Cyber Security, Information Technology, Automation, or equivalent practical experience

• understand and know how to operate in ICS systems and possess understanding of 24/7 production environment

• are familiar with IT networks like, Purdue model, firewall, data diodes etc.

• hold knowledge about EIC 62433, ISO 27001 and "Lov om styrket Beredskab i Energisektoren" as we operate according to this legislation

• are a good team player and at the same are strong on being responsible of incl. conducting your own tasks – you need to be fluent in both Danish and English language as well due to nature our stake holder landscape

• are flexible - both in terms of taking on tasks outside your comfortzone, being curious in learning new areas and assist your team in whatever tasks are needed.

Some travel within Denmark to the different sites must be expected in the this role.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

jobs.occupation: Tax Professional, Customer Handling, Securities Tax Services (Copenhagen)
jobs.description:
**Job Description

**Are you customer-focused, structured and motivated by working in an operational area where quality, documentation and service delivery are key? Do you enjoy supporting customers and advisers, coordinating with internal stakeholders and ensuring that processes run efficiently from start to finish?

We are looking for a detail-oriented colleague to join our Customer Handling Team/Tax Services team in Copenhagen. The team serves as a primary point of contact for advisers and customers and plays an important role in onboarding, documentation management, customer support and service delivery related to securities tax services.

On clients’ behalf, Danske Bank applies for a reduction in foreign tax on returns from securities held in customers’ custody accounts. This includes relief of foreign dividend and interest tax, either at source or through tax reclaim processes. The service is complementary to Danske Bank’s custody service and is particularly relevant for clients earning income on foreign financial instruments, where a tax reduction may be available under applicable double taxation agreements.

**About Securities Tax Services

**Securities Tax Services is part of Danske Bank’s tax area and is responsible for handling services related to withholding tax on securities. The area consists of several teams located in Denmark and Lithuania, working closely together across locations, functions and customer segments.

You will join a team of skilled specialists who support corporate, institutional and other customer segments. We value collaboration, curiosity, continuous learning and a strong focus on delivering high-quality service in a well-controlled environment.

**Your role

**As a team member in Customer Handling, you will support customers and advisers with inquiries, documentation and service-related matters. You will help ensure that customer agreements, onboarding, offboarding and service changes are handled correctly and efficiently.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• Acting as a first point of contact for customer and adviser inquiries

• Handling customer onboarding and offboarding activities

• Ensuring customer agreements and service documentation are sent, received and registered correctly

• Collecting, reviewing and maintaining required customer documentation

• Supporting changes to customer preferences and service setups

• Following up with customers and advisers on outstanding documentation and requests

• Coordinating with internal stakeholders to ensure efficient service delivery

• Participating in client meetings and supporting customer relationship management

• Maintaining and updating information in internal systems

• Supporting controls to ensure accurate and compliant processing

• Contributing to continuous improvement of customer processes and service quality

The role combines recurring operational tasks with customer interaction and collaboration across teams. You will get exposure to securities services, withholding tax processes, custody-related services and post-trade operations.

**About You

**We are looking for a structured and service-minded colleague who enjoys working with customers, documentation and operational processes. You take ownership of tasks, communicate clearly and can manage several activities while maintaining attention to detail.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience from customer service, client support, operations, financial services or a similar area

• Have a customer-centric mindset and strong communication skills

• Are comfortable working with documentation, regulations and operational processes

• Can manage multiple tasks while maintaining high accuracy

• Collaborate well with colleagues and stakeholders across teams and locations

• Are proactive, curious and willing to learn in a complex environment

• Have strong English skills, both written and spoken

Experience from Asset Services, post-trade operations, custody services or withholding tax is considered an advantage.

**What We Offer You

**You will join a supportive team environment where you can develop your expertise through varied work and mentorship opportunities. We operate a hybrid working model with 3 to 4 days per week in the office to promote collaboration and knowledge sharing. Your career will progress through exposure to diverse tax challenges and continuous learning opportunities.

**Are you ready for the next step?

**We would be delighted to hear from you if this opportunity aligns with your career aspirations. Please reach out to our hiring manager Nicolai William Schou Hansen at nicoh@danskebank.dk for any questions about the role. We look forward to hearing from you!

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

• Excellent written and spoken English.

• Structured and reliable, with strong attention to detail.

• Analytical, with an interest in strategy and how a company grows.

• Comfortable juggling many topics and stakeholders at once, and able to take ownership without being told every step.

• Confident with digital tools and quick to learn new systems.

**Practical Information

**

• Start date: As soon as possible.

• Hours: minimum of 24 hours per week, flexible around your studies.

• Location: Our office in Herlev, with the option to work from home. You'll be at the office at least 3 days a week.

**What We Offer

**

• A competitive part-time salary.

• Direct collaboration with the Founder & CEO, with insight into strategy, board work and fundraising.

• Real responsibility and a broad view across finance, HR, operations and systems.

• A mission-driven, international team.

• Flexibility to balance work with your studies.

**How To Apply

**Apply through The Hub with your CV and a short motivation statement explaining why this role suits you. We review applications on a rolling basis.

Levitate Technology ApS is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are committed to an inclusive workplace.

**Job Description

**SOUNDBOKS is an innovative tech company and aspiring lifestyle brand. You may have seen us at a music festival, street party, or your friend’s celebration (think: private events combining festival-grade sound with beat-enhancing lights) where special moments are turned into memories. We create the loudest, most durable, and arguably coolest Bluetooth speakers and audio reactive lights on the market.

At SOUNDBOKS, trust and community go hand in hand. People are encouraged to take ownership of their work while knowing they have the support of the team behind them. Voices are heard, ideas are welcomed, and collaboration is what pushes us forward.

This is more than a job - it’s a community where people care about each other, celebrate together, and share the energy of creating something meaningful. Life at SOUNDBOKS is bold, fast, and full of passion - for the product, for the mission, and for showing up as your true self. With 70 team members, this is a place where you can do your best work and truly belong.

ROLE AUDIO ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

HOURS FULL TIME

LOCATION COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

START DATE OCTOBER 2026 or ASAP

The Product Development team at SOUNDBOKS is the group responsible for the exciting product journey, taking every step of the development process toward and into mass production. In it’s heartbeat you’ll find collaborative and self-driven team members with a large cross-discipline understanding tied to ownership. They are there to make a difference - for the products, the team and the SOUNDBOKS customers as a whole.

Working closely with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams, you'll help shape the technologies behind our next generation of speakers.

Okay, let’s make things a little more concrete. Here’s what we expect your daily life to look like:

• Explore new approaches to improve audio performance across products.

• Collaborate with the Acoustics, Hardware, and Firmware teams during concept development.

**Signal Processing & Simulation

**

• Perform advanced signal processing simulations with a focus on sound pressure level (SPL), sound quality, and system efficiency.

• Simulate the interaction between acoustics, amplifiers, electronics, and battery performance.

• Evaluate and develop signal processing algorithms to improve overall product audio performance.

**System Performance & Collaboration

**

• Work closely across the entire Product Development team in order to evolve and improve the audio performance across our future product portfolio.

• Apply signal processing methodologies to improve sound pressure, sound quality, and battery performance.

jobs.occupation: Senior Hardware Productization Engineer / Mechatronics Lead
jobs.description:
The role

We are looking for a senior hardware/product development engineer with strong experience taking physical products from prototype through engineering validation and into manufacturing.

You will work directly with the founder and take ownership of the physical architecture of Dreamspire.

This is not primarily a firmware role and it is not a pure industrial-design role.

We need someone who can look at a prototype and systematically turn it into a product.

You should be comfortable moving between:

• mechanical engineering

• electronics integration

• manufacturing

• prototyping

• reliability

• assembly

• suppliers

• cost

• compliance

• user experience

A large part of the work will initially be hands-on.

Your first mission

Your first objective will be to create a clear Dreamspire Product Architecture V1.

You will examine the existing prototype, identify its weaknesses and determine how we should build the next generation of the system.

This includes answering questions such as:

• Which prototype mechanisms are suitable for a real product?

• What needs to be redesigned?

• Which components should be custom versus off-the-shelf?

• How should cameras, lighting, electronics and mechanical systems be integrated?

• How do we make assembly simple and repeatable?

• What are the major reliability risks?

• What manufacturing processes should we use?

• What should the production BOM look like?

• What needs tooling?

• What can initially be produced in low volume?

• What compliance and certification work will be required?

• How do we move from one prototype to 10, 100 and eventually thousands of units?

The objective is not to rush into manufacturing.

The objective is to progressively remove technical and manufacturing risk until the product is ready.

Responsibilities

You will:

• Audit the existing Dreamspire hardware and mechanical architecture.

• Design and build improved prototype generations.

• Own mechanical design and product engineering.

• Integrate cameras, PCBs, lighting, power, cabling, connectors and sensors into the physical product.

• Design enclosures, mounts, mechanisms and structural components.

• Define tolerances and mechanical interfaces.

• Design for manufacturing and assembly — DFM/DFA.

• Reduce part count, assembly complexity and manufacturing cost.

• Select appropriate materials and production methods.

• Decide when to use CNC, sheet metal, 3D printing, injection molding or other processes.

• Work with PCB/electronics engineers where specialist electrical work is required.

• Develop production BOMs and cost estimates.

• Source and evaluate components and suppliers.

• Communicate directly with prototype houses and manufacturers.

• Design test fixtures and production test procedures.

• Establish reliability and lifecycle testing.

• Help define EVT, DVT and PVT stages.

• Identify CE, EMC, electrical safety and other relevant compliance requirements.

• Help design the system for serviceability and repair.

• Help prepare Dreamspire for small pilot production and eventually mass production.

What we are looking for

The most important requirement is:

You have personally helped ship real physical products.

Ideally, you have taken products through several stages of:

prototype → engineering validation → manufacturing → production → customer

You should have strong practical experience with several of the following:

• Mechanical engineering

• Mechatronics

• Consumer electronics

• Product development

• DFM / DFA

• CAD

• Injection-molded plastic parts

• CNC and rapid prototyping

• Electronics packaging

• PCB integration

• Cameras / optical systems

• Sensors

• Motors or electromechanical systems

• Tolerance analysis

• Supplier management

• BOM optimization

• Production testing

• Reliability testing

• Manufacturing ramp-up

You should be comfortable physically building, modifying and debugging prototypes rather than only designing them.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

Experience from products such as these would be especially relevant:

• Consumer electronics

• Robotics

• Smart-home products

• Interactive toys

• Gaming hardware

• IoT products

• Camera systems

• Medical or laboratory devices

• Small electromechanical products

Experience working in a startup or small product-development team is a major advantage.

What we are not looking for

This is probably not the right role if your experience is primarily:

• Arduino hobby projects

• Pure firmware development

• PCB design without product/mechanical ownership

• Industrial design without engineering responsibility

• CAD work without manufacturing experience

• Large-company engineering where manufacturing and suppliers were handled entirely by other teams

We are looking for someone who understands the whole physical product.

How you work

You should enjoy environments where the product is still evolving.

You should be able to say:

“This prototype mechanism works, but it will not survive production.”

or:

“We can remove these five components if we redesign this assembly.”

or:

“Don’t spend money tooling this yet — we need to validate this part first.”

We want someone who challenges assumptions and prevents expensive mistakes rather than simply implementing specifications.

Working with the founder

You will work closely with the founder, who currently develops the software, computer-vision systems, embedded systems and game concepts.

You will therefore have considerable influence over the architecture of the product.

The expectation is that you become the technical owner of the physical Dreamspire platform, while working closely with software and game development.

If the collaboration works well, the role could evolve into something resembling:

Head of Hardware / Head of Product Engineering

as Dreamspire grows.

Location

The role is based around Copenhagen.

Much of the work can be done remotely, but during prototype development we expect regular hands-on work with the physical Dreamspire system.

Candidates elsewhere in Denmark or the Øresund region are welcome if they can work regularly in Copenhagen.

Relocation support is not available at this stage.

Employment

We are open to:

• Full-time employment

• 3–4 days/week

• An initial senior consulting/fractional arrangement that can develop into a permanent role

For a strong permanent candidate, expected salary is approximately:

65,000–75,000 DKK/month + pension, depending on experience.

Exceptional candidates with significant consumer-product leadership experience may be above this range.

Why this role is interesting

Dreamspire is not another incremental electronics product.

The aim is to create an entirely new category of tabletop gaming platform and then build multiple games on top of it.

The fundamental question is:

Can we create something with the physical presence and social experience of a board game, but with systems and mechanics that were previously only practical in video games?

A large part of whether that succeeds depends on making the hardware disappear into the experience.

That is the problem we want you to help solve.

How to apply

Email jobs@dreamspire.dk with your CV and a few lines about the physical products you have helped ship. We read every application and use it only to assess it; see how we handle your data.
