jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Reality Capture for Digital Twinning of Built Structures - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
The aim of this project is to develop technologies for creating building information models of existing built structures. This is part of a larger goal of using digital techniques to support sustainability in construction - specifically by making it easier to repurpose buildings.

Responsibilities
You will work within the area of visual computing. Much of the work will be based on machine learning and in particular vision language models. The use of generative methods will be central to your research whose overarching goal is to study how it is possible to extract information about a construction from photographs and other data sources and generate a precise building information model with little or no user input.

You will be affiliated with CEBE (Civil Engineering and the green transition in the Built Environment) which is a Danish cross-university research programme focusing on the sustainable development of the built environment. CEBE’s vision is to promote science-based circular, low-carbon and resilient built environment within planetary boundaries. CEBE is supported by the Villum Foundation.

You will be matriculated at the DTU Compute PhD School, employed at DTU Compute, and embedded in the Section for Visual Computing. The Section for Visual Computing is focused on medical image analysis, geometry and appearance modelling, computer vision, multivariate statistics for images and analysis of 3D microstructures. Within these areas, our overarching research aim is to make methodological contributions of broad applicability but motivated by applications.

Qualifications
To qualify for this position, you must have a background in visual computing (computer graphics and computer vision), a good understanding of the basics of computer-aided design and machine learning. These qualifications must be underpinned by a strong background in applied mathematics. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Andreas Bærentzen, janba@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 3 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• 
A letter motivating the application (cover letter)

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Compute
DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in theoretical chemistry, “Towards quantum-enhanced computational algorithms for discovering sustainable energy materials” - DTU Chemistry
jobs.description:
The project focuses on the development of next-generation quantum-enhanced algorithms for predicting the electronic excited-state properties of organic molecules. By integrating quantum chemistry, quantum computing, and computational materials design, the project aims to enable the efficient screening and discovery of sustainable materials for solar energy conversion and other clean-energy technologies. The PhD project is a collaborative effort between Sonia Coriani (DTU Chemistry, principal supervisor), Piotr de Silva (DTU Energy Conversion and Storage, co-supervisor), and Achintya Kumar Dutta (IIT Bombay, co-supervisor), and is cofinanced through a DTU Alliance PhD fellowship and the Novo Nordisk Foundation-funded Hybrid Quantum Chemistry on Hybrid Quantum Computers (HQC)² project.

As part of the Alliance partnership, the PhD student is expected to spend two research stays of approximately three months each (or one stay of 6 months) at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, working under the supervision of Achintya Kumar Dutta and collaborating closely with a PhD student based at IIT Bombay. The project will also involve close interaction with the research teams associated with the (HQC)² project, providing access to a broad international network and expertise at the interface of quantum chemistry and quantum computing. 

Responsibilities and qualifications

• Design computational methods for predicting excited-state properties, in particular algorithms suitable for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) and Early fault-tolerant quantum computers.
• Generate high-quality benchmark datasets
• Implement computational software and workflows
• Use developed algorithms to: screen candidate organic molecules, support inverse molecular design, discover sustainable energy materials for next-generation solar-energy technologies 
• Disseminate the results of the research in scientific articles and at conferences 
• Participate in the group meetings and activities
• Teaching-related activities at the Department of Chemistry, Technical University of Denmark, including (co)supervision of BSc and MSc student projects
The following additional qualifications are considered as a boon:

• Solid mathematical background and experience within quantum chemistry, computational spectroscopy and programming in Fortran and/or C/C++ and/or Python
• Experience in the development and implementation of correlated wavefunction methods of quantum chemistry, for instance Coupled Cluster or multireference methods.
• Experience on the development of quantum computing algorithms for NISQ and/or (early) Fault Tolerant quantum computers
• Experience with quantum computing software libraries like IBM’s Qiskit or Pennylane
Equally important, you are highly motivated, able to work independently and confident in both written and spoken English. You strive towards scientific excellence, are ambitious and hard working. You enjoy collaborating with others from diverse backgrounds as well as supporting more junior group members. Only applicants, who seek to be among the brightest in their field and do science at the highest international level, will be considered

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree, in either Chemistry (preferably with a focus on theoretical and computational chemistry), Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or Quantum Information Science.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by a panel composed by Prof. Coriani, Prof. De Silva and Assoc. Prof. Kumar Dutta.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position.

The position is available with start on January 1, 2027 or as soon as possible after 01/01/2027.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Enquires about the position may be made to Professor Sonia Coriani, soco@kemi.dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Chemistry at www.kemi.dtu.dk, and about Coriani’s group at https://www.kemi.dtu.dk/english/Research/Physical-Chemistry/sonia-coriani-group

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 6 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications (if any), including the master and bachelor theses
• List of up to three scientists with whom you have closely worked in your past research, whom we may contact for references
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Chemistry is an internationally leading institute with research and teaching in the main areas of chemistry: physical (incl. theoretical/computational), biophysical, organic and inorganic chemistry. Academic excellence, innovation and entrepreneurship are core to its research activities, and drivers of academic and industrial collaborations, spinouts, and high impact publications. The Department has a long-standing tradition of training PhD students and Postdoc fellows who move on to successful careers within academia and industry.

The department actively contributes to both basic chemical research and applied research in energy, pharmaceuticals, catalysis and materials. Strong relationships exist with neighbouring areas such as physics, nanotechnology, biochemistry, including collaboration with industry and universities at home and abroad. Many research projects are also closely linked to applications. The institute has approx. 180 employees.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
**Product Management at Dalux, Innovating the Construction Industry

As a Product Manager at Dalux, you’ll operate at the intersection of customer needs, technology, and business strategy. You’ll take ownership of the product roadmap and collaborate closely with Product Design and Development teams to deliver intuitive, high-performing BIM experiences.

You’ll play a key role in evolving how our users view, navigate, understand, and collaborate around building models. Combining an understanding of BIM, UI/UX, and computer graphics, you’ll help turn complex technical capabilities into tools that work effortlessly for our users.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Product Discovery: Evaluate and prioritize new product opportunities, balancing user value, technical feasibility, and business impact.

• Customer Insights: Work closely with users to understand their BIM workflows, uncover pain points, and translate feedback into meaningful product improvements.

• User Experience: Collaborate with Product Design to make complex BIM interactions intuitive, from navigating 3D models to finding and understanding building information.

• BIM and Visualization: Work with engineers on model visualization and interaction, balancing visual quality, responsiveness, and performance when handling large and complex building models.

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Align with engineers, designers, and fellow product managers to deliver cohesive experiences across Dalux products.

• Feature Ownership: Lead new features from discovery and definition through development, delivery, and validation with users.

• Product Strategy: Help define the direction of BIM at Dalux, identifying opportunities and deciding where we should invest to deliver the greatest value.

**What To Expect As a Daluxian

**At Dalux, we offer a creative, collaborative, and supportive environment where your ideas make an impact. Here’s what you can look forward to as part of our team:

• A central location in Copenhagen, a focus on work/life balance, and no dress code.

• An active social environment with monthly events and social clubs.

• A flat organization with open communication, a short path from idea to product, and the creative freedom and trust to create tangible value for our users.

• A highly specialized, international team with room for creativity and professional growth.

• A strong focus on diversity and inclusion, where your ideas are heard and opportunities are available to all.

• Attractive employee benefits, including health insurance, a lunch plan, coffee and fruit, free fitness facilities, and free parking.

• Support for your professional development and personal well-being.

**About You

**We believe you have a solid background in product management and experience working closely with software development teams, preferably on SaaS platforms. You’re curious about how technology works and motivated by making sophisticated tools easy to use.

We also believe you:

• Have 5+ years of experience in product management, taking products or features from discovery to delivery.

• Have a background in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Understand BIM workflows and how building models and their data are used across design, construction, and operations.

• Have a strong understanding of UI/UX principles and can work with designers to evaluate interaction flows, challenge unnecessary complexity, and validate solutions with users.

• Have a working understanding of computer graphics concepts such as 3D geometry, rendering, and model interaction, enabling you to discuss technical trade-offs with engineers.

• Can balance strategic thinking with attention to detail, particularly where usability, model complexity, and performance meet.

• Are comfortable working in agile development environments and prioritizing based on user insights and product outcomes.

• Communicate clearly and fluently in English, both written and spoken.

Experience with IFC, BIM viewers, or other software for working with 3D models would be an advantage.

**Ready for the next step?

**If we have managed to pique your interest, we would love to hear from you. Send us your motivated CV and an application.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your application today.

**About Dalux

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics. Despite being the world’s second-largest industry, construction remains one of the least digitalized, with only 30% of onsite time spent on actual building tasks. At Dalux, we’re changing this by providing end-to-end solutions that streamline the entire lifecycle of a building—from design and construction to maintenance and eventual demolition—reducing waste, time, and costs.

We stay ahead by using cutting-edge technology, including cloud solutions, drones, computer vision, and AI, to transform how the construction industry works. Over the last five years, we’ve grown by 60% annually and now have over 700 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

If you’re curious to learn more about Dalux and our products, feel free to visit our LinkedIn or website, where you can find videos and descriptions of our events, products, and the work we do.

**As soon as possible

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Software Engineering: Program Analysis and Repository Mining
jobs.description:
A 2-year postdoctoral researcher position is available at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) in the Software Engineering section of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI). The successful candidate will contribute to the VILLUM Experiment project “Is Correctness Necessary? An Experiment in Test-Free Program Repair.” The project investigates whether software bugs can be repaired using information found in the code itself, without relying on test suites or specifications. The position is available from February 1, 2027. 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Project Description

Generating code is becoming cheap; establishing whether it is correct is not. Large language models can now produce and modify software at remarkable speed, and practices such as “vibe coding” are widening the gap between code generation and validation. Requiring a carefully designed test suite or specification for every generated fragment is unlikely to scale. Yet most automated repair techniques depend on exactly such a correctness oracle: without a failing test or specification, they have neither a clear repair target nor a way to assess a proposed change.

This project challenges that dependency by investigating whether software bugs can be repaired using evidence already present in the code. It will combine program analysis with patterns mined from existing software to explore whether multiple, independent sources of evidence can guide repair when tests or specifications are unavailable. The approach will be studied across different programming languages and evaluated on both real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants. The broader aim is to determine when code contains enough information to support its own repair and when knowledge of the intended behavior remains essential.

 

What we offer 

We offer a dynamic and supportive research environment within an internationally recognized institute. You will join an open, collaborative team that values teamwork, professional diligence, and innovation. The Software Engineering section provides flexible work conditions and strong support for individual development, including mentorship and opportunities to expand your skills and responsibilities.

As part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, our section is involved in a variety of national and European research projects and enjoys a robust network of academic and industrial partners. This position provides an opportunity to engage with these collaborations and work on real-world challenges. We encourage and support our postdocs to publish their research in renowned journals and conferences, and to engage in knowledge exchange with colleagues and external research and industrial partners. The working language is English, and we pride ourselves on a diverse, inclusive, and inspiring workplace that fosters personal and professional growth.

 

What we expect 

The appointed researcher will investigate whether software defects can be repaired without relying on test suites or specifications. The candidate will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of a framework that combines program analysis with patterns mined from existing software. The work will involve experiments with real-world bugs and code modified by AI coding assistants across multiple programming languages. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who meets the following qualifications and characteristics:

• 
A PhD (completed or close to completion) in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Programming Languages, Artificial Intelligence, or a closely related field.

• 
Research experience or a strong interest in one or more of the following areas: program analysis, mining software repositories, automated software engineering, software testing, or software repair.

• 
An interest in software reliability challenges arising from AI-generated and AI-modified code.

• 
Experience with empirical evaluation, software repositories, or bug benchmarks is an advantage.

• 
Experience with one or more of C, Java, and Python is an advantage.

• 
Proficiency in written and spoken English, with good communication skills.

• 
Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a research team.

• 
A strong research record or demonstrated research potential through publications or other relevant research outputs.

 

Workplace description 

The postdoc will be employed in the Software Engineering section at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute (MMMI), SDU. MMMI is an internationally recognized research institute within the Faculty of Engineering, known for its contributions to software engineering, robotics, and artificial intelligence. The Software Engineering section encompasses a range of research areas in software development, data analytics, and intelligent systems, and it plays a key role in several ongoing European projects.

Our workplace is truly international and collaborative. Researchers in the section come from diverse backgrounds and work closely together on cross-disciplinary projects. We benefit from state-of-the-art facilities and a strong administrative and technical support structure. The institute maintains close collaboration with other departments and centers at SDU, as well as with industry partners, providing a vibrant environment where theoretical research meets practical application. The position will be located on SDU’s Odense campus, which offers an attractive setting and a rich campus life in the city of Odense, Denmark’s hub for robotics and technology development.

 

Further information 

For further information, please contact Associate Professor Abhishek Tiwari (abti@mmmi.sdu.dk) or Assistant Professor Jyoti Prakash (jyp@mmmi.sdu.dk)

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from February 1, 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Computational Proteomics and Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark
Location: Odense, Denmark
Duration: 2 years, with the possibility of a 1-year extension
Starting Date: 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter

Project Description
We invite applications for a postdoctoral position at the interface of computational proteomics, machine learning, and mass spectrometry. The successful candidate will join a pioneering research program focused on peptide ionization and fragmentation in LC-MS/MS, with the aim of developing new computational approaches for peptide fragmentation analysis.

The project centers on large-scale, experimentally curated tandem mass spectrometry datasets and the development of new computational strategies for fragmentation analysis under analytically underexplored conditions. It relies on modern machine learning approaches to model fragmentation behavior, support spectral interpretation, and enable future advances in peptide identification workflows.

The position is embedded in the Protein Research Group (PRG) at the University of Southern Denmark, an internationally recognized environment in proteomics and biological mass spectrometry. The postdoctoral researcher will work in close collaboration with experimental colleagues generating high-quality tandem MS data for computational development.

Research Environment and Collaborative Structure
The Protein Research Group comprises eight PI-led teams and more than 50 researchers and students, offering a highly interactive and interdisciplinary research environment. The successful candidate will play a central role in the computational arm of the project and will collaborate closely with experimental researchers developing new mass spectrometric methods and generating large-scale fragmentation datasets.

The position offers substantial scientific independence and the opportunity to help shape a new research direction at the intersection of machine learning, peptide chemistry, and proteomics.

Responsibilities
The postdoctoral researcher will be expected to:

• 
Develop computational and machine learning workflows for large-scale analysis of tandem mass spectrometry data 

• 
Contribute to the structuring, curation, and quality control of large experimental MS/MS datasets 

• 
Build data-driven models for peptide fragmentation analysis using experimentally generated spectra 

• 
Integrate relevant variables such as peptide sequence, precursor charge state, collision energy, and peptide modifications into computational frameworks 

• 
Evaluate model performance using suitable similarity, quality, and generalization metrics 

• 
Contribute to the extension of computational models toward chemically and biologically relevant peptide classes, including selected post-translational modifications 

• 
Investigate how computational models may help reveal fragmentation trends and chemically meaningful patterns in large-scale MS/MS datasets 

• 
Work independently on model development, implementation, and computational problem solving, while interacting closely with experimental researchers in the group 

• 
Contribute to reproducible and well-documented computational pipelines, data structures, and analysis workflows 

• 
Disseminate findings through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and open scientific resources where relevant 

Required Qualifications
Applicants must have:

• 
A PhD in computational proteomics, bioinformatics, machine learning, computer science, chemometrics, analytical chemistry, or a closely related field 

• 
Strong experience in machine learning and/or deep learning applied to complex scientific datasets 

• 
Demonstrated ability to independently develop computational solutions, including model design, implementation, evaluation, and documentation 

• 
Proficiency in Python and relevant machine learning/data science frameworks 

• 
Experience with data preprocessing, curation, and quality control for large and complex datasets 

• 
A strong analytical mindset and the ability to work independently on computational research problems 

• 
Interest in working at the interface of computation, chemistry, and mass spectrometry 

Desirable Qualifications
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:

• 
Experience with mass spectrometry-based proteomics, computational mass spectrometry, or peptide fragmentation-related data analysis 

• 
Experience with neural network architectures relevant for sequence-based prediction tasks 

• 
Experience with model interpretability, explainable AI, or feature analysis in scientific machine learning 

•

jobs.occupation: Two Post Doctoral positions on the drivers of green capital accumulation in global value chains – GreenWorlds ERC Advanced project
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School (CBS) invites applications for two 3-year Post Doctoral positions on the drivers of green capital accumulation in global value chains, located at the Department of Management, Society and Communication (MSC).

The selected candidates will contribute to the ERC Advanced research project Green Worlds: The material and normative drivers of green capital accumulation in global value chains (GreenWorlds), led by Professor Stefano Ponte.

Overall Project Focus

The GreenWorlds project investigates a core tension in the global economy: how capitalism adapts to ecological pressures and normatively legitimizes itself while maintaining its core logic of capital accumulation alongside the carbon economy. To explore this, the project examines how a variety of ‘green worlds’ of value and valuation emerge, consolidate and decline. Green worlds are different sets of internally coherent principles that are drawn upon by value chain actors to deal with challenges and critiques. They are flexibly assembled by a variety of actors in different value chains and situations to enact justifications related to framing products and/or operations as ‘green’.

The research project asks: What counts as green and for whom? What kinds of practices underpin different green worlds – and how do they shape value chain governance? What are the main features of the green regime of accumulation that crystallizes around these worlds? How does this regime in turn support or disrupt dominant green worlds in particular locations and value chains, and in time—reinforcing, adjusting or breaking a green cycle of capital accumulation?

By comparing selected agro-food value chains (avocados, biodiesel, coffee and wine) in five countries (Argentina, Colombia, Indonesia, Italy and South Africa), the project seeks to explain the contradictory entanglement of ecological concern and capital accumulation, and the limits and possibilities of green transformations.

As part of GreenWorlds, the Post Doctoral candidates will contribute to activities such as:

• Conducting literature reviews and theoretical analysis for publication in top-tier academic outlets.
• Conducting and participating in field research (especially by carrying out key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and participant observation).
• Collaborating in coding of qualitative data (including the basics of natural language processing)
• Presenting, writing and publishing academic papers in peer-reviewed international journals, also in collaboration with the other members of the team
• Engaging in public outreach activities (e.g., blog posts, Linkedin entries, short videos, podcasts).
• Post Doc 1 would be expected to work empirically on two agro-food value chains (wine and biodiesel), especially in Argentina but also globally.
• Post Doc 2 would be expected to work empirically on two agro-food value chains (wine and avocados), especially in South Africa but also globally.
Qualifications

The applicant has obtained a PhD or equivalent by the start date of the Post Doctoral position. In assessing applications, particular emphasis will be placed on research potential – both theoretical and empirical.

The Post-Doctoral positions are non-tenured positions for a 3-year period with research obligations.

To meet the research obligations, the selected candidate is expected to be on site and take part in departmental activities.

Emphasis is placed on research relevant to the job description.

Applicants should have:

• A PhD in the social sciences (e.g., political science, sociology, economic geography)
• Experience with qualitative fieldwork
• Knowledge of the academic literature on international political economy, and/or environmental politics, and/or pragmatic sociology/convention theory, and/or global value chain analysis
• High-level English Language proficiency
• Willingness to reside in Denmark and engage regularly with the CBS research community
• For Post Doc 1, ability to conduct fieldwork in Spanish is required

The Department

The Department of Management, Society and Communication (MSC) brings together scholars from a range of research areas within management, communication and the broader social sciences and humanities, studying organizations in global environments and the interaction and interdependencies of business, society and government. They share a common interest in studying organizations in global environments and the relations of organizations to the wider society. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/msc.

MSC is a significant supplier of research-based teaching to a broad portfolio of programs, which includes undergraduate, graduate and doctoral teaching and supervision as well as executive education in the fields of:

• Responsible management, leadership and governance
• Corporate responsibility and sustainability
• Business and development (with an emphasis on the emerging/growth economies context)
• Organisational communication (corporate communication, strategic communication, leadership communication, marketing communication, international business communication)
Copenhagen Business School has a broad commitment to the excellence, distinctiveness and relevance of its teaching and research programmes. Candidates who wish to join us should demonstrate enthusiasm for working in an organisation of this type. 

For further information please contact:

• Academic Contact: Professor Stefano Ponte spo.msc@cbs.dk 
• HR and hiring process contact: jobcall.msc@cbs.dk 
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organisation.

The application must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link.

The application must include:

• Cover letter (summary of research skills) discussing your alignment with the research objectives of GreenWorlds
• An independently written and original (this means no generative AI usage) 3-year project proposal related to the research objectives of GreenWorlds (max 5 pages / 2,000 words excluding references).
• Complete publication list (mark up to 5 for assessment with *)
• Copies of selected publications (English only)
• Documentation of fieldwork and, if relevant, research management experience
• Transcript(s) and all academic diplomas
• A full and up-to-date CV
• Names and contact details of up to 3 academic referees
It must be clearly indicated in the cover letter as well as the project proposal if the application concerns Post Doc project 1 or Post Doc project 2. If an applicant wishes to apply for both positions, a separate project description must be submitted for each.

Recruitment procedure

The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. 

The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment.

Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application materials by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

Application due: Friday, 6 November 2026. No applications will be accepted beyond the deadline.
Expected starting date: March 2027 or soon thereafter.

You will report to our Engineering Manager and work closely with colleagues across our Engineering teams, both in-house and near-shore.

**What You Will Be Working On

**

****Must-have

**

Would you like to play a key role in leading and coordinating test activities where testing and quality are critical to advanced software solutions? Apply your expertise in a complex and specialized engineering environment. Come and join us!
 We are facing an exciting future with considerable growth and demanding changes, as we deliver advanced technologies and mission critical solutions for the defense and aerospace industry. Our systems provide security for people on land, at sea and in the air. Therefore, we are looking for Test Manager to become part of this journey and contribute to our overall purpose – securing people through advanced technology.
 
Your role in our team
 As our new Advanced Test Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our advanced software solutions within the R&D Defense Test Management department. You will be part of the Test Management team, working closely with experienced test engineers across R&D.
With a strong understanding of systems engineering, verification and validation processes, you will be responsible for securing product quality through strategic test planning, team leadership, test execution, test automation, and close collaboration with stakeholders.
 There is an increasing focus on CI/CD and multiple levels of test automation, which forms an important part of the role and is carried out in close cooperation with software developers, system engineers, fellow testers, and other technical specialists.
 The Test Management department is located across our offices in Lystrup and Søborg, and we expect you to work onsite as it is required for the role.
 
How you will make a meaningful contribution
 Your responsibilities will cover a wide range of testing activities to ensure the quality and reliability of our software solutions. Your key responsibilities include:
·         Plan, monitor, and control the integration and verification of the system
·         Responsible for the Verification Master Plan
·         Point of contact for the verification effort
·         Plan and drive in all test activities and ensure that the system meets the required standards and specifications
·         Support the integration of automated tests with the CI-CD pipeline
·         Contribute to a Test Community of Practice: Engage with other test enthusiasts to share knowledge, best practices, and continuously improve testing methodologies and processes
·         Continuously Improving Ways of Working: Participate in process improvement initiatives to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of testing activities
 
Bring your world class expertise into play
You are fluent in English both in writing and verbal at a professional level. Danish is an advantage but not a requirement. Moreover, we are also looking for a new colleague with the following qualifications:
·          You hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree within Software Engineering or a similar field of study
·         You are certified in software testing principles (ISTQB, TMAP, or similar)
·         You have solid experience with planning and leading test activities in software development
·         You have experience with testing complex systems
·         You have knowledge of software development and an understanding of the fundamentals of software testing and the concepts of system engineering, verification and validation
·         You understand agile development methods (Scrum) and project-oriented processes as well as test automation frameworks and tools 
 
As a person, you have a strong enthusiasm for testing and engineering, motivated by contributing to software solutions that enhance safety through advanced technology. You thrive in complex and specialized environments and maintain a structured, composed approach in fast-paced and demanding situations. With strong communication and leadership capabilities, you are able to lead the test effort effectively while promoting collaboration across teams.

jobs.occupation: Associate Consultant, Netcompany Application Services (Swedish speaking)
jobs.description:
At Netcompany, we’re looking for recent graduates with a bachelor’s degree who want a challenging, social, and fast-developing start to their career as an Associate Consultant. Do you want to help build some of Denmark’s most complex and business-critical IT solutions — in a role where software development, project management, and close client collaboration shape your everyday work?

The Associate Consultant role exists across both Application Services and Consulting. The main difference lies in how you work with clients and solutions, and which setup fits your interests best — either a more project-oriented environment (Consulting) or a more long-term, team- and solution-driven setup (Application Services).

Responsibilities & Technologies

As an Associate Consultant, you’ll help translate client needs into the right technical solutions. We use the technologies that best fit the project and the client, so it’s important that you enjoy working with new and varied technologies and domains while continuously developing your skill set.

A large part of our projects are based on web technologies such as Angular or React, combined with Java or C# on Java or .NET platforms. We also work with several enterprise platforms including Microsoft, Salesforce, IBM, Oracle, Adobe, Snowflake, Guidewire, and more.

As an Associate Consultant, you’ll contribute across the full software development lifecycle with a strong technical focus. Your tasks and responsibilities will vary from project to project and evolve over time, but your day-to-day work will typically include:

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**The Director acts as a statistical expert supporting the clinical development of compounds as compound and/or indication lead for both early and late-stage programs, and/or as trial responsible statistician with responsibilities as described below. The Director contributes to clinical development strategies and plans.

**Responsibilities

**Compound/Indication Level

• Act as lead and main point of contact related to Statistics for designated compound/indication

• Follow scientific and technical progress within the field of biostatistics in drug development and advise of new methodologies that may support innovation and improve efficiencies

• Engage with regulatory authorities on compound/indication level discussions

• Acts as a role model

• Ensures consistency of statistical methods and data handling across trials

• Ensures all compound/indication related work and information is shared between biostatisticians involved in the compound and with the vendor

• Supports compound responsible programmer in developing an integrated database specification

**CDT Member

**

• Responsible for giving statistical input to overall strategy and the synopsis development in the CDT

• Provide scientific advice to the CDT including design of trials, analyses and analyses requiring advanced statistical methodologies/techniques

• Represent the CDT/the company at regulatory meetings, during Key Opinion Leaders meetings, network and/or Partner meetings, as applicable

• Drive design and synopsis development together with relevant stakeholders

• Ensure transparent communication to relevant stakeholders from the CDT

• Ensure availability of integrated database(s), as needed, and planning and conduct of integrated analysis to support development decisions, submissions, and marketing needs

• Support development and communication in relation to communication strategy and/or scientific input to presentations, posters, and articles

Trial Level

• Represent Genmab during meetings/congresses and courses and perform professional networking

• Engage with regulatory authorities on trial level discussions

• Arranges/attends lessons learned to share learnings

• Represents Genmab during Key Opinion Leaders meetings

• Ensure biostatistician review of partner synopsis, protocols, statistical analysis plans, results meetings presentations and clinical trial reports

• Coordinate data transfers from/to business partners in collaboration with the programmer and the data manager, as applicable

• Ensures state of the art statistical work which includes but is not limited to:

• Applying adequate methods for which a solid scientific foundation exists

• Ensure proper documentation of work done

• Keep oversight and QC essential documents/data provided by vendors

• Ensure trial related work is performed in accordance with Genmab SOP/processes and standards and ICH-GCP

**CTT Member

**

• 
Participate and represent Biostatistics

• 
Review and provide input to protocol and amendment development

• 
Perform vendor oversight according to applicable SOPs

• 
Give input to eCRF setup, edit checks, validation plan, protocol deviations classifications, DSUR, IB updates, tables, figures, and listings etc.

• 
Review assay validation reports, as applicable

• 
Perform exploratory analysis, ad hoc analyses, and modelling of data

• 
Review and approve randomization and stratification plans

• 
Perform UAT of Randomization part of the IRT system as applicable

• 
Ensure procedures for blinding are in place as applicable

• 
Support timely delivery of statistical deliverables

• 
Responsible for planning and conducting trial result meetings

• 
Review and approve the CSR

• 
Attend trial and investigator meetings if/as needed

• 
Collaboration with Genmab Global Drug Safety:

• 
Participate in definition, review, and approval of data packages for Data Monitoring Committees

• 
Review and approve any amendments, corrections, and updates of data packages

• 
CRO selection and collaboration

• 
Perform vendor qualification (Request for proposal, bid defense meetings etc.) in terms of Statistics and define/specify scope of work for functional tasks

• 
Review scope of work (within own project) in collaboration with relevant stakeholders and review/challenge major work orders (WOs)/change orders (COs)/change notification forms (CNFs)

• 
Attend operational and steering committee meetings, as applicable

• 
Support regulatory submission/filing activities

**Experience

**

• Master's or PhD in a statistical discipline

• 12+ years of experience in relevant area preferred, or demonstrated capability

• Experience in statistical analysis, modelling and simulation and adaptive trial designs

• Experience with drug development in biologics, targeted therapies, and companion diagnostics preferred

• Experience working with FDA, EMA, and ICH guidance for drug development pertaining to statistics

• Experience with the relevant regulatory requirements for biostatistics processes and SOPs

• Experience with regulatory submissions including BLAs and previous experience in dealing with Health authorities such as discussions/negotiations in filing strategies

• Experience working with SDTM, ADaM, eSUB, and CDISC requirements for regulatory submissions

• Experience directing multiple complex projects/studies in a technical capacity

• Experience leading and mentoring teams

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

$203,440.00---$305,160.00

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

Job Description Summary

Activities contributing to the design, development, and lifecycle support of products, solutions, and systems. Includes activities linked to new product development and technical improvement of existing products and components. The role impacts approaches, projects, and programs within the functional area and supports both R&D and manufacturing activities. Impacts quality, efficiency, and effectiveness of the team. Has significant input into technical priorities and engineering decisions. Guided by professional practices and policies while requiring a high level of operational judgment.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

• Responsible for electronic hardware design and engineering, including designing, developing, modifying, and evaluating electronic circuits, assemblies, and subsystems for medical devices and other hardware systems. Common skill sets include Power Electronics, Analog, Digital, Mixed Signal, Power Management, Battery Systems, DC/DC Converters, Microcontrollers, and Embedded Hardware.

• Develop specialized knowledge within the power electronics discipline and serve as a technical resource within the team. Maintain awareness of the latest technical developments and contribute to engineering strategy, best practices, and technology decisions.

• Apply technical expertise to design robust, reliable, and manufacturable electronic solutions. Perform circuit analysis, hardware debugging, verification testing, root cause investigations, and evaluation of design alternatives.

• Support products throughout their lifecycle, including manufacturing support, production issue resolution, component obsolescence management, design improvements, and implementation of engineering changes.

• Use judgment to solve moderately complex technical problems across product development, manufacturing, quality, and supplier interactions. Take a practical and data-driven approach to identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions.

• Participate in Engineering Change Request (ECR) and Engineering Change Order (ECO) activities, including impact assessments, technical documentation, verification planning, and implementation of design changes.

• Act as a resource for colleagues with less experience. May lead small projects with moderate risks and resource requirements. Explains difficult or sensitive information and works across functions to build consensus and drive technical solutions.

Required Qualifications

• Experience in Engineering/Technology and Electronic Hardware knowledge level is comparable to a Master's degree from an university or college (or equivalent relevant experience).

• Strong background in electronic hardware development with demonstrated experience in power electronics.

• Working knowledge of analog and digital electronics and the integration of complete electronic systems.

• Experience with laboratory testing, troubleshooting, debugging, and verification of electronic hardware.

• Experience supporting manufacturing activities, including root cause analysis, corrective actions, and implementation of hardware improvements.

Desired Characteristics

• Strong experience with power electronics, power supplies, power management, battery-powered products, or related disciplines.

• Experience supporting products in production environments and working with manufacturing, quality, sourcing, and suppliers to resolve technical issues.

• Familiarity with ECR/ECO processes, design transfer, production launch, and lifecycle management activities.

• Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong interpersonal and leadership skills. Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems. Established project management and cross-functional collaboration skills.

Additional Information

**Product Management At Dalux – Built On Real Construction Experience

**Dalux continues to grow rapidly, and we're looking for a Product Manager with something particularly important for our Field product: deep knowledge of how construction actually happens on site.

Dalux Field is used every day by contractors, subcontractors, site managers, quality managers, safety professionals, and other construction professionals around the world.

To continue improving these products, we want even more real-world construction experience within our Product organization.

You might already be working in Product Management or construction technology. But you might also currently be a Site Manager, Construction Manager, Project Manager, BIM/VDC Manager, Digital Construction specialist, or similar and be interested in using your industry experience to improve the digital tools used across construction.

For this role, deep construction knowledge and a strong product mindset are more important than previous Product Manager experience.

**Your responsibilities will include:

**

• Product Discovery: Identify and understand problems experienced by construction professionals and turn them into product opportunities.

• Customer Insights: Spend time with customers and users to understand how work is actually performed on construction sites – not just how processes are supposed to work.

• Domain Expertise: Bring practical construction knowledge into Product and Development and challenge assumptions about real-world workflows.

• Feature Ownership: Lead new capabilities from initial problem discovery through development, release, and validation with users.

• Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with developers, Product Designers, and fellow Product Managers to translate complex construction processes into simple digital experiences.

• Product Prioritization: Balance customer needs, strategic opportunities, technical feasibility, and business impact when deciding what we should build.

• Product Strategy: Help shape the future direction of Dalux Field and identify where technology can fundamentally improve how construction work is performed.

**About You

**Unlike many Product Manager positions, we don't require you to already be an experienced Product Manager .

What we care deeply about is your understanding of construction.

We believe you:

• Have significant practical experience from construction projects, preferably working close to the construction site.

• Understand the everyday workflows of contractors, subcontractors, site managers, and other on-site stakeholders.

• Have experience with areas such as quality assurance, inspections, defects, health & safety, site coordination, documentation, progress, or similar construction processes.

• Understand the difference between how construction processes are designed and how people actually work on site.

• Are passionate about improving construction through digitalization.

• Are curious, analytical, and naturally interested in understanding why problems occur rather than simply accepting existing processes.

• Can communicate effectively with both construction professionals and technically oriented colleagues.

• Are comfortable taking ownership and making decisions.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Previous Product Management or software-development experience is an advantage, but not a requirement.

If you have spent years using construction software and regularly found yourself thinking "surely there must be a better way to do this" , this might be an opportunity to help build that better way.

**What To Expect At Dalux

**At Dalux, you'll join a product-driven company where ideas quickly become reality and where you'll have a direct impact on the products we build.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

**Ready for the next step?

**We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your resume and application as soon as possible.

**About Dalux

**Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics.

Over the past years, we’ve grown by 40% annually and now have over 900 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

**Application deadline:

**As soon as possible

jobs.occupation: Compliance Officer for Financial and Non-Financial Risk Areas
jobs.description:
**About The Role

**Would you like to be part of an ambitious Compliance team where you play a key role in ensuring that Saxo meets its regulatory obligations within financial and non-financial risk areas?

If so, this may be the right opportunity for you at Saxo.

You will join the Prudential Oversight team within Group Compliance, Saxo's second line of defence function, based at our headquarters in Hellerup. Our team oversees compliance risks across a broad range of areas, including the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk, as well as non-financial risk areas such as ICT, operational risk, model risk, data governance and strategy, supporting the business in meeting regulatory requirements, market standards and internal policies.

Your primary responsibility will be to conduct compliance oversight and monitoring across the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk as well as non-financial areas such as operational risk, model risk and strategic risks in relation to policies, procedures, segregation of duties, limits, calculations, samples, controls, etc.

However, if you are curious about the other areas covered by the team, we will help you develop your skills and knowledge within these areas.

As a team, we balance professionalism with a sense of humour and maintain an informal atmosphere where people enjoy coming to work.

**Responsibilities

**

• Perform compliance risk assessments

• Provide advice and compliance opinions to the business on managing compliance risks and regulatory requirements

• Conduct compliance monitoring activities

• Contribute to regular compliance reporting to senior management of the bank

• Participate in developing the bank’s compliance framework

• Interact with the business across organisational levels and seniority

**Your profile

**We are looking for a colleague with experience from working with one or more prudential risk areas, who is motivated to develop deeper expertise in these areas.

**Further We Expect You To Have

**

• At least 2 years of relevant experience from the financial sector, preferably within compliance, risk management, audit, finance, credit or another relevant first-line function

• A relevant educational background within economics, finance, accounting, audit or similar

• Interest in prudential risk areas such as capital, liquidity, market risk, credit risk, model risk, strategic risk, operational risk areas, governance, and internal controls

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements such as CRR/CRD, Basel guidelines, EBA/ESMA guidelines, the Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks and other relevant Danish financial regulation is an advantage

Moreover, we are looking for someone who is detail-oriented, can work independently while taking an active role in teamwork and enjoys collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across the entire organisation.

It is an advantage if you thrive in an environment with constant change, bring a positive and curious mindset to work, and do not buy into the word ‘cannot’.

You must possess strong stakeholder management skills and use your communication skills to ensure positive collaboration and progress in joint tasks. We are looking for a colleague who always brings a positive attitude when liaising with the business.

Please note! International applicants are encouraged to apply. To help us understand your circumstances, we kindly ask candidates currently based outside Denmark to include a brief summary of their relocation plans and expected timeframe for relocating to Denmark.

**We get curious people invested in the world

**When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

**How To Apply

**Click here to create an account and upload your resume and a short motivation. We look forward to getting to know you better!

jobs.occupation: Oliver Wyman – Senior Consultant- (m/f/d) – Stockholm or Copenhagen
jobs.description:
**Who We Are

**Oliver Wyman is a global management consulting firm. We work with clients through their most defining moments, combining deep industry knowledge, specialized expertise, and the power of perspective to help them adapt, grow, and thrive.

We believe diverse perspectives make the work stronger. Our consultants bring different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking to help solve complex problems and create lasting impact for clients, colleagues, and communities.

At Oliver Wyman, we are proud of the values that we aspire to live by. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their full potential.

**What You Will Do

**As a Senior Consultant, you will play a pivotal role in shaping client engagements from problem definition through implementation. You will work alongside colleagues of all levels and clients to solve complex problems and drive meaningful change.

You’ll help teams understand client strategic challenges while helping develop the next generation of consultants.

**You will:

**

• Lead workstreams on client engagements, structuring analyses and developing actionable recommendations that support client decision-making.

• Frame hypotheses, identify key business questions, and direct quantitative and qualitative research to generate insights.

• Apply structured problem-solving and analytical thinking to solve complex business issues.

• Develop high-quality client deliverables, including presentations, analysis, workshops, models, and discussions that help move projects forward.

• You’ll have the opportunity to work across our industries and capabilities, with the flexibility to specialize early or explore different areas before choosing a path.

• You’ll likely have the chance to travel within your home market and internationally. No two weeks are ever the same.

• Manage and coach junior team members, fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and high-performing team environment.

• Build trusted relationships with clients through clear communication and effective stakeholder management.

**Why join us?

****You can be your best here

**At Oliver Wyman, you will find meaningful work, talented people, and a culture built on trust, support, and growth.

**Create solutions that have impact

**

• Work on challenging projects that help clients solve complex problems, make better decisions, and create meaningful impact.

• Have the opportunity to work across different industries, capabilities, and cultures, contributing to work that has lasting impact for clients, industries, and society.

• Be part of teams that measure success not just by deliverables, but by the difference created together.

**Develop as a leader

**

• Lead workstreams and develop expertise that colleagues and clients seek out.

• Mentor junior consultants while continuing to build your own leadership capabilities.

• Take ownership of client relationships and increasingly complex engagements.

**Learn and grow without limits

**

• Continue developing specialized expertise through challenging projects and formal learning opportunities.

• Collaborate with industry specialists and global experts across Oliver Wyman.

• Build a sustainable career supported by coaching, mentoring, and continuous professional development.

• You’ll have support around you as you grow, including a dedicated buddy, a career advisor, your talent manager, and communities that help you find your place.

**Thrive in a vibrant and inclusive culture

**

• Work with genuine colleagues who stand by their beliefs, collaborate across differences, and support one another.

• Be part of an open, inclusive, and down-to-earth culture where diverse perspectives strengthen the work.

• Connect with colleagues through employee resource groups, office communities, and social activities.

**Experience Rewards That Work For You

**

• We believe in flexibility, including hybrid working, and in helping colleagues build sustainable careers.

• Over time, you’ll have access to opportunities, programs, and experiences designed to help you perform, grow, and thrive — including non-profit fellowships, sabbaticals, and externships.

• Enjoy competitive local benefits designed to support your well-being, development, and life outside of work.

**Who can apply?

**We are looking for top-performing professionals who are passionate about solving complex business problems, enjoy developing high-impact content, and are excited to build a long-term career at a leading strategy consulting firm characterized by sustained double-digit growth, an entrepreneurial spirit, and a strong focus on culture and career sustainability.

**Required Qualifications

**

• 3+ years of relevant experience in a top-tier strategy consulting firm.

• Experience serving clients within Banking and Financial Services, Finance and Risk, Restucturing, Insurance, Logistic, is highly advantageous.

• Undergraduate or advanced degree in STEM, Finance, Economics, or a related quantitative discipline from a leading university.

• Outstanding analytical and quantitative problem-solving capabilities with the ability to structure ambiguous business problems.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across different audiences and seniority levels.

• Demonstrated experience working collaboratively in cross-functional, fast-paced environments.

• Proven ability to deliver results under pressure while managing multiple priorities.

• Fluent business English and another Scandinavian language

• Willingness to travel internationally as client needs require.

**Nice to have

**

• Data analytics, advanced quantitative modelling, or data science capabilities.

• CFA or equivalent professional certification.

• MBA or Master's degree from a top-tier university.

**What we're looking for?

**Successful candidates demonstrate:

• Intellectual curiosity and structured problem solving.

• Strong ownership and accountability.

• Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills.

• An inclusive leadership style and commitment to developing others.

• Adaptability, resilience, and entrepreneurial thinking.

• A collaborative mindset with the ability to work respectfully across diverse teams and cultures.

**How to apply?

**Please submit your CV, cover letter, and academic transcripts. If you would like to find out more information about Oliver Wyman, please visit our website.

**What to expect during the interviews process?

**At Oliver Wyman, we want you to shine in your interview. Our process is designed like our work environment — it’s challenging, exciting, and fun.

With a mix of conversational and case interviews, our approach not only helps us to get to know you better, understanding your strengths and interests, but it also enables you to learn more about our people and our business..

Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective.
