jobs.description:
Picture yourself serving as a trusted advisor to the Danish management team in a global company, where your contribution can truly make a difference. Then imagine holding this meaningful position while working on what you do best – analysis, forecasting, and numbers.

Basico is recruiting a Senior Finance Business Partner on behalf of Circle K.

Allow us to bring the vision to life! At Circle K they are looking for you, with experience from similar roles - ready to step into this position and become part of our ambitious and highly skilled team in the Performance Management Analytics (PMA) department, based out of the Danish headquarter in Copenhagen, Sydhavn, Denmark.

It’s a numbers game – and you’ve mastered it

Circle K is one of the leading companies in Denmark in the convenience, energy, and fuel delivery sector. In Denmark, Circle K operates two different brands – Circle K and INGO – spread across 436 locations, with 211 of those operated under the Circle K brand.

As a part of Circle K’s PMA team, you will have 3 skilled colleagues you can consult with on financial matters. However, as you will be working with many different stakeholders, you will quickly learn that cooperation and collaboration across the organization is key – especially for this role.

As Senior Finance Business Partner, you will be the responsible sparring partner to both their Mobility and Sales department, translating numbers into actionable insights, building business cases, and much more. This involves sparring and partnering with the organization on matters such as fuel, E-Mobility, Car wash, B2B Customers, and more.

To be specific, your main responsibilities will be to:

· Partner with the Mobility and Sales department to create transparency in financial figures and drive qualified decision-making through fact-based recommendations.

· Work closely with the business to identify challenges and optimization opportunities.

· Analyze business performance and bring financial insights and recommendations to management.

· Improve and execute budgeting and forecasting processes within your area of responsibility, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and alignment with other areas.

· Analyze and explain developments in month-end figures.

· Build and review business cases.

· Communicate and present business cases and ad hoc analysis to management and other stakeholders.

Your business acumen makes you the preferred advisor

To be successful in this role, we imagine you have at least a few years' experience from a similar role. Since you are used to managing the interests of many different stakeholders, you have already tested your ability to work in a structured and proactive manner in an ever-changing environment, where balancing tasks is key to success.

You might hold a degree in Economics and Business administration, Accounting or Finance. Most important is however your authentic curiosity to understand causal relationships, developments, trends, and the willingness to dive into an Excel sheet full of numbers to grasp what is happening.

If you are an ambitious profile with solid understanding of finance processes, has an analytical mindset, and are motivated to make a difference, you will be a great match for the PMA team.

As sparring partner to the business, it is also important that you are able to simplify complex issues and present them with confidence to all levels in the organization in an inspiring way that makes people listen.

As you become part of an international organization where you advise colleagues from different countries, it is necessary that you are fluent in both English and Danish.

On the right path – Come join Circle K!

You will become part of an international organization in rapid development, working with many exciting initiatives redefining the future of Circle K’s business. Furthermore, when they say that diversity and sustainability are on the agenda, they mean it, and they care—also about future generations. Circle K have several initiatives they would love to tell you more about when you meet.

Circle K’s four core values—One Team, Do The Right Thing, Take Ownership, Play To Win—reflect the culture you will become a part of. When joining the PMA team, you will learn that humor, professionalism and a willingness to take responsibility are significant parts of the company’s DNA. If you have the same DNA, we will look forward to hearing from you.

Do you have all the facts you need to make your next move? Then send us your CV and application via the link below. We process applications confidentially and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

If you have any questions about the position, please feel free to contact Gitte Hjortskov Larsen, Director of Executive Search & Recruitment at Basico, by phone at +45 2510 2217.

At Circle K, there is room for everyone, and they always work together as One Team! Circle K value diversity and different ways of thinking and working. We therefore encourage you not to include a photo on your CV.

On behalf of our client, Anticimex Innovation Center, Asgaard Recruitment is seeking a Senior Firmware Engineer to strengthen the firmware engineering team and contribute to the development, improvement, and industrialization of smart, connected products operating in demanding real-world environments.

Anticimex is a global leader in modern pest control and prevention. At Anticimex Innovation Center, ideas move from sketch to prototype to smart devices that transform pest control into a data-driven and more sustainable industry.

The role

As Senior Firmware Engineer, you will take a central role in developing and improving the firmware that brings connected devices to life, working closely with electronics, mechanics, and software/cloud teams to ensure that hardware and firmware perform reliably together.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Develop and improve firmware for low-power, wireless IoT devices, from bring-up through production release

• 
Lead the structured transition of selected firmware development and verification activities from external partners to internal ownership, including tooling, documentation, and knowledge transfer

• 
Own firmware architecture in selected projects, including driver development, wireless connectivity stacks, and over-the-air (OTA) update mechanisms

• 
Contribute to verification and validation activities, including hardware/firmware bring-up, test planning, troubleshooting, certification readiness, and release processes

• 
Strengthen Stage-Gate execution, design review practices, documentation quality, engineering change processes, and controlled releases

• 
Collaborate closely with firmware architect, electronics, mechanics, software/cloud, production colleagues, internal stakeholders, and external suppliers

Who you are

You are an experienced firmware engineer with deep technical expertise and a strong interest in building connected products for the real world. You enjoy hands-on embedded development, structured problem-solving, and turning technical findings into robust, production-ready solutions.

• 
7–10+ years of experience in embedded firmware development

• 
Strong experience with embedded C/C++ and real-time operating systems (e.g. FreeRTOS, Zephyr) or bare-metal development

• 
Experience with battery-powered IoT devices and low-power wireless connectivity (e.g. BLE, LoRaWAN, or cellular IoT)

• 
Experience with firmware architecture, driver development, and over-the-air (OTA) update mechanisms

• 
Experience with version control, automated testing, and CI/CD for embedded systems

• 
Experience working in structured product development models such as Stage-Gate

• 
Knowledge of security practices for connected devices (Ideally RED+CRA)

• 
Professional proficiency in English

Anticimex Innovation Center is at a pivotal moment. Moving from a fast-moving scale-up approach toward a more professional and scalable product-development organization, without losing agility.

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
AI-augmented Physiological Modelling for Prediction and Mitigation of Heat Stress in Pigs

Research area and project description:
Heat stress is an increasing challenge to pig production and animal welfare, particularly during hot seasons. Effective mitigation requires not only the detection of elevated heat load, but also the ability to predict how animals respond dynamically and to determine when and how cooling interventions should be applied. Existing mechanistic thermal models provide an important basis for representing animal heat balance and physiological responses. However, their ability to incorporate real-time physiological observations, account for model assumptions and environmental stochasticity, and support timely intervention decisions remains limited. At the same time, purely data-driven black-box approaches are challenging to develop and validate when high-quality physiological datasets are limited, as is often the case in controlled animal experiments.

This PhD project aims to develop a physics-informed digital model for predicting and mitigating heat stress in pigs. Building on conventional mechanistic models of pig physiological responses, the project will investigate how physiological modelling can be combined with AI approaches to develop a more robust and interpretable representation of the pig’s thermal state. To further enhance the accessibility and practical use of the model, the project will also explore how large language models (LLMs) can be integrated with the physiological model to facilitate interactive exploration of model behaviour and predictions.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:
• A MSc degree in Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or related filed.
• A strong academic background and interest in HVAC systems in buildings, and fluid and thermal systems modelling.
• Proven experience in data analytics, machine learning, and optimisation.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams.
• Excellent written and spoken English skills.It is considered an advantage if you have:
• Knowledge of animal heat stress and animal welfare.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Sustainable Supply Chain Management and Organization - DTU Management
jobs.description:
Are you a collaborative and ambitious master's graduate with strong intercultural awareness and a curiosity for exploring sustainability challenges across different contexts and disciplines? Would you like to help shape the next generation of sustainable and regenerative global supply chains through a unique collaboration between the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Nairobi, Kenya? DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship at the intersection of supply chain management and organization studies. Focusing on global agricultural commodity chains, the project explores how supply chains can create positive environmental and social impacts rather than simply reducing negative ones. It examines regenerative approaches that renew ecological and social systems while being collectively organized with local communities.

The PhD position is anchored at DTU Management and contributes to the department's strategic focus on developing viable and sustainable systems. You will join an international research environment at the forefront of sustainable supply chain management and organization studies, collaborating with researchers and partners in Denmark and Kenya. The project combines literature-based and empirical research on regenerative agri-food supply chains with fieldwork and data collection in Denmark and Kenya. The project will be supervised by Associate Professor Lærke Højgaard Christiansen and Assistant Professor Lara Schilling at DTU and will include an extended research stay at the University of Nairobi under the co-supervision of Senior Lecturer Thomas Ombati and Lecturer Veronica Wambui Mwangi. 

Based in Copenhagen – consistently ranked among the world's most livable cities – you will enjoy a high quality of life, a safe and sustainable urban environment, and a thriving cultural scene. At the same time, you'll be part of a vibrant, interdisciplinary research community at one of Europe's top technical universities, known for its commitment to innovation, societal impact, and diversity.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how global agricultural commodity chains, such as tea or coffee, can be managed based on regenerative principles. The project offers a unique opportunity to develop an international and interdisciplinary research profile at the intersection of organization studies and supply chain management. As part of the DTU Management PhD Program, you will follow a structured research and training program that combines independent research, academic coursework, teaching, and professional development.

Mandatory requirements:

• You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
• An educational background in the social sciences 
• A familiarity with supply chain management, organization studies, or related fields such as (human) geography
• Have a strong interest in sustainability, regenerative systems, and the organization of global supply chains
• Strong speaking and writing skills in English
Further, the following qualities will be valued highly in the assessment:

• Research vision and potential 
• Evidence of academic accomplishment (e.g., high grades, timely graduation)
• Knowledge and experience with qualitative research methods and empirical fieldwork 
• Scholarly/academic writing skills 
• Familiarity with Kenya’s socio-cultural context, or experience in settings with transferable relevance, is desirable but not required.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years. The envisaged starting date is as soon as possible. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Lara Schilling (larasc@dtu.dk) and Lærke Højgaard Christiansen (laerc@dtu.dk)

You can read more about the Department of Technology, Management and Economics at https://www.man.dtu.dk/english

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A research statement (2–3 pages) outlining your research ideas and explaining your suitability for carrying out the project. Please engage with relevant scholarly literature on regenerative supply chains and organization. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and potential; it is not a binding proposal, and the research plan may be further developed and refined in collaboration with the supervisory team upon enrolment in the PhD program.
• One copy of a selected written work (e.g., master’s thesis)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Management
DTU Management conducts excellent research at the intersection of management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master, and PhD levels across DTU's study programs. The department has 250+ employees with around half of staff coming from abroad. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral positions and DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowship at the Cosmic Dawn Center
jobs.description:
The Cosmic Dawn Center (DAWN) invites applications for both the DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowship and postdoctoral positions to work on specific projects.

  DAWN is a Center of Excellence funded by the Danish National Research Foundation (DNRF) and is located in the Copenhagen area at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen and the Space division of the Danish Technical University (DTU-Space). In addition, DAWN has several associates at major research institutes across Europe, North America, and Australia. DAWN brings together experts in all aspects of early Universe research and is deeply involved in major existing and upcoming surveys with JWST and HST (e.g. SPURS, COSMOS3D, FRESCO, COSMOS-Web, RUBIES, BEACON, and CLUTCH), ALMA (e.g. CHAMPS), and Euclid (e.g. Cosmic Dawn Survey of the deep fields), as well as simulations. 

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended for outstanding scientists whose research falls within DAWN’s research themes focused on the early Universe: first stars, high-redshift galaxy evolution, reionization and evolution of the IGM, high-redshift transients and supernovae, dust and ISM in the early Universe, massive galaxy evolution, and dark matter. DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows are expected to pursue their own independent, cutting-edge research programs in collaboration with DAWN members.

  Postdoctoral positions

  Up to two postdoctoral position are available as part of the DFF Sapere Aude-funded project “Revealing Massive Stars at Cosmic Dawn” in Associate Professor Charlotte Mason’s group at DAWN/NBI to work on both observational and theoretical projects on galaxy formation and reionization, with a particular focus on JWST spectroscopy from the SPURS survey. Applicants with interests and expertise in any of galaxy formation, stellar populations, Lyman-alpha emission, IGM/CGM evolution, galaxy-dark matter connections at high redshift, JWST NIRSpec spectroscopy, statistical inference and comparing hydrodynamical simulations to observations are strongly encouraged to apply.

  Additional postdoctoral positions may be available to work on specific projects at DAWN funded through individual group leadership grants. Applicants with research interests in any of the above DAWN research themes are strongly encouraged to apply. 

  Applicants to this position will be automatically considered for all available postdoctoral and Postdoctoral Fellowship positions at DAWN/NBI. We note a separation application is required for applications to the positions at DAWN/DTU in the group of Associate Professor Kasper Heintz.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows and postdocs are encouraged to collaborate with DAWN’s international associates, and have the opportunity to supervise students and to apply for grants and observing proposals as PI. More information on DAWN’s activities and researchers is available at https://cosmicdawn.dk.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships and postdoc positions are for up to three years. The employment can start as early as Spring 2027 or upon agreement with the chosen candidate.

  Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to Associate Professor Charlotte Mason charlotte.mason@nbi.ku.dk.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellows and postdocs receive generous support for computing, travel and publication expenses. Most non-Danish citizens are eligible for a favorable tax scheme. Copenhagen is a beautiful, family-friendly city with a large international community, a lively and diverse cultural scene, and a very high quality of life. We offer an attractive starting salary plus pension and negotiation for a salary supplement is possible. Benefits include six weeks paid vacation and generous benefits including: pension, full health cover (also for family), paid sick leave and paid parental leave. More on employment conditions and living in Copenhagen: http://ism.ku.dk. 

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter – maximum 1 page, describing your motivation for applying to DAWN 	
• Research plan – maximum 3 pages including figures and references, description of current and future research plans 	
• Curriculum vitae, including a list of up to 3 people who could be contacted for references 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree, if applicable, or equivalent – a letter from your university/supervisor stating you have completed requirements for these degrees and are in the final year of a PhD is fine) 	
• Publication list   The deadline for applications is 6 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in Economics at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one fully funded PhD scholarship at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark. The position is based at SDU’s Esbjerg campus.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the 5+3 PhD programme. The programme includes a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offers a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January 2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within five research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; Microeconomics; and Environmental and Resource Economics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Environmental and Resource Economics (ERE) group, which focuses on Environmental and Natural resource economics on a variety of topics, namely ecosystem conservation and use, marine resource use, management and conservation, energy transitions, climate regulation, and interdisciplinary research at the interface between economics and the natural sciences. The group applies economic theory and tools to policy and analysis to provide guidance for more efficient use of environmental and natural resource goods and services.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professors Ana Faria Lopes and Melina Kourantidou.  Part of the work will contribute to the BRAVE (Biological Invasions Resolved through Adaptable, Versatile, and Engaging Nature-Based Solutions) project, a Biodiversa+ -funded project that investigates the complex ecological and societal challenges associated with invasive species and their management. In particular, the research will contribute to the Danish BRAVE case study on the invasive Pacific oyster in the Wadden Sea, including work on stakeholder preferences, economic values, and trade-offs associated with its management. For further information about the project, please see this link or this link.

The project relies on the application of economic theories, namely non-market valuation and bioeconomic modelling, to investigate the management of invasive species. We welcome candidates with strong quantitative and analytical skills from economics or related disciplines, including candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds and an interest in environmental and resource management.  There will be considerable scope for the PhD student to develop their own research questions within the broader themes of the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, through both collaborative research and independent work, including a single-authored paper. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Ana Faria Lopes as the main supervisor and will join a research group that includes postdoctoral researcher and research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Environmental and Resource Management, Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in data analysis and applied quantitative methods using R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have willingness to participate in stakeholder engagement activities and communicate research findings to different audiences. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, non-market valuation, press analysis, GIS and/or bioeconomic modelling.

• 
Experience conducting empirical research.

• 
Demonstrated interest in environmental and resource economics.

• 
Knowledge of Danish or another Scandinavian language would be an advantage for stakeholder engagement and work with locally relevant material but is not a requirement.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

The application must include (all attachments must be in Adobe PDF format): 

• 
Detailed CV - the education and work history must be month and year specific.

• 
A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results.  Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used.

• 
A motivational letter describing why the applicant is a good match for analyzing the topic and how the applicant’s skills provide a solid foundation to do so (max. 5 pages incl. reference list).

• 
A project description (max 5 pages of 2400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.).

• 
When applying for a PhD scholarship, please fill in the application form available on our web page. 

On the webpage of the PhD-school, you can find the guidelines for preparing your project proposal.

All non-Danish documents must be translated into English.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.

Once the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the portion of the evaluation that pertains to them.

Applications that are incomplete regarding the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee.

Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process.

As part of the overall assessment of the applicant’s qualifications, an interview may be applied.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

The application and CV must not exceed 10 MB.

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, 23.59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website. Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked) or Word format.

We recommend that you read the guideline for applicants. If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk before the application deadline.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in High-Speed Hyperspectral and Super-Resolution Terahertz Imaging - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in pushing terahertz (THz) imaging beyond today’s limits in speed, bandwidth, and spatial resolution? 

At DTU Electro, you will work at the interface of ultrafast THz photonics, nonlinear optical detection, coherent imaging, and machine learning to develop a new generation of high-speed hyperspectral THz imaging technology.

The PhD project is part of the DFF-funded INSPIRING project (High-speed hyperspectral and super-resolution terahertz imaging). INSPIRING will combine broadband THz-to-near-infrared upconversion with CMOS-array detection to enable high-speed THz imaging. Your main role will be to establish the imaging platform and develop hyperspectral and machine-learning methods for super-resolution imaging and material identification.

You will work in an international, interdisciplinary team at DTU Electro. The project includes a planned 3–6-month research stay in Prof. Xi-Cheng Zhang’s group at the University of Rochester, USA.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on high-speed coherent THz imaging with machine learning. 

You will:

• Develop and operate a broadband coherent THz imaging platform using optical rectification and/or laser-induced plasma THz sources.
• Implement wide-field imaging based on THz-to-NIR upconversion and CMOS focal-plane-array detection.
• Acquire and analyze time-domain hyperspectral THz data with a target bandwidth above 10 THz.
• Apply machine-learning methods, including CNN and autoencoder-type architectures, for super-resolution reconstruction and material identification.
• Study semiconductors, polymers, multilayer structures, and industrial test samples, and collaborate with project partners in Denmark and abroad. 
• Publish your results in peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences.
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with a strong background in experimental photonics, optics, applied physics, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. Experience with THz spectroscopy, ultrafast laser systems, nonlinear optics, or optical imaging is highly desirable. Experience with scientific programming, data analysis, image processing, or machine learning will be considered an advantage. You should have a strong interest in experimental research and be comfortable working with complex optical setups as well as analyzing large multidimensional datasets. We value creativity, independent problem-solving, and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. You should also have good communication skills and be able to present and communicate your scientific results clearly in written and spoken English.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Associate Professor Binbin Zhou, Professor Peter Uhd Jepsen, and Associate Professor Francesco Da Ros. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The start date is 1 January 2027 (or by mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Binbin Zhou at zhou@dtu.dk. 

You can read more about DTU Electro at www.electro.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Picture your typical week: on Monday you’re on-site at a pharmaceutical client, leading a cross-functional team through a critical MES go-live. By Wednesday you’re working with the IT leadership to turn your delivery results into a business case for the next phase. Friday, you’re back at Emendo’s Nordhavn office sharing what you learned and sharpening the methods your colleagues will use on their projects. If that sounds like work you’d love, keep reading.

Why We’re Hiring Now

We paused hiring over the past year to be deliberate about the team we build next. The consulting market in Denmark has tightened, and our clients have changed how they buy: they want fewer consultants with more experience, people who can walk into a complex situation and show measurable progress within weeks, not months. We are now making a small number of senior hires — each one matters, and we are taking the time to find the right people.

About Emendo

Emendo is a 200-person consultancy built by people who used to sit on the client side — running transformation programmes inside pharma before deciding to do it for a living. We understand the pressure a site director feels before a go-live, we know what an inspector looks for, and we speak the language of the people who operate the systems we implement. We work across the full pharmaceutical value chain from R&D through shipping, with offices in Copenhagen, Kalundborg, Odense, Silkeborg, Munich, and Raleigh (USA). Our strategy is simple: deliver faster, prove value in hard numbers, and use our methods and AI tools to do what we do well — only quicker.

We are a methods-driven firm rooted in operational excellence and Lean. Our motto, Observe, Think, Improve, is itself a method: go to the floor, understand what is actually happening, analyse it rigorously, then design and implement a concrete improvement. That simplicity is what makes it reliable when the project gets complicated and the usual playbooks stop working.

The Role

You will lead IT/OT transformation engagements for clients in pharma and regulated industries — operating at the intersection of technology, business process, and organisational change. You are expected to create measurable impact from the outset, build trusted relationships with client stakeholders, and identify opportunities to expand Emendo’s footprint within your accounts. At Emendo, seniority means more than years served: it means sound judgement in ambiguity, credibility with demanding stakeholders, and the willingness to raise the standard of the whole team.

What You Will Do

• Lead client engagements on-site, owning delivery of IT/OT implementations across enterprise, operations management, process control, and process equipment layers

• Drive measurable progress in short cycles — the kind your client’s leadership can point to in a steering committee: cost reduced, lead time shortened, risk closed out

• Manage project governance, solution architecture alignment, and validation concepts within complex, multi-stakeholder environments

• Shape how Emendo works — contribute to our methods, package what you learn into repeatable offerings and case studies, and use AI tools to deliver faster without cutting corners

• Build lasting client relationships — become a trusted partner to your stakeholders, spot opportunities for follow-on work, and contribute to Emendo’s business development by turning strong delivery into new engagements

• Apply Observe, Think, Improve as your foundation — and mentor junior colleagues to do the same

What It Takes

Must-Have Qualifications

• Master’s degree in engineering, IT, or a related discipline

• 6–10+ years of hands-on delivery experience in IT/OT project management, product ownership, or solution implementation — ideally within pharma or other regulated industries, though strong candidates from adjacent sectors are welcome

• Track record of delivering quantifiable business outcomes (cost reduction, lead-time improvement, risk mitigation) — not just on-time/on-budget projects

• Strong command of project governance, stakeholder management, and the ability to engage credibly with C-suite and senior client leadership

• Deep understanding of at least one area: enterprise systems (ERP/MES), process control, IT–OT convergence, or value chain technology

• Fluent English, both written and spoken; Danish skills are strongly preferred, or a commitment to learn

• Willingness to work on-site at client locations in Denmark and occasionally internationally

Nice to have — but not required

None of the following are dealbreakers. If you tick even one or two, it tells us you will ramp up faster — but we have seen great consultants arrive without any of them and build the expertise here.

• Experience with GxP compliance, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), or regulatory frameworks in life sciences

• Familiarity with AI/automation tools applied to enterprise transformation or operational settings

• Background in operational excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement methodologies

• Experience working across multiple sites or geographies in global transformation programmes

• Comfort with outcome-based or fixed-price engagement models

What Makes Emendo Different

• Measured on outcomes, not utilisation — you work directly with industry leaders on engagements that matter

• One integrated firm with deep methods: cross-unit collaboration across Implementation, Engineering, Digital, and R&D, backed by a Lean toolbox and AI accelerators

• Freedom under responsibility — challenging projects with room to shape the solution and your own career

• A flat culture where your input matters and your wins are celebrated

• Competitive compensation reflecting the seniority and impact expected in this role

This role is probably not for you if:

• You prefer purely advisory work with limited implementation responsibility.

• You work best with narrow ownership and very clear boundaries.

• You have strong technical exposure but limited experience leading cross-functional change.

Ready to Make an Impact?

We are hiring two to three Senior Consultants this year. Each one joins a team that has led some of the largest IT/OT programmes in US and European pharma — people who chose Emendo because they wanted senior-level impact in a firm that still feels personal. If that resonates, we’d like to hear from you.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. We will be in touch promptly.

For further information, reach out to Mikael Elley (me@emendo.com or +45 24 83 62 01).

jobs.occupation: Are you our new GTM Engineer?
jobs.description:
About the Role

In this cross-functional, individual-contributor role, you will build, operate, and iterate Accutics' GTM revenue system across the entire sales lifecycle: Accounts → contacts → signals → outreach → meetings → pipeline → revenue → expansion.

You will not only be responsible for filling the funnel; you will own the systems, data, routing, and operational efficiency to ensure a seamless handoff, maximum conversion velocity, and a reliable path from activity to revenue using a modern GTM stack (Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...).

You will work side-by-side with our AEs, Product Marketer, and CPO, and report directly to the CEO. This is a hands-on role for a technical self-starter who builds things themselves, takes ownership, experiments quickly, and turns successful tests into production systems.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead Generation & Demand Capture: Build, operate, and iterate targeted, multi-channel campaigns across outbound, ABM, and account expansion to generate qualified meetings, pipeline, and revenue. Build account/contact lists, enrich prospects, identify signals, and activate contacts through appropriate channels.

• Sales Enablement & Alignment: Act as a GTM systems partner to the sales team. Deliver well-qualified accounts and contacts equipped with deep contextual data, signals, and account intelligence. Onboard sales reps into workflows and ensure system transparency so it saves them time rather than becoming a black box.

• AI-Supported Revenue Operations: Build and operate the GTM technology and data stack. Build robust enrichment, scoring, routing, synchronization, and automation workflows.

• Market & Persona Strategy: Translate ICP, enterprise account, and persona strategies into repeatable GTM workflows and continuously iterate based on performance.

• Flawless Tracking: “Drink our own champagne.” Utilize the Accutics platform internally to guarantee that our own campaign tracking, naming conventions, and metadata are perfectly structured from the point of creation. Maintain high-quality GTM and CRM data so pipeline and revenue can be reliably measured.

• Full-Funnel Analytics: Monitor the GTM system and its commercial performance from initial account targeting through closed-won revenue and account expansion. Identify bottlenecks and build solutions to fix them.

What We Are Looking For

Required:

· Enterprise GTM Execution: 1–3 years of hands-on experience in GTM Engineering, GTM Operations, or RevOps, preferably in GTM agency or B2B SaaS. Proven track record taking outbound, ABM, and expansion campaigns from concept to production.

· GTM Engineering & Data: Hands-on experience with Clay (including Function and Workflow capabilities), bidirectional CRM sync with Salesforce, APIs, webhooks, and automation workflow logic.

· AI / Agentic GTM: Experience experimenting with and deploying production multi-agent GTM systems built with Claude Code, Codex, or similar tools.

· Working Style: Highly autonomous, operationally disciplined, and commercially minded, measuring success by quality pipeline and revenue, not top-of-funnel metrics.

A Plus:

· Experience with GTM tools such as email and LinkedIn sequencers, unified inboxes, email infrastructure, enrichment, intent/signal, LinkedIn social warming, call dialer.

· Experience building other GTM workflows: account expansion/ churn/ partner sales/ inbound flywheel.

· Experience building Salesforce CRM data foundation, CRM data cleaning routines for modern GTM.

· Comfortable handling SQL, Agent loops.

What We Offer

· Ownership: Build, operate, and iterate Accutics' new GTM revenue system across the sales lifecycle.

· Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with Clay, Claude Code/Codex, Instantly, HeyReach, ...

· Commercial Impact: Direct impact on pipeline generation, deal velocity, and revenue while returning time to sales teams.

· Agile Environment: Small, international SaaS team with high autonomy, short decision paths, and direct leadership access.

· Copenhagen Office: Central Copenhagen location, Nordic work-life balance, flexible hours, and regular social events.

· Package: Permanent full-time position, competitive salary, pension, and benefits.

Requirements

• You have a valid work permit to work in Europe (Denmark).

• You are fluent in English, both verbally and in writing.

• You are located in the Greater Copenhagen Area (Denmark) or will be relocating here.

Hiring Process

1. GTM Builder Interview: Meet a GTM builder and demonstrate systems you have built and deployed.

2. CEO Interview: Discuss Accutics, the role, and how you will shape the GTM engine.

3. Build Together Session: Collaboratively solve a real GTM challenge to demonstrate your build and testing approach.

What Success Looks Like (3-6 Months)

· Take full build and iteration responsibility for Accutics' GTM revenue system.

· Establish and run daily operational routines, onboarding sales reps to maintain workflow transparency.

· Bring the Salesforce data foundation up to the standard of your new GTM system.

· Continuously test new tools, workflows, and solutions to eliminate sales friction and deliver quality pipeline and revenue.

About Accutics

Accutics is a Copenhagen-based B2B SaaS company providing the ultimate data foundation for global enterprise marketing. We work with the world’s leading brands. Our platform standardizes campaign tracking, governs taxonomy, and ensures data is AI-ready, eliminating manual QA loops for confident, data-informed decisions.

Proud of our Nordic roots, we combine deep domain expertise with close collaboration. We are a small, international team looking for a GTM Engineer to build, operate, and continuously improve a modern, AI-native revenue system across the entire funnel.

How to Apply

Think you’re the right fit? Apply today by submitting your resume and a brief cover letter. You can email it to careers@accutics.com.

Would you like to help build and develop the platform that makes it easier for Whiteaway’s software Engineers to develop, deploy and run their solutions?

Whiteaway Group is looking for a skilled Platform Engineer to join their Platform Squad in Aarhus.

As a Platform Engineer, you will become part of a strong technical environment focused on building and continuously improving the platform used by Whiteaway’s development teams in their daily work.

This is not traditional IT operations. Instead, the focus is on creating automated, stable and scalable solutions that make it easier for Engineers to develop, deploy and run their software.

Whiteaway is a digital-first company where technology plays a central role in the business. The company operates some of the largest online stores in the Nordics within electronics and home appliances, and its technical platforms are an important part of the continued development of the business.

Your role

You will play a central role in developing and improving Whiteaway’sinternal platform and will work closely with software Engineers and the other members of the Platform Squad.

A key part of the role is the close collaboration with Engineers. You will be curious about how they work, understand their needs and challenges, and use their feedback to identify how workflows, processes and platform tooling can be made simpler, faster and better.

Over the coming years, Whiteaway will be taking the platform to a significantly higher level. A key focus will be reducing and removing legacy and building a more modern, scalable and developer-friendly platform. AI will also play an increasingly important role in how the platform develops and how Whiteaway’s Engineers work.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Developing and continuously improving the cloud platform

• Automating deployment and development processes

• Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD pipelines

• Containerisation and Kubernetes

• Cloud infrastructure – primarily AWS

• Monitoring, observability and reliability

• Engineering tooling and self-service solutions

• Security and access management

• Troubleshooting and optimising platform performance and stability

The role offers a high degree of freedom, and you will have the opportunity to take ownership and influence both the technology and the way the team works.

Whiteaway believes in freedom under responsibility. You will have the opportunity to take ownership, influence technical decisions and help shape both the platform and the way the team works.

We imagine that you…

You have a strong technical background and experience within software development, cloud, DevOps or platform engineering. Perhaps you are already working as a Platform Engineer, Cloud Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer or Senior Software Engineer with strong cloud and infrastructure experience.

Your title is less important than your motivation to work hands-on with platform engineering and your ability to thrive at the intersection of software development, cloud and operations. Experience with general software development is an advantage, particularly Node.js and/or Go.

We would like you to have experience with several of the following technologies and tools:

• AWS

• Kubernetes

• Docker

• Terraform / Infrastructure as Code

• CI/CD

• Git/GitHub

• Linux

• Node.js and/or Go

• Datadog

• ArgoCD

• Spacelift

• Cloudflare

• Monitoring and observability

• Networking and cloud infrastructure

Experience with GitOps is an advantage, but not a requirement. Experience with security or with the intersection between operations and software development is also considered an advantage.

You do not need to know everything. What matters most is that you have strong technical curiosity, can understand complex problems and are motivated to continuously improve the way things are done.

Your professional development is important to Whiteaway.

You will have the opportunity to work with development plans, strengthen your technical skills and take your expertise to the next level. At the same time, knowledge sharing is an important part of the culture – you are expected not only to develop yourself, but also to help lift others around you.

On a personal level, drive, determination and humility are highly valued. You take ownership and get things done, while remaining curious, collaborative and motivated to find the best solutions together with others.

What Whiteaway offers

At Whiteaway, you will be part of an informal, inclusive and supportive leadership culture where Engineers have real ownership and the opportunity to influence their work. The culture is built around experimentation, knowledge sharing and continuous learning, with opportunities to take part in hackathons, pair programming and MOB programming, as well as access to learning resources.

The social side of working together is also important. People at Whiteaway genuinely enjoy working together, and there is a strong focus on building good relationships across the team. Through activities such as hackathons, Improvement Mondays and other social initiatives, there are plenty of opportunities to come together, share knowledge, experiment and have fun.

Whiteaway also values a healthy work-life balance, a great lunch and good colleagues. The office is located in Skejby, with free parking.

About Whiteaway Group

Whiteaway Group is a tribe of 300+ passionate people working across Scandinavia, selling and shipping appliances through e-commerce, franchise stores and B2B channels.

Around 250 employees are based at the headquarters in Aarhus, covering the group’s central functions. Around 45 people work within Tech across IT, Engineering and Product. The Platform Squad currently consists of four Platform Engineers, and the team is expected to grow in the coming years as the demands on and use of the platform continue to increase – including with the growing use of AI.

With brands like Skousen, Tretti and Whiteaway, the group is grounded in innovation and honesty, always pushing for better customer experiences through technology.

Interested in joining Whiteaway Group?

Bloom is handling the recruitment process on behalf of Whiteaway Group and is actively reviewing applications. We look forward to receiving your application and CV in Danish or English as soon as possible.

If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact IT Recruitment Manager Dorte Pape at Bloom at dp@bloom.dk or on +45 3160 9365.

Building AI keeps getting cheaper and faster. Deciding what's worth building, and getting an organisation to actually commit to it, does not.

At Heyra, we build AI systems, workflows and data platforms that are meant to live in production from day one. We work closely with companies that are moving quickly and need a partner who can hold both the strategic picture and the delivery reality in one head.

We're looking for a Deployment Strategist: the person the client's leadership talks to. You own the relationship and the outcome. You sit with a C-suite buyer, understand where their business is actually trying to go, and translate that into a sharp, sequenced plan for what we build and why. Then you steer a strong engineering team to make it real - without being the one in the codebase.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo's security surface is unusual. We train models on-premise on dedicated GPU infrastructure, run the product across AWS and GCP, and operate a fleet of tens of thousands of cameras deployed at clubs and venues worldwide. That is a scope most SaaS security engineers never touch: physical devices in the field, heavy on-prem compute, and multi-cloud production, all in one role.

We are forming a Security Enablement Team that makes it easier for every engineering and IT team at Veo to build, ship, and operate secure systems. As the most senior engineer on the team, you will own the technical direction of the platform security, identity, and network security slice, partnering with the teams that own these systems so security is built in from the start. As an enablement function, the team does not run these systems day to day. We build the paved roads, tooling, and patterns that let the owning teams operate securely by default.

You will join during a pivotal moment. We are standing the team up, defining what good looks like across platform security, identity, and network security, and rolling out the first paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, CVE response, CI/CD identity, and a unified internal network across our datacenters (GCP, AWS) and offices (Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen). You'll have direct impact on how 100+ engineers write, review and ship secure systems.

What You Will Do

You will join a focused platform security team and operate as its most senior engineer. Everything below follows the same pattern. We design the paved road, prove it works, and hand it to the team that will own it. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities, and we expect this role to set the bar.

• Design and build the paved roads for image scanning, SBOM generation, and CVE response, running inside the pipelines teams already use, with findings routed to the owners who can fix them under tracked SLAs

• Lead the design, reviews, and tooling for a unified internal network and VPN across GCP, AWS, and our Miami, Berlin, and Copenhagen offices, while the team that owns the network keeps running it

• Work with the auth service maintainers on identity and access, including MFA rollouts, removal of shared accounts, and cleanup of long-lived tokens, so the patterns stay theirs to own

• Make workload identity the paved road for CI/CD, using OIDC between GitHub Actions and AWS or GCP, packaged so teams can migrate themselves

• Build audit logging as a shared capability that teams plug into rather than reinvent

• Turn GRC controls into technical implementations, with evidence pipelines that produce auditable output without manual follow-up

• Own the contracting cycle for external penetration tests and build the intake, classification, and tracking system that routes findings to named owners, while the owning teams remediate

• Hand each capability off cleanly, with a runbook, a named owner, and an escalation path, and run office hours where product and platform teams can get a security review or a paved-road question answered

• Mentor the rest of the team and raise the security bar across Builders

As the team matures, you will help shape our multi-environment network architecture, our identity and access patterns, and the long-term security posture of the product.

What You Could Bring

This is a deliberately merged platform security and identity role. You do not need to be world class at both. You likely have several years of production infrastructure and security experience behind you, and you are deep and credible in one of these areas and ready to grow into the other.

That depth tends to show up in several of the following:

• Platform security: you have run vulnerability scanning, CVE management, and image scanning at scale, and you know the operational reality of getting CVEs fixed, beyond standing up the tooling

• Identity and auth: you have worked hands-on inside an auth codebase, rolled out MFA on live systems, and managed token lifecycles in CI/CD with OIDC and workload identity

• Network security at scale: you have designed and run a unified internal network across multiple cloud providers and offices, with a VPN approach that holds up

• Platform-as-product mindset: you have built internal security tooling that other teams chose to adopt, with guard rails built into the tools developers already use and manual review as a last resort, and you gathered feedback and measured the impact

• Infrastructure as Code: strong experience with Terraform, Crossplane, or similar

Nice to have: GitOps tools such as Flux or ArgoCD, Cilium, Kubernetes security at scale, and experience building security into a GRC evidence pipeline.

How We Work

You'll join a Copenhagen-based Security Enablement Team of three engineers plus a manager. We operate as an enablement function: we build shared tooling and golden paths, and we step in for focused, high-leverage missions where no other team is positioned to deliver. We do not run a SOC and we do not carry a security pager.

You'll collaborate regularly with the Platform, Product, IT, Firmware, and GRC teams. We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. This role sets the technical direction for the team's quarterly missions. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

If you read that list and matched on three or four items but not all of them, apply anyway. The "deep in one, ready to grow into the other" framing above is not a hedge, it is how we actually hire at this level. We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.

Join our Identity and Access Management (IAM) team within our broader technology department. In this role, you will work cross-functionally across Security, HR Ops, Privacy, and IT to manage critical access and secure resources enterprise-wide. We foster a healthy, transparent, and highly collaborative environment where you can work with state-of-the-art tech and leverage our AI investments to innovate in the IAM space.

As an Identity & Access Management Analyst, you will take ownership of the day-to-day disciplines that govern how colleagues access the systems they need. Working directly within the wider IT Operations and Identity & Access Management function, you will run the joiner, mover and leaver processes, handle incoming access requests, administer privileged access, and run and improve our access review programme, working with system owners to confirm who should have access, and with auditors to evidence that it is right. Your efforts will directly shape how quickly and securely our team members get the access required to do their best work.

This role needs both sides. You will configure access, troubleshoot sign-in issues and grow into application onboarding with Single Sign-On (SSO) and automated user provisioning (SCIM). Just as much of your week will be spent working with people: walking system owners through access reviews, agreeing who should have access to what, answering auditors' questions, and keeping HR Ops in step on starters and leavers. We are looking for someone who is as comfortable leading a conversation with a system owner or auditor. You will have support from senior team members on more complex work.

What You'll Be Doing

• Access Administration & Ticketing: Serve as the operational contact for IAM ticketing, managing end-to-end user access lifecycles, including ticketing queues, approvals and access provisioning, while driving process improvements through automation.

• Identity Lifecycle & Provisioning Management: Partner with HR Operations to oversee end-to-end Joiner, Mover, and Leaver (JML) workflows for employees and contractors—ensuring precision day-one access, timely deprovisioning, and swift operational pivot capabilities during last-minute schedule and scope shifts.

• Access Reviews & Certification: Run and continuously improve our access review programme. Set up new review cycles as applications come into scope, walk reviewers through what they are being asked to confirm, chase completion, and make sure revocations are carried out.

• System Ownership & Access Coordination: Connect regularly with system owners to help clarify access roles, coordinate baseline permission levels, and maintain clear, straightforward review guidelines for teams.

• Audit & Compliance Partnership: Be the point of contact on access controls for internal audit, external auditors (SOC 2) and financial systems audits. Walk auditors through how our controls work, provide evidence, and follow findings through to closure with the relevant teams.

• Manage Elevated Permissions: Administer privileged and administrative access, ensuring elevated permissions are time-bound, justified, and regularly reviewed.

• Maintain Reliable Identity Data: Govern group memberships, access roles, and HR system integrations to ensure identity data remains accurate across systems.

• Application Onboarding: Integrate new SaaS tools with our Identity Management (IdP) using SSO (SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect) and SCIM where supported, defining access groups and initial permission levels. Where SCIM is not supported, follow a documented manual process with proper checks.

• Stakeholder & Vendor Liaison: Support internal system owners and external software providers by helping troubleshoot user access requests and ensuring platform permissions stay accurate and up to date.

• Solve Access Challenges: Support colleagues when access issues arise, looking into root causes to build lasting, friendly solutions rather than short-term fixes.

• Automate & Streamline: Look for repetitive tasks that can be simplified or automated, and work with the team to improve them.

Who You Are

• Identity Experience: Background in an IT or Identity & Access Management role using a modern identity provider. Experience with IdP is a plus, but experience with a comparable platform is welcome.

• Confident with Stakeholders: Confident in proactively reaching out to new colleagues, facilitating structured discussions, and serving as a trusted advisor to help leaders at any level navigate and understand access policies.

• Governance Experience: Has run or supported access reviews, and is comfortable walking an auditor through how a control works. Experience with SOC 2 or financial systems audits (IT general controls) is a strong plus.

• Hands-on Lifecycle Experience: Practical experience handling joiner, mover and leaver work, access requests, or user administration, with an appreciation for why accurate access matters to people's day-to-day work.

• Influences Without Authority: Partner thoughtfully with busy system owners and leadership to complete routine access reviews and remove unnecessary permissions, using clear communication, proactive follow-ups, and genuine professional relationships to keep security hygiene on track.

• Single Sign-On & Provisioning: Practical experience configuring enterprise SSO alongside vendors or app owners, backed by an understanding of SAML, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Exposure to SCIM, or a solid grasp of the concepts. Comfortable with scripting or keen to learn.

• Familiar with Modern Security: Comfortable with access controls like multi-factor authentication and conditional access, as well as modern sign-in options, from one-time codes to authenticator apps, passkeys and certificates, and why some offer stronger protection.

• Ownership & Follow-Through: Chases the open review, closes the loop on the finding, and doesn't let a ticket go quiet. Juggles requests, review deadlines and last-minute HR changes without dropping things.

• Curious & Methodical Problem-Solver: Able to troubleshoot sign-in flows independently and find the root cause rather than the quick fix, recognising that identity work carries a low tolerance for mistakes.

• Clear Communicator: Explains things clearly in person and in writing, including documentation and evidence that an auditor can follow without a walkthrough.

• Contribute to the design and implementation of DevOps practices.

• Design and improve the resilience, scaling, security, and robustness of production infrastructure systems

• Proactively react to outage or service level degradation scenarios

• Continuously improve regular operations by automating procedures and optimizing processes.

How you’ll succeed

• Raise awareness and improve understanding of CI/CD practices in the Engineering departments and across the company

• Effectively gather information and use analytical skills to make data-led decisions

• Balance multiple tasks and priorities

• Deliver high-quality work while meeting business deadlines

• Create innovative ideas to solve problems

• Prioritize customer experience

What you’ll need

• Experience as a DevOps Engineer

• Strong understanding and knowledge of CI/CD processes

• Experience with designing and building automation

• Experience in IaC and with configuration automation tools such as Ansible and Terraform.

• Thorough understanding and experience in Docker and Kubernetes.

• Experience with Agile development methodologies – Scrum, Kanban, etc.

• Experience with:

• Google Cloud (and other cloud providers)

• One or more programming languages (Java preferred)

• Cloud migration

• Monitoring tools (Datadog, Grafana)

Bonus points

Benefits
