JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

The Senior Manager, Quality Global Affiliates Excellence, develops and owns selected shared Quality processes that enable Genmab’s affiliates to operate compliantly and efficiently as the business expands. The role simplifies ways of working, reduces duplication and affiliate workload, and builds scalable solutions that can be deployed across existing and new markets.

Working closely with affiliate Quality leads, global process owners and cross-functional partners, the role combines process ownership with hands-on implementation. A key responsibility is ownership of the affiliate training framework, including shared curricula, governance and ongoing maintenance. The scope of other process ownership is agreed with the Head of Quality Global Affiliates and relevant global process owners, with clear interfaces to local responsibilities.

The role serves as a key connection point between Global Quality and affiliate Quality organizations, coordinating implementation activities, promoting standardization, and enabling the exchange of best practices and lessons learned across markets.

Responsibilities

Affiliate QMS and launch readiness

• Support new affiliate establishment, onboarding of local Quality leads and Responsible Persons, and implementation of the global Quality Management System. Work with local experts to identify and address additional local requirements

• Coordinate Quality readiness activities for market entry and commercial launches, tracking dependencies, milestones and risks and escalating issues requiring decisions or additional resources

• Support inspection readiness through shared tools, knowledge exchange and follow-up on recurring findings and improvement opportunities

Process ownership and scalable ways of working

• Own the design, implementation, maintenance and continuous improvement of assigned affiliate processes, including procedures, tools, governance, performance measures and user support

• Review affiliate workflows with local Quality leads to identify duplication, unnecessary complexity and activities that can be managed centrally or through shared services. Prioritise improvements based on compliance risk, affiliate effort and business needs

• Move agreed repeatable activities into shared solutions with clear responsibilities, handovers and support arrangements, reducing the need for each affiliate to develop and maintain its own approach

• Partner with global process owners to make global Quality processes practical for affiliates. Establish a common core with justified local adaptations, preserving local Quality oversight and statutory responsibilities

Affiliate training framework

• Own and maintain the affiliate training framework in partnership with Global Training, including role and task curricula, assignment principles, onboarding pathways and change governance

• Lead the affiliate training coordinator network and coordinate consistent implementation across markets. Maintain shared training matrices and coordinate updates following changes to global procedures

• Establish efficient arrangements for training assignment, administration and reporting with Global Training and affiliate coordinators. Retain clear local responsibility for identifying local requirements and confirming role applicability

• Monitor training completion and effectiveness, address recurring gaps with relevant stakeholders, and simplify training requirements and administration where justified

Quality oversight and continuous improvement

• Streamline affiliate Quality Management Reviews through common inputs, reporting and follow-up tools, and facilitate Quality Risk Management activities across affiliates

• Use process performance, affiliate feedback, inspection findings and workload data to identify improvements. Measure benefits through reduced duplication and effort, timely implementation and sustained process effectiveness

• Partner with relevant system owners to introduce proportionate digitalisation and automation

Project delivery and capability building

• Lead cross-functional improvement projects from problem definition through implementation and benefit evaluation, managing priorities and dependencies across multiple affiliates

• Build stakeholder commitment, provide practical guidance and training, and follow through on adoption so that improvements become part of everyday work

• Capture and share best practices and lessons learned through reusable guidance, peer networks and onboarding materials, strengthening the capabilities of small affiliate Quality teams

Requirements

• Master’s degree in pharmacy, life sciences, engineering or a related scientific discipline

• Approximately 7–10 years of relevant Quality experience within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry

• Strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice and other GxP requirements relevant to affiliate operations, with experience implementing or improving Quality Management Systems

• Demonstrated experience owning or substantially improving processes across multiple markets or functions, with measurable gains in simplicity, efficiency or effectiveness

• Experience with Quality Risk Management and inspection readiness, including the ability to coordinate these activities across multiple markets

• Experience developing and implementing Quality guidance, tools, and training to enable structured, consistent, and scalable ways of working across affiliates

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and process-improvement capabilities, with the ability to identify trends, simplify processes, and drive harmonization across markets with differing regulatory requirements

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across global and local organizations and drive outcomes without direct authority

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK666.400,00---999.600,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

About Genmab

Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Are you interested in underground infrastructure and complex tunnelling projects? Do you want to help shape the transport networks of the future and contribute to some of the most challenging tunnels and infrastructure projects in Denmark and internationally? Would you like to be part of a large, highly skilled team of tunnel and geotechnical experts and have the opportunity to contribute to important projects? If so, we would like to hear from you.

COWI is a global consulting group that delivers innovative and sustainable solutions to complex challenges within transport, energy, environment, water, industry, buildings, and urban planning. Together with our 7,500 skilled employees, we advance engineering design worldwide.

Our geotechnical and tunnel engineering team in Denmark consists of more than 120 highly skilled professionals and offers a full range of high-level skills within geotechnical engineering and tunnel design. Combined with solid local presence and international experience, this enables us to take on some of the world's most challenging infrastructure projects.

We work across a broad range of disciplines, contributing to projects including highways, metros, railways, bridges, tunnels, buildings, stormwater systems, energy infrastructure, and ground investigations. We cover all phases of the project lifecycle - from concept and design to construction, supervision, operation, and maintenance.

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

As a Senior Tunnel Engineer, you will play a key role in delivering high-quality solutions as part of a highly professional team providing consultancy, design, and project management services.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Taking technical ownership of tunnel and underground structures design scopes, ensuring robust engineering solutions across all project phases.

• Leading the design and review of TBM tunnel systems, segmental lining design, launch and reception arrangements, and construction methodologies.

• Contributing to the planning and design of NATM/SEM tunnels, temporary and permanent support systems, excavation sequences, and risk mitigation measures.

• Leading and reviewing rock engineering assessments, including rock mass characterization, excavation support design, rock reinforcement systems, stability analyses for rock slopes and underground openings, and construction risk assessments.

• Coordinating multidisciplinary interfaces between civil, structural, geotechnical, MEP, and construction teams.

• Providing technical leadership, mentoring junior engineers, and conducting technical reviews to ensure high-quality project delivery.

• Assisting the tunnelling teams with strategic bids.

• Performing and reviewing advanced engineering analyses, including numerical modelling and geotechnical assessments using industry-standard software.

• Advancing to a technical point of contact for clients, contractors, authorities, and project stakeholders, communicating technical solutions, risks, and project opportunities clearly.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

You are an experienced tunnel engineer with a solid technical background in underground construction, tunnelling methods and rock engineering. You take responsibility for your work, thrive in multidisciplinary project environments, and enjoy mentoring colleagues while delivering technically robust and buildable solutions.

You combine advanced analytical capabilities with practical construction understanding and have extensive experience in tunnel and underground infrastructure projects across soil and rock conditions, from feasibility and design through construction and commissioning.

In addition, you have:

• A Bachelor's, Master's, or equivalent degree in Civil Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering, Rock Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related discipline.

• Minimum 10 years of experience in tunnel engineering, underground structures, and geotechnical engineering.

• Practical experience with TBM tunnelling projects, including tunnel lining design, construction methodology, and geotechnical interface management.

• Experience with NATM/SEM tunnelling, underground stations, caverns and temporary support systems.

• Experience leading/working in multidisciplinary design teams and coordinating complex technical interfaces.

• Experience and understanding of the needs and approaches to the engineering consultancy and design markets, including relationships with clients, work planning and commercial management.

• Extensive experience with numerical modelling and design software such as PLAXIS 2D/3D, FLAC, RS2/3, Rocscience, GeoStudio, or equivalent tools, with a clear understanding of their capabilities and limitations.

• Strong expertise in Eurocodes and other relevant industry standards.

• Effective report writing skills with the ability to self-check and produce accurate work.

• Good communication skills and confidence to liaise with clients. Danish language skills are considered an advantage.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Head of Discipline for Tunnels and Deep Excavations, Ganesh Kale, LAKE@cowi.com.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Equal opportunity employer

COWI provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, COWI complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

If you're organized, enthusiastic about project management, and ready to set new standards in modern space technology, we’d love to hear from you.

At Wingmen Security, we are experiencing significant growth and increasing demand for our cybersecurity and observability solutions. We are looking for a technically strong Splunk Senior Consultant to join our team of 50+ dedicated colleagues.

The Role

As a Splunk Senior Consultant, you will act as a trusted technical advisor to our clients while being a core member of our dedicated internal Splunk specialist team. You will work on client-facing advisory and implementation tasks, backed by a strong internal community rather than working in isolation.

• Workplace: Søborg office(Copenhagen), with client visits and travel.

• Employment: Full-time (37 hours/week).

Your Profile

• Splunk Core architecture, administration, and performance optimization.

• Search Processing Language (SPL) and dashboard development.

What We Offer

FirePoint Rocket Technology is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark - a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. Our ambition is significant: we are scaling from the early operational phase to 200+ employees within the next 18 months.

It is a Danish-based defense technology company, part of the international Fire Point Group — a fast-growing ecosystem born out of Ukraine’s innovation and resilience. The group was founded by engineers and entrepreneurs who, during the first months of the full-scale war, decided to use their expertise to create advanced defense technologies — including long-range drones and precision systems.

Joining FPRT now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

They are looking for a Maintenance & Engineering Manager who will establish and execute an absolute, zero-compromise reliability strategy from day one.

The Role

As the Maintenance & Engineering Manager, you are responsible for the operational integrity, availability, and safety of all production assets and process equipment. Manufacturing rocket propellant leaves no room for trial and error—our process equipment must be predictable, fully mastered down to the individual component, and maintained at peak condition.

Reporting directly to the Chief Production Officer (CPO), you will lead the technical team in deep equipment mastery, anticipating service intervals with precision, and proactively replacing high-risk components before failures occur. You will work in close functional alignment with Process Engineering, Manufacturing Automation, EHS, Quality, and Production Planning to ensure seamless, compliant operations.

What You Will Do

1. Production Maintenance Strategy & Asset Management

• Develop and implement a preventive and predictive maintenance strategy for all production equipment, focusing on long-cycle and batch-based processes (mixers, thermal curing ovens, polymerization, climate-controlled chambers) to ensure thermal stability and high uptime.

• Minimize downtime by transitioning from reactive repairs to condition-based monitoring and planned interventions.

• Lead the selection, implementation, and management of a CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) to track work orders, asset history, and maintenance costs.

• Integrate maintenance requirements into the equipment acquisition process alongside QA, establishing preventive risk assessments and managing obsolescence planning.

2. Process Utilities & Production Support Engineering

• Oversee point-of-use process utilities directly feeding production lines, such as process vacuum, specialized process gas loops, and line-dedicated thermal fluids.

• Coordinate with internal and external facility teams on utility drop interfaces to ensure production machinery interface readiness.

3. EHS & Process Safety Compliance

• Enforce strict adherence to EHS standards across all equipment maintenance activities.

• Rigorously execute Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures and "Permit to Work" systems on energetic material processing machinery and hazardous equipment zones.

4. Production Spare Parts & Technical Inventory

• Define critical spare parts strategies for production machinery to balance inventory costs with operational risk mitigation.

• Partner with the Warehouse team to track, store, and preserve technical production spares correctly.

• Monitor market lifecycle status for key equipment components and execute end-of-life obsolescence planning.

5. Team Leadership & Technical Development

• Lead, mentor, and schedule a team of production maintenance technicians and equipment specialists.

• Ensure the team is fully trained in safety protocols (ATEX, energetic materials) and advanced technical troubleshooting.

• Plan technician resources and build mechanical redundancy strategies to protect production during interventions or unplanned events.

6. Production Line CapEx & Commissioning Support

• Support the installation, mechanical integration, and commissioning of new production lines with Process Engineering and Automation.

• Provide early input on machine "serviceability and accessibility" during the design phase to eliminate future shop-floor bottlenecks.

First 90 Days – Expected Outcomes

• Critical spare parts inventory analysis completed and gaps identified.

• Preventative Maintenance (PM) schedule established for all key production assets.

• Maintenance team skills matrix assessed and training plan initiated.

• Design of the “obtain equipment” process and equipment lifecycle framework completed in collaboration with QA.

What We Offer

• A rare career opportunity to lead the engineering and maintenance function for one of Denmark's most unique industrial and defense-tech projects.

• A role where your technical expertise directly determines the reliability and safety of high-stakes, safety-critical production.

• A professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose.

• Brand-new factory & equipment.

• Real authority, Greenfield impact, Zero toxic culture, Mastery over busywork.

• Top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

We Are Looking For

You are a highly structured, disciplined, and hands-on leader who thrives on the shop floor and maintains an absolute zero-compromise approach to equipment safety and operational reliability.

Requirements:

• Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Experience: 5+ years of maintenance management experience within heavy industry, chemical processing, pharma, defense, or similar high-safety manufacturing environments.

• Leadership: Proven track record of managing technical teams, scheduling resources, and coordinating external contractors and facility service providers.

• Regulatory Knowledge: Experience working in highly regulated environments (ATEX, SEVESO, or similar energetic/hazardous contexts).

• Systems & Methods: Experience implementing or optimizing CMMS systems (e.g., SAP PM, Maximo) and utilizing OEE and Root Cause Analysis (FMEA, 8D, 5 Whys).

• Technical Mastery: Strong working knowledge of mechanical systems (hydraulics, pneumatics, rotating equipment), electrical systems, and industrial automation (PLC, SCADA).

Head of Data Platform – build Gubra’s data foundation from the ground up

Do you want to build the data foundation behind scientific innovation in a growing biotech company? Gubra is looking for a Head of Data Platform to take end-to-end ownership of a new enterprise data platform connecting scientific, operational, and business data across the organisation.

This is a director-level role combining technical ownership, people leadership, and greenfield development. You will shape the architecture and roadmap, build the team around the platform, and remain close enough to the technology to take part in key technical decisions.

The ambition is to create a scalable data foundation that supports research, laboratory operations, machine learning, and selected business functions across Gubra.

Build the platform – and the team around it

Gubra is investing in its digital and data foundation, and you will join at an early stage.

As Head of Data Platform, you will lead the design, implementation, and operation of the platform, built around AWS and Databricks. You will work across architecture, data pipelines, reusable data products, governance, and security while translating scientific and business needs into technical priorities.

At the same time, you will build and lead the data engineering team. Two Data Engineers are planned to join, an external Data Architect is already supporting the initial design, and the team is expected to grow further. You will report directly to the CTO and become part of the CTO’s leadership team.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading the design and development of a scalable and secure enterprise data platform

• Building reliable data pipelines and reusable data products for scientists, ML teams, engineers, and business users

• Defining the platform roadmap and driving key architectural and technical decisions

• Establishing data governance, security, access control, and documentation standards

• Building, mentoring, and developing the data engineering team

• Working closely with stakeholders across research, laboratory operations, software engineering, and the wider business.

Who are you?

You have a strong background in data engineering, analytics, or data platforms and experience leading both people and technical delivery. You combine leadership with enough technical depth to challenge architectural decisions and engage credibly with engineers.

You bring extensive experience with AWS and Databricks and have designed scalable, secure, and governed data solutions before. Experience with lakehouse architecture, data mesh, medallion architecture, Airflow, Delta Lake, or Unity Catalog is an advantage.

Experience from biotech, pharma, life sciences, or another research-intensive environment is beneficial but not required. The same applies to experience with regulated environments and GxP.

Personally, you are a pragmatic and collaborative leader who can create a clear direction, bring stakeholders and employees with you, and balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

About Gubra

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. The organisation combines Biotech, CRO, and Venture activities and brings scientists, engineers, and business teams together across the organisation.

Digital, Data & IT is strengthening the foundation beneath this work by connecting scientific, operational, and business data and enabling advanced analytics and machine learning.

The position is based at Gubra in Hørsholm, Denmark.

If you have any questions about the position, you are always welcome to contact Kathrine Schlegel Rasmussen at ksr@capaxrecruitment.com.

Capax Recruitment manages the recruitment process on behalf of Gubra.

Principal Enterprise Architect – shape the technology choices behind Gubra’s growth

Build, buy, integrate or simplify? As Gubra grows, so does the number and complexity of technology decisions across the organisation. Gubra is therefore looking for a Principal Enterprise Architect who can bring direction and coherence to its technology landscape.

In this newly established role, you will become a close architectural partner to the CTO and work across business, science, and technology. Your job is not to own one particular platform or technology. Instead, you will help Gubra make the right technology choices across scientific systems, enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, and integrations.

Turn complex needs into pragmatic technology choices

As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will work closely with business leaders, scientists, Product Managers, and technology teams to understand what they are trying to achieve before translating those needs into architecture options and recommendations.

That could mean assessing whether to build a capability internally or invest in a SaaS platform. Another could involve defining how a new solution should integrate with Gubra’s existing landscape, exploring an AI opportunity, or helping a new venture establish a technology foundation that works today without limiting it tomorrow.

You will also help establish the architecture principles, standards, and guardrails that create consistency across Gubra. The ambition is not architecture for architecture’s sake, but enough direction to enable teams to make better decisions independently.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Advising on technology choices across enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, security, and integrations

• Evaluating COTS and SaaS solutions and supporting build-vs-buy decisions

• Defining and evolving architecture principles, standards, and reusable patterns

• Translating business and scientific needs into pragmatic architecture recommendations

• Working with Software, Data, ML, Infrastructure, and Security teams to ensure decisions are technically viable

• Identifying opportunities for AI and modernisation across the organisation

• Following developments within AI, cloud, data sovereignty, and emerging technologies.

An architect who asks the right questions

You bring 5+ years of relevant experience as an Enterprise Architect, Principal Architect, or in a similar role, with broad experience across enterprise applications, data, cloud, integrations, security, and modern software platforms.

You understand ERP and enterprise business systems and how they connect to a broader technology landscape. You are comfortable discussing APIs, integration patterns, identity, security, cloud architecture, and data interoperability, and you have experience assessing COTS or SaaS platforms and making technology recommendations.

You also understand modern AI architecture and how AI capabilities can become part of real business workflows. Experience from pharma, biotech, life sciences, drug discovery, or another R&D-intensive environment is relevant, while experience with GxP is an advantage.

Just as importantly, you are curious enough to challenge the problem before proposing the solution. You can discuss opportunities with business leaders and scientists and then go into sufficient technical depth with engineers to make decisions credible and implementable.

You are comfortable influencing across teams without formal authority and know when architecture adds value – and when it simply adds another layer of complexity.

Where science, business and technology meet

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. Its activities span Biotech, CRO, and Venture, creating a technology landscape that needs to support different business models, scientific disciplines, and ways of working.

Digital, Data & IT works across these areas to create the digital foundation supporting both scientific innovation and business operations. As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will have a broad view across that landscape and help ensure technology decisions support where Gubra is going next.

The position is based at Gubra in Hørsholm, Denmark and reports directly to the CTO.

If you have any questions about the position, you are always welcome to contact Kathrine Schlegel Rasmussen at ksr@capaxrecruitment.com.

jobs.occupation: Start your career as an Audit Graduate at Deloitte Copenhagen 2027
jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 2700 employees Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, and Consulting.

Would you like to start your audit career at Deloitte's head office?

At our Copenhagen office you will get 600 Audit & Assurance colleagues across departments. We have a strong sense of community, with many joint events, from Friday bars to courses and development opportunities. This gives you plenty of opportunity to build a strong network and a foundation for where your career at Deloitte will take you.

Job Description

As an audit graduate, your day-to-day work will take place in either our Portfolio or Large & Complex departments. You will be assigned to one of our four client segments: Public, Private, Financial Services, or Top Tier and your daily work will be team-based. You will have a dedicated department manager and a coach to support your personal and professional development.

You will quickly become part of your new community and have ample opportunity to build new relationships.

As an audit graduate you:

• Always work in audit teams and be in close contact with both colleagues and clients - often working on site at the client's premises.

• Acquire extensive knowledge of your department's clients and, most importantly, the skills to advise and audit them.

• Assist in planning client's audits, coordinating efforts with, for example, Deloitte's Service and Delivery Centres, which handle many of our administrative tasks, ahead of the reporting season.

• Contribute to risk assessments of accounting areas, using your knowledge of the client's internal processes.

• Work with an experienced audit team to conduct audits to ensure that the financial statements give a true and fair view.

Your role will vary depending on which department you join but we promise that your days will not be the same. There will be room to learn, to ask for help, and to grow and take on the responsibility you want.

NEXT - our graduate development programme

When you join as an audit graduate, you enter a full-time role and will join our internal development programme, NEXT, along with around 100 other graduates across the country. You are regularly brought together for training and to prepare for new roles.

Depending on where you are in your training when you join us, you will also be studying part-time at the university. And for your first 100 days with us, you will be assigned a buddy who has been through the experience of being a new graduate and will help you settle into your new role.

Qualifications

There are several paths to become an audit graduate in our audit business. We are open to your educational background and to you completing a level of training while you are with us. The most important thing is that you have the interest and motivation to learn. And it is important that you:

• Want to develop personally.

• Are curious about auditing.

• Have social skills that will support your future relationships with clients and colleagues, and team-based working.

• Can show relevant professional experience or extra curricular activities , in which you have excelled.

• You speak and understand both English and Danish, or any of the other Nordic languages.

• You are eligible to work within the EU, either as a citizen or with the correct permits.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we still encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can make an impact on our team.

Additional Information

Click on "I am interested" above to apply for this position.

Please attach your CV and grades from your current and previous education. Please do not upload a traditional cover letter. Through the application process we will also ask you to answer a few questions about your motivation for the joining Deloitte.

We process applications and arrange interviews continually.

jobs.occupation: Computational and Data Staff Scientist Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design
jobs.description:
We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent computational and data scientist to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD), University of Copenhagen (UCPH). The post suits someone with experience in computational chemistry, biology, and/or structural biology, as well as managing big data. This is a full-time position, starting 1 February 2027 and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research
 The CPD is a new initiative at UCPH. It is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, that is, designing proteins that are fit for purpose such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Data science at CPD: Increasingly, modern protein science is about data: collecting it, organising it, analysing it, and learning from it to build a deeper understanding of how proteins fold and function. Protein design is no different. Indeed, through the application of generative AI, it is at the leading edge of the confluence of data science and protein science. To coordinate this in the CPD, we are looking for someone experienced in and excited about working at this interface.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/

  Your job
 Specifically, we seek a talented computational and data scientist and team player to help develop research infrastructure, including hardware and computational tools, to advance the CPD’s research and mission. The successful candidate will join a growing multidisciplinary team to help collect, organise, analyse, and exploit data from computationally designed protein sequences and structural models, through protein expression levels, and onto a wide range of experimental structure-function studies. A key part of the role will be integrating into the wider team and working collaboratively with CPD researchers, rather than simply providing a data-management service. For example, we anticipate that the successful candidate would assist with and lead on various projects with CPD researchers to develop robust, reliable, and scalable data and computational tools to enable the very best protein design.

  Key responsibilities will include

   	
• Helping establish CPD's computational infrastructure to provide computing and data management for its researchers 	
• Developing automated pipelines that convert raw instrument output files directly into data plots suitable for analysis, saving time and resources across the research pipeline 	
• Collecting data and generating databases of designed proteins, e.g., constructs, sequences, models, and biophysical data (LIMS) 	
• Assisting in the development of new predictive models based on the gathered experimental and computational data using machine learning methods 	
• Being responsible for data management plans at the CPD and coordinating these plans with the host departments 	
• Related to the above, managing (i.e., best practice in collecting, organising, accessing) data generated by computational protein design workflows and by the CPD’s Protein Biophysics Facility 	
• Advising and training CPD scientists in creating and analysing large computational datasets, linking their experimental data and computational data to extract key information, and managing their computational protein design pipelines 	
• Contributing to, and where appropriate leading, grant applications for and publications from CPD research projects 	
• Teaching appropriate aspects of the above on CPD Master’s and PhD courses 	
• Serving as the primary technical bridge between the CPD and central KU IT to set up CPD’s computing systems in close collaboration with KU IT and establish internal data processing environments   Qualifications and expectations
 To succeed in this role, we anticipate that your areas of expertise could include one or more of the following:

   	
• Computational protein modelling and, ideally, design 	
• Protein or biomolecular sequence data and analysis 	
• Collection, manipulation and use of data from protein biophysics and structural biology 	
• Use and understanding of modern biomolecular statistical data analysis, including ML and AI methods, and generative AI for protein modelling and design 	
• Experience of establishing computational infrastructures for the above   Essential experience and skills

   	
• A PhD in bioinformatics, data science or a related domain, e.g. computational/structural biology 	
• Excellent knowledge of scientific computing and coding languages, e.g., Python 	
• Documented experience (e.g., scientific publications) in machine learning, scientific computing, and similar 	
• An active interest in protein design, engineering, and structure  	
• A proven ability to work with others on challenging multidisciplinary problems 	
• A team player keen on collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds and who is service-minded with clear organisational, communication, and networking skills. 	
• Excellent skills in written and spoken English   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Knowledge of experimental protein science, for example, biophysical methods and/or structural biology 	
• Experience in computational molecular/structural biology   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Salary and terms of employment
 The employment is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with a fixed-term until 31 July 2032. The starting date will be 1 February 2027.

  Depending on qualifications the position will take place as Special Consultant or Senior Consultant in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority), with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Center Manager Gretchen Repasky, Gretchen.repasky@bio.ku.dk.

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page). 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two referees) (max. two pages)  	
• List of publications including preprints (no limit, but do not include copies of the papers) 	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below.

  Application deadline: 8 November 2026

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.
 The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration. 

  As part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching to the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

What we can offer you

• A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions.

• A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity.

• Fast feedback and recognition of your contributions in a high-growth company.

• Strong team spirit - successes are celebrated with company events and trips.

Practicalities

To apply, please send us your CV, and attach your BSc and/or MSc grade transcripts to your application. If your profile looks like a good match, we will get in touch to coordinate an online technical test as a first step in the interview process.

If you have specific questions about the role, you are welcome to email us at quant_jobs@alipescapital.com. Please do not send in your applications to this email address, as our interview team will not have visibility to review.

Do you want to turn complex information security risks into decisions and actions that protect the business and enable its strategic ambitions? At COWI, you will work at the intersection of cybersecurity, enterprise risk management, business operations, technology, and digital transformation. You will play a central role in identifying the information security risks that matter most and ensuring they lead to clear ownership, informed decisions, and effective risk reduction.

At COWI, we create sustainable solutions that improve the quality of life for people today and generations to come. Our experts work across infrastructure, energy, water, environment, architecture, and buildings, delivering projects that shape societies and support critical services around the world.

As a trusted advisor to clients and partners, information security is an essential part of how we deliver projects, protect information, manage risk, and maintain trust. Our increasing use of digital platforms, data, artificial intelligence, and software-based delivery models creates new opportunities, but also increases our exposure to cybersecurity, regulatory, supply-chain, and delivery risks.

Your role, responsibilities, and team

COWI is strengthening its approach to information security risk management as part of a broader development of Information Security and Enterprise Risk Management across the Group.

Our ambition is to identify and understand the most important information security risks facing COWI, enable informed management decisions, drive effective risk treatment, and provide transparency and assurance to Executive Management and the Board.

This role has been established to help turn that ambition into practice.

As Senior Information Security Risk Specialist, you will be responsible for driving the information security risk management process across COWI. You will develop a consolidated and business-relevant risk picture, facilitate complex risk assessments, challenge assumptions, and translate material risks into decision-ready treatment options.

An important part of the role is ensuring that significant risks are not simply recorded in a risk register. You will help transform prioritized risks into clearly defined initiatives and projects, with accountable business owners, realistic delivery plans, measurable outcomes, and transparent reporting.

You will be part of the Group CISO and the ERM function, and you will work closely with IT, Legal, Procurement, Process & Quality, Transformation Office, and Business Lines, incl. operational risk owners across all of these.

Your primary responsibilities will include

• Leading the identification, analysis, evaluation and prioritization of information security risks across COWI’s business operations, projects, digital solutions, information assets, and third-party dependencies.

• Translating technical, regulatory and operational security issues into clear business-risk scenarios, including credible causes, consequences, existing controls, risk exposure and treatment options.

• Facilitating strategic risk assessments and cross-functional risk workshops with senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, and accountable risk owners.

• Preparing decision-ready risk analysis and reporting for the Group CISO, Executive Management, the ERM Committee, the Audit Committee, and the Board of Directors.

• Developing risk treatment proposals and project charters for prioritized risks, including proposed scope, ownership, governance, outcomes, dependencies, resource requirements, milestones and measures of risk reduction.

• Supporting risk owners in defining practical key risk indicators, treatment progress measures and evidence that demonstrate whether risk exposure is being reduced.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

You are a proactive and accountable driver who identifies what needs to happen, aligns stakeholders, and delivers results—not just recommendations. Structured, pragmatic, and solution-oriented, you thrive in fast-paced environments, manage diverse requests effectively, and stay focused on the priorities that create the biggest impact. You build trust across teams, challenge yourself constructively, and drive decisions when security requirements must be met. At the same time, you are curious and committed to continuous learning, staying ahead of threats, standards, and best practices while turning knowledge into practical improvements.

On top of that, you will have:

• Strong experience with information security, governance and risk management.

• Excellent stakeholder management skills and the ability to translate complex topics into clear, actionable guidance.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to influence and create momentum

Can you own the platform and pipelines that EIVA’s software is built on?

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. Our customers operate within renewable energy, oil & gas exploration, seabed-to-surface construction and hydrographic surveying – often in demanding environments where timing, precision and safety margins matter.

You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

• Doing hands-on development and engineering work across the team's core technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and internal tooling (around 80% of the role)

• Making the final technical decisions within the team's decision domain, and helping define where that domain's boundaries sit versus where the team needs external alignment

• Securing technical quality in the team – code and infrastructure-as-code review, best practices, testing and automation standards

• Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team

• Participating in refinement, securing that features, stories and tasks describe architectural dependencies, feasibility, quality requirements and operational aspects such as reliability, security, cost and developer experience

• Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation

• Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

• Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers

• Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback

• Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines

• Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally

• Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments

• Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team

• Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

• Has a background in software engineering or computer science

• Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling

• Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain

• Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform

• Has a collaborative mindset – comfortable gathering feedback from stakeholders across teams and using it to design clean, well-reasoned solutions

• Is a team player who's good at knowledge-sharing and educating peers, and takes proactive ownership of their domain

• It's a bonus if you also have experience with licence management systems, but not a requirement.

Joining the EIVA crew

ROLE DESCRIPTION

INVISIO is looking for a commercially minded and pragmatic Corporate Legal Counsel to support its global business. This is a broad legal generalist role with a strong commercial focus, where you will work closely with the business and provide legal support across a wide range of matters, with particular emphasis on international contracts, tenders, customer projects and other commercial legal matters.

As Corporate Legal Counsel, you will become part of a small legal team together with Signe Karstoft, Legal Director, to whom you will report. The role is based at INVISIO’s headquarters in Hvidovre, and the legal function is organisationally anchored within INVISIO’s Sales & Program function, which consists of approximately 50 employees globally, including around 25-30 in Denmark. You will primarily support the global sales organisation and work closely with colleagues across the business. Much of your work will involve large and complex customer contracts, tenders and projects.

You will provide legal support across INVISIO’s international business, including in relation to US contracts, such as contracts within the defence sector, and support sales teams across Europe and other markets. You will also support INVISIO in connection with major public tenders, including tenders involving ministries and defence organisations, providing legal support on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

As a technology company, intellectual property is an important part of INVISIO’s business. While dedicated specialists handle areas such as patents, you may also advise on IP-related matters as part of the broader commercial legal support. Experience with IP or from a technology or other IP-intensive business would therefore be an advantage.

In addition to the day-to-day legal support, you will contribute to developing and improving the way Legal supports the business. This includes driving legal improvement initiatives, maintaining and developing contract templates and legal guidelines, and conducting workshops and awareness activities for the business.

The role is highly international and outward-facing, with significant interaction with customers and stakeholders at all levels. You will have opportunities to join customer visits and negotiate contracts abroad, as well as participate in trade fairs in Denmark, Europe and the US.

The role is expected to involve approximately 25 travel days per year.

As INVISIO continues to grow rapidly, you will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and no two days are the same.

AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

INVISIO is looking for an independent and commercially minded lawyer who takes ownership and enjoys working closely with customers and colleagues across the organisation. Your key responsibilities will include:

Commercial contracts and negotiations:

• 
Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial contracts, including large international sales contracts, non-disclosure agreements, letters of intent, consulting agreements, tender-related contracts and distribution agreements.

• 
Take an active role in customer dialogue and contract negotiations and provide commercially focused legal advice, working closely with relevant stakeholders to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives.

• 
Provide pragmatic legal advice on contractual and other commercial matters arising in the day-to-day business.

**

Tenders and customer projects:**

• 
Provide legal support in connection with major public tenders, including reviewing tender documentation and advising on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

• 
Advise on legal and contractual aspects of tender structures, including which INVISIO entity should participate and any related intercompany arrangements.

• 
Support and, where relevant, take a coordinating role in customer projects and other commercial initiatives, including advising on contractual set-ups, priorities and how existing solutions can be applied in different markets etc.

**

IP and export control:**

• Ad hoc Advise on IP and export control matters, including IP considerations in commercial agreements and questions relating to export restrictions and requirements in connection with international sales and customer projects.

**

Legal development and business support:**

• 
Develop, maintain and improve contract templates, legal guidelines and other tools.

• 
Drive legal improvement initiatives and conduct workshops and legal awareness activities for the business, for example in relation to NDA’s.

• 
Provide ad hoc legal advice and support across INVISIO as required.

REPORTING AND TITLE

Reporting to: Signe Karstoft, Legal Director.

Title: Corporate Legal Counsel.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Education: You hold a master’s degree in law (cand.jur. or cand.merc.jur.).

Work experience: You have approximately 3-6 years of relevant legal experience from an in-house role, for example in a technology or software company or another larger international industrial company.

Legal areas of specialisation: You have strong experience in drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements and are comfortable handling contractual matters independently. You also have experience supporting tender processes and advising on the legal and contractual matters that arise in this context.

In addition, you have a broad legal profile and are able to navigate a varied range of legal matters. Experience with IP-related matters, particularly from a technology or other IP-intensive business, would be an advantage. Knowledge of export control would also be beneficial.

Commercial: You have a strong commercial mindset and understand how legal advice fits into the broader business context.

You have experience working directly with customers and are comfortable collaborating with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. You are able to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives and provide pragmatic, solution-oriented advice.

Language skills: You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and verbal.

PERSONAL CAPABILITIES

Independent & proactive: You work independently, take ownership of your responsibilities and proactively drive matters forward.

Outgoing & interpersonal: You are outgoing and enjoy interacting with people with different backgrounds and at all levels, both internally and externally. You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable engaging with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Analytical & pragmatic: You have strong analytical skills and are able to understand complex legal and commercial matters while maintaining a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach.

Structured & able to prioritise: You work in a structured manner, maintain a good overview of your responsibilities and are able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment where new and urgent matters frequently arise. You remain calm and focused when priorities change or deadlines are tight.

Stakeholder management & collaboration: You build strong relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and organisational levels. You are a team-oriented colleague who contributes to a strong sense of teamwork across the organisation and is able to influence stakeholders in a constructive manner.

Positive & constructive: You have a professional approach to your work and interact with others with maturity and integrity. You bring positive energy, are resilient when challenges arise and remain constructive in a busy environment.

INVISIO’S VALUE PROPOSITION TO YOU

INVISIO is a rapidly growing company with ambitious growth targets. The company achieves these ambitions through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts will be important to INVISIO’s continued success, and by joining the company, you will become part of an international headquarter with an informal working environment.

INVISIO offers a wide range of professional and social employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

ABOUT INVISIO

INVISIO is a global leader in communications technology for professionals working in mission-critical environments. Established in Denmark in 1999, the company develops and markets advanced, integrated communication systems for defence and public safety professionals, helping users communicate clearly and safely in demanding environments.

INVISIO’s modular and scalable portfolio includes headsets, control units, intercom systems, hubs and software designed to work together across dismounted, vehicle-based and command operations. The solutions are marketed under the INVISIO and Racal Acoustics brands.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, INVISIO has an international presence across Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 330 employees globally, including around 215 in Denmark, and is growing rapidly. INVISIO is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (Large Cap).

INVISIO is characterised by a strong focus on innovation, close customer collaboration and an international working environment. Its core values are Passion, Innovation, Teamwork and Customer First.

You can learn more about INVISIO here: www.invisio.com.

APPLICATION AND CONTACT

If you believe this position is a good fit for you, we look forward to receiving your application. Please attach your CV and any relevant documentation. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please don’t hesitate to contact Camilla Krogh at (+45 51261264) or Mikkel Falkenberg at (+45 29993065) from the team at RESOLVA.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process

All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. jobs.occupation: Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for byggeri og Bygni
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling

Research area and project description
Predictive control can reduce energy costs and CO2 emissions of heating and cooling homes. However, its performance depends on knowing when residents are home and what they find comfortable.

You will develop a natural-language interface, based on a large language model, between residents and a predictive controller. Residents can then tell the controller, when they are away, report how the rooms feel, or ask for a warmer bathroom etc. In return, the controller explains what it did and why, shows what the next hours cost in money and CO2, and suggests alternatives that residents can accept or decline. The comfort limits are thus set by the residents; with the information they need.

This dialogue can save energy in three ways. Knowing when people are home and which rooms they use enables occupancy-based control, heating only where and when needed. Reports on how the rooms feel train personal comfort models, so setpoints match each household. The third, and least explored, is energy sufficiency: residents knowingly accept less heating or cooling, for example 20 °C instead of 21.5 °C on an expensive evening, while remaining free to say no. A central question is whether explaining alternative control actions and their cost changes how residents judge the same indoor conditions (their thermal acceptability), and whether the change lasts. All three look the same on the energy meter, so the project must separate them.

Few people want a system that talks all the time. Residents differ in how much information they want, in what form, and whether the system should take the initiative or only respond when asked (proactive versus on-demand interaction). Engagement may also fade as the novelty wears off. The project will study these differences and design for them.

You will:
• couple the language model to the controller, so that residents' requests become control actions within safe limits
• run a climate chamber experiment on whether explanations change thermal acceptability
• carry out a field study in occupied Danish homes through a winter and a summer, covering heating and overheating
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a M.Sc. in engineering, computer science, building science or a related technical field. Applicants with a B.Sc. and at least one year of master's studies can apply through the 4+4 programme.

You should be able to program, preferably in Python, and be comfortable analysing data. Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: model predictive control or optimisation, large language models, statistics and the design of experiments with people, and field measurements in buildings. Nobody will have all of these, and you should be willing to learn what you lack.

The field study involves installing equipment in people's homes and talking with the residents, so you should be comfortable working with people. Danish is an advantage for the field work but not a requirement.

Applicants from neighbouring fields with relevant technical skills and a clear motivation for the topic are encouraged to apply.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Arhus C., Denmark.
