You will have the opportunity to work across industries, applying your expertise to help some of Denmark’s most exciting companies develop and strengthen their business.

_

**Responsibilities

**

At Netcompany, we pride ourselves on a culture built around high agility, low hierarchy, fast decision-making, and strong team spirit.

We develop solutions for a wide range of clients, from smaller private companies to large-scale public sector projects. Regardless of the project size, you as a Business Consultant will make a noticeable impact together with some of the industry’s most talented colleagues.

We are looking for a Business Consultant with a strong and well-documented interest in digitalisation to support initiatives related to user involvement, training, benefits realisation, process optimisation, and change management. Your work will be tied to our large-scale projects across both the public and private sectors.

As a Business Consultant, you will help ensure that Netcompany’s IT projects are successfully anchored within our clients’ organisations and business processes. You will also play a key role in making sure users have the right capabilities and readiness, so that both users and the organisation are fully prepared when new solutions go live.

The role is diverse and dynamic. Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Supporting clients with change management initiatives.

• Preparing user guides and training materials, as well as conducting user training sessions.

• Performing analyses and reporting on organisational change readiness.

• Mapping processes and facilitating workshops with clients.

• Defining benefits tracking models and preparing communication plans.

• Building strong domain knowledge by participating in and facilitating analysis work, testing, and refinement activities.

**About you

**

You actively seek understanding by asking questions and encourage learning through curiosity and dialogue. Deadlines do not intimidate you and you are willing to go the extra mile when needed. To succeed in this role, you:

• Are either a recent graduate or have a few years of experience — ideally working at the intersection of IT, business, and organisation, for example as an IT project manager or consultant.

• Have an interest in IT and digitalisation.

• Hold a relevant master’s degree, such as Cand.merc., Cand.it., Cand.scient., or similar.

• Have strong written and verbal communication skills and are fluent in both Danish and English.

• Have experience working professionally with PowerPoint and Excel.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

**Continue developing with us

**

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

**Send us your application

**

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

_All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

_

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance.

Do you want to create something new? Do you want to fundamentally change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments? Do you want to be part of a unique opportunity in the largest university in Denmark? Then you might be our new SCIENCE Makerspace Operation Director.

  We invite applications for a 5-year position as Operation Director for the SCIENCE Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. The Faculty of Science is committed to sustainably continuing the Makerspace activities at the end of the 5-year period, providing the possibility for extending the position long-term.

   

  About the SCIENCE Makerspace

  We are establishing a top-tier Makerspace at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen, spearheaded by the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), and the Department of Science Education (IND). The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is built upon a foundation of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) and aims to create an inclusive learning environment that bridges disciplines, supports different ways of learning, and attracts students with diverse backgrounds and interests. Everyone is welcome, and no prior knowledge of makerspaces, machines, or materials is required.

  The SCIENCE Makerspace will be established as a 600 sqm facility centrally located at Nørre Campus, with a budget of 42 million DKK over 5 years supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The Makerspace is expected to host 1-3 university courses per academic quarter, independent projects for BSc/MSc/PhD students, and be a venue for extracurricular workshops and 'blue sky' ideas from faculty and students. The Makerspace will also facilitate the integration between traditional and non-traditional forms of knowledge production within an Expert-in-residence program.

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen is one of Scandinavia's largest science faculties, with over 4,000 staff, ~9,000 students, and an annual turnover exceeding DKK 3 billion, located in the heart of Copenhagen. SCIENCE hosts 12 departments spanning a breadth of disciplines from molecular biology and chemistry to mathematics, computer science, and geoscience, united by a commitment to curiosity-driven, high-impact research. 

   

  Description of the position

  We offer a unique opportunity for you to become the Operation Director of the ‘yet-to-be-build' 600 sqm SCIENCE Makerspace centrally placed at the Northen Campus in Copenhagen. The SCIENCE Makerspace vision is to design, build and run an inclusive and innovative learning space that bridges disciplines, allows for multi-modal learning activities, and attracts a diversified and balanced cohort of students from different educational programs (BSc, MSc, PhD) across the 12 Departments.

  The Operations Director will direct the SCIENCE Makerspace and be the manager for the Makerspace team. The Operation Director is responsible for ensuring that principles for DEIB are mainstreamed in all decisions in the Makerspace. 

  You will be part of the core decision-making on how to organize, establish, and run the ‘one-of-a-kind' Makerspace. You will collaborate with committed faculty from DIKU, NBI, and IND in the establishing phases, and with the Deanery for Education for long-term engagement across the departments in making the Makerspace vision a reality.

  You will be part of hiring the team who will run the makerspace together with you including Technical Lab Manager, Lab Technician, and a group of student mentors.

  This is a unique opportunity to be part of creating something new, in the largest university in Denmark, which fundamentally will change how we organize teaching and learning at the SCIENCE departments.

   

  You will need four core competences to succeed in the position:

   	
• You will need skills and expertise which allow you to strategize and develop ideas which will foster success for the SCIENCE Makerspace vision. This includes the work of identifying and understanding upcoming challenges for e.g. DEIB [DK3] (organizationally, socially, technically, and spatially) and finding solutions, while pro-actively execute required actions. Further, the Operation director must be able to function within an ‘entrepreneurial atmosphere’ where everything is not settled yet. 	
• You will need leadership and management competences which will allow you to lead a mixed Makerspace team of both highly skilled lab manager and lab technicians whose work requires levels of trust and autonomy, as well as student mentors who need clear instructions and guidance. 	
• You will need to navigate and understand the organizational and social structures of academia and university life, this includes considering the intrinsic motivation of researchers/teachers and PhD students, and how they might differ for MSc/BSc students. Such competence can arrive from your own experience during your education and does not require that you have worked in a university setting previously. 	
• You need interest in ‘making’ and Makerspaces. Furthermore, it is important that you consider consulting relevant experts about their views and perspectives, which will allow you to take qualitatively and well-founded decisions about our joint Makerspace.   You will not be a one-person army, instead you will have three main groups with different types of competences and experiences you can draw on in the position, including the Makerspace team, an experienced team of administrative management colleagues, and the Faculty of SCIENCE teaching committee.

  To read more about the vision, plans, and background for the SCIENCE Makerspace, please visit ucphmakerspace.dk

   

  Qualifications

  You are pro-active, find solutions where others see barriers, and are excited about being a core part of establishing, building, and running the brand-new SCIENCE Makerspace at University of Copenhagen, Denmark. 

  You have a relevant higher education or experience from similar positions. 

  You care for students and want to make it possible for all students at SCIENCE to experience learning activities where ‘making’ plays a role, e.g. as part of courses, project work, tech workshops, and extracurricular activities. 

  You are committed to the agenda of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), know about Universal Design, and strongly believe that all activities and decisions in the pioneer SCIENCE Makerspace must take into account the multiple, intersecting dimensions of groups including, but not limited to genders, internationality, neurodiversity, socioeconomic backgrounds, and physical feasibility.

  Our ideal candidate can be described as:

   	
• Have management experience - potentially from a university or a politically governed organization. 	
• Demonstrates a high degree of trust under responsibility towards our employees, who are self-driven and accountable. As a manager, you help set the overall direction, contribute to daily well-being and cohesion, and support the development of individual employees and the team, while maintaining an overview of strategic initiatives in collaboration with your staff. 	
• Has an understanding of others’ work situations, you are able to develop strong collaborative relationships across employees with different educational and professional backgrounds. 	
• You have personal or professional making experience, pedagogical expertise and DEIB expertise 	
• You are structured, service-minded, approachable, and able to build commitment to strategic decisions. 	
• You thrive in a diverse environment with a wide variety of tasks. 	
• You have collaboration skills and the ability to build networks across professional groups, including across the organization 	
• You have strong communication skills in English (oral and written) and is ready to learn Danish.    

  Living in Copenhagen

  The university is situated in Copenhagen, which is consistently rated among the world's top 10 most livable cities. Located in Denmark, ranked in the top three happiest countries globally, Copenhagen boasts a vibrant culture, rich in music, theater, and community organizations. Life for families is made easier via a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual-career opportunities, maternity/parental leave, and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark. Useful information is also available at the university’s International Staff Mobility (ISM) office, which offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Terms of employment

  The Operation Director reports to the Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm. You will be employed as a senior consultant with managerial responsibility in accordance with the collective agreement for academics in the state sector. There is an opportunity to negotiate additional allowances based on qualifications.

  Note that Denmark protects the economic, social, and physical well-being of its workers, which includes robust health care, childcare, elder care, and other generous benefits. Thus, direct salary comparisons across nations are typically not meaningful.

   

  Further information

  For dedicated information on the new Makerspace, go here: ucphmakerspace.dk

  You are welcome to contact Head of Administration, Department of Computer Science, Camilla Lillholm (camillaj@di.ku.dk), or the Academic Director Professor Pernille Bjørn (pernille.bjorn@di.ku.dk) if you have any inquiries about the position.

   

  Filing of application

  As part of the application for the position, please write and submit a 1-page appendix labeled "Core Competences - NAME” in English, where you answer the below questions (one paragraph for each question), considering the description of the position as well as the SCIENCE Makerspace vision, which you can read more about at ucphmakerspace.dk.
 You are not allowed to use AI when writing the appendix. The questions are:

   	
• What is your approach for leadership and management of the SCIENCE Makerspace 	
• What makes you excited about the SCIENCE Makerspace?  	
• What do you expect will be the most challenging part of making the SCIENCE Makerspace vision a reality?   Please submit your application, including appendix, CV and relevant documentation, electronically via the Job Portal (click the link “APPLY FOR THE POSITION” at the bottom of the advertisement), so that it reaches us no later than 14 November 2026. We expect to hold interviews on 27 November 2026 and 4 December 2026.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion, or sexual orientation. Appointments will be based solely on qualifications.

jobs.occupation: Embedded Software Engineer, Electric Floor Heating
jobs.description:
Embedded software developer looking for new challenges at an industry-leading company? Want to work with a skilled R&D team to keep advancing our successful thermostats for underfloor heating systems? Keen on working for a smaller company, where your work really matters every day? Then please read on and tap “Apply” below.

OJ Electronics, a global producer of underfloor heating solutions and HVAC drives and controllers, is looking for an embedded software engineer to join our impressive and highly diverse R&D department.

Working with skilled and experienced colleagues in software development, hardware development and cloud-based solutions, your main job will be to help develop real-time embedded systems that control our energy-efficient heating solutions.

You will be involved throughout the product lifecycle, from initial idea to shipped firmware. And your day-to-day work will involve tackling challenges in areas as diverse as wireless communication, home automation protocols, display technologies and control-system engineering.

Your role

Reporting directly to our R&D development manager, you’ll be expected to:

• Develop embedded C/C++ code for microcontrollers

• Integrate software with custom hardware

• Contribute to system design and architecture

• Maintain code quality through testing and refactoring (unit and integration tests)

• Contribute to system design and architecture

• Participate in agile ceremonies and code reviews

• Use simulation tools to model and validate physical systems and control strategies.

Our expectations

When reviewing your application, we will look for:

• Proficiency in C/C++ for embedded systems

• At least three years of work-experience in embedded software development

• Experience with microcontrollers and real-time programming (Free RTOS and/or “bare metal”)

• Familiarity with embedded debugging tools (e.g., oscilloscopes, JTAG)

• Understanding of hardware/software interfaces

• Ability to read and interpret schematics and datasheets

• Experience with version control (Git + Git Flow) and CI/CD

• Basic knowledge of communication protocols (e.g., UART, I2C, SPI)

• Structured problem-solving and debugging skills

• Clear and concise technical communication (in English)

• Team-oriented mindset and agile collaboration experience

• Independence, accountability, and a friendly demeanor

• A willingness to work on-site from our office in Sønderborg. A remote or hybrid setup is not possible for this job

• Experience using simulation tools to model and validate physical systems and control strategies

In addition, useful skills include:

• Experience with embedded display technologies (e.g. TFT, LCD)

• Familiarity with touch interfaces (capacitive/resistive)

• Experience with UI frameworks for embedded systems and optimizing UI/UX for embedded systems with limited resources

• Experience with system modeling, simulation, and control engineering is considered a significant advantage

• Driver development for display controllers and touch sensors

• Development with wireless protocols such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)

• Understanding of Apple HomeKit (AHK) integration and certification flows

• Knowledge of Matter (Connectivity Standards Alliance) and smart home integration

• Knowledge about security for embedded systems

Working at OJ

Looking for a company where you matter every day? At OJ, you’ll find:

• A flat organizational structure where decisions are implemented quickly

• Opportunities to grow by taking on greater responsibility over time

• An informal, friendly and open workplace culture

• An employee satisfaction score over 80 for several years running

Note that this position requires a day-to-day physical presence at our offices in Sønderborg, Denmark.

The application process

For this position, we will be interviewing on an ongoing basis until we find the right person. Due to the summer holidays we expect to start interviewing mid to late August.

About OJ Electronics

Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Sønderborg, Denmark, OJ Electronics produces electronic controls for underfloor heating and HVAC controls and drives. Our products are available through partners and distributors worldwide, and we have subsidiaries and sales offices in key markets, including the United States and Poland. Everywhere, we are known for our innovative approach, insistence on product quality, and deep application knowledge – all of which helps customers differentiate themselves in the market.

In June 2023, OJ Electronics was acquired by BITZER Electronics, a BITZER Group company also headquartered in Sønderborg. This makes OJ Electronics part of the BITZER Group family, which is represented at 75 locations in over 40 countries and employs some 4300 people worldwide, 185 in OJ Electronics, Sønderborg, Denmark.

If you have any questions, please contact

Jesper Højmark Esbensen

Phone: 82 30 78 28

Application deadline:

As soon as possible

If you’re an experienced embedded software engineer who enjoys working where SOFTWARE, POWER ELECTRONICS, MOTOR TECHNOLOGY and CONTROL ENGINEERING meet, this could be the job for you.

OJ Electronics – a Danish producer of HVAC drives, AHU controllers, and thermostats for electric floor heating – is looking for an intermediate/senior-level embedded software engineer to join our Drives software team in Sønderborg, Denmark.

Your main job will be to develop the embedded software behind our VARIABLE SPEED DRIVES for energy-efficient HVAC applications – working on solutions that combine sophisticated control with robust, real-world performance.

You’ll be involved throughout the development process, from early ideas and system architecture to simulation, testing and validation. And because our products bring software and hardware closely together, you’ll work across disciplines rather than disappearing into a software silo.

Your role

Reporting directly to our R&D development manager, you’ll be expected to:

• Develop embedded software solutions, primarily for power electronics and variable speed drives

• Participate in cross-functional development projects

• Contribute during early ideation phases

• Solve complex development challenges

• Contribute to system design and architecture

• Build robust simulation models to validate control concepts early in the development cycle

• Take responsibility for documentation

• Participate in testing and validation

Broad-based collaboration

As part of our diverse R&D team, you’ll work alongside hardware engineers and other specialists, contributing to the entire product lifecycle and getting involved in challenges ranging from communication and automation protocols to motor technologies and control-system engineering.

You’ll also have the satisfaction of seeing your own code running in thousands of products – helping improve everyday comfort and energy efficiency for users around the world.

Must-have qualifications

• A bachelor’s or master’s degree in embedded software, electronics engineering or a similar field

• At least three years of professional embedded software development experience

• Strong C/C++ skills for embedded systems

• Experience with microcontrollers and real-time programming

• Experience with motor control systems

• Understanding of control engineering in embedded systems

• Hands-on experience with hardware/software debugging tools such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and JTAG

• A good understanding of hardware/software interfaces

• The ability to read and interpret schematics and datasheets

• Experience with Git, Git Flow and CI/CD

• Knowledge of communication interfaces such as UART, I2C and SPI

• Practical laboratory testing and validation experience

• Structured problem-solving and debugging skills

• Clear and concise technical communication in English

• A team-oriented mindset and experience with agile collaboration

Nice-to-have qualifications

Experience with:

• Modbus or BACnet

• MATLAB simulation

• Wi-Fi or Bluetooth Low Energy

• Embedded-system security

Working at OJ

At OJ Electronics, you’ll find an informal, open and collaborative culture where people take pride in doing quality work.

We offer:

• A flat organizational structure where decisions are made quickly

• Opportunities to grow your expertise and responsibility over time

• A healthy work-life balance and flexible working hours

• Competitive salary and pension package

• A modern workplace with canteen and good facilities

Employee satisfaction scores average 85 – and we take pride in maintaining a workplace where people truly thrive.

Please note that this position is based in Sønderborg, Denmark, and requires your physical presence on site. This is not a hybrid or remote position.

The application process

For this position, we will be interviewing on an ongoing basis until we find the right person.

About OJ Electronics

Founded in 1964 and headquartered in Sønderborg, Denmark, OJ Electronics produces electronic controls for underfloor heating and HVAC controls and drives. Our products are available through partners and distributors worldwide, and we have subsidiaries and sales offices in key markets, including the United States and Poland. Everywhere, we are known for our innovative approach, insistence on product quality, and deep application knowledge – all of which helps customers differentiate themselves in the market.

In June 2023, OJ Electronics was acquired by BITZER Electronics, a BITZER Group company also headquartered in Sønderborg. This makes OJ Electronics part of the BITZER Group family, which is represented at 75 locations in over 40 countries and employs some 4300 people worldwide, 185 in OJ Electronics, Sønderborg, Denmark.

jobs.occupation: EY-Parthenon - Senior Consultant - Technology in M&A
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 1706128

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go.

Join EY and help to build a better working world.

As you write your next chapter, what shape will it take?

Are you ready to take the next step in your M&A career and work on some of the most exciting deals in the market? We are looking for a Senior Consultant to join our Transaction Strategy and Execution team in Copenhagen.

In this role, you will be part of a high-performing team that supports clients across the full deal lifecycle: from M&A strategy to execution. You will work closely with clients on complex, high-impact engagements, where your insights and capabilities will drive real results. At the same time, you will play an active role in shaping our team, contributing to a strong culture and supporting the development of future leaders.

Shape your future with confidence.

Skills and attributes for success

You are analytically strong and comfortable working with complex data and problem-solving, using AI-enabled tools to enhance analysis and insight generation. You bring a structured and pragmatic approach, combined with strong business understanding and attention to detail.

You thrive in fast-paced environments and can manage ambiguity while maintaining focus on delivering high-quality outcomes. At the same time, you communicate clearly and confidently, translating complexity into actionable insights for both clients and colleagues.

You bring experience from client-facing or in-house roles across M&A execution (pre- and/or post-deal) and operational delivery, for example:

• Product and technology diligence

• Assessment of the product portfolio and roadmap, together with the underlying technology and R&D setup to evaluate commercial attractiveness/value creation potential

• IT diligence

• Evaluating the IT environments, from strategy to costs, to identify risks and opportunities, and to inform the investment case

• Technology integration and separation

• Leading technology workstreams, from strategy to execution/operationalization

• Digital value creation

• Assessing digital and AI-driven value creation opportunities, and implications for the deal theses and post-deal value capture

As a Senior Consultant, you will work across a range of M&A engagements spanning M&A strategy, operational diligence, as well as value creation and deal management. You are passionate about the operational aspects of M&A, thrive in fast-paced and ambiguous environments, and build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Conducting operational due diligence/value creation analysis

• Managing and driving workstreams across pre- and post-deal engagements

• Supporting business development through pitch content, proposals and client conversations

What we look for

As our new colleague you bring 3-6 years of experience from strategy and M&A consulting or industry experience. You bring an inclusive approach, building strong relationships with both clients and colleagues and are a strong communicator who can translate complex ideas into clear and actionable insights. You take ownership of your work with a consistent focus on quality and impact.

What’s in it for you

• Work on complex, high-profile M&A and divestment engagements

• Collaborate with integrated teams across geographies and disciplines

• Continuous coaching, feedback and formal learning to support your development

• A purpose-led culture focused on creating long-term value for clients and society

• Hybrid work model, balancing in-office and client-site collaboration with flexibility

• A role with broad responsibility and room to shape how we deliver and grow

What you can expect during the recruitment process

• Interview process will include a take-home case and an on-the-spot case

• Your CV gives us the basics; a strong cover letter helps us understand your motivation and relevant experience beyond M&A consulting

Please submit your application no later than 1 December 2026. Selection and interviews are ongoing. If you have any questions or need more information about the role, please contact Ludvig Anderberg at Ludvig.Anderberg@parthenon.ey.com For questions regarding the recruitment process, contact Jakob Damsted at jakob.damsted@dk.ey.com.

EY | Building a better working world

EY is building a better working world by creating new value for clients, people, society and the planet, while building trust in capital markets.

Enabled by data, AI and advanced technology, EY teams help clients shape the future with confidence and develop answers for the most pressing issues of today and tomorrow.

EY teams work across a full spectrum of services in assurance, consulting, tax, strategy and transactions. Fueled by sector insights, a globally connected, multi-disciplinary network and diverse ecosystem partners, EY teams can provide services in more than 150 countries and territories.

Highlights:

• Full-Stack Python/TS engineer needed for a B2B SaaS startup in Copenhagen (with plenty of traction!)

• We have a lean, get-stuff-done team. No annoying extra management layers or unnecessary bureaucratic rituals. And we are "AI-forward" in our own development practices.

• You will own features end to end, from the data model through to the screen, on a platform that manufacturers rely on to keep production lines running.

• You will work in a small engineering team, directly with the person who decides what we build, and the problems you spend your time on are hard because the domain is hard, not because the organization is.

• We're building legitimately useful tools for the industries and companies that make the world go around.... manufacturers. Both AI-tools and just "plain-old-good-software" tools.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality, all in a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth.

The platform now covers more ground than the team that built it. We are hiring engineers to keep that pace sustainable, and to go deeper on the parts of the product our customers are pushing hardest.

The role

You will join a small engineering team and work across the whole stack: Python on the backend, TypeScript on the frontend and in the AI layers. There is no split between people who design and people who implement. You will take a problem from a customer conversation or a product decision through to something running in production for real manufacturers.

You will work directly with our co-founder and CEO, who is a hands-on product builder himself. That means short conversations instead of tickets thrown over a wall, and it means your questions about why something should work a certain way get answered by the person who decided it.

The domain is genuinely complicated, and that is the interesting part. Supplier relationships in automotive involve deep hierarchies, long-running approval processes, strict audit requirements and a lot of state that has to be exactly right. Modeling that well is most of the job.

Title and level flex with experience. We are open to strong mid-level engineers and to senior engineers who want more scope than their current company gives them.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and on a codebase with this much implicit context, working through problems with the rest of the team in person is much faster than doing it in writing. Sensible flexibility when you need it is a given; full-time remote is not what we are offering.

Our current stack:

• Backend: Python / Django

• Frontend: Vue (but no specific Vue experience is needed)

• Infrastructure: AWS (mostly)

• Agents: Cloudflare (TypeScript) + Claude & OpenAI platform

What you will do

• Build features end to end, from data model and backend logic through to the TypeScript frontend our customers actually click on.

• Build end-to-end / front-to-back AI features (in-app AI assistants, background worker agents, email-routing agents, customer-configurable agent framework components)

• Design and evolve the relational data model that sits under supplier relationships, approvals and quality records.

• Take vaguely defined customer problems and turn them into something specific enough to build, then build it.

• Work on integrations between Supplios and customer systems (ERP and adjacent tooling), where failures have visible consequences for a production line.

• Improve the parts of the codebase that need it, rather than routing around them.

• Review other people's code and have yours reviewed; we keep the loop tight and unbureaucratic.

• Help keep the platform healthy in production across our regions: errors, performance and the boring things that keep customers trusting us.

• Take part in product decisions. Engineers here are expected to have opinions about what we build, not just how.

What we are looking for

Essential

• Professional experience with Python. This is not negotiable; the backend is Python and you need to be effective in it.

• Solid TypeScript experience and genuine comfort working on the frontend.

• Experience building and running SaaS products, including the part after launch where real users depend on them.

• AI-forward development techniques. (This does not mean you no longer write code.)

• A track record of owning work end to end without waiting to be told what to do next.

• The temperament for a small, senior company: high ownership, low ceremony.

• You want to work primarily from an office in central Copenhagen, with a small team.

Nice to have

Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. Nobody has all of these.

• Experience with B2B enterprise SaaS, especially where customers are large and demanding and implementations are not self-serve. This is a significant plus.

• Experience with complex relational data modeling, and with large, long-lived codebases that you did not write yourself. A big plus.

• Experience building AI-based products, using the latest frameworks/harnesses and infrastructure components (including RAG) is a significant plus.

• Familiarity with any of: domain-driven design, the actor model, finite state machines, CQRS, event-driven architecture. We use these ideas where they earn their place, and it helps if the vocabulary is already yours.

• Startup experience, particularly early stage. A significant plus.

• Knowledge of manufacturing, automotive or supply chain. Useful, but we can teach you the domain; we cannot teach you the craft, so do not rule yourself out on this.

Language

English is the only important language for this position; we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• The scope is unusually large for the stage. You are one of a small number of engineers on a platform that serves demanding customers globally. What you build ships, and it ships soon.

• No layers between you and the decisions. You work directly with the co-founder and CEO, who runs product. There is no committee to navigate and nobody to translate your work for you.

• Hard problems that are not artificially hard. The complexity comes from the domain (hierarchies, state, audit trails, integrations that must not fail), not from organisational overhead.

• Real customers already, and real gaps. The product has paying customers in automotive and clear places where it needs to get better. Both halves of that are true, and both are why this is a good job.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc position in the intellectual history of corporate politics
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment
Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organization. Information about CBS as a workplace is available at www.cbs.dk/en/about-cbs/jobs-cbs. 

For further information, please contact: PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen, email: mhj.bhl@cbs.dk, or Head of Department Pia Bramming, e-mail pib.bhl@cbs.dk. Information about the department may be found at www.cbs.dk/bhl. Information about Copenhagen Business School is available at https://www.cbs.dk/en.

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Details about Copenhagen Business School and the department are available at www.cbs.dk.

The European Spallation Source (ESS) is one of Europe’s largest research infrastructure projects and is building the world’s most powerful neutron source. The Research Software Engineering (RSE) group develops and maintains critical software systems that make neutron scattering experiments at ESS possible and successful.

As a Scientific Software Engineer, you will contribute to the development of key platforms supporting the scientific user journey, including the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information systems. You will work closely with scientists, software engineers, and stakeholders across ESS to gather requirements, understand user needs, and develop robust software solutions that integrate seamlessly with the wider ESS ecosystem.

The RSE group uses modern web technologies and software engineering practices to deliver high-quality software with a long operational lifetime. In addition, the group is expanding its focus on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning solutions that can enhance the scientific user experience. As part of this effort, you will contribute to new AI-related initiatives and help establish RSE as a centre of expertise and development for AI applications within the Science Directorate.

This position is well suited for an experienced software engineer with a strong technical foundation, excellent collaboration skills, and a passion for building software that enables world-class scientific research.

• Design, develop, test, and maintain software systems supporting the scientific user journey at ESS.

• Contribute to the development of the ESS User Portal, metadata catalogue, electronic notebook, and related scientific information management systems.

• Gather, analyse, and refine requirements from scientific and technical stakeholders across ESS.

• Design and implement integrations between RSE applications and other ESS services and platforms.

• Apply modern software engineering practices to deliver reliable, maintainable, and high-quality software solutions.

• Contribute to technical and process improvements within the SIMS group.

• Participate in AI and Machine Learning initiatives supporting the Science Directorate.

• Collaborate with scientists, software engineers, and international partners to develop innovative solutions for scientific computing and data management.

• Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing within the team when appropriate.

• Contribute to software architecture discussions and technology decisions within the group.

Required qualifications

• Typically 4-7 years of relevant professional experience in software development.

• Experience developing modern web applications and services.

• Strong programming skills and experience with modern software development practices.

• Experience gathering requirements and working directly with stakeholders and end users.

Desirable qualifications

As Manager, Reverse Logistics & Compliance you will develop and manage global reverse logistics processes across Genmab’s distribution network in the US, EU and APAC.

The role covers product returns, recall logistics, expired and damaged inventory, and product destruction, ensuring traceability, inventory accuracy and effective coordination with Quality, Finance and relevant compliance functions.

You will also coordinate compliance across global supply chain activities, working closely with Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal and Finance to embed applicable regulatory requirements and internal controls into operational processes. • Change assessment and training: Partner with Quality and compliance functions to assess the supply chain impact of regulatory and operational changes, translate agreed requirements into procedures and controls, and coordinate training for internal teams and external partners.

• Management of stakeholders: Corporate and Regional Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Commercial/Trade, Procurement, IT and serialization teams, alongside 3PLs, distributors, transportation providers and authorized destruction partners.

• Familiarity with ERP and warehouse management systems, preferably SAP, and operational reporting tools.

• Experience supporting supplier oversight, deviations, corrective actions, audits and controlled documentation.

You’re probably wondering at this stage, and Famly are...? Well, it all began when our co-founder Henrik’s daughter was ready to start at daycare. Top-notch work equipment (including noise cancelling headphones for those focus periods!).

We believe collaboration happens best in person, so we have the default of four days a week in office - but with plenty of flexibility for when life happens outside the office too.

Drive meaningful impact across the life sciences industry.

As our next Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups -locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most.

About the role

As a Manager - Business Advisory and Project Management, you will work closely with clients and colleagues to address complex challenges across the life sciences value chain. You will take ownership of your work and contribute to delivering solutions that create real, lasting impact. This is a Senior role designed to provide project and program leadership to deliver strategic technical solutions that address complex client issues in the Life Sciences industry. You will be handling implementation/migration projects and programs to achieve desired outcomes and ensure successful business growth. You will also seek new business opportunities to help BASE life science grow its presence within existing and new customers.

Additionally, you will contribute to internal initiatives and training to further strengthen BASE life science’s project and program management methodologies, approach, and tools.

You will lead teams consisting of multiple workstreams, which could include BASE/Infosys, external third party, or client stakeholders. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in, project/program management and the ability to translate business requirements into technical specifications.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing responses to Requests for Proposals (RfPs), ensuring adequate planning for scope, timelines and budget

• Monitoring project/program status including milestones, risks, issues, budgets, etc.

• Acting as a delivery escalation point and proactively ensuring escalations are handled promptly with a clear action and communication plan.

• Creating and delivering tailored communication based on audience, i.e., executive level summaries for client stakeholders, or senior executives in BASE life science, status reports at a project or program-level at a suitable cadence for team members

• Intervening, when necessary, to ensure costs, timelines and quality are on track.

• Lead a cross-functional team to deliver projects/programs to the required scope, on time, within budget, and to the satisfaction of our life science industry stakeholders.

• Collaborate with business stakeholders in the life science industry to understand their needs and translate them into executable plans for the project team.

• Develop plans, timelines, and budgets for projects/programs for which you are responsible.

• Track and report on project/program progress, identifying and mitigating risks as needed.

• Facilitate communication and collaboration between the project team, life science industry stakeholders, and other teams within BASE life science.

You bring:

• 5+ years of experience as a technical project/program manager within Regulatory, Clinical, Quality or other GxP areas in the life science industry.

• Experience leading technical teams and delivering data driven projects/programs.

• Experience selling either projects or products to clients.

• Experience working with Veeva Vault, SalesForce or similar technologies.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2015, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting company working exclusively in life sciences, built on a simple purpose: grow our people, and deliver real impact for our customers.

We don't think AI is a feature you bolt onto existing systems — we think it's the layer through which a life sciences company's strategy actually gets executed, end to end. With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Spain, Switzerland, the UK, Germany, France, Italy, and the US, we work with top-10 pharma and ambitious biotechs alike, and with technology partners including Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Google, AWS, Microsoft, and Amass — turning that belief into deployed, compliant, sellable solutions, not slideware.

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact — grounded in five core values: team spirit, trust, openness, ambition, and execution.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

Desirable

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

jobs.description:
Shape the future of real-time vision in sports technology

Join Trackman’s new Simulator Technology team and help build next-generation camera systems for the world’s leading golf simulators. We are looking for an experienced engineer with expertise in real-time video pipelines, camera integration, and low-latency systems.

About the team

Trackman is the global leader in indoor golf technology, delivering advanced simulator experiences through precision tracking, virtual golf software, and in-bay technology.

Our new Simulator Technology´s (SimTech) mission is to drive innovation across the entire in-bay customer experience: cameras, projectors, kiosks, moving floors, and the software that ties them together. The team works in close collaboration with Trackman's hardware, tracking, ML, and Virtual Golf teams to deliver seamless, world-class experiences. This is a unique opportunity to become one of the first engineers shaping the future of Trackman’s simulator technology used by elite athletes and golfers around the world.

The role

You will help build a Windows-based real-time vision platform that captures camera streams, runs AI-based image analysis, and outputs video overlays. The role focuses on low-latency camera integration and high-performance video pipelines. This work sits at the heart of SimTech's camera platform the low-level foundation that everything from swing capture to AI coaching will be built on. Our current team is strong in vision/ML, and we need an engineer who specializes in camera integration and real-time video pipelines.

What you will do

• 
Design and implement low-latency camera capture pipelines on Windows.

• 
Integrate with 3rd party cameras using vendor SDKs as well as our own custom camera modules

• 
Build reliable frame pipelines from capture to inference handoff to overlay output.

• 
Optimize for stable FPS, low jitter, and deterministic end-to-end latency.

• 
Implement robust camera lifecycle handling: hot-plug, disconnect/reconnect, error recovery.

• 
Work closely with ML engineers to define frame formats, metadata, and timing contracts.

• 
Build diagnostics: dropped-frame counters, latency telemetry, and health logging.

• 
Support production readiness across different camera models and hardware configurations.

Success in this role means delivering stable, low-latency dual-camera pipelines with reliable recovery mechanisms, robust telemetry, and a well-documented architecture that enables the broader SimTech team to confidently build on the platform.

Job requirements

• 
5+ years in real-time video, machine vision, or camera systems engineering.

• 
Strong C++ (C++17 or newer) - preferably on Windows.

• 
Hands-on with Media Foundation and/or DirectShow capture stacks.

• 
Proven integration experience with industrial camera SDKs (IDS peak / uEye SDK strongly preferred).

• 
Deep understanding of pixel formats, color conversion, timestamps, and buffering.

• 
Solid grasp of USB3 Vision / GenICam concepts and camera controls (exposure, gain, trigger modes).

• 
Experience with multithreaded/parallel pipelines and performance profiling.

• 
Practical OpenCV experience for image handling and overlay operations.

• 
Experience designing fault-tolerant long-running services/applications.

Preferred qualifications: Experience with GStreamer or FFmpeg, GPU acceleration, multi-camera synchronization, inference runtimes, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and GenICam / USB3 Vision standards is considered a plus.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Data & AI Architecture, based in Copenhagen or London, to lead our team of four Data, AI and Solution Architects and serve as the design authority for Pandora’s Data & AI platform. This is a genuine dual role. You’ll set the architectural direction and standards, while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge, review and approve the designs that matter.

Our target architecture is Databricks, including Delta Lake, medallion patterns and Unity Catalog, while Azure Synapse and its conformed enterprise models continue to power a significant part of the estate across supply chain, commerce, manufacturing, corporate technology and omni-channel.

A critical part of the role is leading the transition to Databricks: shaping the target architecture, determining where ownership sits as the platform evolves, and ensuring existing solutions remain coherent and supported throughout the journey.

The role is approximately 60% architecture and 40% people leadership. You’ll lead and develop four architects, but this is not a role where technical accountability is delegated to the team. Both sides of the role are real, and you’ll be expected to lead both.

Scope and authority

• Design authority for Data & Analytics: approves data and AI solution designs, and can require rework, attach conditions to an approval, or withhold approval.

• Chairs the architecture review forum, setting its standards, cadence and quality gates, and deciding what requires review against what is already covered by an approved pattern.

• Resolves conflicting design positions across architects, lead engineers and delivery teams.

• Owns reference architectures, solution patterns, data contracts and architecture decision records — accountable for their adoption, not just their publication.

• Owns the team's roadmap, capacity allocation across workstreams, and budget, including engagement of external consulting resources.

• Translates and enforces the Data & AI architecture strategy set by the Global Director, and informs how it evolves.

Job Responsibilities

Architecture

• Set and enforce the standards for what is built on Databricks as the target architecture, what remains on Synapse for now, and what is retired — and on what evidence.

• Decide how data products are aligned: source-aligned versus domain-aligned versus consumer-aligned, where ownership and stewardship sit, and where a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) serves better than distributed ownership.

• Review technical designs from solution architects and lead engineers against platform standards; give feedback that changes the design, not just documents it.

• Define and evolve reference architectures, solution patterns and data contracts so that quality is built in rather than inspected in.

• Lead design sessions with architects, engineering and business stakeholders on complex or contested problems.

• Oversee transitional architectures through to legacy decommission, maintaining business continuity and closing the parallel run.

AI architecture

• Set and enforce architecture standards for agentic systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation, guardrails and observability.

• Set and enforce architecture standards for ML systems: feature reuse, training and serving topology, model lifecycle, and monitoring for drift.

• Approve AI solution designs with enough depth to arbitrate them on the technical merits, and in line with AI policy and applicable regulation.

Governance and regulation

• Embed privacy-by-design and personal data handling requirements into platform patterns, particularly across commerce and omni-channel.

• Maintain computational governance: data quality frameworks, contracts and lineage as platform capability rather than project effort.

Team leadership

• Line management for four architects: coaching, performance, career development, hiring.

• Establish ways of working — review process, documentation standards, quality gates — and hold the team to them.

• Represent architecture in leadership forums, steering committees and cross-functional planning.

• Keep architects hands-on and embedded with engineering teams; architecture produced at a distance from delivery does not land.

What you will have done by month 12

• A published and adopted standard for what is built on Databricks, with evidence of designs changed by it.

• A clear model for data product alignment and ownership, applied on live work rather than documented in isolation.

• An architecture review forum running to a predictable cadence, with a visible ADR record and a known path for challenging a decision.

• Approved agentic and ML reference patterns in use.

• At least one legacy component fully decommissioned, not just superseded.

• A development plan in place for each of the four architects, and any open roles filled.

Essential experience

• 5+ years designing and delivering production data platform solutions at enterprise scale, hands-on.

• At least 2 years line-managing technical specialists, including performance management, career development and hiring.

• Has held a design approval or architecture governance mandate, including declining designs and making that decision hold.

• Has led a platform migration or a parallel-run estate through to legacy decommission.

• Deep working knowledge of Databricks (Delta Lake, medallion, Unity Catalog) as a target architecture, plus enough Azure Synapse (star schemas, conformed models, dedicated pools) to govern what remains there, and pipeline orchestration with ADF or Databricks Workflows.

• Has designed source-aligned, domain-aligned and consumer-aligned data products, with a clear view of where distributed domain ownership beats a conformed enterprise model (CDM/RDM) and where it does not.

• Has implemented or governed a domain ownership model — data mesh or similar — including the federated governance and stewardship that makes it work.

• Has architected agentic and ML systems: orchestration, tool and data access boundaries, evaluation and guardrails; feature and model lifecycle, serving, and monitoring for drift.

• Has set architecture standards that others adopted — solution patterns, reference architectures and architecture decision records.

• Has implemented data quality frameworks, data contracts or computational governance in production.

• Holds an architectural position under delivery pressure, and judges well when to concede.

• Communicates architecture clearly to technical and business audiences, including solution designs, ADRs and data flow diagrams.

• Understanding of retail, manufacturing, finance or supply chain business processes and how data flows through a business.

Desirable

• Familiarity with EU AI Act obligations and enterprise AI governance.

Did we get your attention?

We hope you got all your questions answered and feel confident applying for this position. If you see yourself in the role and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply! We are an international team, so please make sure to send us your application in English to be considered. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Digital & Technology Hub in Copenhagen, in a rapidly growing environment of highly skilled and experienced colleagues, which is a key initiative that goes along with Pandora’s experience & ambitions.Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.
